# Spin-offs and demergers — NiftyTotalMarket

*Run 2026-11-20 · filings window 2024-06-13 → 2026-11-15 · 4708 restructuring filings across 558 companies · 33 confirmed demergers, 18 partial spin-offs (subsidiary IPOs), 11 completed demergers, 0 probable, 11 indicated, 471 rights / preferential offerings, 893 other restructurings · judge: claude-opus-5 read the schemes, three years of calls and the segment pages.*

**The method, in one paragraph.** Spin-offs are where the notes say the bargains hide: the new stock is sold by holders who never chose it for about a year, the parent is often the better buy before the split, insiders tell you what they think through the stock and options they take in the new entity, and a pro-forma statement plus the peer P/E prices what the market is ignoring. This report puts the CONFIRMED demergers first — a demerger scheme on the exchange record — each with when the new entity lists, why management is doing it (three years of calls, with the transcript each point came from), the parent's last three years with charts, P/E and cash flows, and the separated business's own numbers from the annual reports and presentations, page-cited. Probable and indicated cases follow, then every other restructuring on file.

# Confirmed demergers — in full

## UPL — UPL Ltd.

**CONFIRMED** (a demerger scheme is on the exchange record) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 7.1/10 · spin-off · 9 filing(s) from CALLS, NSE · first 2026-01-19, latest 2026-08-01

> **Listing:** NOT YET — scheme at 'exchange_noc' stage; UPL Global Sustainable Agri Solutions Limited will list only after NCLT sanction, effectiveness and a record date; indicated timeline: Not a stated listing date. Press release February 20, 2026: “The transaction is expected to be completed within 12–15 months”. NSE letter July 29, 2026: UPL Global “shall ensure that steps for listing of specified securities are completed and trading in securities commences within sixty days ___ of receipt of the order of the Hon'ble High Court/NCLT”. As of November 2, 2026 the Scheme remains subject to shareholder, regulator and NCLT approvals

**The stages, as filed:** exchange_noc (2026-07-29)

**Stated in the filings:** resulting company **UPL Global Sustainable Agri Solutions Limited**; entitlement **1 for every 1**.

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** India Crop Protection Business demerged into UPL 2, then combined with UPL's international (global) crop protection business — class `value_unlocking`.

- *Insiders:* Promoters hold 100% of UPL 2 pre-Scheme, 71.56% post (33.09% of UPL 1); UPL 2 Promoters voluntarily retain entire holding, no transfer for eighteen months from Listing Date; Mike Frank to be UPL Global CEO
- *What it reveals:* Crop protection is the bulk of UPL: segment revenue Rs 42,399 cr of Rs 51,839 cr FY26. UPL Cayman alone: USD 4,187 Mn turnover, USD 1,599 Mn net worth; demerged India undertaking 31.15% of UPL 1 turnover. CFO frames it as deleveraging and balance-sheet strengthening
- *Selling pressure:* likely — 1 new UPL 2 share to every UPL 1 holder, a crop-protection-only line; promoters (71.56%) locked 18 months, so only public float trades
- *Parent or spin:* spin · *option pricing date:* July 31, 2026 — ESOP Swap Transaction completed; UPL Cayman 2 option holders issued new options in UPL Cayman 1 under UCPL LTI Plan 2026 (strike/pricing not stated)
- *Read next:* The Composite Scheme of Arrangement with Joint Valuation Report and J.P. Morgan fairness opinion, on the company's scheme-of-arrangement webpage
- *In their words:* “UPL 2, which shall be listed pursuant to the Scheme would be a dedicated crop protection platform.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

Management's stated reason is that UPL is a conglomerate whose crop protection business is trapped inside a diversified holding structure and is therefore mis-valued: Bikash Prasad said on the May 2026 Capital Markets Day that "even today market is valuing us using a single conglomerate multiple" and that UPL carries "a huge conglomerate discount," so separation would make "the sum of the parts... much, much clearer." The Scheme (board-approved 20 Feb 2026) is a three-step composite arrangement: amalgamate UPL Sustainable Agri Solutions (UPL SAS, India crop protection, 90.91% owned, FY25 turnover INR 24,120 Mn or 31.15% of UPL's turnover) into UPL Limited; demerge that India crop protection undertaking into UPL Global Sustainable Agri Solutions (UPL 2) on a 1:1 share entitlement; then amalgamate UPL Crop Protection Holdings Ltd., Cayman (UPL Cayman, the 77.78%-held international crop protection vehicle, FY25 turnover USD 4,187 Mn, net worth USD 1,599 Mn) into UPL 2 at 1,000 UPL 2 shares for every 213 UPL Cayman shares, with UPL SAS holders getting 1,000 UPL shares per 48 UPL SAS shares. The problems it is said to solve: a split holding structure created by the 2022 platform carve-out that left India and international crop protection in separate vehicles; a single conglomerate multiple and no value visibility per platform; crop protection's cash-flow and capital-allocation needs being, as COO Toshan Tamhane put it in Feb 2026, "very different from that of the seeds business" (he cited Corteva's own crop protection/seeds split); and inability to raise capital or set governance per platform — the filing says the Scheme lets UPL 1 and UPL 2 "raise capital independently" and "optimize its capital structure," and Prasad said platforms with "independent capital structure, independent governance structure... will grow much faster." The demand came from several directions: analysts and investors gave five pieces of feedback that Prasad catalogued (reporting consistency, the four below-EBITDA items worth ~INR 5,000 crore or 60% of FY25 EBITDA, and debt/liquidity), rating agencies and lenders drove the deleveraging that Jai Shroff said had removed the leverage drag on the multiple, and private investors needed exits — KKR (which wrote a "$300-plus million check" into Advanta) and Alpha Wave (USD 350 Mn for ~12.44%, of which USD 250 Mn secondary from UPL Limited), plus The Upswing Trust, the UPL SAS investor that swapped into UPL Cayman and ends with 16.78% of UPL 2 as a public shareholder with one board nomination right. The result is two listed entities: UPL Limited as a diversified agri and specialty-chemicals platform keeping SUPERFORM as its manufacturing arm and incubating new verticals, and UPL Global as what Mike Frank (its CEO-designate) called "the world's second largest listed pure-play crop protection platform" in 140+ countries with 9 R&D centres, 25 formulation facilities and a 14% innovation rate. Shroff framed it as each business needing "a kind of independent life" and said the plan went through advisors and "at least 10 different structures," expected to complete in 12-15 months.

**How it evolved:** The idea surfaced as an unspecified value-unlock exercise on the 1 Aug 2025 Q1FY26 call, where Prasad said advisors had just been engaged to "explore unlocking value across all platforms" with "no firm decision on any structure," after Jai Shroff's press-release comment on restructuring; before that, on 31 Jan 2025, the only visible step was private monetization of Advanta (Alpha Wave's USD 350 Mn) and a net-debt/EBITDA target of ~2x. On 6 Nov 2025 it broadened to "restructuring or strategic fundraising, potential liquidity events like IPO," explicitly linked to deleveraging, alongside the DECCO-into-Advanta integration. By 2 Feb 2026 it had a timetable and a first concrete step — Advanta's DRHP filed 19 Jan 2026, described as "the first such step in this direction," with corporate actions for all platforms "within a period of 1 to 3 years" — and management argued seeds and crop protection are fundamentally different businesses. The crop protection scheme itself was announced 20 Feb 2026 (CCI clearance 2-3 Jun 2026, exchange observation letters and the Upswing swap completed 29-31 Jul 2026), and by the 11 May 2026 Capital Markets Day the debate had shifted to the structure's fairness, with Old Bridge calling it "fairly detrimental to the current shareholders," Shroff defending it and Prasad promising to take investor feedback "unfiltered to the board" within a month or two.

**What management expects from it:** UPL Global: pure-play crop protection across 140+ countries, independent capital structure and governance, faster growth, wider investor and lender base. UPL Limited: diversified agri and specialty-chemicals platform retaining SUPERFORM, incubating new ventures, deleveraged with net debt/EBITDA below 1.6x. Both: independent fundraising, clearer sum-of-parts valuation removing the conglomerate discount, sharper board and managerial focus.

And if some of those we decide to take, that would also help in terms of deleveraging the balance sheet.”

It's not a primary transaction. So the cash is not going to Advanta. It is coming to the selling shareholders, which are KKR and UPL Limited in this case.”

- *Scheme* — The 20 Feb 2026 board-approved Composite Scheme consolidates UPL SAS (India crop protection) and UPL Cayman (global crop protection) into UPL Global, to be listed; UPL Limited stays listed as a diversified agri and specialty-chemicals platform. “The Scheme proposes to consolidate the India Crop Protection Business held in UPL SAS and Global Crop Protection Business held in UPL Cayman, under a single entity, creating a focused, pure-play crop protection platform.”
- *Scheme* — Independent capital raising and capital-structure optimisation for each entity is given as a core benefit, alongside simplification of the group structure created by the 2022 platform carve-out and enhanced managerial and board focus. “The Scheme will allow UPL 1 and UPL 2 to raise capital independently, allowing each entity to optimize its capital structure and pursue business opportunities more efficiently and effectively.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

Astra Microwave is splitting itself into two sector-focused listed companies: the parent (AMPL) keeps Radar Electronics, Electronic Warfare and Telemetry, while the Space, Meteorology and Hydrology business is demerged on a going-concern basis into its wholly-owned subsidiary Astra Space Technologies Pvt Ltd (ASTPL), which will itself be listed on BSE and NSE. On the May 27, 2026 call MD S.G. Reddy said the board had given in-principle approval and framed the objective as creating 'sharper strategic and operational focus,' enabling dedicated management teams to chase sector-specific opportunities, enhancing governance and accountability, simplifying the corporate structure and creating 'clearer investment propositions to shareholders,' with focused growth, better capital allocation and improved operational efficiency over the medium to long term. The sizing numbers management gave: FY26 standalone turnover INR1,157 crore of which radar was ~60% and space plus meteorology ~16%; the scheme puts the demerged undertaking's FY26 turnover at ~INR157 crore, i.e. 13.58% of standalone turnover; the Dec-2025 order book of INR2,226 crore contained INR249 crore of space and INR369 crore of meteorology/hydrology orders. The scheme's stated reasoning is that space/met/hydro has 'distinct industry characteristics, competitive dynamics, regulatory environment, and risk profile' needing a differentiated strategy, and that a standalone entity would be 'better positioned to attract investors, strategic partners, lenders, and other stakeholders with sector-specific interests,' thereby unlocking the value of that undertaking for shareholders. Mechanically there is no cash consideration: shareholders get 1 ASTPL share of Rs 2 for every 1 AMPL share of Rs 2, ASTPL's existing promoter-held capital is cancelled, and post-scheme ASTPL mirrors AMPL (promoters 6.45%, public 93.55%). No investor, lender or partner is identified anywhere as having demanded the separation — it is presented as management/board-initiated strategic re-alignment, though Atim Kabra had repeatedly argued on earlier calls that the embedded space business was worth far more than the market credited (Aug 2025: 'very, very valuable'; Nov 2025: peers raising at $750-800m valuations with almost no revenue, close to Astra's whole market cap). The move is also backed with people: MD S. Gurunatha Reddy took on oversight of the demerger, stepped down as AMPL MD and director from close of September 30, 2026 to join ASTPL as a director, and Joint MD Dr M.V. Reddy became AMPL's MD from October 1, 2026. As of the last filings, BSE gave 'no adverse observations' and NSE 'no objection' on October 29, 2026, SEBI/NCLT approvals are still pending, and no effect of the scheme has been taken into the Q2 FY27 accounts.

**How it evolved:** Through the Aug 14, 2025 and Nov 13, 2025 calls there was no demerger talk at all, but the groundwork was visible: Astra Space Technologies had been incorporated as a wholly-owned subsidiary with Bangalore clean rooms and a ~INR230-239 crore space order book, and Atim Kabra argued the space business was being carried inside Astra at far less than standalone peers' valuations. On the Feb 13, 2026 call there was still no mention of a demerger, only Kabra's hint about needing to 'be creative' on financing and 'watch the space.' The board granted in-principle approval on Feb 27, 2026, which surfaced publicly in the April 3, 2026 press release (tied to the MD succession) and was first spoken to investors on the May 27, 2026 (Jun 2026) call, where the detailed scheme was promised 'over the next few weeks.' The board approved the full Scheme of Arrangement on June 10, 2026, and the stock exchanges issued their observation/no-objection letters on October 29, 2026; notably, not a single analyst asked a question about the demerger on the May 27, 2026 call.

**What management expects from it:** AMPL becomes a radar/EW/telemetry-focused listed company; space/met/hydro becomes a separately listed entity with its own management team, tailored growth strategy and capital allocation, sharper focus, better governance and accountability, a simpler structure, improved operational efficiency, easier access to sector-specific investors, partners and lenders, a clearer investment proposition and unlocked shareholder value. No margin, EBITDA or valuation targets were quantified.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *[Jun 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=78f3aacc-b7ef-4d51-b1e1-d6e5863786b8.pdf)* — First disclosure on a call: the board has in-principle approved demerging the space, meteorology and hydrology business, with the formal scheme to follow within weeks. “On a strategic front, the Board of Directors have in-principle approved demerger of our space, meteorology, and hydrology business.”
- *[Jun 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=78f3aacc-b7ef-4d51-b1e1-d6e5863786b8.pdf)* — The stated objective is focus, not cash or deleveraging. “The objective of this move is to create sharper strategic and operational focus for business segments.”
- *[Jun 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=78f3aacc-b7ef-4d51-b1e1-d6e5863786b8.pdf)* — The specific problems named: management bandwidth, governance/accountability, a complicated corporate structure and an unclear investment case for shareholders. “The proposed structure will enable dedicated management teams to pursue sector-specific growth opportunities, enhance governance and accountability, simplify the corporate structure, and create clearer investment propositions to shareholders.”
- *[Jun 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=78f3aacc-b7ef-4d51-b1e1-d6e5863786b8.pdf)* — Expected outcome framed over the medium to long term, including capital allocation. “Over the medium to long term, we believe this initiative will support focused growth, better capital allocation, and improved operational efficiency.”
- *[Jun 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=78f3aacc-b7ef-4d51-b1e1-d6e5863786b8.pdf)* — Scale of the business being separated, as management described FY26 revenue mix: space and meteorology ~16% versus radar ~60%. “Our radar business continued to be a primary growth driver, contributing nearly 60% of our revenue, while space and meteorology segment contributed around 16%, demonstrating our expanding footprint in strategic and high-technology domains.”
- *Scheme* — The June 10, 2026 scheme disclosure states the purpose as creating two separately listed sector-focused companies — radar/EW/telemetry on one side, space/met/hydro on the other. “The proposed demerger is intended to create two sector-focused listed entities, namely: (a) Radar Electronics, Electronic Warfare and Telemetry business focused entity; and (b) Space, Meteorology and Hydrology focused entity;”
- *Scheme* — Core argument: the two businesses face different industry, competitive, regulatory and risk conditions and therefore need different strategies. “The Space, Meteorology and Hydrology business operates in a sector with distinct industry characteristics, competitive dynamics, regulatory environment, and risk profile, necessitating a differentiated growth strategy aligned with its specific market opportunities.”
- *Scheme* — Capital-access rationale — the only place any outside constituency (investors, partners, lenders) is invoked, and as a prospective benefit rather than as a party that asked for the split. “A standalone Space, Meteorology and Hydrology entity would be better positioned to attract investors, strategic partners, lenders, and other stakeholders with sector-specific interests.”
- *Scheme* — Explicit value-unlock objective for AMPL shareholders. “unlocking the value of the Demerged Undertaking for the shareholders of the Demerged Company.”
- *Scheme* — Size of the carve-out quantified in the filing: ~INR157 crore of FY26 turnover, 13.58% of the parent's total. “The turnover of the Demerged Undertaking of the Company for the financial year ended 31st March 2026 was approximately INR. 157 Crores , representing 13.58% of the total turnover of the Demerged Company for the said year.”
- *Scheme* — No cash changes hands; a 1:1 share entitlement mirrors AMPL's register into ASTPL (promoters 6.45%, public 93.55% post-scheme), and ASTPL shares will be listed on BSE and NSE. “For the purpose of the demerger of Demerged Undertaking ( as defined in the Scheme ) of Demerged Company into Resulting Company, the Resulting Company shall issue 1 fully paid-up equity share of INR 2 (Indian Rupees 2/- only) each for every 1 fully paid-up equity share of INR 2 (Indian Rupees 2/- only) each held in the Demerged Company ("Share Entitlement Ratio").”
- *Scheme* — Leadership is being split alongside the businesses: MD S. Gurunatha Reddy was given the demerger and will move to ASTPL, with Dr M.V. Reddy taking over as AMPL MD from October 1, 2026 (April 3, 2026 press release; confirmed in the August 10, 2026 board outcome). “In this role, he will lead the adoption of tailored growth strategies and capital allocation frameworks suited to the Space, Meteorology and Hydrology sector, thereby enabling focused management attention, enhanced operational efficiency and the unlocking of value for the shareholders of the Company.”

*Not explained on the calls:* No segment margins/EBITDA, asset-debt-employee split, ASTPL standalone financials, listing timeline, transaction costs, or where ARC/MMIC sit; no analyst questioned it; no requesting party named.

## LEMONTREE — Lemon Tree Hotels Ltd.

**CONFIRMED** (a demerger scheme is on the exchange record) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 6.4/10 · spin-off · 29 filing(s) from CALLS, NSE · first 2026-01-10, latest 2026-09-22

> **Listing:** NOT YET — scheme at 'nclt_sanction' stage; Fleur Hotels Limited will list only after NCLT sanction, effectiveness and a record date; indicated timeline: Press release of 9 January 2026: "The entire process to listing of Fleur is expected to be completed within 12 to 15 months"; on the 29 May 2026 call Keswani said 12 months from then if NCLT is quick, otherwise 18 months; NSE observation letter of 22 September 2026 requires trading to commence within sixty days of the NCLT order

**The stages, as filed:** exchange_noc (2026-09-22) → nclt_sanction (2026-01-10)

**Stated in the filings:** resulting company **Fleur Hotels Limited**; demerged undertaking: ), w ill be demerged into Fleur Hotels; appointed date 2026-04-01; pro-forma statements referenced.

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** Asset-heavy hotel ownership and development undertaking: 12 hotels (11 operating, 1 under construction) plus development capabilities, demerged into Fleur Hotels — class `value_unlocking`.

- *Insiders:* Promoters Patanjali Govind Keswani and Spank Management hold 22.28% of LTH, 7.34% directly in Fleur post-scheme; Keswani non-retiring Executive Chairman of Fleur, turns non-executive at Lemon Tree March 2027
- *What it reveals:* Fleur becomes India's largest hotel owner by rooms (5,556 rooms, 39 hotels; FY25 revenue Rs 1,189 cr, net EBITDA Rs 509 cr), carries all group debt, and gets Warburg's Rs 960 crore; Lemon Tree is left debt-free, 80% EBITDA-margin fee business
- *Selling pressure:* likely — Odd-lot entitlement (20 Fleur shares per 311 LTH shares) in a newly listed asset-heavy company whose investor base differs from asset-light Lemon Tree
- *Parent or spin:* both · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* Fleur's pro-forma financials in the Q4 FY26 presentation (FY27 net EBITDA ~Rs 850 crore) and Fleur's Information Memorandum
- *In their words:* “This structure ensures that the shareholders of the Company directly participate in the economic value of the hotel-ownership and development undertaking through listed shares of the Transferee Company.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

Management framed the demerger as splitting one company that had been doing two businesses with two different investor bases: an asset-heavy business that designs, develops, finances and owns hotels (pension funds, insurance companies betting on inflation, repricing and annuity yield) and an asset-light business that monetises brand, management, loyalty, distribution and technology with almost no capital intensity. Keswani said Lemon Tree had only built hotels in 2004-2007 because owners would not hand their hotels to an unknown brand, and that with the brand now widely recognised (MakeMyTrip's CEO told him 20-25% of occupancy comes from them the moment a Lemon Tree opens) there was no reason to keep owning assets rather than monetise the brand — explicitly the Marriott/Host Hotels and Hilton/Park Hotels playbook. Mechanically (Composite Scheme approved 9 Jan 2026, appointed date 1 April 2026): Carnation Hotels and Hamstede Living merge into LTH; Oriole Dr. Fresh, Canary, Sukhsagar and Manakin merge into Fleur against shares to LTH; and the Demerged Undertaking — 11 operating hotels plus Aurika Shimla under construction, the investment in Arum (Aurika Shillong, 165 rooms) and the entire development capability/team with exclusivity on all future ownership, leasing and development — demerges into Fleur, with 20 Fleur shares for every 311 LTH shares (demerged division turnover Rs 23,037.34 lakh, 59.90% of LTH standalone turnover; 1,563 operating rooms across 15 hotels per the presentation, 1,820 keys/17 hotels per the press release). A second stated problem was conflict of interest: development capability was moved to Fleur with 'Chinese firewalls' so Fleur shareholders could never feel Lemon Tree was cherry-picking the best assets for itself, and Lemon Tree must refer new acquisition/development opportunities to Fleur. All group debt (about Rs 1,300 crore at demerger, Rs 1,500 crore total borrowings at FY26-end, cost of debt 7.42%) goes to Fleur, leaving Lemon Tree debt-free with only technology and marketing spend, forcing the Board to frame a dividend/shareholder-reward policy. Warburg Pincus (Coastal Cedar Investments B.V.) bought APG's entire 41.09% of Fleur and committed up to Rs 960 crore of primary equity, giving Fleur roughly Rs 3,000 crore of deployable capital at 1:1 debt-equity against 2,500+ rooms under active discussion and Aurika Nehru Place (572 rooms, ~Rs 700 crore); post-scheme LTH shareholders own ~74% of Fleur (32.96% direct plus ~41% through LTH) versus the 59% LTH owns today, and Fleur lists separately for 'transparent price discovery and market-driven valuation of the asset-heavy business'.

**How it evolved:** The idea was first visible as a Fleur listing aspiration in the Nov 2024 call, where Keswani said debt-freedom would come sooner 'if we list Fleur before that' and put an IPO 'within the next 2-3 years at most'; in the Aug 2025 call he disclosed that committees of directors had been set up in both Lemon Tree and Fleur to evaluate transferring LTH's assets into Fleur via a demerger and listing it, alongside splitting the management teams (Neelendra Singh for LTH from 1 October, Saurabh Shatdal for Fleur), with listing hoped for end-CY2026. In the Nov 2025 call it was 'in process' with a Board subcommittee and a promise of 'some other even more exciting stuff' within three months; the scheme, the Warburg/APG transactions and the 74%/26% shareholding math were announced in the Jan 2026 (15 January) dedicated call with a 12-15 month path to listing. By the Feb 2026 call Keswani confirmed the scheme was effective from 1 April and, responding to Ashish Kumar's request, promised pro forma financials for both entities; those pro formas appeared with the Jun 2026 (29 May) results, where CCI approval (April 2026), Warburg's completed purchase of APG's stake and a longer 12-18 month NCLT-dependent timeline were given, followed by NSE/BSE observation letters on 22 September 2026.

**What management expects from it:** Lemon Tree: debt-free, fee/brand/tech-only, EBITDA margin from ~60% pro forma to 70-80% steady state, ~60% PAT margin, high ROCE, free cash funding dividends. Fleur: India's largest owner (5,600 rooms, 39 hotels), net EBITDA Rs 850 crore FY27 and Rs 1,000+ crore FY28, ~48%+ post-fee margins, Warburg-backed capital for 2,500+ rooms, capital growth not dividends, and separately listed for market valuation.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *[Jan 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=098527b9-fd65-4aa9-9c6d-1ac184b2eda0.pdf)* — Asked directly by Kunal Lakhan (CLSA) what was wrong with the old structure, Keswani said the hotel business has two subsets with two different investor types — developers/owners wanting chunky yield and inflation-linked annuity returns versus asset-light investors betting on brand and management — and Lemon Tree was a combination of both. “We have actually separated 2 types of businesses. One is asset heavy, long -term appreciating asset, capital intensive. It has a different kind of investor, and this business has a very different kind of investor, and we wanted to actually attract both types of investors.”
- *[Jan 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=098527b9-fd65-4aa9-9c6d-1ac184b2eda0.pdf)* — He explained the historical accident being corrected: hotels were built only to establish the brand, and with the brand now established the company should monetise it instead of owning assets. “We were forced to build hotels to build our brand. But once we build our brand, technically, we do not need hotels because now it is time for Lemon Tree to monetize its brand, which is enormous recall.”
- *[Jan 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=098527b9-fd65-4aa9-9c6d-1ac184b2eda0.pdf)* — The transfer of the development capability and exclusive development mandate to Fleur was driven by a conflict-of-interest problem — Fleur minorities fearing Lemon Tree would keep the best projects for itself — and was solved with firewalls. “Development capability was an issue which was raised in order to maximize Fleur's growth, we did not want shareholders of Fleur to ever feel that Lemon Tree when it recommends any assets was cherry -picking, which means Lemon Tree would say, I have got this very nice asset in Delhi, why should I offer it to Fleur.”
- *[Jan 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=098527b9-fd65-4aa9-9c6d-1ac184b2eda0.pdf)* — All of Lemon Tree's debt moves to Fleur: Fleur carries roughly Rs 1,300 crore of debt against a ~Rs 900 crore net EBITDA and can borrow another ~Rs 1,300 crore, while Lemon Tree goes to zero debt. “Firstly, when this demerger happens, all the debt, including the Lemon Tree's debt, after adjustment is being transferred to Fleur. Fleur will have 100% of our debt and Lemon Tree will have zero debt.”
- *[Jan 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=098527b9-fd65-4aa9-9c6d-1ac184b2eda0.pdf)* — Keswani justified keeping a ~41% indirect stake in Fleur (challenged by Jinesh Joshi on hold-co discount) as Lemon Tree retaining 'skin in the game' as Fleur's manager, with natural dilution as Fleur raises capital; he quantified that Rs 1,000 crore deployed by Fleur generates ~Rs 350 crore of turnover, Rs 170-180 crore EBITDA and ~Rs 30 crore of fees for Lemon Tree. “We felt it was prudent to have significant skin in the game at this stage, which means that going forward, it is very possible that Lemon Tree may dilute or even increase its stake over time; this will obviously be a Board decision .”
- *[Jan 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=098527b9-fd65-4aa9-9c6d-1ac184b2eda0.pdf)* — Warburg's Rs 960 crore primary commitment plus Fleur's own cash and 1:1 debt gives roughly Rs 3,000 crore to deploy pre-listing against 2,500 rooms in active discussion; Keswani guided Fleur to over Rs 1,000 crore net EBITDA by FY28 and Lemon Tree to 80% EBITDA margin / 60% PAT margin. “We have potentially about Rs 3,000 crores available to deploy in this growth before we list.”
- *[Jun 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=a03e8364-4037-407c-8929-d956c0976b96.pdf)* — Opening the call with pro forma financials for both entities, Keswani described the transaction as simple — Warburg has bought APG's Fleur stake, Lemon Tree transfers 17 hotels and development capabilities in exchange for Fleur shares to LTH shareholders, and Fleur lists. “This scheme will result in 2 distinct financially sound businesses.”
- *[Jun 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=a03e8364-4037-407c-8929-d956c0976b96.pdf)* — He restated the economic outcome for each entity: Lemon Tree debt-free, high-margin, high-ROCE and fee/brand-driven; Fleur the consolidated owner of a fully renovated portfolio, post-scheme India's largest hotel platform by inventory at 5,600 rooms and 39 operational hotels. “Post the reorganization , Lemon Tree will emerge as a debt -free, high-margin, high ROCE company generating strong free cash flows from fees and brand -related income.”
- *[Jun 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=a03e8364-4037-407c-8929-d956c0976b96.pdf)* — Shareholder arithmetic: LTH shareholders end up with close to 74% of Fleur (33% direct, ~41% through Lemon Tree) versus the 59% Lemon Tree directly owns in Fleur today, before Warburg's primary infusion; Keswani also said he will cease to be executive at Lemon Tree from March 2027 and focus on Fleur as Executive Chair. “Post reorganization , Lemon Tree shareholders will effectively own close to 74% of Fleur Hotels, 33% directly and about 41% indirectly through Lemon Tree.”
- *[Jun 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=a03e8364-4037-407c-8929-d956c0976b96.pdf)* — Answering Achal Kumar, Keswani confirmed Fleur will be brand-agnostic post-demerger and may hand assets to other operators — Lemon Tree has no automatic right to Fleur's hotels and must earn them on results. “Yes. But Lemon Tree must be able to deliver best results to get it . Just because Lemon Tree has skin in the game with Fleur does not mean that it has an automatic right to any asset that Fleur develops.”
- *[Jun 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=a03e8364-4037-407c-8929-d956c0976b96.pdf)* — On capital allocation after the split, Lemon Tree is expected to need almost no capital and move to distributing profits, while Fleur will retain capital for growth rather than pay dividends. “Lemon Tree will not need any significant capital other than potentially investments in technology or in marketing and so on. It will be essentially a zero -debt cash accretive company.”
- *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=b0215f7f-3372-4231-8b2f-7f433eb77faf.pdf)* — Keswani confirmed the scheme is effective from 1 April and that Lemon Tree becomes debt-free from next year, with all assets and debt going to Fleur and fee income becoming free cash; the Board must decide a dividend policy within six months. “What will happen is in the scheme of demerger, all the assets of Lemon Tree, including its debt will be transferred to Fleur. Lemon Tree will immediately effectively be a debt -free company from next year.”

*Not explained on the calls:* Absolute valuation of the demerged undertaking and Warburg's price for APG's stake, Fleur's issue price, hold-co discount size, post-demerger ROE, and fate of the two retained leases.

## NATCOPHARM — NATCO Pharma Ltd.

**CONFIRMED** (a demerger scheme is on the exchange record) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 6.4/10 · spin-off · 20 filing(s) from CALLS, NSE, NSE-BM, NSE-deep · first 2025-11-14, latest 2026-09-09

> **Listing:** NOT YET — scheme at 'exchange_noc' stage; Natco Crop Health Sciences Limited will list only after NCLT sanction, effectiveness and a record date; no listing timeline stated

**The stages, as filed:** announced (2026-03-24) → exchange_noc (2026-09-09)

**Stated in the filings:** resulting company **Natco Crop Health Sciences Limited**.

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** Agrochemicals (Crop Health Sciences) division — pesticides, insecticides, herbicides, biostimulants — demerged into Natco Crop Health Sciences Limited — class `value_unlocking`.

- *Insiders:* Promoter and Promoter Group hold 8,84,65,126 of 17,91,09,870 shares (~49%); 1:1 entitlement carries that stake into the Resulting Company. Demerged Company retains 20% post-listing; director P.S.R.K. Prasad sits on Natco Crop Health Sciences' board.
- *What it reveals:* Demerged turnover was only ₹60.62 crore, 1.48% of total; FY25 agro segment result was a ₹1,458 million loss. Management says it reached ~₹140 crore sales and roughly EBITDA breakeven. Separation removes a loss-maker from pharma and exposes an early-growth agro business.
- *Selling pressure:* likely — Tiny (1.48% of turnover), loss-making, different industry; 4,22,879 pharma shareholders receive 1:1 agrochemical shares, with parent holding 20%.
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* The revised Scheme to be filed with Stock Exchanges post Rights Issue — check the share swap ratio and agro segment numbers.
- *In their words:* “The segregation is also expected to unlock the value of the business verticals of the Demerged Company.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

NATCO is demerging its Crop Health Sciences (Agrochemicals) division into Natco Crop Health Sciences Limited, leaving the listed parent as a pure pharmaceutical company (FDFs, APIs, oncology-led branded/complex generics). Management's stated reason is that the two verticals carry different risk-reward profiles and serve entirely different customers — Rajesh Chebiyam said the demerger "gives a more focused approach because the business, ultimately, the customers are quite different" — so a dedicated management, channel and product strategy (differentiated, patent-controlled, limited-competition molecules like the fungicide GLANZ and CTPR combinations) can be run without competing for attention inside a much larger pharma P&L. The second reason is valuation and capital: agro turnover was only INR 60.62 crore in FY25, i.e. 1.48% of total turnover, against FY25 group revenue of INR 4,784 crore and PAT of INR 1,883.4 crore, and Rajeev Nannapaneni said shareholders "will get another business which is not being valued in our system because it is of a very tiny business and a very large business in pharma"; separately listed, "it can raise its own capital and grow by itself." The timing was deliberately set after the division approached breakeven — segment loss of about INR 150 crore in FY25 (including a INR 50 crore non-cash PP&E impairment taken in Q4 FY25), narrowing to a INR 3.2 crore loss in Q1 FY26 on INR 34.7 crore of sales, EBITDA-positive at INR 52.4 crore of sales in Q2 FY26, and roughly INR 140 crore of FY26 sales versus INR 60 crore the prior year, against the INR 150–170 crore management had said was needed for EBITDA breakeven. The Scheme adds the corporate-finance logic: focused growth, operational rationalisation, optimum use of resources, and the ability for each business to "address independent business opportunities, pursue efficient capital allocation and attract different sets of investors, strategic partners, lenders and other stakeholders," plus unlocking the value of the verticals. Shareholders get 1 share of the resulting company for every 1 NATCO share, with NATCO retaining 20% of the post-listing equity to keep supporting a business "still at its early growth stages" — so holders retain 100% of the ultimate economic interest (80% direct, 20% through NATCO). The push came from public-market shareholders, not lenders or partners: an investor on the Nov 14, 2025 call asked directly about "value unlocking for the shareholders," and management separately cited shareholder feedback that NATCO's profit base was too concentrated. Agro is almost entirely domestic ("predominantly domestic" sales, with 25–30% input cost inflation flagged in 2026), which management contrasts with the export-weighted pharma business.

**How it evolved:** On the Feb 13, 2025 and May 29, 2025 calls there was no demerger talk — only agro losses, the INR 50 crore impairment and a INR 120–170 crore breakeven target; the Aug 13, 2025 call reported the loss down to INR 3.2 crore with still no mention. The board gave in-principle approval to evaluate the demerger on Sep 25, 2025, and Rajeev first discussed it publicly on the Nov 14, 2025 call ("demerge this business from the main company and list it separately... targeting that for the year 2026"), framing it as value unlocking plus the ability to raise its own capital; the board approved incorporating the wholly-owned resulting company on Nov 14, 2025. On Feb 12, 2026 the timeline was guided to "October, November" 2026 (8–9 months), and the Scheme itself was approved on Mar 24, 2026 with a 1:1 share entitlement, appointed date Oct 1, 2026 and 20% retained by NATCO; the May 29, 2026 call reiterated focus and different customers as the primary reason. By Sep 9, 2026 the Scheme had stock-exchange observation letters but had not been filed with the NCLT, because the INR 1,279.36 crore rights issue at INR 750/share (allotted Oct 23, 2026) changes the capital structure — the board decided to re-cut and re-file the Scheme after the rights issue while keeping the same swap ratio.

**What management expects from it:** Agro: dedicated management focus, its own capital raising, differentiated limited-competition products, growth past breakeven from roughly INR 140 crore sales. Pharma: a cleaner, focused oncology/complex-generics entity. For shareholders: value unlocked in a business "not being valued in our system," a complete see-through into both, operational efficiency, efficient capital allocation, and distinct investor/lender bases.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=ac8f848f-8703-4403-9ae3-cb2d420d47da.pdf)* — First public confirmation of the plan: demerge Crop Health Sciences out of the parent and list it separately, targeted for 2026, disclosed alongside the division reaching roughly EBITDA breakeven at INR 52.4 crore of quarterly sales. “I think we have announced earlier that we will demerge this business from the main company and list it separately and we are targeting that for the year 2026.”
- *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=ac8f848f-8703-4403-9ae3-cb2d420d47da.pdf)* — Rajeev defines the value-unlock logic in response to an investor question: separate listing gives the business special focus and the ability to raise its own capital and grow independently, now that it is breaking even. “Value unlocking means I think what we see is this business now is about breaking even now. So, we will list it separately and then we will have special focus on this and it can raise its own capital and grow by itself.”
- *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=ac8f848f-8703-4403-9ae3-cb2d420d47da.pdf)* — The core valuation argument: the agro business is too small to be valued inside a pharma company of NATCO's size, and shareholders will get a complete see-through into both businesses. “I think you will get another business which is not being valued in our system because it is of a very tiny business and a very large business in pharma.”
- *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=7ea4dc21-a77e-4e6d-967e-2da2d51bc890.pdf)* — Timeline guidance: the process has started, with an internal goal of completing in the next 8–9 months (around October–November 2026), but no firm date committed. “I think we have started the process. So , I think roughly, we're thinking by October, November, but I don't want to say any definite time lines, but this is our, what should I say, goal to do.”
- *[Jun 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=230327e4-9a77-4095-b46d-b9c836cc9b96.pdf)* — Management's clearest operating rationale, from the head of Crop Health Sciences: a focused approach is needed because the agro customer base is entirely different from pharma, with FY26 agro sales of about INR 140 crore versus INR 60 crore the year before. “So, as you're aware, so we're in the process of demerging the business. And one of the primary reasons we felt also it gives a more focused approach because the business, ultimately, the customers are quite different.”
- *[Jun 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=230327e4-9a77-4095-b46d-b9c836cc9b96.pdf)* — Growth plans — new differentiated, patent-controlled, limited-competition products, more channel partners and more people — are tied directly back to the demerger as the reason for sharper focus. “So I think we're fairly confident going forward. And that's also one of the main reasons for demerging and having more focus on the business.”
- *Scheme* — The Mar 24, 2026 Scheme of Arrangement grounds the demerger in differing risk-reward profiles of the pharmaceutical and agrochemicals verticals; agro turnover was INR 60.62 crore in FY25, 1.48% of total company turnover. “The Board of Directors of the Demerged Company believe that the risk and reward associated with each of the aforesaid business verticals are different.”
- *Scheme* — The Scheme's capital-markets rationale: each business can chase its own opportunities, allocate capital efficiently and attract its own investor and lender base, alongside focused growth, operational rationalisation and value unlocking. “Each business would be able to address independent business opportunities, pursue efficient capital allocation and attract different sets of investors, strategic partners, lenders and other stakeholders.”
- *Scheme* — NATCO keeps 20% of the post-listing equity of the resulting company so it can keep funding and strategically supporting an early-stage business; shareholders get 1 new share for every 1 NATCO share, retaining 100% of the ultimate economic interest (80% direct plus 20% indirect). “Further, the Demerged Company intends to retain the current shareholding in the Resulting Company (20% of post listing shareholding) in order to continue to offer support to the Agrochemicals Business which is still at its early growth stages and help in monitoring the progress and providing strategic support.”
- *Scheme* — The Nov 14, 2025 board filing states the purpose as unlocking value in the core pharmaceutical business while giving each entity operational flexibility, dedicated management and separate brand positioning. “To demerge the Agro business of the Company into a separate entity, the move shall enable value unlocking of the core business (pharmaceuticals) and enhance long -term growth.”
- *[Jun 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=d43e2593-6819-4d99-b9a6-c3019c901490.pdf)* — Pre-demerger baseline for why the division was a drag: a INR 50 crore non-cash impairment on agro property, plant and machinery in Q4 FY25, FY25 agro revenue of about INR 60 crore, and INR 160–170 crore needed just to be EBITDA positive. “So, I think this year, we feel we are going to hit that critical mass where we'll start breaking even. We are doing about INR60 crores net revenue last year. So, I think we need to hit about INR160 crores to INR170 crores at least to have that EBITDA positive.”
- *Scheme* — The Sep 9, 2026 board update: the Scheme had received observation letters from both exchanges but was not filed with the NCLT because the INR 1,300 crore rights issue changes the capital structure, so the Scheme will be amended and re-filed post-issue with the swap ratio unchanged. “The fund raising by way of a Rights Issue proposed at the meeting of the board of directors held on September 09, 2026 is expected to result in change to the Company's capital structure and shareholding pattern and consequently would require necessary changes to the Scheme.”

*Not explained on the calls:* No standalone agro financials, debt/asset split, valuation or swap-ratio basis; no post-demerger profitability, capital needs, board/management, listing date, or revised Scheme terms.

## VEDL — Vedanta Ltd.

**CONFIRMED** (a demerger scheme is on the exchange record) · **LISTED <1Y — selling-pressure window; the bargain forms here** · score 6.4/10 · spin-off · 42 filing(s) from CALLS, NSE, NSE-register · first 2025-10-18, latest 2026-10-03

> **Listing:** LISTED — Talwandi Sabo Power Limited trades since about 2026-05-01 (record date 2026-05-01)

**The stages, as filed:** announced (2026-07-30) → nclt_sanction (2025-12-16) → record_date (2026-05-01)

**Stated in the filings:** resulting company **Talwandi Sabo Power Limited**; record date 2026-05-01; pro-forma statements referenced; size hint: 11% of ebitda.

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** The Merchant Power Undertaking — merchant thermal power — demerged into Talwandi Sabo Power Limited, renamed Vedanta Power Limited — class `value_unlocking`.

- *Insiders:* Promoter Vedanta Resources held 54.72% of VEDL (Twin Star 40.02%, Vedanta Holdings Mauritius II 12.60%, Welter 0.98%); 1 TSPL share per VEDL share, proportionate, so promoter stake carries over unchanged
- *What it reveals:* Power carried the heaviest leverage of the five: pro forma EBITDA $0.14bn, gross debt $0.9bn, net debt $0.8bn, 4.7x vs group 0.95x. Residual Vedanta kept Zinc India (56% margin) at 0.4x; combined market cap of resulting companies rose over ₹71,000 crore in Q1FY27
- *Selling pressure:* likely — Every VEDL holder received 1 TSPL share; standalone thermal power is a different industry from metals, smallest EBITDA share, highest leverage 4.7x
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* Vedanta Power's own first standalone results — 4.7x pro forma net debt/EBITDA and Athena Unit 1 restart timeline
- *In their words:* “Vedanta's demerger is unlocking significant shareholder value, with combined market cap of resulting companies growing by over ₹71,000 crore in the 1st quarter.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

Management's stated reason is structural: Vedanta Limited is being split into five independent, sector-specific "pure-play" companies — residual Vedanta Limited (Zinc India/HZL, Zinc International, Copper, Ferrochrome/FACOR, Nickel), Vedanta Aluminium Metal, Vedanta Power (Talwandi Sabo Power), Vedanta Oil & Gas (Malco Energy) and Vedanta Iron & Steel — so each can "chart out their own growth trajectory and attract respective thematic investors," with simpler structures and sharper accountability (Apr 2026). The second pillar is capital structure: the demerger was "architected with precision on capital structure, aligning debt with earning strength and growth stage of each resulting company," carving the $5.5bn net debt (group leverage 0.95x, down from 1.22x) so Oil & Gas is nil-debt, Iron & Steel ≤$0.2bn, Aluminium carries $3.5bn at 1.3x, Power 4.7x on long-dated 7–10 year PFC/REC maturities, and residual Vedanta ~$1bn at 0.4x. Lenders were an explicit gating party — debt allocation was "broadly aligned with the bankers as a precondition for granting NOC for demerger approval" (Jan 2026) — while shareholders and creditors voted on 18 Feb 2025 and MoPNG objected in NCLT over oil & gas disputed dues (~$512m), a concern settled by a Vedanta corporate guarantee, alongside a ₹660 crore full-and-final SEPCO settlement that "paved the way" (Nov 2025). Governance flexibility is a named benefit: five independent boards, with dividend policy moving from prescriptive/rule-based (minimum 30% of profit; HZL dividend upstreamed within six months) to descriptive/principle-based, removing the HZL upstreaming mandate (Apr 2026). Differentiated capital structures were also pitched as a financing route — "many anchor investors domestically and globally are very keen to come in the cap table" as an additional deleveraging avenue, relevant to the $4.7bn still at Vedanta Resources (FY27 need ~$1bn: ~$0.3bn debt plus ICL and ~$0.45bn interest, funded by ~$400m brand fee and a 4–5% dividend). Specific economics were quantified only for copper: post-demerger its brand fee falls from 3% to 0.75% (~$65m on $3.1–3.2bn revenue), lifting EBITDA by 2.25% and taking a "wafer-thin" ~1% margin trading business to at least 5% in FY27. Post-completion filings supply the value-unlock arithmetic — ₹225.50 at the 29 Sep 2023 announcement versus ₹932.05 combined on the 15 June 2026 listing (>300% upside) and combined market cap up over ₹71,000 crore in Q1 FY27 — and the same logic is then reused for a sixth separation: ~2,264 acres and ~53,185 sq ft of surplus real estate into Vedanta Property Platforms (1 share for every 20), because that portfolio sat "embedded within the operating business" with sub-optimal visibility and potential value of ₹30,000 crore+.

**How it evolved:** The idea pre-dates this window (announced 29 Sep 2023) and by Feb 2025 was "in the important stage of execution" with the shareholder/creditor meeting on 18 Feb 2025, moving to the NCLT second-motion petition, and Apr 2025 framed it as creating "pure-play entities" targeted for September 2025. It then slipped repeatedly: Aug 2025 reported the 2 July NCLT hearing left incomplete (next 20 August) plus an NCLAT interim stay on the TSPL power order and MoPNG's objection; Nov 2025 cleared the blockers via a ₹660 crore SEPCO settlement and a Vedanta corporate guarantee for MoPNG's alleged claims, with final hearing set for 12 November and listing guided "by the end of FY26." Jan 2026 reported NCLT approval (16 December for four businesses, 9 January for power), Ind AS 105 discontinued-operations accounting and a 1 April effective date; Apr 2026 pushed effective/record date to 1 May 2026 with listing by mid-June and added the newly disclosed mechanics — five dividend policies, HZL upstreaming mandate dropped, copper brand fee cut to 0.75%, entity-wise debt split. After listing (15 June 2026), the 30 July 2026 filing extended the same rationale to a further demerger of surplus real estate into Vedanta Property Platforms, targeted for FY28.

**What management expects from it:** Each entity: sharper strategy, own board, dividend and M&A mandate (holdco keeps cross-portfolio deals), and a balance sheet sized to its own cash flows. Copper margin from ~1% to at least 5% in FY27 on a 0.75% brand fee; Zinc International EBITDA from ~$100m to ~$450m by FY28; Power targeting 10–12 GW more; thematic and anchor investors to lift valuations and fund growth.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *[Apr 2026](https://www.vedantalimited.com/uploads/investor-overview/financial-results/2026/Vedanta-Transcript-Apr29-2026.pdf)* — Goel defines the deal: five independent sector-specific pure-play companies, each free to pursue its own growth path and court its own investor base, effective 1 May 2026 with listing targeted in Q1 FY27. “This will entail creation of five independent sector-specific pure-play companies, allowing each company to chart out their own growth trajectory and attract respective thematic investors.”
- *[Apr 2026](https://www.vedantalimited.com/uploads/investor-overview/financial-results/2026/Vedanta-Transcript-Apr29-2026.pdf)* — The debt split was deliberately engineered pre-demerger to match each entity's cash generation and growth stage; group leverage was 0.95x going in. “The de-merger has been architected with precision on capital structure, aligning debt with earning strength and growth stage of each resulting company.”
- *[Apr 2026](https://www.vedantalimited.com/uploads/investor-overview/financial-results/2026/Vedanta-Transcript-Apr29-2026.pdf)* — Goel gives the entity-wise net debt: Oil & Gas debt-free, Iron & Steel ≤$0.2bn, Aluminium $3.5bn at 1.3x, Power mostly long-dated PFC/REC debt at 4.7x, residual Vedanta ~$1bn at 0.4x. “So even before de-merger on 1st of May, Vedanta Oil and Gas will have nil debt, so it will be debt-free company.”
- *[Apr 2026](https://www.vedantalimited.com/uploads/investor-overview/financial-results/2026/Vedanta-Transcript-Apr29-2026.pdf)* — Each of the five boards gets its own dividend policy; Vedanta's shifts from rule-based (minimum 30% payout, HZL dividend passed on within six months) to principle-based, and the HZL upstreaming mandate is removed. “Currently, Vedanta's policy on dividend is more prescriptive; it will become more descriptive.”
- *[Apr 2026](https://www.vedantalimited.com/uploads/investor-overview/financial-results/2026/Vedanta-Transcript-Apr29-2026.pdf)* — Asked how VRL's remaining $4.7bn debt gets addressed, Goel names the demerger itself as a new funding lever via differentiated capital structures and anchor investors entering individual cap tables. “Now as we de-merge all the five companies, additionally we'll have the optionality of a differentiated capital structure and in that case, many anchor investors domestically and globally are very keen to come in the cap table, and that will be additional avenue for de-leveraging.”
- *[Apr 2026](https://www.vedantalimited.com/uploads/investor-overview/financial-results/2026/Vedanta-Transcript-Apr29-2026.pdf)* — Only quantified per-business economic gain: copper's brand fee is re-benchmarked down from 3% to 0.75% (≈$65m on $3.1–3.2bn revenue), taking a ~1%-margin trading business to at least 5% in FY27; the 3% rate holds for the others to FY29. “So the brand fee for copper from the current 3% will go down to 0.75% and that alone from India's viewpoint means higher EBITDA by 2.25%.”
- *[Apr 2026](https://www.vedantalimited.com/uploads/investor-overview/financial-results/2026/Vedanta-Transcript-Apr29-2026.pdf)* — Naidoo explains the post-demerger operating model: CEOs mandated to deliver each company's own 2x/3x organic growth, with cross-portfolio M&A sitting above them at a holdco alongside the Chairman. “Anything outside of the portfolio would still happen at the holdco level.”
- *[Jan 2026](https://www.vedantalimited.com/uploads/investor-overview/financial-results/2026/Transcript_29Jan2026.pdf)* — On NCLT approval (16 Dec 2025 order; certified copy 21 Jan 2026), Naidoo frames the purpose as sharper strategy, stronger balance sheets and faster growth per business. “This marks a defining moment in our journey, one that empowers our businesses to sharpen the strategies, strengthen the balance sheets and accelerate growth with the aim of unlocking shareholder value.”
- *[Jan 2026](https://www.vedantalimited.com/uploads/investor-overview/financial-results/2026/Transcript_29Jan2026.pdf)* — Lenders effectively dictated the debt carve-up: bank NOCs for the demerger were conditional on agreeing the allocation of the ~$6.7bn Vedanta India consolidated net debt across entities. “When we went to the banker seeking NOC, in that case, debt allocation was broadly aligned with the bankers as a precondition for granting NOC for demerger approval.”
- *[Jan 2026](https://www.vedantalimited.com/uploads/investor-overview/financial-results/2026/Transcript_29Jan2026.pdf)* — Goel calls the demerger an opportunity on taxation and structuring, and states the intent to hand over a debt-free oil & gas and near-debt-free iron & steel, part-funded by the ₹3,000 crore HZL OFS used for deleveraging. “And as I earlier mentioned, our intent is to make oil and gas business debt-free, and also our iron steel business almost debt-free.”
- *[Jan 2026](https://www.vedantalimited.com/uploads/investor-overview/financial-results/2026/Transcript_29Jan2026.pdf)* — Litigation is ring-fenced by business: the $512m MoPNG arbitration outcome, gain or loss, follows oil & gas post-demerger rather than the group. “It is ring fenced to oil and gas, whatever the decision.”
- *[Nov 2025](https://www.vedantalimited.com/uploads/investor-overview/financial-results/2026/VEDL_Q2FY26_Transcript.pdf)* — A long-standing creditor dispute was settled in cash specifically to unblock the scheme — ₹660 crore to SEPCO, booked as an exceptional item alongside the ₹1,407 crore TSPL provision. “As part of demerger proceedings, a full and final settlement of Rs. 660 Cr has been done with SEPCO, thereby resolving a long-standing dispute, paving the way for a proposed demerger process.”

*Not explained on the calls:* No per-entity valuation or multiple math, no demerger cost/tax leakage, no reason HZL and semiconductors stay in residual Vedanta, no view on duplicated listed-company overheads.

*Calls read (36 months):* [Apr 2025](https://www.vedantalimited.com/uploads/investor-overview/financial-results/Vedanta-CallTranscript-Apr30-2025_v2.pdf), [Aug 2024](https://www.vedantalimited.com/uploads/investor-overview/financial-results/call-transcript-fy2025.pdf), [Aug 2025](https://www.vedantalimited.com/uploads/investor-overview/financial-results/2026/Vedanta_Transcript_Jul31_2025.pdf), [Feb 2025](https://www.vedantalimited.com/uploads/investor-overview/financial-results/VedantaEarnings-transcript-Jan31-2025.pdf), Jan 2024, [Nov 2023](https://www.vedantalimited.com/uploads/investor-overview/financial-results/Transcript_VEDL_Earnings_Call_2QFY24.pdf), [Nov 2024](https://www.vedantalimited.com/uploads/investor-overview/financial-results/Vedanta-Earnings-Nov08-2024.pdf), [Nov 2025](https://www.vedantalimited.com/uploads/investor-overview/financial-results/2026/VEDL_Q2FY26_Transcript.pdf)

## APOLLOHOSP — Apollo Hospitals Enterprise Ltd.

**CONFIRMED** (a demerger scheme is on the exchange record) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 5.7/10 · spin-off · 25 filing(s) from CALLS, NSE · first 2025-12-24, latest 2026-06-26

> **Listing:** NOT YET — scheme at 'nclt_sanction' stage; the resulting company will list only after NCLT sanction, effectiveness and a record date; indicated timeline: On May 21, 2026 management said the NCLT-convened shareholder meeting was called for June 24 and they were "hopeful the demerger process is completed by Q4 FY27 as planned earlier," with "end of December or early Q4 FY27" when Apollo Healthtech should get demerged and listed; NSE's December 23, 2025 observation letter requires trading to commence within sixty days of receipt of the NCLT order

**The stages, as filed:** exchange_noc (2025-12-24) → meetings (2026-05-21) → nclt_sanction (2026-04-03)

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** Apollo's omnichannel pharmacy and digital health business, demerged into a separately listed company — class `value_unlocking`.

- *Insiders:* Promoter group held 4,02,87,130 shares (voted 100% for). Shobana Kamineni to be Executive Chairperson of Resultant Company; Rasmeli-funded upside share agreement (max 9% of upside at 4x MOIC) to her and identified employees; new ESOP to be established
- *What it reveals:* A pharmacy/digital platform at ~INR 25,000 crore run-rate revenue with 6.5-7% targeted EBITDA margin, digital losses near breakeven, Keimed distribution consolidated; promoter and investor incentives concentrated in the spin, not the hospital parent
- *Selling pressure:* likely — Shares distributed to all 1.75 lakh AHEL holders in a different industry (pharmacy distribution/digital health) than the hospital parent they own
- *Parent or spin:* spin · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* The Scheme's Demerger Share Entitlement Ratio and the Part E abridged-prospectus disclosures for Apollo Healthtech
- *In their words:* “During the year, we also announced a strategic restructuring of the omnichannel pharmacy and digital health business, an important step towards sharpening focus on unlocking long-term value across our integrated health care platform.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

The business being separated is AHEL's omnichannel pharmacy and digital health vertical — Apollo HealthCo, comprising the ~7,500-store Apollo Pharmacy retail/front-end network and the Apollo 24/7 digital platform (46mn users, INR 528 cr quarterly platform GMV) — which is being demerged into Apollo Healthtech Ltd, with Apollo Healthco Ltd and the promoter-linked distributor Keimed Private Limited (which supplies ~60,000 pharmacy stores) amalgamated into the same vehicle, which is then renamed Apollo Healthco Limited and listed; hospital-based pharmacies stay inside Healthcare Services, since as A. Krishnan put it in Aug 2025, 'what we are spinning out is only the retail pharmacies and the online.' The Scheme's own rationale states the problem plainly: the Identified Business Undertaking is 'distinct from other businesses undertaken by the Demerged Company' and 'necessitates a differentiated strategy aligned to its industry specific risks, market dynamics, and growth trajectory', so separation lets hospitals and retail/digital each focus on 'their respective businesses, efficient management, and control', consolidates HealthCo's and Keimed's distribution 'in an independent company focusing exclusively on digital health and pharmacy distribution', and lets the new entity 'build a wider capital and financial base, by attracting a different set of investors, strategic partners, lenders and stakeholders' — plus supply-chain integration, wider assortment, 'improved transparency in the supply chain preventing the entry of counterfeit or substandard medicines', administrative efficiency, board/managerial rationalisation and economies of scale. The financial case management repeated for six straight quarters is scale plus margin convergence: pro-forma combined revenue of INR 4,430 cr in Q1 FY26 (~INR 17,000 cr run-rate, INR 19,000 cr for FY26) becoming a INR 25,000 cr run-rate at 7% EBITDA by Q4 FY27; Sanjiv Gupta's arithmetic was that a 3.2% blended FY25 margin is already 6.4% once Apollo 24/7's losses and the accelerated ESOP charge are stripped out, with offline pharmacy going 7.4%→8-9% on private label (15.5% of pharmacy sales) and Keimed 3.1%→3.5%. The loss drag has in fact collapsed — digital cash losses fell from INR 111 cr (Q4 FY24) and INR 101 cr (Q2 FY25) to INR 29 cr in Q3 FY26 and INR 16 cr in Q4 FY26, with breakeven ex-ESOP guided to Q1 FY27 and including ESOP (~INR 50 cr FY27) by Q3 FY27 — and Apollo HealthCo crossed INR 10,000 cr of annual revenue in FY26, making it listable on its own. Keimed's merger was justified on concrete synergies: shared technology, data, people and product categories, cheaper dark stores (22 today) to push beyond the top six metros to the next ten cities, and private-label penetration across Keimed's franchise base. The push is not purely internal: Rasmeli Limited, the investor holding Class A/B compulsorily convertible preference shares in Apollo Healthco, receives a nominee director in the Resultant Company and signed a June 30, 2025 Upside Agreement sharing up to 9% of its own upside (only above 4x MOIC) with Ms. Shobana Kamineni — proposed Executive Chairperson — and identified employees; after shareholder and proxy-adviser pushback the Company issued clarifications on June 15 and June 19, 2026 adding 10% fall-away thresholds on nomination rights, tiered caps on promoter nominees, an individual 5% waiver, six independent directors and a Lead Independent Director. A second, separate separation was announced in May 2026: AHLL's Apollo Cradle and fertility verticals (INR 450 cr FY26 revenue, INR 45 cr IGAAP EBITDA) were combined with Cloudnine at INR 1,550 cr — 35x EBITDA — for cash plus a 9.9% stake, with the INR 750 cr of cash redeployed into primary care and diagnostics, which management called the funnel into Apollo.

**How it evolved:** The idea surfaced before this window as the 'strategic intent' for Apollo HealthCo (Aug 14, 2024 call) and was tracked through Feb 11, 2025 and the May 31, 2025 (Jun 2025) call purely as the Keimed merger 'progressing well', with a ~15-month timeline and Sanjiv Gupta's 3.2%→7% FY27 margin bridge; the composite Scheme itself was board-approved and filed on June 30, 2025. On the Aug 13, 2025 call management first spelled out the full shape — Apollo HealthCo as it stands gets demerged and separately listed by Q4 FY27, all steps within 18-21 months, only retail plus online moving out, Keimed folded in for technology/data/people/product synergies. Nov 7, 2025 and Feb 11, 2026 were process updates (statutory steps on track; CCI and SEBI approvals obtained, NSE no-objection Dec 23, 2025, NCLT filed and hearings begun, Keimed's subsidiaries consolidated to 100%), and the May 21, 2026 call set the NCLT-convened shareholder meeting for June 24, 2026 with completion still Q4 FY27. In the final stretch the plan changed on governance rather than structure: clarifications dated June 15 and June 19, 2026 added nomination-right fall-away thresholds in response to shareholder feedback, and on June 24, 2026 the Scheme passed with 90.44% of all votes and 85.71% of public votes in favour, but 14.31% of institutional votes against.

**What management expects from it:** Apollo Healthtech becomes a pure-play pharmacy and digital health company: INR 25,000 cr run-rate revenue at 6.5-7% EBITDA by Q4 FY27 (FY26 exit 4.3%), digital at breakeven, Keimed 3.1%-to-3.5%, offline pharmacy 8-9% on private label, its own investors, lenders and board. AHEL keeps hospitals and AHLL at 25.4% ROCE, redeploying cash into beds, primary care and diagnostics.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *[Aug 2024](https://www.apollohospitals.com/apollo_pdf/Transcript-of-Apollo-Hospitals-Q1-FY25.pdf)* — Earliest reference in the window: integration of the acquired distribution business plus offline pharmacy growth is framed as the path to HealthCo's 'strategic intent' over three years, before any demerger language appears. “Transaction integration and healthy growth in offline pharmacy distribution revenues will drive Apollo HealthCo towards its stated strategic intent in the next 3 years.”
- *[Feb 2025](https://cdn.apollohospitals.com/apollohospitals/apollo_pdf/Transcript-of-Apollo-Hospitals-Q3-FY25.pdf)* — The restructuring is still presented as a merger-plus-breakeven story, with Sanjiv Gupta quantifying the FY27 target for the combined entity at INR 25,000 crore of revenue and 6-7% EBITDA, against a then run-rate of ~INR 17,000 crore at 6.5% excluding digital losses. “So, we are looking at about INR 25,000 crore of revenue and about 6% to 7% of EBITDA in FY 27.”
- *[Jun 2025](https://www.apollohospitals.com/sites/default/files/2025-06/transcript-of-apollo-hospitals---q4-fy25-earnings-call---1-.pdf)* — Suneeta Reddy's closing remarks on the Q4 FY25 call tie the Keimed merger explicitly to scale and margin durability in pharmacy, not to a listing. “The Keimed merger process is also progressing well, which will further enhance scale and margin resilience in our Pharmacy business.”
- *[Jun 2025](https://www.apollohospitals.com/sites/default/files/2025-06/transcript-of-apollo-hospitals---q4-fy25-earnings-call---1-.pdf)* — Sanjiv Gupta gave the margin bridge that underpins the 7% target: removing Apollo 24/7's operating losses and the ESOP charge (INR 100 cr in FY26, falling to a third thereafter) lifts the blended 3.2% to 6.4% even on then-current numbers. “If I remove these two things, if I assume these two things even today and remove these losses and the ESOP cost, the new number that comes for the EBITDA percentage is 6.4%.”
- *[Aug 2025](https://www.apollohospitals.com/sites/default/files/2025-08/transcript-of-apollo-hospitals---q1-fy26-earnings-call---13-august-2025.pdf)* — First explicit statement on a call of the demerger and separate listing, with the 18-21 month timetable and the INR 25,000 crore / 7% EBITDA end-state for the scheme concluding by FY27. “The strategic reorganization of our omni -channel pharmacy and digital health business is proceeding as planned , and we expect to complete all steps within 18 to 21 months, a timeline that we had earlier announced.”
- *[Aug 2025](https://www.apollohospitals.com/sites/default/files/2025-08/transcript-of-apollo-hospitals---q1-fy26-earnings-call---13-august-2025.pdf)* — A. Krishnan confirmed the mechanics in answer to an investor: HealthCo in its current form is the entity being demerged and listed by Q4 FY27, by which time Keimed's NCLT merger will also have happened. “What will happen is Apollo HealthCo., as you are seeing in the current form, is what is going to be demerged and will be listed separately by Q4 of FY27.”
- *[Aug 2025](https://www.apollohospitals.com/sites/default/files/2025-08/transcript-of-apollo-hospitals---q1-fy26-earnings-call---13-august-2025.pdf)* — Scope limit made explicit — hospital-based pharmacies stay with Healthcare Services; only the ~6,500-store retail chain and the online business leave, alongside Keimed, which supplies about 60,000 third-party pharmacy stores. “The hospital -based pharmacies continues as part of hospitals, which I am sure you know, but it is something that , remember, what we are spinning out is only the retail pharmacies and the online out of that.”
- *[Aug 2025](https://www.apollohospitals.com/sites/default/files/2025-08/transcript-of-apollo-hospitals---q1-fy26-earnings-call---13-august-2025.pdf)* — Madhivanan Balakrishnan listed the Keimed synergies: shared technology, data and people, cheaper dark stores (22 at the time) enabling expansion from the top 6 cities to the next 10 and beyond, and private label (then 14.6% of sales) pushed across Keimed's franchises. “So , technology, data, people, and product categories , all the four synergies should start playing out as this merger comes in place.”
- *[Nov 2025](https://drupal-cdn-hfaeddcdbng5hfbg.a01.azurefd.net/sites/default/files/2025-11/transcript-of-apollo-hospitals---q2-fy26-earnings-call---7-november-2025....pdf)* — Process update framing the combination as the way to capture scale benefits inside HealthCo; separately Madhivanan said merging Keimed, Apollo Pharmacy and the digital business would release further cost synergies from the next financial year. “The statutory processes for the restructuring within Apollo HealthCo and the Keimed merger continue to proceed as per plan, and we remain well positioned to capture the full benefit of scale within Apollo HealthCo.”
- *[Feb 2026](https://drupal-cdn-hfaeddcdbng5hfbg.a01.azurefd.net/sites/default/files/2026-02/transcript-of-ahel-q3fy26-concall_11feb2026.pdf)* — Regulatory progress is reported and the combined-entity target is restated verbatim as INR 25,000 crore run-rate revenue with 7% EBITDA. “We have also made progress with respect to the regulatory integration process for the com posite scheme of Keimed merger and demerger of Apollo HealthCo and remain well positioned to capture the full benefits of scale with the combined entity to achieve a run rate of INR 25,000 crore in combined revenues with 7% EBITDA.”
- *[Feb 2026](https://drupal-cdn-hfaeddcdbng5hfbg.a01.azurefd.net/sites/default/files/2026-02/transcript-of-ahel-q3fy26-concall_11feb2026.pdf)* — Obul Reddy itemised the approvals obtained (CCI, SEBI) and the NCLT filing, and confirmed Keimed had been cleaned up so that its subsidiaries are 100% owned before the merger. “We have obtained Competition Commission approval and SEBI approval. We have filed with NCLT.”
- *[May 2026](https://www.apollohospitals.com/sites/default/files/2026-05/transcript-of-apollo-hospitals---q4-fy26-earnings-call.pdf)* — The purpose is stated in value terms for the first time in opening remarks — sharpening focus and unlocking long-term value across the integrated platform — in the same breath as HealthCo crossing INR 10,000 crore of annual revenue. “During the year, we also announced a strategic restructuring of the omnichannel pharmacy and digital health business, an important step towards sharpening focus on unlocking long -term value across our integrated health care platform.”

*Not explained on the calls:* Calls never discussed the share entitlement ratio, debt/cash split, AHEL's residual stake, Keimed's purchase valuation or related-party pricing, the 14.31% institutional dissent, or the Upside Agreement.

*Calls read (36 months):* [Aug 2025](https://www.apollohospitals.com/sites/default/files/2025-08/transcript-of-apollo-hospitals---q1-fy26-earnings-call---13-august-2025.pdf), [Feb 2026](https://drupal-cdn-hfaeddcdbng5hfbg.a01.azurefd.net/sites/default/files/2026-02/transcript-of-ahel-q3fy26-concall_11feb2026.pdf), [May 2026](https://www.apollohospitals.com/sites/default/files/2026-05/transcript-of-apollo-hospitals---q4-fy26-earnings-call.pdf)
