## HINDUNILVR — Hindustan Unilever Ltd.

**CONFIRMED** (a demerger scheme is on the exchange record) · **LISTED <1Y — selling-pressure window; the bargain forms here** · score 5.7/10 · spin-off · 18 filing(s) from CALLS, NSE, NSE-register · first 2025-10-30, latest 2026-02-13

> **Listing:** LISTED — the resulting company trades since about 2026-02-13 (record date 2025-12-05)

**The stages, as filed:** exchange_noc (2025-11-23) → nclt_sanction (2025-11-11) → effective (2025-10-30) → record_date (2025-12-05) → listed (2026-02-13)

**Stated in the filings:** entitlement **1 for every 1**; record date 2025-12-05; appointed date 2025-12-01.

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** HUL's Ice Cream Business Undertaking, demerged on a going-concern basis into Kwality Wall's (India) Limited — class `value_unlocking`.

- *Insiders:* Not stated. Entitlement is 1 KWIL share per HUL share, so holdings mirror HUL; KWIL has a dedicated management team (Chitrank Goel, Deputy MD; Prashant Premrajka, Executive Director & CFO).
- *What it reveals:* Cost-of-acquisition split allots only 1.91% to KWIL vs 98.09% to HUL (based on HUL net worth and Ice Cream net assets at 30 Nov 2025), so a very small, cold-chain business carrying Kwality Wall's, Cornetto and Magnum is separated from a 23.6% EBITDA-margin FMCG parent.
- *Selling pressure:* likely — Tiny relative value (1.91% of cost basis), distributed 1:1 to every HUL holder; distinctive ice cream operating model, different from HUL's FMCG portfolio.
- *Parent or spin:* spin · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* KWIL's first standalone results, and the net assets of the Ice Cream Business Undertaking at 30 November 2025 underlying the 1.91% allocation.
- *In their words:* “The aforesaid ratio has been determined based on the net worth of HUL and the net assets of the Ice Cream Business Undertaking, as at 30 November 2025, in accordance with Sections 49(2C) and 49(2D) of the Act.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

The business being separated is HUL's Ice Cream business — brands Kwality Wall's, Cornetto and Magnum — demerged into Kwality Wall's (India) Limited (KWIL) under a Sections 230-232 scheme sanctioned by NCLT Mumbai on 30th October 2025 (rectified 6th November 2025), effective (and appointed) 1st December 2025. The stated commercial logic in the scheme is creation of a leading listed Indian ice cream company with focused management having 'greater flexibility to deploy strategies suited to the Ice Cream businesses' distinctive operating model and market dynamics, to realise its full potential'; on the Feb 2026 call Priya Nair framed the same point as 'a dedicated management team and singular focus' letting KWIL capitalise on a growing India market. The financial problem it solves for HUL is dilution: management sized Ice Cream at 'roughly 3-odd percentage of our business' earning 'low single-digit margin' — below HUL average, and even below that in FY26 because of monsoon and investment impacts — so removing it adds 50-60 bps to reported EBITDA margin, which is exactly how the band moved from 22-23% to an implied 22.5-23.5% (confirmed by Niranjan Gupta as 'the implied number' and restated as the mid-term guide in May 2026). The business was also volatile and seasonal: September quarter 2025 Ice Cream 'declined year on year, impacted by extended monsoon in addition to GST transition', while March quarter 2025 had double-digit volume-led growth. Execution was a deliberate two-step: demerge and report Ice Cream as a discontinued business from the December 2025 quarter, then list — KWIL allotted 2,34,95,91,262 equity shares of Re. 1 on a 1:1 entitlement to HUL holders of record 5th December 2025, listing and trading from 16th February 2026, with cost of acquisition apportioned 98.09% HUL / 1.91% KWIL based on HUL net worth versus Ice Cream net assets at 30th November 2025. Accounting consequences disclosed were a one-time non-cash gain inside reported PAT of Rs 6,603 crores (+121% y-o-y) in the December 2025 quarter, and loss of PLI benefit accruals that had flowed through other operating income. Strategically it is presented as one leg of continuous portfolio rotation toward 'fewer, bigger bets' — alongside Pureit divestment (circa Rs 600 crores), Minimalist (90.5%), OZiva (remaining 49% for Rs 824 crores) and the Nutritionalab exit (Rs 307 crores) — with May 2026 citing the Ice Cream demerger as already 'enhancing the growth mix of the portfolio'.

**How it evolved:** On the Apr 2025 call (24th April 2025, March quarter FY25) it was only a progress line — on track with regulatory requirements, completion expected by end of FY26 — bundled with Pureit, Minimalist and OZiva as portfolio rotation. By the Oct 2025 call (23rd October 2025) Ritesh Tiwari hardened both timing and economics: demerger in the December quarter with listing in Q4 FY26, a two-step 'demerger then listing' sequence, Ice Cream at ~3% of business on low single-digit margin, and a quantified 50-60 bps uplift to reported EBITDA margin on top of the 22-23% guidance. Filings then closed the mechanics: NCLT sanction 30th October 2025, effective 1st December 2025, record date 5th December 2025, 1:1 allotment of 2,34,95,91,262 shares, 98.09%/1.91% cost apportionment, listing from 16th February 2026 — and on the Feb 2026 call (12th February 2026) Priya Nair declared the demerger complete, reported the continuing business ex-Ice Cream, attributed part of the Rs 6,603 crores reported PAT to a one-time non-cash demerger gain, and reset margin guidance to an implied 22.5-23.5%. By the May 2026 call (30th April 2026) it was retrospective justification — a completed action improving portfolio growth mix, with Foods explicitly kept 'outside the perimeter of the Unilever transaction'.

**What management expects from it:** HUL: reported EBITDA margin up ~50-60 bps (guidance rebased 22-23% to an implied 22.5-23.5%), a better growth mix, and capital redeployed into bigger bets (Rs 3,500 crores acquisitions, Rs 2,000 crores premium-format capex). KWIL: dedicated management, singular focus and flexibility for ice cream's distinct operating model to capture a growing India market. Shareholders: direct 1:1 listed exposure.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *Scheme* — The scheme's own stated benefit is a focused, separately listed Indian ice cream company whose management can run strategies fitted to ice cream's different operating model and market dynamics. “Creation of a leading listed ice cream company in India with focused management having greater flexibility to deploy strategies suited to the Ice Cream businesses’ distinctive operating model and market dynamics, to realise its full potential”
- *[Apr 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=57aad284-8283-4c21-8035-99627387a92d.pdf)* — First mention in the window is purely a status update on regulatory progress and completion timing, listed alongside Pureit divestment and the Minimalist/OZiva portfolio moves. “The demerger of Ice cream business is progressing on track with regulatory requirements, and we expect it to be completed by the end of financial year 2026.”
- *[Oct 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=2eb875fe-ef79-4b40-88b8-228ccc8be17e.pdf)* — Ritesh Tiwari quantified the margin rationale: Ice Cream runs below HUL's average margin, so its exit lifts reported EBITDA margin by 50-60 bps over the 22-23% guided band. “Coming to EBITDA margin, Ice Cream demerger is expected to result in an improvement of 50-60 bps to the reported margin as Ice Cream business operates at a margin lower than HUL average.”
- *[Oct 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=2eb875fe-ef79-4b40-88b8-228ccc8be17e.pdf)* — He sized the business being removed — about 3% of HUL turnover earning low single-digit margins, and even lower in FY26 because of monsoon and investment impacts. “Ice Cream, as we had called out even earlier, it's roughly 3-odd percentage of our business. and the business makes low single-digit margin.”
- *[Oct 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=2eb875fe-ef79-4b40-88b8-228ccc8be17e.pdf)* — The plan was explicitly sequenced in two steps — demerge and report Ice Cream as a discontinued business from the December quarter, then list the entity in the March quarter. “So, this is two-step process, demerger, reporting discontinued business for December quarter and then listing the business in March quarter.”
- *[Oct 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=2eb875fe-ef79-4b40-88b8-228ccc8be17e.pdf)* — The segment's in-quarter weakness underlined its seasonality and volatility: it declined year-on-year on extended monsoon plus GST transition, and its PLI benefit would stop flowing into HUL's P&L. “Ice Cream business declined year on year, impacted by extended monsoon in addition to GST transition.”
- *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=38a5c0b9-6eee-4de5-bdd8-98ac200204cc.pdf)* — Priya Nair stated the completion and gave the focus argument for KWIL — a dedicated management team with singular focus to pursue India's growing ice cream opportunity; listing set for 16th February. “With a dedicated management team and singular focus, we are confident that KWIL is well positioned to capitalise on the growing market opportunity in India and deliver sustained performance.”
- *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=38a5c0b9-6eee-4de5-bdd8-98ac200204cc.pdf)* — The guidance band was formally rebased for the demerger — 22-23% plus roughly 50 bps, which Niranjan Gupta confirmed as an implied 22.5-23.5%; December quarter EBITDA margin of 23.3% was reported excluding Ice Cream. “We also outlined that the range, therefore, you will see a benefit of the ice cream demerger to the extent of 50 basis points.”
- *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=38a5c0b9-6eee-4de5-bdd8-98ac200204cc.pdf)* — Accounting effect disclosed: reported PAT of Rs 6,603 crores (+121% y-o-y) included a one-time non-cash gain from the Ice Cream demerger recognised per the approved scheme. “And the second item is one- time non -cash gain arising from I ce Cream demerger accounted for in accordance with the approved scheme of demerger and applicable accounting standards.”
- *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=55988411-440d-4801-8c08-90a5908c4a04.pdf)* — The demerger is retrospectively grouped with the OZiva and Minimalist investments as portfolio rotation that has already improved the quality and growth profile of what remains. “Strategic actions such as the demerger of Ice Cream, along with the investments at OZiva and Minimalist, are already enhancing the growth mix of the portfolio.”
- *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=55988411-440d-4801-8c08-90a5908c4a04.pdf)* — On perimeter: asked why HUL is doubling down on Foods while Unilever globally exits foods, Priya Nair said HUL's Foods (Tea, Coffee, Lifestyle Nutrition, Kissan) was deliberately left out of the Unilever transaction. “So therefore that, combined with the opportunities that exist in India in Foods, is the reason why Foods is outside the perimeter of the Unilever transaction that we have done, and Foods continues to be a very important area and focus of strategy for HUL.”
- *Scheme* — Mechanics and shareholder economics: 1:1 entitlement, 2,34,95,91,262 KWIL shares of Re. 1 allotted to HUL holders of record 5th December 2025, trading from 16th February 2026, with cost of acquisition split 98.09% HUL / 1.91% KWIL based on net worth versus Ice Cream net assets at 30th November 2025. “In accordance with the provisions of the Scheme, KWIL has allotted 2,34,95,91,262 (Two Hundred Thirty -Four Crore Ninety -Five Lakh Ninety -One Thousand Two Hundred Sixty -Two Only) Equity Shares of  Re. 1 /- each to the shareholders of HUL”

*Not explained on the calls:* No KWIL standalone financials, cold-chain capex or stranded costs; no Unilever brand-licensing/royalty terms; no named investor, lender or partner demand; no demerger-versus-sale comparison or valuation target.

### The business being separated — its own numbers

**Ice Cream Business (reported as 'Discontinued Operations' in the FY2025-26 segment note; Demerged Undertaking demerged into Kwality Wall's (India) Limited, KWIL)** · unit ₹ crore · Revenue = 'Segment Revenue from Discontinued Operations' (segment revenue; note states there are no intersegment transactions, so effectively external). Operating profit = 'Segment Results from Discontinued Operations', i.e. segment result = profit before other income, finance costs, exceptional items and tax (EBIT-type, not EBITDA). PAT = 'Profit/(Loss) for the year from Discontinued Operations'. FY2026 figures cover only part of the year (Kwality Wall's ceased to be a subsidiary / demerger effective 30th November, 2025), and FY2026 PAT of 4,407 is dominated by the one-off positive impact of the Ice Cream demerger accounted per the approved scheme, not by trading profit; FY2026 PBT before exceptional items from discontinued operations was (135). ## QUESS — Quess Corp Ltd.

**CONFIRMED** (a demerger scheme is on the exchange record) · **LISTED 1–2Y — the second-year window** · score 5.7/10 · spin-off · 6 filing(s) from CALLS, NSE, NSE-register · first 2025-04-15, latest 2026-10-05

> **Listing:** LISTED — Digitide Solutions Limited trades since about 2025-04-15 (record date 2025-04-15)

**The stages, as filed:** record_date (2025-04-15)

**Stated in the filings:** resulting company **Digitide Solutions Limited**; entitlement **1,889 for every 10,000**; record date 2025-04-15; size hint: 2% of revenue.

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** Digitide Solutions (technology/BPM) and Bluspring Enterprises (industrial/facility services) separated from Quess, leaving a pure-play workforce staffing company — class `value_unlocking`.

- *Insiders:* not stated
- *What it reveals:* Reveals parent as a thin-margin volume business: FY26 EBITDA margin 2.0% versus ~4–4.5% pre-demerger, since higher-margin skilling and Brainhunter left. Offset by zero debt, ₹271 crore net cash, 20% ROE, ₹11 dividend
- *Selling pressure:* likely — Management notes "the stock saw some weakness immediately following the demerger"; resulting companies sit in different industries (technology, industrial services)
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* Digitide Solutions and Bluspring Enterprises standalone results — the EBITDA and debt that left Quess
- *In their words:* “Where there was one company, there are now three separately listed companies: Quess Corp, Bluspring Enterprises and Digitide Solutions, each with its own focus and its own management.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

The separation Quess management describes is a completed three-way demerger of the old Quess Corp, effected from 1 April 2024 under a Composite Scheme of Arrangement in which Quess Corp was the Demerged Company and Digitide Solutions Limited (Resulting Company 1, holding the Global Technology Solutions/BPM, platform, foundit and Brainhunter businesses) and Bluspring Enterprises Limited (Resulting Company 2, holding Operating Asset Maintenance — IFM, food & beverage, security, Vedang telecom infra, and the Golden Star facility-management contracts) were carved out, leaving Quess Corp as a pure-play workforce/staffing company in General Staffing, Professional (IT) Staffing, Overseas staffing and the Hamara digital platforms. The stated reason was focus and value unlocking: management repeatedly said the demerger gives each entity 'its own focus and its own management', a 'sharper strategic identity', agility and the ability to unlock value for shareholders, with Quess itself able to concentrate on 'high-margin, high-growth core segments'. The separation was explicitly used as the trigger for portfolio cleaning: in the run-up, Digitide's service lines were rationalised for low-margin/low-efficiency contracts, and at Quess, the Board and management decided to exit non-core, outcome-based projects in skilling and utilities, booking INR158 crore of Q4 FY25 exceptionals (INR119 crore accelerated expected credit loss on discontinued projects, INR26 crore goodwill impairment — INR7 crore Stellarslog and INR19 crore Quess International Services — and INR13 crore of demerger costs, mainly stamp duty), after INR22 crore of demerger expenses in Q3 FY25; skilling alone had been roughly INR300 crore of revenue at ~20% EBITDA margin. Management conceded the cost: standalone workforce margins of 2.4–2.5% pre-demerger became 1.8% post-demerger because of newly allocated corporate overheads, and the old 4–4.5% consolidated margin is 'noncomparable' since skilling was discontinued and Brainhunter (US/Canada) moved to Digitide — so the goalpost was reset to 2% exit margin. The quid pro quo was balance-sheet and capital-allocation discipline: net cash of INR255 crore and gross debt of only INR12 crore at 31 March 2025, consolidated DSO cut from 44 to 37 days, a new dividend policy returning up to 75% of free cash flow over a rolling three-year block, FY25 dividend of INR10 per share, adjusted ROE moving from high teens to above 20%, and no acquisitions planned — investment to go into AI/sourcing technology instead. Strategically, the separated Quess was to tilt its mix from volume to value: profitability from General Staffing fell from 59% (FY25) to 50%, with Professional Staffing (~30%) plus Overseas (~20%) now half of operating profit (42% a year earlier), Professional Staffing margins rising from ~4.5–4.7% in FY20–21 to 12.7% by Q4 FY26, and 'Quess 2.0' targeting 65% of profit from Professional Staffing plus Overseas and dollar-linked revenue from 7% to over 20% in three to four years. By the AGM, Ajit Isaac framed the outcome as value created from the INR1,270 crore of IPO/IPP capital reinvested, with the three listed companies together generating about INR500 crore of EBITDA and employing over 600,000 people, while Quess remained debt-free with FY26 revenue of INR15,305 crore, EBITDA of INR312 crore (up 19%) and 20% ROE. No call attributes the decision to a demand from investors, lenders or partners — only to the Board and management.

**How it evolved:** In the Feb 2025 (Q3 FY25) call the demerger was still in flight — first NCLT approval received, shareholder and creditor approvals on 9 December 2024, second-motion NCLT pending, INR22 crore of demerger costs booked, listing of all three companies guided for Q1 FY26 — and Digitide's low-margin contracts were already being rationalised 'as a run-up to demerger'. By the May 2025 (Q4 FY25) call it was done ahead of timeline and framed as Quess's 'first earnings call as an independent entity', with INR158 crore of exceptionals for exiting non-core skilling and utilities projects, a new 75%-of-FCF dividend policy, and a reset margin goalpost of 1.8% to 2%. The Aug 2025 and Nov 2025 calls shifted entirely to execution of the 'pure-play staffing leader' model and the 50/50 profit-mix target, while Feb 2026 used the demerger retrospectively to explain why margins are 2% rather than the old 4–4.5% (skilling discontinued, Brainhunter moved to Digitide) and why the INR120 crore ECL related to demerger-era discontinued businesses. The May 2026 call, 'one year post our demerger', applied the same demerger-era test to exit a further 7,000-headcount, milestone-based project worth about INR200 crore (1.3% of revenue), and the August 2026 AGM closed the arc with the three-company outcome and the 'Quess 2.0' mix targets.

**What management expects from it:** For Quess: a pure-play, zero-debt staffing company with sharper focus on high-margin segments — margins rebuilt from 1.8% to 2%+ (2.4% medium term), Professional Staffing 11–12% and Overseas 6%+ lifting their profit share from 50% to 65%, dollar-linked revenue 7% to 20%, ROE above 20%, 80% EBITDA-to-cash conversion and up to 75% of free cash flow returned. Digitide and Bluspring get independent focus, management and technology/industrial platforms.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *CALL Feb 2025* — With the first NCLT approval done and shareholder/creditor approvals obtained on 9 December 2024, Guruprasad framed the pending three-way split as a value-unlocking and positioning exercise for each entity. “This transition marks an important step in unlocking shareholder value and positioning each entity for its future success.”
- *CALL Feb 2025* — CFO Kamal Pal Hoda described the internal work — internal controls, process streamlining and separate leadership teams — as aimed at creating agile, independently focused entities; demerger-related expenses of INR22 crore were booked in the quarter and more were flagged for Q4. “Our aim is to create independent entities that are agile, strategically focused and well positioned to unlock value for all stakeholders in the long term.”
- *CALL Feb 2025* — The separation was already being used to clean the portfolio of the entity going into Digitide, by exiting low-margin, low-efficiency service lines to lift long-run operating margins. “As a run-up to demerger, with a new entity, Digitide, we are examining our existing service lines and rationalizing low-margin low-efficiency contracts, which would give a sustainable upside to our long-term operating margins.”
- *CALL May 2025* — First call as a standalone company: the completed three-way demerger was presented as delivering sharper focus, value unlocking and strategic transformation, alongside net cash of INR255 crore, gross debt of INR12 crore and DSO improved by 7 days to 37. “This important milestone leads to a sharper focus and unlocking value, strategic transformation, and delivering sustained growth.”
- *CALL May 2025* — Guruprasad tied portfolio streamlining post-separation directly to profitability, capital efficiency and long-term value creation for the remaining staffing core. “Moving forward as we streamline our business portfolios, it will enable a sharper focus on high-margin, high-growth core segments.”
- *CALL May 2025* — The demerger triggered a comprehensive business review and Board-approved exit of non-core outcome-based projects in skilling and utilities — INR158 crore of exceptionals (INR119 crore accelerated ECL, INR26 crore goodwill impairment in Stellarslog and Quess International Services, INR13 crore demerger/stamp-duty costs); skilling had been ~INR300 crore of revenue at ~20% EBITDA margin. “As part of the demerger transformation, we revisited some of our businesses through a comprehensive review, and we will be exiting certain non-core projects in line with the position taken by the management and the Board to discontinue such projects.”
- *CALL May 2025* — Asked about new geographies, management said the point of the separation was to go deeper in existing core businesses rather than expand, with no acquisitions planned and investment redirected to AI-led sourcing productivity. “See, as part of this demerger, Siddharth, our focus is going to be on the core businesses and how much more we can do and bring in more efficiency and stay profitable.”
- *CALL Aug 2025* — The identity after separation was stated plainly in the closing remarks — a pure-play staffing company with a simplified structure, zero gross debt at quarter-end, and 53%/29%/21% profitability contribution from General Staffing, Professional Staffing and Overseas. “So, as we strengthen our position as a pure-play staffing leader, we remain deeply committed to operational excellence, innovation and continuously evolving our offerings to meet the dynamic needs of our clients.”
- *CALL Nov 2025* — The post-separation design goal was restated as a 50/50 profit split between scale (General Staffing) and the higher-margin Professional Staffing (11–12%) and Overseas (6%+) businesses — a point management said it had set out two or three quarters earlier and had now reached. “I think we had made one point about 2 or 3 quarters ago where we said we would like to have a healthy state where General Staffing on a growing base contributes 50% of the profitability of that company.”
- *CALL Feb 2026* — Answering why margins are ~2% versus 4–4.5% historically, new CFO Neeraj Jain explained the pre-demerger comparison is invalid: the high-margin skill development business was discontinued and Brainhunter (US/Canada operations) went to Digitide; Kushal added the demerged balance sheet applies from 1 April 2024. “With all of those business with high EBITDA margins, we were averaging around 4%, 4.5%, but that businesses have been discontinued and Brainhunter as part of demerger has moved into Digitide.”
- *CALL Feb 2026* — On the INR120 crore expected credit loss taken in Q4 FY25, Guruprasad confirmed it related to the government skilling receivables of the businesses discontinued as part of the demerger, with collections still being pursued (delayed into Q4 by a new RBI escrow process) and any recovery to be a write-back. “If you recollect, in Q4, these were the discontinued businesses as part of the demerger that we had announced to the Street, and we had taken an exceptional credit loss on that.”
- *CALL May 2026* — One year after the demerger, the same exit test was applied again: a 7,000-headcount milestone-based project was closed down, costing about INR200 crore or 1.3% of revenue, with no further such events known. “As you would remember, closer to our demerger timeline, we had said any business which does not meet the financial metrics of the company and does not yield us the cash realization, we will exit and discontinue such businesses.”

*Not explained on the calls:* Who initiated or demanded it; sum-of-parts or valuation math; how assets, debt and corporate costs were allocated between the three; Digitide/Bluspring economics or listing details.

## SIEMENS — Siemens Ltd.

**CONFIRMED** (a demerger scheme is on the exchange record) · **LISTED 1–2Y — the second-year window** · score 5.7/10 · spin-off · 7 filing(s) from BSE-screener, CALLS, NSE, NSE-register · first 2025-04-07, latest 2026-11-06

> **Listing:** LISTED — the resulting company trades since about 2025-04-07 (record date 2025-04-07)

**The stages, as filed:** nclt_sanction (2025-11-14) → effective (2026-08-11) → record_date (2025-04-07)

**Stated in the filings:** record date 2025-04-07; appointed date 2025-03-01; size hint: 10.5% of revenue.

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** The Energy business of Siemens Limited, transferred to Siemens Energy India Limited under a Scheme of Arrangement — class `not stated`.

- *Insiders:* not stated — no promoter or management shareholding, stake, or incentive in Siemens Energy India Limited is disclosed anywhere in these documents
- *What it reveals:* Energy left with net assets of Rs 37,846 million including Rs 25,478 million cash; it earned Rs 9,418 million PBT on Rs 61,580 million revenue in FY2024. Parent remains cash-rich (Rs 77,905 million cash and bank, 30 Sep 2026) with a Rs 47,034 crore backlog.
- *Selling pressure:* unlikely — Energy was large, not a stub (FY2024 revenue Rs 61,580 million); management said combined share prices rose ~40%
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* Siemens Energy India Limited's own results and the Scheme, for the Rs 37,846 million net assets and Rs 25,478 million cash transferred
- *In their words:* “Pursuant to receipt of necessary statutory approvals and in accordance with the Scheme, the Company has demerged the Energy business effective 25 March 2025, with appointed date being 1 March 2025, as per the Scheme.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

Siemens Ltd. has separated two businesses, and the one management explained in the most detail is the Low Voltage Motors (LVM, plus geared motors and related customer service) business, sold as a going concern on a slump-sale basis to Innomotics India Private Limited for an enterprise value of INR 22 billion (INR 2,200 crore), cash-free/debt-free. The trigger was not Indian: on 1 October 2024 Siemens AG sold the global Innomotics business — and all of its intellectual property — to KPS Capital Partners, leaving the Indian unit as, in Sunil Mathur's words, a licensed sales organisation with no IP, no manufacturing (contract-manufactured to Innomotics design, ~97% of the Business's revenue) and survival dependent on an Agency & Distributorship Agreement and a Technical Cooperation & License Agreement with an entity now controlled by a private-equity owner. So the counterparty, not investors or lenders, effectively forced the decision: the Board stated the Business could not be sold to anyone else because Innomotics owns the IP, making the only alternatives selling to Innomotics India or restructuring the Business and bearing those costs. The numbers management cited were small and deteriorating: for the 12 months to 30 September 2025, revenue from operations of INR 9.67 billion (INR 967 crore) and profit from operations of INR 0.35 billion (INR 35 crore) — 6% of the company's revenue and ~2.2% of its profit from operations ex-Energy — with net capital employed of negative INR 1.38 billion, orders down 6.9% y/y in Q2 FY25, H1 EBITDA of 7.8% (down 130bps on lower price realisation and higher royalties paid to Innomotics), volumes that 'have not increased', cyclicality tied to private-sector capex and copper, and only 89 sales employees; the filing also recorded negative net worth of INR 1,175.66 million and 4.53% of revenue in FY24. Management said synergies with the rest of Siemens Ltd. were 'very limited' and framed the exit as portfolio optimisation that creates value and cash while giving customers and employees continuity. Price was set after negotiation using two independent valuations (Grant Thornton Bharat LLP and KPMG Valuation Services LLP) as at 30 September 2025, and Mathur stressed INR 22 billion was 'the same price that had been offered earlier on by the parent company' despite volumes having since declined. The earlier, larger separation was the Energy demerger into Siemens Energy India Limited (appointed date 1 March 2025, effective 25 March 2025), justified as creating two independent pure-play companies focused on their relevant markets, each with a large backlog; it transferred net assets of INR 37,846 million including INR 25,478 million of cash, cost INR 1.0 billion of demerger expenses in FY25 versus INR 0.1 billion in FY24, and under the November 2023 disclosure the promoters agreed procedures to let Siemens Energy AG acquire a majority in the new listed entity.

**How it evolved:** Dec 2024 call (20 Dec 2024): only the Energy demerger is discussed as a separation — 'on track', creating two independent companies, with LVM not yet flagged as a portfolio issue. May 2025 call (20 May 2025): after the Siemens AG–KPS Innomotics deal of October 2024 and visible margin pressure from royalties paid to Innomotics, management formally said it would 'explore options for the future' of LVM. Dec 2025 (board 8 Dec 2025; analyst meet 12 Dec 2025): the option became a signed slump-sale agreement with Innomotics India at INR 22 billion, justified by lost IP, no local manufacturing, declining volumes (6% of revenue, 2% of profit) and shareholder interest, with closing guided to mid-2026. Jun 2026 call (28 May 2026) reconfirmed completion 'on track for June 2026'; the sale closed 1 June 2026 with a provisional gain of INR 20,990 million, while in the opposite direction the Board approved amalgamating subsidiary Siemens Rail Automation into the parent (26 May 2026) and took C&S Electric to 100% via capital reduction (NCLT order 24 September 2026).

**What management expects from it:** For Siemens Ltd.: a cleaner three-business technology portfolio (DI, SI, Mobility), removal of a sub-scale, negative-capital-employed, royalty-burdened unit worth 6% of revenue but only 2% of profit, INR 22 billion of cash plus an INR 2,099 crore gain, and portfolio optimisation 'creating value and cash'. For Innomotics India: ownership aligned with the IP it already holds, continuity for LVM customers and the 89 sales staff. For Energy: an independent pure-play.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *[May 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=2ae69c31-b96b-4781-9858-035146160df1.pdf)* — CFO Wrumnig first links LVM's fate to the parent's global divestment of Innomotics to KPS Capital Partners and to the Indian unit's technical dependence on that business, announcing an options review. “In view of this sale and the dependency on the global Innomotics business, we will now explore options for the future of the Low Voltage Motors business.”
- *[May 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=2ae69c31-b96b-4781-9858-035146160df1.pdf)* — The economics were already visibly impaired: weak orders, price pressure and royalties payable to the new KPS-owned owner of the IP compressing margins. “Year-to-date, the business reported an EbitDA margin of 7.8%, down by 130bps due to lower price realization and higher royalties paid to Innomotics, the former global Siemens business, now owned by KPS Capital Partners.”
- *[Dec 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=82783258-f887-444b-a6f1-cbeaf34f0b62.pdf)* — Mathur describes what Siemens Ltd. actually owned in LVM — a licence to sell someone else's product, with outsourced manufacturing and no IP rights in India. “It is within Siemens Limited. It is outsourced manufacturing. Revenues are cyclical, as you know, for motors.”
- *[Dec 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=82783258-f887-444b-a6f1-cbeaf34f0b62.pdf)* — The volume thesis that justified keeping the business had failed, tied to muted private-sector capex and copper prices. “The expectation was that the volumes will increase. Those volumes have not increased in the country.”
- *[Dec 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=82783258-f887-444b-a6f1-cbeaf34f0b62.pdf)* — Board approval of the slump sale to Innomotics India at INR 22 billion, explicitly the same price the parent had offered earlier, with closing guided to mid-2026. “And this was then finally approved by the board of Siemens Limited in terms of a sale and transfer on a slump sale basis to Innomotics India at a purchase price of 22 billion, which I will remind you was the same price that had been offered earlier on by the parent company.”
- *[Dec 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=82783258-f887-444b-a6f1-cbeaf34f0b62.pdf)* — Materiality and shareholder-interest framing: the business had shrunk to 6% of volumes and 2% of profits. “Considering the fact that the volumes have declined, in the meantime, it is only 6% of the overall volume of Siemens and only 2% of Siemens profits in the meantime.”
- *[Dec 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=82783258-f887-444b-a6f1-cbeaf34f0b62.pdf)* — The prior, bigger separation is presented as completed and successful — Energy is now a separately listed pure-play, leaving Siemens Ltd. with DI, SI and Mobility. “A major development during this period has been the demerger of Siemens Energy India Limited, which is now a separately listed pure play energy company.”
- *[Dec 2024](https://assets.new.siemens.com/siemens/assets/api/uuid:dc7b02ca-736c-4db6-8118-da2b47754aa6/Analyst-Call-Transcript-website.pdf)* — Rationale originally given for the Energy demerger: two focused, independently capitalised companies each with large backlogs. “Both companies are very well prepared for the future growth, focusing on their relevant markets.”
- *[Jun 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=f8a31e42-7fdf-46ab-8ac9-a4540a097f8b.pdf)* — Final status update before closing; the quarter also shows demerger-related expenses falling by INR 500 million as separation costs roll off. “And third, on the portfolio topic, the sale of the low-voltage motors business is on track for completion in June 2026.”
- *Scheme* — Filing of 8 Dec 2025 states the hard constraint: without Innomotics/KPS support Siemens Ltd. cannot run the business, which is why the only buyer was the counterparty itself. “The Company itself does not have the requisite intellectual property or other capabilities to service the Business without support from Innomotics GmbH which is now owned by KPS.”
- *Scheme* — Strategic-fit argument plus the stated financial benefit of exiting — portfolio optimisation generating value and cash. “Synergies between the Business and the rest of the Company’s businesses are very limited.”
- *Scheme* — Price discovery and process: negotiated against two independent valuations as at 30 September 2025, outside any scheme of arrangement and not a related-party transaction. “The consideration for the sale and transfer of the Business has been determined after negotiation between the Company and the Buyer, taking into account two separate independent valuation reports of the Business as at 30th September 2025 pursuant to independent valuation exercises conducted by each of Grant Thornton Bharat LLP and                 KPMG Valuation Services LLP .”

*Not explained on the calls:* No post-sale margin, ROCE or capital-deployment guidance; no bridge from the 2024 parent offer to INR 22 billion; silent on employee transfer terms, ADA/TCLA wind-down, and buyer-selection alternatives.

## SKFINDIA — SKF India Ltd.

**CONFIRMED** (a demerger scheme is on the exchange record) · **LISTED 1–2Y — the second-year window** · score 5.7/10 · spin-off · 10 filing(s) from CALLS, NSE, NSE-register · first 2025-10-15, latest 2026-08-20

> **Listing:** LISTED — the resulting company trades since about 2025-10-17 (record date 2025-10-15)

**The stages, as filed:** exchange_noc (2025-11-28) → nclt_sanction (2025-11-15) → record_date (2025-10-15) → listed (2025-10-17)

**Stated in the filings:** record date 2025-10-15; size hint: 15% of ebitda.

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** The Industrial business (Demerged Undertaking) — bearings for infrastructure, railways, renewables, cement, heavy engineering — into SKF India (Industrial) Limited — class `value_unlocking`.

- *Insiders:* Mirror-image demerger: one SKF Industrial share per SKF India share, 4,94,37,963 shares allotted; shareholding pattern mirrors the Demerged Company. Promoter stake percentages and management incentives in the new entity not stated.
- *What it reveals:* Cost-of-acquisition apportionment gives Industrial 53.12% versus automotive 46.88%, so the departing half is the larger one. Remaining automotive PBT margin fell to 12.3% against pre-demerger talk of 16-19% EBITDA; management calls the one-offs transitory, loading exceeds 90%, INR 500 crore capex to 2028.
- *Selling pressure:* likely — Every SKF India holder received industrial shares 1:1 in a different industry; shares remained frozen in depositories until listing permission.
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* SKF India (Industrial) Limited Information Memorandum and its standalone results — margins of the 53.12% cost-apportioned half.
- *In their words:* “The demerger gives us the strategic clarity to sharpen our priorities, accelerate growth, and unlock greater value for all stakeholders.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

Management framed the separation as a group-level, mirror-image reverse carve-out in which the Industrial undertaking was hived off into SKF India (Industrial) Limited and the listed SKF India Limited was left as the pure automotive company, with shareholders getting one new INR 10 share for every share held (PwC share-entitlement report 24 Dec 2024, Saffron Capital fairness opinion 25 Dec 2024). The stated logic rested on three differences management repeated at every call: macro drivers (automotive = BS-VII/CAFE and emission norms, a 30% EV penetration target by 2030, premiumisation/SUVs, last-mile commercial vehicles; industrial = infrastructure spend, Make in India/PLI/NIP, China-plus-one, railways/metro/Vande Bharat, renewables capacity doubling by 2030), customer needs (a handful of auto OEMs wanting application-specific, long-cycle engineered parts — 60-65% engineered-to-order — versus thousands of small industrial customers across verticals needing uptime, service and 2-3 new products a year), and manufacturing philosophy (auto: large batch, small/medium bearings, automation, cycle-time efficiency; industrial: small batches, wide assortment, medium/large bearings, fast changeovers, plus traded product). On that base it promised independent management focus, tailored capital deployment, manufacturing efficiency, agility, tailored innovation and separate financial visibility to attract investors aligned to each business. The problem it solved was that the two were 'so deeply integrated' that neither could be run or funded on its own terms: at the time of the split Industrial was ~52-53% of INR ~4,900-5,000 crore revenue, Automotive ~39-40% and exports ~8%, auto was >90-95% localised while industrial was only ~30-35% (ISEA ~50%, target 70%) and capacity-constrained in both — so capex was raised from INR 130-150 crore a year to ~INR 250 crore and ~INR 1,200 crore over five years, including a brand-new industrial-only plant in Pune by 2028 (INR 450-500 crore) plus INR 350-450 crore of line expansion, and INR 500-600 crore for automotive capacity to 2030. The physical split was spelled out: Bangalore 10 lines (7 auto / 3 industrial, the 3 moving to Pune so Bangalore becomes 100% auto), Pune 22 lines (12 auto / 10 industrial), Haridwar 4 lines all auto; land 85:15 Bangalore, 52:48 Pune, 100% Haridwar; manpower 55-60% auto / 40-45% industrial. Carve-out economics shown were FY24 EBITDA ~18% automotive and ~17% industrial with PBT ~16% for both, and guidance of 10-12% auto and 8-10% industrial growth to FY28 at 17-19% margins. It was driven by SKF AB's own global automotive/industrial split (Kerstin Enochsson, President Automotive, sat on the India board) and endorsed by shareholders on 14 July 2025 and by investors such as Ravi Purohit, who 'wholeheartedly supported this demerger initiative'; no lender or JV-partner demand was ever cited, and SKF India bore the demerger costs — INR 184 million in Q1 FY26 alone, mostly SAP/IT separation and consultants, guided to cost 1.5-2% of margin into H1 FY27, plus stamp duty and registration on asset transfers landing in the industrial entity.

**How it evolved:** The process began in Q4 CY2024 and was first explained in full on the dedicated demerger update call of 9 April 2025 (rationale, pro-forma FY24 carve-out financials, 12-15 month timeline), then detailed operationally on 19 May 2025 (which plants go where, a new industrial-only Pune plant) and on 30 June 2025, when management first disclosed segment-level revenue mixes and gave FY28 guidance of 10-12% auto / 8-10% industrial growth at 17-19% margins. At the NCLT-convened meeting of 14 July 2025 shareholders approved the scheme 1:1 while pressing on why India would end up with three SKF entities and on the capex jump from ~INR 150 crore to ~INR 350-400 crore a year; the 6 August 2025 AGM called it 'unlocking the power of two' and the 7 August 2025 Q1 FY26 call put hard numbers on the split (lines, land, 55-60% manpower) and on costs (INR 184 million in the quarter, 530 bps margin drop, 1.5-2% drag into H1 FY27). NCLT Mumbai sanctioned the scheme on 26 September 2025, it took effect 1 October 2025, the record date was 15 October and 4,94,37,963 industrial shares were allotted on 17 October 2025, with cost of acquisition apportioned 46.88% auto / 53.12% industrial. By the 21 May 2026 Q4 FY26 call the story had shifted from value unlock to transition pain — sustainable PBT guidance cut to 11-12% against the 16-19% communicated pre-demerger, FY26 EBITDA 15.3%, continued trading from the industrial entity because auto is capacity-short, and sustained investor complaints that disclosure had 'dropped substantially'; the 14 August 2026 AGM then rebranded the automotive entity SKF Vertevo.

**What management expects from it:** Two fit-for-purpose, independently listed companies with their own boards, sales, manufacturing and capital allocation: automotive to lead e-mobility, launch faster, grow 10-12% and hold 16-19% EBITDA from FY28 (near-term guidance since cut to 11-12% PBT); industrial to grow 8-10%, then faster once a dedicated Pune plant lifts localisation from ~30% to ~70%; sharper investor visibility, better valuation, 1:1 shareholding preserved.

- *Apr 2025* — Management named the three structural differences that justified separation — industry dynamics, customer needs and manufacturing philosophy. “The reason is, first, there is -- the dynamics of the industries are fundamentally different. Second, the customer needs themselves are different in the Automotive and Industrial. **CONFIRMED** (a demerger scheme is on the exchange record) · **LISTED 1–2Y — the second-year window** · score 5.7/10 · spin-off · 23 filing(s) from NSE, NSE-register · first 2025-10-14, latest 2026-11-01

> **Listing:** LISTED — the resulting company trades since about 2025-10-14 (record date 2025-10-14)

**The stages, as filed:** meetings (2025-11-28) → record_date (2025-10-14)

**Stated in the filings:** demerged undertaking: , undertaking; record date 2025-10-14.

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** The Commercial Vehicles business of Tata Motors Limited, demerged into a separate listed entity — class `regulatory_strategic`.

- *Insiders:* Promoter and promoter group held 1,565,402,703 of 3,682,582,902 shares (~42.5%), receiving 1:1 shares in the Resulting Company. MD Shailesh Chandra holds 1,50,029 shares plus PSUs under Scheme 2024, subject to Scheme Clause 9.
- *What it reveals:* Cost apportionment implies 68.85% of value in TMPV versus 31.15% in CV. Parent keeps JLR plus India PV/EV: FY26 consolidated net debt Rs 30,000 Cr sits almost entirely at JLR (Rs 33,000 Cr) while India PV is cash positive Rs 7,000 Cr.
- *Selling pressure:* likely — 1:1 shares pushed to all 64,60,243-shareholder base of a large parent; commercial vehicles is a different business from cars/SUVs.
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* Tata Motors Limited (formerly TML Commercial Vehicles) standalone results and its Rs 4 dividend — the spin's own profitability.
- *In their words:* “In this regard, we wish to inform that TMCV has intimated the Company today that it has received approval from BSE Limited and National Stock Exchange of India Limited for listing and trading of its equity shares, effective November 12, 2025.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

The business being separated is the Commercial Vehicles (CV) business of the erstwhile Tata Motors Limited, carved out under a Composite Scheme of Arrangement into TML Commercial Vehicles Limited (since renamed Tata Motors Limited), while the listed parent was renamed Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Limited (TMPV) and simultaneously absorbed its wholly-owned subsidiary Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Limited by amalgamation — the Scheme's stated purpose there being 'consolidating the Passenger Vehicles Business with TML'. The net effect, as the Scheme describes it, is that 'the Commercial Vehicle and Passenger Vehicle businesses of the Company are housed in two separate entities' from October 1, 2025, leaving TMPV with India PV, EV (Tata Passenger Electric Mobility) and JLR, plus Tata Technologies and Tata Motors Holdings Singapore in 'others'; segment reporting was recast accordingly and prior-period balance sheets declared non-comparable. Critically, across all six transcripts management never articulates a strategic reason for the split — no dis-synergy, focus, capital-allocation or value-unlock argument is given; the demerger appears only as a corporate action with dates, approvals, accounting and costs. The economics disclosed are: CV was valued at about Rs 94,000 Cr by third-party agencies against a transferred book value of about Rs 11,000 Cr, producing a Rs 83,000 Cr accounting profit on disposal of the CV undertaking that is 'only a notional gain' because of an equal contra deemed-dividend entry, so there is 'absolutely no impact on either distributable reserves or on our net worth'. Shareholders got one CV share for every one share held (1:1), the split is Section 2(19AA)-compliant so it is not a transfer in shareholders' hands, and cost of acquisition was apportioned 31.15% to CV and 68.85% to TMPV. Costs cited were a Rs 400 Cr stamp duty provision in Q3 FY26 (within Rs 1,600 Cr of exceptionals) rolling into the Rs 4,100 Cr of FY26 exceptionals alongside cyber and labour-code charges. Governance was split too — separate boards and KMP, Shailesh Chandra as MD & CEO of TMPV, P B Balaji moving to CEO of JLR — and capital structures now report separately (India PV net cash ~Rs 5,000 Cr at Q3 FY26 and ~Rs 7,000 Cr at year-end versus JLR net debt of ~Rs 33,000–39,000 Cr). No investor, lender or partner is named as having asked for the separation; the only constituency cited is shareholders, who approved it with 'overwhelming votes in our favor', plus SEBI/stock exchange NOCs and NCLT sanction.

**How it evolved:** In the Feb 2025 (Jan 29, 2025) call the demerger appears only as a corporate-action status item — filings done, NOC from the exchanges and SEBI awaited, appointed date July 1 and effective date around October 1, 2025 — and by the Jun 2025 (May 13, 2025) call management reports 'overwhelming votes' from shareholders and reaffirms those dates. In the Aug 2025 (Aug 8, 2025) call the NCLT final hearing had concluded that same day with judgment reserved, with the October 1 effective date still 'on plan'; the Nov 2025 (Nov 14, 2025) call is the first reported as a post-demerger listed entity, dominated by mechanics: segment recast, non-comparable balance sheets, and the Rs 83,000 Cr notional disposal gain against the Rs 94,000 Cr valuation and Rs 11,000 Cr book value. Thereafter it shrinks to a cost line — a Rs 400 Cr stamp duty provision in Feb 2026 (Feb 5, 2026) and stamp duty inside Rs 4,100 Cr of FY26 exceptionals in Jun 2026 (May 14, 2026), where the only forward-looking framing offered is that TMPV's Rs 3 dividend plus TMLCV's Rs 4 equals Rs 7 against Rs 6 paid by erstwhile Tata Motors. At no point in that sequence does the stated rationale evolve, because none is ever stated.

**What management expects from it:** Little quantified. Post-separation TMPV holds PV, EV and JLR only; segments recast to automotive plus others. India PV stays net cash (~Rs 5,000–7,000 Cr), giving 'flex' to fund its product cycle toward double-digit EBITDA; CV lists separately with its own board and dividend. Combined dividend rose to Rs 7 from Rs 6; net worth unchanged.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *[Feb 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=28345af3-7271-4146-8cf3-8da0f9c73222.pdf)* — The demerger is reported purely as a process milestone: regulatory no-objections from the exchanges and SEBI awaited, operational separation work advanced, appointed date July 1 and effective date around October 1, 2025. “We are expecting the NOC from the Stock Exchange and SEBI any time now, all filed and done.”
- *[Jun 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=80350d5e-9578-469f-bf9f-31610098f897.pdf)* — Shareholder approval is confirmed as emphatic and the timetable reaffirmed; the only related substantive disclosure is that the Tata Capital stake goes with the CV business. “The demerger update: we had overwhelming votes in our favor and therefore we are on track for an appointed date of July 1st and an effective date of October 1st 2025.”
- *[Aug 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=2a91a004-4cbd-440e-93d3-2ca8967ff37b.pdf)* — The NCLT final hearing concluded on the day of the call with judgment reserved, and management still guided to an October 1 effective date, expecting completion within the quarter. “We had the NCLT final hearing today and it has been concluded and the judgment is reserved.”
- *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=e6684a03-5a4d-4c7a-8da0-d5b2c52ec7d1.pdf)* — First results as the post-demerger listed entity: CV is out of segment reporting, the automotive segment is now JLR plus Tata Passenger Vehicles, others is mainly Tata Technologies and Tata Motors Holdings Singapore, and prior-period balance sheets still include CV so are not comparable. “It's a pleasure speaking to you as we report our first quarterly earnings as a listed entity.”
- *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=e6684a03-5a4d-4c7a-8da0-d5b2c52ec7d1.pdf)* — The accounting: CV was independently valued at about Rs 94,000 Cr versus about Rs 11,000 Cr of net assets transferred, giving a Rs 83,000 Cr disposal profit that is purely notional because of an offsetting Rs 83,000 Cr deemed dividend. “As part of demerger accounting entries, we have recorded a profit of ~Rs. 83,000 Cr on disposal of the CV undertaking, which is essentially the fair value of the CV assets, less the book value of net assets transferred.”
- *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=e6684a03-5a4d-4c7a-8da0-d5b2c52ec7d1.pdf)* — Capital structures are now shown standalone — auto net debt moved from net cash to ~Rs 20,000 Cr (all at JLR) while India PV is net cash, which is the one place management links the standalone balance sheet to funding its product cycle. “Domestic India business is net cash which gives a lot of flex to fund the rich product investment cycle that will be coming through in the years.”
- *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=7907e958-7953-4b49-b831-aab03d6e2746.pdf)* — The demerger is now only a reporting and cost item: CV permanently out of segments, and a Rs 400 Cr stamp duty provision taken within Rs 1,600 Cr of quarterly exceptionals alongside Rs 800 Cr of cyber costs and a Rs 400 Cr wage-bill charge. “I would like to call out that this excludes exceptional for Rs. 1,600 Cr: Rs. 800 Cr at JLR - additional impact because of the cyber incident, Rs. 400 Cr one-time Wage bill impact for India business, and another Rs.400 Cr provision we have taken for the stamp duty impact.”
- *[Jun 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=b4d386d7-de53-4409-8e90-187e08cb4a91.pdf)* — FY26 PBT of Rs 2,500 Cr is stated before Rs 4,100 Cr of exceptionals that include the demerger stamp duty, and the two entities' dividends are presented together as evidence shareholders are better off post-split. “So this actually represents a total dividend of Rs. 7 in the year when the demerger was undertaken and an increase over the Rs. 6 that we have paid for the last two years.”
- *Scheme* — The Scheme has two legs: the CV undertaking demerges out of Tata Motors into TML Commercial Vehicles Limited on a going-concern basis, and the PV subsidiary amalgamates into the parent so that the passenger business is consolidated in one listed company, with the subsidiary dissolved. “Amalgamation of TMLPV with TML with an objective of consolidating the Passenger Vehicles Business with TML and consequent dissolution of TMLPV without being wound up.”
- *Scheme* — Shareholders received 1 CV share for every 1 share held, the demerger is Section 2(19AA)-compliant so not a transfer in their hands, and cost of acquisition splits 31.15% to the new Tata Motors (CV) and 68.85% to TMPV; separate boards and KMP were constituted for both entities, with CV shares listed from November 12, 2025. “the Commercial Vehicle and Passenger Vehicle businesses of the Company are housed in two separate entities”

*Not explained on the calls:* Calls never state the strategic rationale, value-unlock or synergy numbers, who asked for the split, total transaction costs beyond stamp duty, or post-demerger capital-allocation, margin and valuation targets.

## ANANTRAJ — Anant Raj Ltd.

**CONFIRMED** (a demerger scheme is on the exchange record) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 5.0/10 · spin-off · 6 filing(s) from NSE, NSE-deep · first 2026-05-11, latest 2026-07-21

> **Listing:** NOT YET — scheme at 'announced' stage; the resulting company will list only after NCLT sanction, effectiveness and a record date; no listing timeline stated

**The stages, as filed:** announced (2026-07-21)

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** The Data Centre and Cloud Services business of ARL and ARCPL, vested in Ashok Cloud Private Limited — class `value_unlocking`.

- *Insiders:* ARL promoters hold 57.42% of ARL; post-scheme ACPL is 28.14% promoters directly plus 51% held by ARL (79.14% total), public 20.86%. Promoter-group Anish Sarin oversees data-centre rollout.
- *What it reveals:* Demerged Undertaking turnover Rs 145.90 cr is only 8.96% of Rs 1,627.72 cr; management cites ~75% data-centre EBITDA margin, 357 MW planned capacity, Rs 20,000 cr capex, net-cash parent with Rs 4,471.64 cr net worth.
- *Selling pressure:* likely — Small (8.96% of turnover), only 20.86% public float in ACPL, and a digital-infrastructure business alien to real-estate holders.
- *Parent or spin:* both · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* The full Composite Scheme: asset/liability split and valuation of the Demerged Undertaking versus ACPL's Rs 74.86 cr rights issue.
- *In their words:* “The Data Centre Business has evolved significantly over the years and is well poised to chart its own growth path and operate as a separate listed entity focused on the rapidly growing Data Centre Business whilst continuing to leverage ARL's institutional strengths, strong brand equity and goodwill.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

Management says Anant Raj Ltd today runs two unlike businesses under one roof — the legacy real estate/infrastructure business (residential townships, luxury housing, commercial leasing, hospitality) and a data centre & cloud services business — and that the Data Centre Business is itself split across two entities, Anant Raj Limited and its wholly owned Anant Raj Cloud Private Limited (ARCPL), with assets, employees, investments and operations housed in both. The Composite Scheme therefore first amalgamates ARCPL into ARL and then demerges the whole Data Centre Business out of ARL into Ashok Cloud Private Limited (ACPL), so all of it sits in one dedicated, separately listed company. The stated problems it solves: the two verticals differ 'significantly in their nature, risk profile, competitive dynamics, and capital requirements', and the Board recorded on May 11, 2026 that keeping both in one company 'does not adequately reflect the true potential and intrinsic value of each business segment, thereby impacting stakeholder returns'; the split is meant to give independent market-driven valuation of a pure-play digital infrastructure asset, dedicated management focus, a simpler ownership structure with intra-group arrangements cancelled/rationalised, and the ability to attract sector-specific capital, strategic investors and partnerships. The numbers cited: the Demerged Undertaking did ₹145.90 cr turnover in FY26 versus ₹1,627.72 cr aggregated (8.96%); ARCPL turnover ₹136.20 cr and net worth ₹49.45 cr versus ARL's ₹1,491.52 cr turnover and ₹4,471.64 cr net worth; ACPL had nil turnover and ₹0.04 cr net worth and was capitalised days earlier via a ₹74.86 cr rights issue (37,43,22,553 shares at ₹2). Scale is the driver: the Board noted an MOU with the Govt. of Andhra Pradesh for 50 MW IT load taking total planned capacity to 357 MW IT load, requiring about ₹20,000 cr of investment — against a real estate business management repeatedly said should carry as little debt as possible. Mechanically, ARL shareholders get 1 ACPL share of ₹2 for every 1 ARL share of ₹2, giving them 49% of ACPL directly (promoters 28.14%, public 20.86%) while ARL retains 51%, so ACPL stays a subsidiary and ARL holders keep 100% of the ultimate economic interest; ACPL will be listed on BSE and NSE under the Rule 19(7) exemption. The ask came from the equity market side — an investor asked about a demerger as early as the Apr 2024 call, and analysts kept pressing for separate real estate vs data centre reporting — not from lenders or partners, who are never cited as requesting it.

**How it evolved:** On the Apr 25, 2024 call Arpit Shah of Stallion Asset asked outright whether there were plans to demerge the business and Amit Sarin refused — 'too soon', focus on execution — while describing the cloud venture as a half-megawatt pilot with TCIL. By the Oct 30, 2024 call (Q2 FY25) management was framing the group as 'two full-fledged divisions' (real estate plus a technology division) with a ₹2,100 cr fundraise earmarked purely for data centre/cloud, and Raj Sarraf pushed for separate data centre revenue disclosure; on the Nov 12, 2025 call (Q2/H1 FY26) the CFO called the company 'at an important inflection point' with a 'legacy real estate business' alongside the data centre/cloud 'future ready platform', the ₹1,100 cr QIP was done, and analysts again asked for a separate segment/EBITDA breakup, which management declined on the 10%-of-revenue threshold. The demerger itself was never discussed on any of the three calls: it surfaced in the May 11, 2026 board note (which recorded the need for merger/demerger and set up a committee of Amit Sarin, Ashim Sarin, Manoj Goyal and Pankaj Gupta to frame a scheme), then was executed as the ACPL rights-issue funding on July 20, 2026 and the Composite Scheme approved on July 21, 2026.

**What management expects from it:** Ashok Cloud: pure-play digital-infrastructure valuation and independent market recognition, sector-specific growth capital, partnerships and acquisitions, dedicated leadership, consolidated ownership (75% EBITDA-margin colocation/cloud, 357 MW plan, ~₹20,000 cr capex). Anant Raj: sharper focus on real estate, infrastructure and hospitality, low debt, continued execution. Both: operational efficiency, agility, faster decision-making, transparency, unlocked shareholder value, with holders participating directly in each.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *[Apr 2024](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=03aa7997-f0a0-4f9b-8373-f4a4684da92d.pdf)* — An investor (Arpit Shah, Stallion Asset) directly asked about demerging the data centre business; management declined to engage, calling the business too young and prioritising execution toward the 300 MW mark in four years. “We are too soon to say anything on that. Let's focus on execution, Arpit.”
- *[Apr 2024](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=03aa7997-f0a0-4f9b-8373-f4a4684da92d.pdf)* — Management set out the different capital philosophies that later justify separation: real estate was to be net debt-free by December 2024 and the only debt acceptable would be lease rental discounting, including against long 10-15 year data centre leases. “And the only debt which Anant Raj is open to taking is LRD and this is one of the best items for LRD because you have long-term leases and good clients.”
- *[Nov 2024](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=27b8b856-615a-44a5-8be4-157fd1831d5c.pdf)* — Management began describing the group as two separate divisions — the historic real estate 'bread and butter' and a new technology division of colocation and cloud — the same two-vertical framing the Scheme later uses. “So Anant Raj Limited will now have two full-fledged divisions. Real estate division which is the historical, the division of the company, the bread and butter of the company as of now and plus the technology division, in which we will be data center, co-location infrastructure and cloud.”
- *[Nov 2024](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=27b8b856-615a-44a5-8be4-157fd1831d5c.pdf)* — The ₹2,100 cr fundraise (₹100 cr promoters, ₹2,000 cr market) was ring-fenced entirely for the data centre/cloud build-out, with real estate funded from internal accruals — distinct funding requirements per vertical, with cloud capex cited at ~₹100 cr per MW on top of ₹26 cr colocation capex. “This is purely data center, sir. This fund is going to be purely for data centers. For our real estate, we are completely funded with our internal sources.”
- *[Nov 2024](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=27b8b856-615a-44a5-8be4-157fd1831d5c.pdf)* — An analyst (Raj Sarraf of Finvestors) asked for data centre revenue to be reported separately from real estate because it would become the major contributor; management conceded the point. “Sir, both the revenues are going to be substantial and we will be breaking them up, sir . We will do that definitely.”
- *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=3ac557ff-2c8f-4014-b2d4-e7e582aa0e59.pdf)* — The CFO positioned the company at an 'inflection point' with a legacy real estate business and a separate future-ready data centre/cloud platform — H1 FY26 revenue ₹1,223.2 cr of which data centre only ₹58.42 cr, ₹1,100 cr QIP completed, net cash positive, ~₹700 cr capital employed in data centres at 75% EBITDA margin. “Our legacy real estate business continues to deliver a consistent growth and strengthen our leadership in high demanding markets. At the same time, our Data Center and Cloud initiatives are shaping up the future ready platform that positions us as a diversified resilient enterprise s.”
- *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=3ac557ff-2c8f-4014-b2d4-e7e582aa0e59.pdf)* — Investors (Sri Gopal of StockHifi, Ashwani Sharma of Emkay) again pressed for separate real estate vs data centre revenue and EBITDA reporting; management said formal segment disclosure was not yet triggered because data centre revenue was under 10% of the total. “In this, you have to give segmental breakup once you do 10%.”
- *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=3ac557ff-2c8f-4014-b2d4-e7e582aa0e59.pdf)* — Asked whether the company should lever up to scale data centres faster, management refused on the grounds that real estate is the backbone and must stay low-debt — a tension a separately funded data centre entity resolves. Capacity plans were 63 MW by Dec 2026, 117 MW by FY28 and 307 MW by FY31-32. “And as it is, we feel that our backbone is still real estate, which will always be. And we feel that real estate should be as low on debt as possible.”
- *Scheme* — The May 11, 2026 board note first records the need for a merger/demerger, citing differing nature, risk profile, competitive dynamics and capital requirements, plus the 357 MW IT load plan (after the 50 MW Andhra Pradesh MOU) needing about ₹20,000 cr; a committee of Amit Sarin, Ashim Sarin, Manoj Goyal and Pankaj Gupta was formed to design it. “The Board of Directors have considered that the Company is presently engaged in two distinct business undertakings, namely Real Estate Development and Data Center Services, which differ significantly in their nature, risk profile, competitive dynamics, and capital requirements and continuing both businesses under a single corporate does not adequately reflect the true potential and intrinsic value of each business segment, thereby impacting stakeholder returns.”
- *Scheme* — The July 21, 2026 Scheme explains the data centre business is split across ARL and ARCPL, so ARCPL is first merged into ARL and the combined Data Centre Business then demerged into Ashok Cloud — consolidating it in one entity and creating two focused listed companies. “The Data Centre Business is presently conducted through ARL and ARCPL, with various assets, employees, investments and business operations pertaining to the Data Centre Business being housed across both entities.”
- *Scheme* — Stated benefit one: independent market recognition and valuation of the data centre business given its distinct operating profile, growth trajectory, risk-return characteristics and funding needs; demerged undertaking turnover was ₹145.90 cr, 8.96% of ₹1,627.72 cr for FY26. “the segregation of the Data Centre Business into a separately listed company would facilitate independent market recognition and valuation of the Data Centre Business, having regard to its distinct operating profile, growth trajectory, risk-return characteristics and funding requirements;”
- *Scheme* — Stated benefit two: a distinct legal entity lets Ashok Cloud attract sector-specific capital, investors, acquisitions and partnerships, with simpler ownership and intra-group arrangements cancelled or rationalised. “the separation of the Data Centre Business into a distinct legal entity will enable Ashok Cloud to effectively attract sector specific resources for its growth requirements and pursue strategic investments, partnerships, thereby unlocking greater value for its shareholders;”

*Not explained on the calls:* Calls never mention the demerger; no appointed date, debt/cash/asset split, valuation or swap basis, why ARL keeps 51%, how ₹20,000 cr capex gets funded, or listing timeline.
