## DBREALTY — VALOR ESTATE Ltd.

**CONFIRMED** (a demerger scheme is on the exchange record) · **LISTED 1–2Y — the second-year window** · score 5.0/10 · spin-off · 6 filing(s) from NSE, NSE-register · first 2025-07-18, latest 2026-01-30

> **Listing:** LISTED — Horizontal Ventures Private Limited trades since about 2025-07-18 (record date 2025-07-18)

**The stages, as filed:** nclt_sanction (2025-11-15) → effective (2025-11-14) → record_date (2025-07-18)

**Stated in the filings:** resulting company **Horizontal Ventures Private Limited**; demerged undertaking: / Discontinued Operations are given as under:; entitlement **1 for every 10**; record date 2025-07-18; appointed date 2025-04-01.

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** The hospitality (hotel ownership) business of Valor Estate, demerged into Advent Hotels International Limited — class `value_unlocking`.

- *Insiders:* Mr. Arshad Balwa is Promoter Director of AHIL; Rahul Pandit is MD & CEO; AHIL governed by own Board post-demerger. Shareholders received 1 AHIL share per 10 Valor shares; promoters held 47.43% of Valor. AHIL promoter stake not stated.
- *What it reveals:* Spin holds 313-key Grand Hyatt Goa and 171-key Hilton Mumbai, five projects under development, EBITDA under Rs.200 crore targeted above Rs.1,200 crore by FY32 (3,100+ keys). Parent left as pure real estate; consolidated borrowings fell sharply post-demerger.
- *Selling pressure:* likely — Only 1 AHIL share per 10 held, so tiny odd-lot positions; hospitality is a different industry from the parent's real estate.
- *Parent or spin:* both · *option pricing date:* 14th August 2025 (Nomination and Remuneration Committee approved grant of 10,00,000 options under ESOP 2024); earlier ESOP 2022 options exercised at Rs. 41.45 per share during quarter ended 30th June 2025
- *Read next:* AHIL's own balance sheet: the Rs. 2,01,956.25 lakhs other non-current financial liabilities transferred with the demerged undertaking
- *In their words:* “A Composite Scheme of Amalgamation and Arrangement was entered into between the Company ("Amalgamated Company" and "Demerged Company") and Esteem Properties Private Limited ("Amalgamating Company"/"EPPL") and Advent Hotels International Limited (formerly known as Shiva Realtors Suburban Private Limited) ("Resulting Company"/"AHIL) ("Scheme") mainly with aim to demerge hospitality business of the Company into Resulting Company and thus unlock overall value for the shareholders.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

No earnings-call transcripts are on file, so the reasoning below is reconstructed only from the filings. The separation is the demerger of Valor Estate Ltd's (formerly D B Realty Ltd) hospitality business into Advent Hotels International Limited (formerly Shiva Realtors Suburban Private Limited) under a Composite Scheme of Amalgamation and Arrangement that also amalgamated Esteem Properties Private Limited into Valor; the Explanatory Statement to the 12th December 2025 EGM says the Scheme was entered into 'mainly with aim to demerge hospitality business of the Company into Resulting Company and thus unlock overall value for the shareholders.' NCLT Mumbai sanctioned it on 12 June 2025, it became effective 1 July 2025 (demerger appointed date 1 April 2025; Esteem amalgamation appointed date 1 April 2024), and shareholders on the 18 July 2025 record date received 1 AHIL share of Rs. 10 for every 10 Valor shares. The carve-out moved consolidated net assets of Rs. 1,02,194.65 lakhs (standalone Rs. 1,01,512.91 lakhs) out of Valor — Rs. 1,49,386.00 lakhs of property, plant and equipment, Rs. 54,858.00 lakhs of goodwill, Rs. 29,117.12 lakhs of intangibles, against Rs. 46,196.17 lakhs non-current and Rs. 16,028.03 lakhs current borrowings, Rs. 2,01,956.25 lakhs of other non-current financial liabilities and Rs. 28,951.71 lakhs of deferred tax liability — and took out a business that had FY25 revenue of Rs. 36,650.21 lakhs and PAT of Rs. 4,468.06 lakhs, now shown as discontinued operations. Management's stated problems solved are focus and structure: Valor 'is now engaged solely in the real estate business, which constitutes its only reportable segment,' so segment reporting ceased, while Advent gets 'its own Board and Management team,' NSE/BSE listing on 13 November 2025 for 'enhanced market visibility, liquidity for existing shareholders, and a strengthened capital structure,' and an asset-heavy growth path (five projects, 3,100 keys, EBITDA from under Rs. 200 crore to over Rs. 1,200 crore by FY32, targeted mid-teens compounded ROE) that a combined entity would have had to fund alongside real estate. The second, smaller separation/consolidation strand is non-core cleanup: Sahyadri Agro and Dairy Private Limited (dairy farming, milk procurement and trading), taken to 76.63% via enforcement of security and then to 100% 'as the transaction relates to the liquidation of non-core assets,' sold its entire dairy business under a Business Transfer Agreement at a gain of Rs. 6,901.20 lakhs with Rs. 1,697.63 lakhs of non-compete fees booked as an exceptional item, is now 'evaluating opportunities to engage in the business of real estate development,' and was amalgamated into Horizontal Ventures Private Limited for structural simplification, synergies, avoidance of duplication and lower compliance and overhead costs. Running alongside is balance-sheet repair the filings tie to the same strategy: consolidated secured debt down to Rs. 730 crore, full redemption of Rs. 235 crore of NCDs out of the Rs. 262 crore Dahisar/Aradhya Park development-rights conveyance, and the Scheme-driven reduction and consolidation of the 8% RPS (Clause 32: Rs. 10 face value cut to Rs. 9, then 10 consolidated into 9) plus Clause 20's 1:10 allotment of AHIL preference shares, followed by the November 2025 proposal to convert KRPL's 6,45,75,000 RPS into 0.0001% CCPS converting into 32,02,330 equity shares at Rs. 201.65 'with a view to conserve the financial resources of the Company.' No filing names any investor, lender or partner as having demanded the separation; the only named partner is Prestige Group, which sits on Advent's side as a 50:50 JV partner in the Sahar project and co-developer at Aerocity.

**How it evolved:** There are no transcripts on file, so the idea cannot be traced call by call; the paper trail runs through filings and the Scheme itself. The Composite Scheme was sanctioned by NCLT Mumbai on 12 June 2025, became effective 1 July 2025 with demerger appointed date 1 April 2025, and the 1:10 entitlement was fixed on the 18 July 2025 record date; the SADPL-into-HVPL amalgamation was approved by both boards on 18 August 2025 with appointed date 1 April 2025. The plan then became visible in public filings in quick succession: Advent's listing press release (12 November 2025), Valor's Q2FY26 results and press release (14-15 November 2025) which first framed the demerger as completed and as the basis for debt reduction, the EGM notice and corrigendum (20 November and 8 December 2025) which disclosed the Scheme's preference-share reduction, consolidation and 1:10 AHIL allotment and layered the RPS-to-CCPS conversion on top, and finally the NCLT order of 29 January 2026 and effective date of 12 March 2026 completing the SADPL consolidation. The shape of the plan therefore widened over time from a single hospitality demerger into a package: demerger plus listing, plus non-core dairy liquidation and merger, plus capital-structure conversion.

**What management expects from it:** Valor: pure-play real estate, single reportable segment, leaner and more efficient capital structure, lower debt (secured debt ₹730 crore), greater financial flexibility, unlocked value. Advent: independent board and management, focused hospitality platform, better visibility, shareholder liquidity, stronger capital structure, 3,100 keys and EBITDA above ₹1,200 crore by FY32, mid-teens compounded ROE.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *Scheme* — The Composite Scheme's stated purpose, as put to shareholders in the EGM explanatory statement, was to demerge the hospitality business into Advent Hotels International Limited and unlock shareholder value; it simultaneously amalgamated Esteem Properties Private Limited into Valor. “mainly with aim to demerge hospitality business of the Company into Resulting Company and thus unlock overall value for the shareholders”
- *Scheme* — Post-demerger Valor is a pure-play real estate company with a single reportable segment, and prior-period hospitality results are reclassified as discontinued operations under Ind AS 105. “Consequent to the demerger, the Company is now engaged solely in the real estate business, which constitutes its only reportable segment.”
- *Scheme* — Management framed the separation as letting each business pursue its own growth path: Chairman Vinod Goenka tied Q2FY26 progress to completing the demerger and listing of hospitality. “We successfully completed the demerger and listing of our Hospitality business, an important milestone that enables each platform to pursue its independent growth path.”
- *Scheme* — The Q2FY26 press release states the problems the split solves on Valor's side: targeted independent strategies for each business, sharper operational focus, and unlocked long-term value. “This development enables each business to pursue a targeted, independent growth strategy, strengthens operational focus, and positions the Group to unlock enhanced long-term value for shareholders.”
- *Scheme* — Advent's 13 November 2025 NSE/BSE listing was justified on visibility, shareholder liquidity and capital structure, with Advent carved out of Valor and run by its own board and management. “The listing will mark a significant milestone in Advent's journey as a dedicated hospitality platform, enabling enhanced market visibility, liquidity for existing shareholders, and a strengthened capital structure to support future growth.”
- *Scheme* — Advent now has independent governance: two operating hotels (313-key Grand Hyatt Bambolim Goa plus 113 keys under development, and a 171-key Hilton in Andheri East, Mumbai). “The Company is governed by its own Board and Management team following the demerger.”
- *Scheme* — Advent quantified the growth the standalone platform is meant to fund: five projects under development including St. Regis and Marriott Marquis at Aerocity Delhi with Prestige Group (FY27), Waldorf Astoria and Hilton at Worli, and a 1,175-key BKC hotel. “With five projects under development, the company is on track to expand to 3,100 keys. EBITDA, currently under ₹200 crore, is projected to surpass ₹1,200 crore as these projects mature by FY32, reflecting the company's robust growth and institutional approach.”
- *Scheme* — Advent's MD & CEO Rahul Pandit cast the separation and listing as a governance and financing fix for an asset-heavy hospitality business; Promoter Director Arshad Balwa targeted mid-teens compounded ROE over the next decade. “This listing enhances our financial flexibility, strengthens governance, and enables sustainable value generation for all stakeholders.”
- *Scheme* — Vice Chairman & MD Shahid Balwa linked the demerger and non-core divestments to deleveraging — consolidated secured debt of ₹730 crore, full redemption of ₹235 crore of NCDs from the ₹262 crore Dahisar/Aradhya Park development-rights conveyance. “The rationalisation of our project portfolio, combined with selective monetisation initiatives, including the divestment of non-core assets, has enabled us to reduce debt levels, bringing us closer to our medium-term objective of a leaner and more efficient capital structure.”
- *Scheme* — Sahyadri Agro and Dairy was treated explicitly as a non-core asset being liquidated: the Group went to 76.63% through enforcement of security, then to 100%, and SADPL sold its dairy assets under a Business Transfer Agreement at a gain of Rs. 6,901.20 lakhs with Rs. 1,697.63 lakhs of non-compete fees as an exceptional item. “As the transaction relates to the liquidation of non-core assets, SADPL has not been consolidated.”
- *Scheme* — The NCLT order of 29 January 2026 records the benefits claimed for folding dairy-turned-real-estate SADPL into Horizontal Ventures Private Limited, a wholly-owned-subsidiary merger inside the group with appointed date 1 April 2025, effective 12 March 2026. “Simplification  and rationalisation  of corporate  struct ure through consolidation;”
- *Scheme* — The same order lists compliance and overhead reduction as the operating rationale for the SADPL-HVPL consolidation, with the petitioners undertaking not to claim Section 72A tax-loss benefits after the Income-tax Officer objected. “Reduction in multiplicity of legal and regulatory compliances,  reduction in overheads, including administrative, managerial and other administrative costs.”

*Not explained on the calls:* No call transcripts supplied; filings never name investors, lenders or partners who asked for it, nor give swap-ratio valuation basis, cost savings, or Advent fundraising plans.

## PRICOLLTD — Pricol Ltd.

**CONFIRMED** (a demerger scheme is on the exchange record) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 5.0/10 · spin-off · 9 filing(s) from NSE, NSE-deep · first 2026-06-27, latest 2026-11-13

> **Listing:** NOT YET — scheme at 'announced' stage; Pricol Autotech Limited will list only after NCLT sanction, effectiveness and a record date; no listing timeline stated

**Stated in the filings:** resulting company **Pricol Autotech Limited**; entitlement **1 for every 1**; appointed date 2026-06-27; size hint: 4.5% of revenue.

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** Driver Information & Connected Vehicle Solutions (DICVS) business — instrument clusters, telematics, sensors, e-cockpit — class `value_unlocking`.

- *Insiders:* Promoters (Mohan family) get 38.51% of Pricol Autotech, then sell their entire 38.51% to Warburg Pincus affiliate for up to INR 1,663.07 crores and exit control; they keep 38.51% of Pricol Limited.
- *What it reveals:* DICVS is the bigger, faster business — INR 2,424.63 crores, 61.17% of FY26 consolidated turnover — yet presented as a "4.5%" small share; Warburg Pincus pays INR 1,663.07 crores for 38.51%, implying ~INR 4,318 crores equity value, plus a 26% open offer.
- *Selling pressure:* likely — Promoters sell entire 38.51% stake; new listing, no index membership, different industry (automotive electronics vs precision engineering).
- *Parent or spin:* both · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* The Scheme of Arrangement on pricol.com/investors — DICVS asset, liability and debt allocation to Pricol Autotech.
- *In their words:* “The turnover of the DICVS Business for the financial year ending March 31, 2026, stood at INR 2,424.63 crores. This represents 61.17% of the total consolidated turnover of the Company for the financial year ending March 31, 2026.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

Management's case, as set out in the 27 June 2026 board filing, press note and demerger presentation, is that Pricol had become two structurally different companies inside one shell: the Driver Information & Connected Vehicle Solutions (DICVS) business — instrument clusters (mechanical, electro-mechanical, LCD/TFT), integrated infotainment, e-cockpit, telematics, battery management systems and some sensors — versus the Actuation, Control & Fluid Management Systems (ACFMS) business and the polymer/precision business held in wholly owned Pricol Precision Products (P3L). DICVS was the bigger half, at INR 2,424.63 crore of FY26 revenue, or 61.17% of consolidated turnover (the press release rounds it to ~INR 2,400 crore and ~60%), against FY26 consolidated revenue of INR 3,963.85 crore and total income of INR 40,523.70 million. The problem they said this solves is divergence: the two now operate with "differing customer needs, competitive dynamics, capital allocation and risk profiles" — DICVS innovation-led (display, electrification, connectivity, e-cockpit, ADAS, software-defined vehicles; risk = technology disruption and the semiconductor ecosystem; partners = display, chip-design and semiconductor firms; talent = embedded software, system architects, cyber-security and functional-safety experts) while ACFMS/P3L is scale-led (manufacturing excellence, cost competitiveness, lightweighting, exports; risk = automotive cyclicality and commodity costs; partners = Tier-2/3 suppliers). Capital deployment priorities were said to be incompatible in one entity: DICVS money goes to talent, software, global R&D centres, technology investments and overseas acquisitions, Pricol Limited's to manufacturing capacity, automation, productivity and domestic acquisitions. Other stated benefits: financial flexibility for each entity, reduced operational complexity and faster decision-making, independent and dedicated management teams, the ability to tailor processes, policies, systems and governance, improved visibility of each business's value and growth prospects, better ability to attract strategic and financial investors, and "appropriate valuation benchmarks for each business, free from conglomerate discount." Consideration is non-cash: 1 Pricol Autotech share of INR 1 for every 1 Pricol Limited share, so Autotech's register mirrors Pricol's (promoters 38.51%, public 61.49%), with listing sought on NSE and BSE; SSPA & Co. gave the share-entitlement report and Saffron Capital the fairness opinion. The 13 November 2026 filing revealed the commercial endpoint the June rationale did not mention: the promoters (Vijay, Vikram and Vanitha Mohan plus family and Pricol Holdings, Pricol Engineering Industries, Shrimay Enterprises and Pricol Logistics) will sell their entire 38.51% — 4,69,34,833 shares — of Pricol Autotech to Topaz Terrace Investments B.V., a Warburg Pincus affiliate, for up to INR 1,663.07 crore, followed by a mandatory open offer for up to a further 26%, after which Warburg controls Autotech and the family keeps ACFMS and polymer with no change in shareholding; no investor, lender or customer is named as having asked for any of this, and the only disclosed initiators are the board and the promoters, who used Veda Corporate Advisors as exclusive financial advisor.

**How it evolved:** The idea is entirely absent from the eleven earnings calls (Nov 2023 through the 15 May 2026 Q4 FY26 call), where management instead talked up a single integrated group — a FY31 INR 8,000 crore target, INR 680–700 crore of FY27 group capex across DICVS, ACFMS and polymer, and converting polymer "from a component maker to a value-added polymer player." The nearest hint is the 30 January 2026 (Feb 2026) call, where Siddharth Manoharan confirmed a newly incorporated subsidiary but attributed it to technology-partnership flexibility and the BOE MOU, saying the plan would be discussed "later"; Pricol Autotech Limited was in fact incorporated on 21 February 2026. The board then approved the scheme on 27 June 2026 — six weeks after a call that never raised it — and the purpose sharpened on 13 November 2026, when the promoters' entire 38.51% of the demerged entity was agreed for sale to Warburg Pincus for up to INR 1,663.07 crore plus a 26% open offer, converting a stated "focus and agility" restructuring into a control exit from the group's largest business.

**What management expects from it:** Pricol Autotech: a focused automotive-electronics platform — innovation-led growth, higher content per vehicle, global R&D, IP-led acquisitions, Warburg's capital and sector network. Pricol Limited: scale-led precision engineering — ACFMS exports, disc brakes, a polymer centre of excellence, domestic acquisitions. Both: dedicated management, tailored capital allocation, faster decisions, separate valuation benchmarks free of conglomerate discount, easier access to strategic and financial investors.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *Scheme* — The 27 June 2026 board filing frames the DICVS demerger as creating a simpler, faster entity matched to fast-changing technology, because the two halves already ran on different customer, competitive, capital and risk logic. “The demerger of the DICVS Business is a strategic decision to create a simpler, sharper and more agile corporate entity, to meet the fast changing needs and technologies related to this business and its dynamic market realities.”
- *Scheme* — The demerged undertaking is the majority of the company: DICVS turnover of INR 2,424.63 crore in FY26, 61.17% of consolidated turnover (press note: ~INR 2,400 crore, ~60%), against consolidated FY26 revenue from operations of INR 3,963.85 crore. “The turnover of the DICVS Business for the financial year ending March 31, 2026, stood at INR 2,424.63 crores. This represents 61.17% of the total consolidated turnover of the Company for the financial year ending March 31, 2026.”
- *Scheme* — Consideration is a mirror 1:1 share entitlement with no cash, so Pricol Autotech starts with promoters at 38.51% and public at 61.49%, and is to be listed on NSE and BSE; Pricol Limited receives nothing and retains no shares. “1 (One) fully paid-up equity share of the Resulting Company having face value of INR 1 (Rupee One only) each for every 1 (One) fully paid-up equity share of INR 1 (Rupee One only) each of the Company.”
- *Scheme* — The presentation makes valuation an explicit objective — separate frameworks for two structurally different businesses, removing the holding-company drag of one blended multiple. “Clear market recognition and appropriate valuation benchmarks for each business, free from conglomerate discount”
- *Scheme* — The side-by-side table splits the two on capital deployment (software, global R&D centres and overseas acquisitions for Autotech versus capacity, automation and domestic acquisitions for Pricol), talent, partners and risk (technology disruption versus automotive cyclicality and commodity costs). “Talent, product development, software, global R&D centres, tech investments & overseas acquisitions”
- *Scheme* — The 13 November 2026 share purchase agreement discloses the endpoint: Warburg Pincus affiliate Topaz Terrace Investments B.V. buys the promoters' entire 4,69,34,833 shares (38.51%) of Pricol Autotech for up to INR 1,663.07 crore, plus a mandatory open offer for up to 26% more. “For completeness, the aggregate consideration payable for the sale by the Sellers of their entire stake of Pricol Autotech of 38.51% (to be issued to the Sellers pursuant to the Scheme) is up to INR 1,663.07 Crores (Indian Rupees One Thousand Six Hundred and Sixty Three Crores and Seven Lakhs) subject to the terms of the Share Purchase Agreement.”
- *Scheme* — Control of the demerged business passes to Warburg and the Mohan family seeks reclassification out of Autotech's promoter group, while the agreement imposes non-compete obligations on the sellers and on Pricol Limited itself; ACFMS and polymer stay with the family with no shareholding change. “Amongst other things, the Share Purchase Agreement contains customary stand still provisions, warranties and indemnities being provided by the Sellers, subject to customary limitations and caps, and certain non-compete obligations on the Sellers and the Company for a specified period.”
- *Scheme* — Vikram Mohan ties the separation rationale directly to handing the business to Warburg, describing DICVS as having been "at the heart" of Pricol's five-decade journey and Warburg as its next owner-custodian. “The proposed demerger will give Pricol Autotech the focus and independence to realise its full potential.”
- *CALL Feb 2026* — Asked on the 30 January 2026 call why a new subsidiary had been incorporated, Siddharth Manoharan attributed it to technology-partnership flexibility and the BOE MOU, not to any restructuring; Pricol Autotech Limited was incorporated on 21 February 2026. “But whenever the plan materializes, we will talk about that in detail later.”
- *CALL Nov 2025* — Management's own segment guidance showed the margin and growth divergence later used as rationale — DICVS at INR 2,100–2,200 crore and 12.5–13% EBITDA, ACFMS at INR 600 crore growing 30–35%, polymer at INR 850–900 crore on 9.5% — though no separation was suggested. “This year, the plastics, the Polymer business will be about INR 850 crores to INR 900 crores with a steady-state margin of 9.5%.”
- *CALL Feb 2025* — A year earlier Vikram Mohan had conceded that consolidating the lower-margin plastics business pulled the group's blended EBITDA down even as rupee profit rose — the conglomerate-mix problem the 2026 presentation addresses via separate valuation frameworks. “Overall margin of Pricol will be maintained, but when Sundaram consolidates, it is going to come down lower because plastics is a single digit margin and not a double digit EBITDA product.”
- *CALL May 2026* — Six weeks before the board approved the scheme, the Q4 FY26 call described a unified group starting a fresh INR 680–700 crore capex cycle across all three divisions, with no hint of a demerger; Ganesh put DICVS at ~60%, ACFMS ~20% and P3L ~20% of revenue. “In fact, this year, in itself, we have planned for about between INR 680 crore to INR 700 crores of CAPEX to cater to all of our new businesses that we have won, new plants, new machines, so on and so forth, which will keep propelling us forward and to maintain this growth momentum.”

*Not explained on the calls:* No call ever mentioned it. Filings omit stranded corporate costs, debt/asset and employee/IP allocation, tax, the INR 1,663.07 crore valuation basis, and why promoters exited DICVS.

- *In their words:* “The Company has received a letter dated August 6, 2026, from the RBI, conveying that the application has been examined and that the request has not been acceded to.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

Religare is demerging its entire financial services business — SME/MSME lending (Religare Finvest), retail broking plus e-governance (Religare Broking and its subsidiary Religare Digital Solutions), affordable housing finance (Religare Housing Development Finance, already an RFL subsidiary), and the related investment and ancillary/support activities — out of the listed holdco REL into RFL, which will itself be listed, leaving REL as a pure-play holder of its 63.2% stake in Care Health Insurance; REL shareholders get 1 RFL share for every REL share, and RFL's pre-scheme capital held by REL is cancelled so RFL's shareholding mirrors REL's. Management framed it as three converging conditions rather than a reaction to distress: the Burman Group's completed takeover as promoters (open offer concluded Feb 2025, board reconstituted July 2025, promoters at 29.75% fully diluted in Feb 2026 and ~30.3% by May 2026 after ~4% of open-market buying, heading to ~34% on warrant conversion), the INR1,500 crore preferential warrant raise subscribed 50:50 by the Burmans and marquee investors (earmarked INR600 crore to Care, INR250 crore to housing finance, INR200 crore to broking, INR75 crore to repay REL's own debt and INR375 crore general corporate purpose), and the fact that the businesses had reached an inflection point where "each business also operates with different capital requirements, risk frameworks, manpower talent and growth trajectories." The stated problems it solves are a conglomerate structure in which insurance (FY26 GWP INR11,417 crore, PBT INR539 crore on 'n' basis, 19.7% retail SAHI share) drowns out a tiny financial services segment (FY25 demerged-undertaking turnover of only INR457.29 crore, 6.2% of consolidated revenue), investors who cannot value the two halves, and management bandwidth: the scheme's four pillars are streamlined focus/simplified structure, value unlocking plus targeted capital raising through a separate RFL listing, dedicated leadership with sector-specific talent and performance-linked rewards, and risk/compliance frameworks tailored to each segment. The financial services side is being restarted from a cleaned-up base — RFL is debt-free with all legacy promoter-era diversion issues provided or written off (including the full INR750 crore Lakshmi Vilas Bank FD), RBI's Corrective Action Plan lifted in July 2025 and bank fraud tags removed, leaving ~INR591 crore cash, ~INR900 crore net worth, 261% CRAR, NOF of INR821 crore and only a ~INR60 crore core SME book — so Arjun Lamba tied the demerger directly to scaling: "Our intent is to scale all of these business to make them meaningful and sizable and part of this demerger is on account of this." Who asked for it: shareholders and analysts had been pressing since the first call back in Nov 2025 (Vikas Shrivastav on demerging Care and removing the holdco discount, Dixit Doshi on IPO vs demerger of Care), and after the announcement nearly every questioner — Umang Shah, Adarsh, Hitaindra Pradhan, Ravi Purohit, Niharika Karnani, Sarvesh Gupta — argued the value sits in Care and demanded a reverse merger giving direct Care shares, citing the Max Financial precedent. Management conceded the point but said IRDAI's 25–26% promoter requirement cannot be met while the Burmans' look-through stake in Care is only ~18–19%, so this was "the first step in that direction," done after evaluating structural alternatives with leading advisors; Lamba refused to amend the scheme and would not commit to a timeline for a second one. Execution has since run into the regulator: exchanges gave no-objection/no-adverse-observation letters on 7 July 2026, but on 6–7 August 2026 RBI informed REL and RFL that their application for no-objection/prior approval "has not been acceded to," and the companies said they would engage further with the regulator.

**How it evolved:** On the Nov 2025 call (Q2/H1 FY26, the first investor call after the Burman takeover) there was no plan — Vikas Shrivastav asked directly what the structure would look like in two years and whether Care would be demerged from the holdco, and CFO Pratul Gupta would only say the board was evaluating options and wanted to make the businesses "larger, better, stronger" before any capital-market action, while Dixit Doshi asked whether Care would be IPO'd or demerged. A Moneycontrol report on 3 Feb 2026 that REL would demerge and list Care drew an exchange query, which REL denied as a disclosable event; eleven days later, on 14 Feb 2026, the REL and RFL boards approved the scheme — and the Feb 2026 call (16 Feb) was where Gupta laid out the full rationale, the four pillars, the 1:1 ratio, the 15–18 month timetable and a Q1 FY28 RFL listing, while every analyst pushed back that Care, not financial services, should have been separated. By the May 2026 call (13 May, Q4/FY26) the framing had shifted from Gupta's structural logic to Executive Director Arjun Lamba's: separating FS from insurance was "number one," the promoters had bought ~4% more stock toward the IRDAI threshold, and he declined to amend the scheme while leaving a later reverse merger of Care open "at an appropriate stage." The 7 July 2026 exchange observation letters cleared the way, but the 7 Aug 2026 filings disclosed RBI had refused to accede to the application, leaving the scheme stalled pending further engagement.

**What management expects from it:** REL becomes a pure-play health insurance holdco around Care (GWP INR11,417 crore, PBT INR539 crore 'n' basis, combined ratio heading from 101.4% to ~100% in two years on operating leverage, 18–24% growth). RFL becomes an integrated, separately listed financial services platform — debt-free, ~INR900 crore net worth, ~INR591 crore cash, 261% CRAR — able to leverage to industry norms, raise targeted capital, hire sector-specific leadership on performance-linked rewards, run tailored risk frameworks, and unlock value via mirror 1:1 listing.

The investment in CARE shall continue to be retained in REL.”
- *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=b273d588-fe12-446c-bee6-b5d6269b6a44.pdf)* — A separate RFL listing is meant to unlock value, widen investor participation and let that business raise its own capital — the second of four stated pillars. “The independent listing of RFL is expected to unlock shareholder value and enhance investor participation.”
- *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=b273d588-fe12-446c-bee6-b5d6269b6a44.pdf)* — Analysts attacked the design immediately: Umang Shah argued demerging Care directly would have removed the holdco discount on the asset that carries most of the value. “I'm a bit puzzled why we chose to demerge financial services and not CARE directly?”

- *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=b273d588-fe12-446c-bee6-b5d6269b6a44.pdf)* — The binding constraint on a Care reverse merger is the IRDAI promoter-shareholding rule against a Burman look-through stake in Care of only ~18–19%, which Gupta confirmed when Vikas Srivastava spelled out the law. “So you are right in terms of the fact that the look - through shareholding of the promoter group today in CARE is at around 18% to 19%.”
- *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=b273d588-fe12-446c-bee6-b5d6269b6a44.pdf)* — Management said the structure was chosen after a full review of alternatives with external advisors, and promised no operational, customer or employee disruption during implementation. “This has resulted after comprehensive evalu ation of various structural alternatives which were discussed with leading advisors.”
- *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=87938b4d-578d-40b0-89a8-7803462a6057.pdf)* — Arjun Lamba restated the core purpose as separating financial services from insurance to give shareholders a clean, understandable structure and management a single focus, while acknowledging the holdco-discount complaint. “And for us, number one has been to separate the FS business from the insurance business and to provide a clean structure so that the shareholders can understand, th e management can be very focused in doing what they have to do.”
- *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=87938b4d-578d-40b0-89a8-7803462a6057.pdf)* — Lamba linked the demerger to the capital allocation plan — INR600 crore to Care, INR250 crore to housing finance, INR200 crore to broking, ~INR375 crore general corporate purpose, with RFL needing none given ~INR900–1,000 crore net worth and ~INR600 crore cash. “Our intent is to scale all of these business to make them meaningful and sizable and part of this demerger is on account of this.”

*Not explained on the calls:* No cost-benefit or synergy quantification, no RFL valuation or AUM/ROE targets, no holdco-discount fix or Care reverse-merger timeline, no stated path to IRDAI's 26%, and no RBI-rejection reasoning.

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

The separation is the demerger of the Industrial undertaking of SKF India Limited (automotive remaining with SKF India Ltd.) into SKF India (Industrial) Limited, a company incorporated 17 December 2024 purely to receive it, sanctioned by NCLT Mumbai on 26 September 2025 with appointed/effective date 1 October 2025, a 1:1 share exchange (49,437,963 shares to SKF India holders on the 15 October 2025 record date) and listing on BSE/NSE from 5 December 2025. Management's stated reason is sector focus: the Q3 FY25-26 release frames it as 'SKF's demerger into two sector-focused, strategically independent organizations, enabling sharper market orientation, faster decision-making, and enhanced long-term value creation for shareholders,' a 'pivotal step in SKF's 102-year India journey,' with the industrial entity 'more agile and focused,' able to 'respond faster to market needs' and 'tailor it's manufacturing capabilities' for manufacturing, railways, renewables, cement and heavy engineering. On the 13 May 2026 call the operating logic is spelled out as the ACES strategy to 2028 (accelerate localization, commercial excellence, disciplined execution, one SKF) plus the point that industrial economics differ structurally from automotive — 'industrial business is all about flexibility in the channels... because the lot size, unlike automotive, is smaller' — and that localization lets it re-enter segments it had exited (wind, freight railways, agricultural tractors). Dedicated capacity is the second half of the logic: the Board approved a new Pune factory on 3 February 2026, part of INR 800 crore+ capex to FY29-30 (including INR 350-400 crore of DGBB/TRB channel additions), commissioning end-CY2028, because the business is 'running out of capacity' and currently relies on SKF India job work. The cost of separating was explicit: INR 1,800.8 million of exceptional demerger charges in Q3 FY26 (IT, professional fees, large stamp duty/transfer premium on the land transferred from SKF India), INR 1,961 million for nine months, and a further INR 183 million of demerger IT cost in Q4, which turned reported Q3 PBT to negative INR 671.4 million against INR 1,129.4 million before exceptionals. Management's payoff case is margin recovery to ~13% once demerger costs lapse by end-CY2026, ~15% by FY29-30 and an aspiration of 16-18%, on 8%+ growth; interim performance cited was Q4 FY26 sales INR 9,457.2 million (+9.8% QoQ, +31% YoY), PBT 9.5% reported and 11.5% ex-one-offs, net working capital down 2.8% to 18.7% of sales, then Q1 FY27 revenue INR 9,707.7 million (+18.3% YoY) at 9.0% PBT.

**How it evolved:** These texts contain no pre-demerger call, so the origin of the idea is not on record here; the earliest document is the Scheme itself (NCLT order 26 September 2025, effective 1 October 2025, listing 5 December 2025). The 4 February 2026 press release, reporting the first post-demerger quarter, carries the only explicit rationale statement (two sector-focused independent organizations, sharper orientation, faster decisions, shareholder value) alongside INR 1,800.8 million of separation costs, and the same Board meeting on 3 February 2026 approved the new Pune factory — converting the rationale into standalone capacity. By the 13 May 2026 Q4/FY26 call the framing had shifted from justification to execution: the ACES strategy 'as we are now a separate listed entity,' INR 800 crore+ capex, re-entry into previously exited wind/railway/tractor business, and a margin path of 13% near term to 15% by FY29-30. The 12 August 2026 Q1 FY27 release continues the 'focused, independent business' framing with 18.3% YoY growth at 9% PBT.

**What management expects from it:** For SKF India (Industrial): sharper market orientation, faster decisions, agility and manufacturing tailored to industrial lot sizes; ~8% growth with PBT recovering to ~13% by end-CY2026, ~15% by FY29-30 (16-18% aspiration); net working capital 19-20% of sales; INR 800 crore+ own capex and a new Pune plant replacing SKF India job work; shareholder value via two independent listed entities.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *Scheme* — The Scheme of Arrangement between SKF India Limited (Demerged Company) and SKF India (Industrial) Limited (Resulting Company) transferred the Industrial Undertaking on a going-concern basis at carrying values, with the difference credited to Capital Reserve; NCLT order dated 26 September 2025, appointed and effective date 1 October 2025. “The Scheme, among other provisions, entails the demerger of the Demerged Undertaking from the Demerged Company into the Resulting Company on a going concern basis.”
- *Scheme* — The only explicit statement of purpose in the filings: two sector-focused, independent organizations for sharper market orientation, faster decision-making and shareholder value, after 102 years of SKF in India. “The results come against the backdrop of SKF's demerger into two sector-focused, strategically independent organizations, enabling sharper market orientation, faster decision-making, and enhanced long-term value creation for shareholders, marking a pivotal step in SKF's 102-year India journey.”
- *Scheme* — MD Mukund Vasudevan's rationale in the 4 February 2026 Q3 FY25-26 release: agility, speed of response and manufacturing tailored to industrial customers, serving manufacturing, railways, renewables, cement and heavy engineering. “As a more agile and focused industrial entity, SKF India (Industrial) is well-positioned to respond faster to market needs, tailor it's manufacturing capabilities, and support India's accelerating infrastructure and manufacturing build-out.”
- *Scheme* — Separation cost quantified as exceptional items: INR 1,800.8 million in Q3 FY26 and INR 1,961 million for nine months for IT cost, professional services and stamp duty including transfer premium on land acquired under the Scheme — which pushed reported Q3 PBT to negative INR 671.4 million versus INR 1,129.4 million before exceptionals. “During the quarter and nine months ended 31 December 2025, the Company accounted certain demerger expenses for IT Cost, professional services and stamp duty, including estimated transfer premium payable to statutory authorities to effect transfer of registration of land acquired under the Scheme, aggregating to Rs. 1,800.8 million and Rs. 1,961 million, respectively, which have been included under "Exceptional items".”

**The stages, as filed:** nclt_sanction (2026-05-20) → effective (2026-06-01) → record_date (2024-12-06)

**Stated in the filings:** demerged undertaking: of Arco Lab Private Limited, a wholly owned subsidiary of Strides Pharma Science Limited; record date 2024-12-06; size hint: 20% of ebitda.

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** Arco Lab's Life Sciences and Digital Innovation businesses, carved out into Pivot Path Private Limited — class `value_unlocking`.

- *Insiders:* Pivot Path capital structure: Strides 19.95%, Investors 65.05%, ESOP Pool 15%. Buyers (Ascent Growth Trust, Vintage Classic) do not belong to promoter/promoter group. Promoter stake not stated.
- *What it reveals:* A profitable services platform hidden inside the GCC: FY26 revenue ₹1,447m, EBITDA ₹169m, only 3% of Strides turnover and 1% of networth, yet valued ~₹2,300m post-money, realising ~₹1,000m cash.
- *Selling pressure:* unlikely — Pivot Path shares allotted to Strides, not to its shareholders; no separate listing — majority stake sold privately to Ascent Capital consortium.
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* Definitive agreements and Q1FY27 results: gain on ~₹1,000m sale, ₹250m deferred receivable, Associate reclassification
- *In their words:* “Upon completion of the transaction, Pivot Path shall be reclassified as an Associate Company.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

The business being separated is not a pharma business at all: it is the Life Sciences business and Digital Innovation business that grew up inside Arco Lab Private Limited, Strides' wholly-owned Global Capability Centre, covering life-sciences consulting, digital transformation, quality and compliance, drug safety and technology-enabled operational services delivered by 400+ subject-matter experts. Management's account is that this began as a captive serving Strides — its FY26 revenue of ₹1,447 million explicitly 'including revenues for services rendered to Strides', with EBITDA of ₹169 million, 3% of Strides' turnover and ~1% of consolidated net worth — but that 'as demand from external pharmaceutical and life sciences companies grew, the business evolved into an independent platform serving industry-leading customers', which it could not remain inside a generics manufacturer's subsidiary. The filings name four specific problems the carve-out solves: supporting the next phase of growth, serving global customers effectively, building agentic-AI platforms, and enabling access to external capital — so the vehicle was created first (Scheme of Arrangement under Sections 230–232, appointed date April 10, 2025, NCLT Bengaluru approval May 18, 2026, effective June 1, 2026, making Pivot Path a direct wholly-owned subsidiary of Strides) and only then sold down. The sale values Pivot Path at ~₹2,300m post-money: Strides divests a majority for ~₹1,000m (₹750m at initial closing, ₹250m on the first anniversary), Ascent Growth Trust and co-investor Vintage Classic Limited take 65.05%, a 15% ESOP pool is carved for the team, Ascent infuses ₹500m of primary capital, Strides keeps 19.95% and reclassifies Pivot Path as an Associate. Strides frames this as a repeatable playbook rather than a distress exit — 'creating, scaling and unlocking value from high-potential businesses while retaining participation in their future growth' — and says it 'strengthens the Company's balance sheet and provides growth capital for Pivot Path', consistent with the three FY26 priorities Badree repeated on the calls (geographic diversification, profitability, balance sheet strength, with net debt at ₹1,437 crores and net debt/EBITDA 1.55x). The stated precedent is the Softgel/OneSource demerger, which Arun Kumar justified in exactly valuation terms — the softgel business was 'adjusting within the generic space at a suboptimal valuation' until its 'true value' was discovered through OneSource, with ₹78.8 billion distributed to shareholders. No investor, lender or partner is named as having asked for the Pivot Path separation; pricing rests on an independent valuation by a SEBI-registered merchant banker, and the deal is stated not to be a related-party transaction.

**How it evolved:** On none of the eight calls (Oct 2024 through May 2026) did management ever mention Pivot Path, Arco Lab's Life Sciences/Digital Innovation business or this Scheme; the only separation discussed was the Softgel-to-OneSource demerger (Oct 2024, Feb 2025, Aug 2025 calls), which established the 'unlock true value outside the generic space' template, and Arco Lab appeared only once, in May 2025, as the wholly-owned subsidiary parked with the retained 1.6% OneSource stake 'for a rainy day'. The Pivot Path track runs entirely through filings: the Scheme was intimated on May 15, 2025 with an appointed date of April 10, 2025, NCLT Bengaluru approved it on May 18, 2026 (the very day of the Q4 FY26 earnings call, which made no reference to it), the order reached the portal May 20 and the certified copy May 25, and the Scheme became effective June 1, 2026. Twenty-six days later, on June 27, 2026, the Board approved the majority-stake sale to the Ascent Capital consortium plus ₹500m primary infusion, with definitive agreements to be executed before June 30 and the share sale to complete by June 30, 2026 and the infusion by July 31, 2026. So the plan visibly changed shape only once: from an internal reorganisation creating a wholly-owned subsidiary into a control sale leaving Strides a 19.95% associate holder.

**What management expects from it:** Pivot Path: ₹500m primary capital, independence to serve global customers, build agentic-AI platforms, scale with a 15% ESOP pool for 400+ experts, and access external capital. Strides: ~₹1,000m cash (₹750m now, ₹250m deferred), a strengthened balance sheet, Associate accounting, continued ~19.95% participation in the upside, and sharper focus on its pharma core.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *Scheme* — The separated unit is Arco Lab's Life Sciences business and Digital Innovation business, demerged into Pivot Path Private Limited under Sections 230–232 of the Companies Act, 2013; on effectiveness Pivot Path became a direct wholly-owned subsidiary of Strides, with the undertaking vesting from the appointed date of April 10, 2025. “The Scheme provides for the demerger of Arco Lab’s Life Sciences business and Digital Innovation business (the “Demerged Undertaking”) into Pivot Path, pursuant to Sections 230–232 of the Companies Act, 2013 and other applicable provisions of the Act and the Rules framed thereunder (“Scheme”).”
- *Scheme* — The stated reason for the carve-out is four-fold and explicit: next-phase growth, serving global customers, building agentic-AI platforms, and access to external capital — i.e. things the business could not do while embedded in Strides' Global Capability Centre. “To support its next phase of growth, serve global customers effectively, build agentic-AI platforms, and enable access to external capital, the business was carved out into Pivot Path pursuant to a Scheme of Arrangement approved by the Hon'ble National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) in May 2026.”
- *Scheme* — The origin story management gives: a captive capability centre function (life sciences consulting, digital transformation, quality and compliance, technology-enabled operational services) that outgrew its captive role as third-party pharma demand arrived. “As demand from external pharmaceutical and life sciences companies grew, the business evolved into an independent platform serving industry-leading customers.”
- *Scheme* — Size and profitability disclosed for the carved-out business for FY26 — and the admission that its revenue still includes intra-group work for Strides, which is why standalone turnover contribution is shown as Nil and consolidated contribution as only 3% of Strides' turnover and 1% of net worth. “For FY26, the carved-out business reported revenue of ₹1,447 million (including revenues for services rendered to Strides) and EBITDA of ₹169 million, demonstrating its operating scale and growth trajectory.”
- *Scheme* — The deal terms: ~₹2,300m post-money valuation, ~₹1,000m to Strides (₹750m at initial closing, ₹250m on the first anniversary), ₹500m primary into the company, and a resultant cap table of Strides 19.95% / investors 65.05% / ESOP pool 15%, with Pivot Path becoming an Associate. “The transaction values Pivot Path at ~₹2,300m on a post-money basis, enables Strides to realise ~₹1,000m while retaining a ~20% stake, and includes a primary capital infusion of ₹500 million to accelerate Pivot Path's next phase of growth.”
- *Scheme* — The corporate-strategy framing: a repeatable incubate-scale-monetise model in which Strides keeps a minority economic interest, with balance-sheet strengthening named as a direct benefit to the parent. “The transaction reflects Strides' strategy of creating, scaling and unlocking value from high-potential businesses while retaining participation in their future growth.”
- *Scheme* — Badree's stated timing logic: the business needs a partner with capital and expertise that Strides itself does not bring, and the separation is what lets Pivot Path scale independently while Strides still participates. “As the business enters its next phase, we believe this is the right time to bring in a strategic investment partner with the expertise and capital to accelerate its growth.”
- *Scheme* — The buyer's rationale is that independence itself is the enabler — combining technology and agentic AI with 400+ subject-matter experts for compliance, digital transformation and drug safety work for global customers. “As an Independent entity, Pivot Path is exceptionally well positioned to combine the power of technology and Agentic-AI with its 400+ subject matter experts in building purpose-built solutions that enable global customers to manage their compliance, digital transformation, and drug safety requirements with greater speed, precision, cost effectiveness and confidence.”
- *Scheme* — Governance framing: pricing rests on an independent SEBI-registered merchant banker valuation, the buyers (Ascent Growth Trust and BVI-incorporated Vintage Classic Limited) are not promoter/promoter-group/group companies, and the transaction is declared not a related-party transaction and outside Regulation 37A. “The transaction has been undertaken based on an independent valuation conducted by a SEBI-registered merchant banker, reflecting the strength of Pivot Path's differentiated capabilities, established customer relationships and long-term growth potential.”
- *[Feb 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=eb0f8605-df29-4b18-89a6-1981d2e97582.pdf)* — The template for this separation — never applied to Pivot Path on any call, but stated for the Softgel/OneSource demerger: a niche business trapped inside the generics platform was being valued suboptimally, so carving it out revealed its true value. “And discussing its true value, while it was adjusting within the generic space at a suboptimal valuation, we discovered its true value of a niche business through OneSource.”
- *[Aug 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=18a7ad25-fba0-4c37-a54f-e50372724d01.pdf)* — Management quantifies the prior unlock as the proof of its shareholder-value method — ₹78.8 billion distributed via demerger and listing — framing further separations as shareholder-value actions rather than disposals. “And the recent one being we distributed INR 78.8 billion back to shareholders in the form of demerger and listing.”
- *[May 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=16b39100-202b-45a3-89a5-d7161626f0d6.pdf)* — The only call reference to Arco Lab, the entity Pivot Path was carved out of: it is described merely as the wholly-owned subsidiary holding the retained OneSource stake, with no hint that a services business inside it was being prepared for separation. “So we retained this in Arco Lab, which is a wholly owned subsidiary of Strides.”

*Not explained on the calls:* Calls never mentioned Pivot Path, Arco Lab's carve-out or the Scheme; no stated investor, lender or partner request; no margin, valuation-gap or post-deal related-party pricing explanation.

## TMCV — Tata Motors Ltd.

**CONFIRMED** (this company IS the resulting company of a demerger, listed on 2025-11-12 — the spun entity in its second year) · **LISTED 1–2Y — the second-year window** · score 5.0/10 · spin-off · 29 filing(s) from NSE, NSE-deep · first 2025-12-01, latest 2026-11-07

> **Listing:** THIS COMPANY IS THE SPIN-OFF — the resulting company of the parent's demerger, listed on 2025-11-12 (373 days ago)

**The stages, as filed:** listed (2025-11-12)

**Stated in the filings:** demerged undertaking: ) to the Company on a going; appointed date 2025-07-01.

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** Tata Motors' commercial vehicle business (trucks, buses, pick-ups, vans), demerged into TML Commercial Vehicles Limited, now renamed Tata Motors Limited — class `not stated`.

- *Insiders:* Promoter stake not stated. Under the Tata Motors Limited Share-based Long Term Incentive Scheme (Board-approved March 11, 2026), participants' outstanding Demerged Company PSUs convert into up to 23,07,647 new-company PSUs at Rs. 2, 0.062% dilution.
- *What it reveals:* A high-quality pure-play CV business: FY26 revenue ~Rs. 77,000 crores, EBITDA margin 13.2% (vs 7.8% in FY23), first double-digit EBIT at 11%, FCF Rs. 9,200 crores (12% of revenue), Auto ROCE 72%, net cash Rs. 7,500 crores standalone.
- *Selling pressure:* unclear — Documents state only that shares listed on BSE and NSE effective 12 November 2025; no index, float or shareholder-disposition detail given.
- *Parent or spin:* spin · *option pricing date:* March 11, 2026 (Board approved TML SLTI Scheme; Exercise Price Rs. 2 per PSU, face value)
- *Read next:* Q1 FY27 results: commodity pass-through after the April 2% price increase, and the Iveco bridge-loan refinancing equity/debt mix.
- *In their words:* “Demerger being effective from 1st of October 2025, Tata Motors is now a pure play commercial vehicle company, and this is a defining shift that changes how we think is most appropriate to present our financials.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

Management presents the separation as a Composite Scheme of Arrangement under Sections 230–232, sanctioned by the NCLT Mumbai Bench amongst Tata Motors Limited (the demerged company, now Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Limited), TML Commercial Vehicles Limited (the resulting company) and Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Limited (amalgamated into the demerged entity), effective 1 October 2025; the resulting company was renamed Tata Motors Limited on 29 October 2025 and its shares listed on BSE/NSE (ticker TMCV) on 12 November 2025, with outstanding PSUs replaced one-for-one under a new scheme covering up to 23,07,647 shares (0.062% dilution). The stated problem the split solves is a reporting and identity one: 'Historically, we reported a CV segment. It was an internal construct that carved out CV operations from within the erstwhile combined entity. That was a practical necessity then' — from Q4 FY26 the company reports standalone financials including the Tata Cummins joint operation as its primary lens, giving 'a cleaner, more complete, and more directly comparable picture'. The separation cost ₹960 crore of one-time demerger expense booked in Q3 FY26 (part of ₹1,500 crore standalone / ₹1,600 crore consolidated exceptionals, alongside ₹603 crore of new labour code and ₹82 crore of Iveco acquisition cost). The pure-play case is argued with numbers: FY26 revenue ₹77,000 crore (vs ₹66,000 crore FY23), EBITDA margin up from 7.8% (FY23) to 13.2% (FY26) — ~550bps of 'structural improvement' — EBITDA doubled from ₹5,100 crore to ₹10,200 crore, PBT before exceptionals ₹8,700 crore, first-ever double-digit EBIT at 11% (the CV segment first crossed it at 10.6% in Q3 FY26), FCF ₹9,200 crore or 12% of revenue, Auto ROCE 72%, cash conversion cycle of negative 31 days, net cash ₹7,500 crore standalone and ₹13,700 crore consolidated, and a maiden final dividend of ₹4/share (~₹1,500 crore outflow). Cyclicality is the second problem: non-cyclical revenue (parts & service, Fleet Edge digital subscriptions, Smart City e-bus operations) is compounding at 2.7x the cyclical CAGR, 'deliberately building this mix', and Q4 working-capital sinks historically concentrated in Q4 have been spread through the year. Third, the standalone CV entity became the acquisition vehicle: its own balance sheet and a committed EUR 3.825 billion bridge from Morgan Stanley and MUFG funded an all-cash voluntary totalitarian tender offer for Iveco Group N.V. at EUR 14.10 (raised to EUR 14.40), valuing Iveco at ~EUR 3.82 billion, creating ~EUR 21 billion (INR 2,28,000 crore+) of combined revenue and ~590k units with Europe ~46%/India ~32%/South America ~8%/RoW ~14% and 'substantially no overlap' — expected to 'drive better operating leverage by spreading its capital investments over larger volumes, generating operating efficiencies and reducing the cash flow volatility inherent in the commercial vehicles sector', plus enhancing Iveco's FPT powertrain business. Structural simplification continues inside the CV entity: TMF Holdings Limited and TMF Business Services Limited (wholly owned subsidiaries) are being amalgamated into it, and Tata Motor Finance had already been folded into Tata Capital (whose October 2025 IPO priced 20–25% below the merger valuation, forcing a ₹2,000 crore mark-to-market loss in Q2 FY26 and a ₹295 crore write-back in Q3).

**How it evolved:** In the Nov 2025 call (Q2 FY26, 13 November 2025) management reported the split as done rather than argued for it — demerger effective 1 October, CV listing completed as TMCV 'as committed previously', Iveco approvals underway and the bridge loan secured. In the Feb 2026 call (Q3 FY26, 29 January 2026) the cost showed up as a ₹960 crore one-time demerger exceptional while the CV segment hit a double-digit EBIT margin (10.6%) for the first time and Iveco approvals were guided to end-March. In the May 2026 call (Q4 FY26, 13 May 2026) the framing shifted decisively: 'Tata Motors is now a pure play commercial vehicle company... a defining shift', the old carved-out CV segment was retired in favour of standalone reporting, three-year pure-play metrics were laid out, and Iveco closure slipped to Q2 FY27 pending French and Spanish financial-regulator approvals. Filings then show execution: offer launched 4 September 2026, 89.42% tendered by 27 October 2026, 96.29% after the reopening on 6 November 2026, triggering the Dutch legal squeeze-out, alongside the TMF Holdings/TMF Business Services amalgamation notices.

**What management expects from it:** Pure-play CV: cleaner, comparable standalone reporting including Tata Cummins joint operations; teens (not mid-teens) EBITDA guidance, double-digit EBIT, capex 2–4% of revenue, FCF ~12% of revenue, 72% ROCE, net cash ₹7,500cr standalone/₹13,700cr consolidated funding a ₹4 dividend and the Iveco bid; with Iveco, ~EUR21bn revenue, operating leverage over larger volumes, less cash-flow volatility. No PV-entity commentary.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *CALL Nov 2025* — First call of the separated entity: management confirmed the demerger took effect 1 October 2025 and that the CV business was listed as Tata Motors Limited under ticker TMCV on both exchanges, describing it as a commitment delivered. “We successfully completed the demerger with Effective date of 1st October.”
- *CALL Nov 2025* — Comparatives had to be derived because the resulting company only came into existence in June 2024 — a direct consequence of the scheme structure. “the prior period financials in this presentation, they reflect the impact of the demerger as it has just been effective since the Company’s incorporation that happened in June 2024.”
- *CALL Nov 2025* — The newly separated CV entity immediately tied up its own acquisition financing for Iveco through a bridge loan, with refinancing options (equity or debt) left open. “On the Iveco acquisition, the regulatory approvals are underway and the initial funding through bridge loan has been secured.”
- *CALL Feb 2026* — The separation carried an explicit one-time cost of ₹960 crore, booked as an exceptional item in Q3 FY26 within ₹1,500 crore of standalone exceptionals (with ₹603 crore labour code and ₹82 crore Iveco acquisition cost). “Demerger cost has been around ₹960 crore.”
- *CALL Feb 2026* — Management flagged the demerger and labour-code charges as non-recurring, separating transaction cost from underlying performance. “And both these are going to be one-time for us. We don't expect this on a recurring basis.”
- *CALL Feb 2026* — The CV business crossed a double-digit EBIT margin for the first time as a standalone reporting unit — the profitability milestone used to validate the standalone case. “The CV segment also achieved the milestone of a double-digit EBIT margin for the first time, which now stands at 10.6%.”
- *CALL May 2026* — The clearest statement of what the separation achieved: a pure-play commercial vehicle company, which management calls a defining shift that changes how the business should be presented. “Demerger being effective from 1st of October 2025, Tata Motors is now a pure play commercial vehicle company, and this is a defining shift that changes how we think is most appropriate to present our financials.”
- *CALL May 2026* — The problem the split solves, as stated: the CV business was previously visible only as an internal carve-out construct inside the combined entity. “Historically, we reported a CV segment. It was an internal construct that carved out CV operations from within the erstwhile combined entity. That was a practical necessity then.”
- *CALL May 2026* — Post-demerger reporting switched to standalone financials including the Tata Cummins joint operation as the primary lens, for transparency and comparability. “This gives you a cleaner, more complete, and more directly comparable picture of the business going forward.”
- *CALL May 2026* — The margin record cited as structural rather than cyclical: 7.8% to 13.2% EBITDA over three years, with EBITDA doubling from ₹5,100 crore to ₹10,200 crore and FY26 EBIT at 11%. “EBITDA margins have expanded from 7.8% in FY23 to 13.2% in FY26. That's nearly 550 bps of structural improvement over three years.”
- *CALL May 2026* — Capital-efficiency case for the standalone entity: ₹9,200 crore FCF (12% of revenue), ₹2,800 crore reinvested, Auto ROCE of 72%, negative 31-day cash conversion cycle, net cash ₹7,500 crore standalone and ₹13,700 crore consolidated. “Finally, the Auto ROCE stands at 72% is an industry-leading number, when EBIT doubles, capital discipline holds, returns follow.”
- *CALL May 2026* — Deliberate de-cyclicalisation of the standalone business via parts & service, Fleet Edge digital and Smart City e-buses, growing far faster than the cyclical truck business. “Over the period, non-cyclical CAGR is running at 2.7x the cyclical CAGR. We've been deliberately building this mix, and this is now showing up meaningfully in the numbers.”

*Not explained on the calls:* Why separate at all — no pre-demerger call is in the record: no stated valuation-unlock, synergy or capital-allocation rationale, no investor, lender or partner named as requesting it, no entitlement ratio.

### The business being separated — its own numbers

**Automotive — Commercial vehicle (reported as the "Commercial Vehicles Segment"; the entity is Tata Motors Limited, formerly TML Commercial Vehicles Limited)** · unit ₹ crore · Revenue = segment external revenue (no inter-segment/intra-segment revenue reported for the commercial vehicle segment). Operating_profit = 'Segment results' = Earnings before other income (excluding incentives), finance costs, foreign exchange gain/(loss) (net), exceptional items and tax — i.e. a segment EBIT measure, not EBITDA or PBT. ## TVSMOTOR — TVS Motor Company Ltd.

**CONFIRMED** (a demerger scheme is on the exchange record) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 5.0/10 · spin-off · 8 filing(s) from NSE · first 2026-03-06, latest 2026-10-28

> **Listing:** NOT YET — scheme at 'nclt_sanction' stage; Home Credit India Finance Private Limited will list only after NCLT sanction, effectiveness and a record date; indicated timeline: Stated 28 October 2026: "Yes, subject to receipt of requisite approvals from statutory and regulatory authorities, the equity shares of the Resulting Company will be listed and admitted to trading on the Stock Exchanges pursuant to the Scheme"; no date given

**The stages, as filed:** nclt_sanction (2026-05-08)

**Stated in the filings:** resulting company **Home Credit India Finance Private Limited**; appointed date 2025-04-01.

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** TVS Motor's consumer finance and related business — lending, investment, leasing and ancillary services, held via subsidiaries — class `value_unlocking`.

- *Insiders:* Shareholding mirrors parent 1:1; promoters hold 50.27% (23,88,12,786 shares) post-Scheme, public 49.71%. Chairman Sudarshan Venu; TVS Motor's own shares in Resulting Company cancelled
- *What it reveals:* Financial segment carries Rs 43,003 Cr of the Rs 66,871 Cr consolidated assets vs automotive Rs 23,868 Cr, H1 segment PBT Rs 782 Cr on Rs 3,921 Cr turnover; separation reveals a leveraged NBFC platform (45 million customers) that can gear up independently of the auto balance sheet
- *Selling pressure:* likely — Every TVS Motor holder gets 1 share of an unlisted financial-services holding company in a different industry from auto; index status not stated
- *Parent or spin:* both · *option pricing date:* 28th October 2026 — valuation report of M/s. Bansi S. Mehta Valuers LLP fixing the 1:1 share entitlement ratio (record date only 'as defined in the Scheme', not stated)
- *Read next:* The Scheme itself on www.tvsmotor.com — Demerged Undertaking's assets/liabilities, record date, and TVS Credit/Home Credit merger terms
- *In their words:* “The turnover of the Demerged Undertaking for the period ended 30th September 2026 was Rs. 3,921  Crore out of the total turnover of Rs. 35,770 Crore of the Company .”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

TVS Motor is carving its consumer finance and related business undertaking — the lending, investment, leasing and ancillary/support activities it runs directly and through subsidiaries, principally the NBFC TVS Credit Services — out of the listed automotive company into Harita ARC Limited, a shell wholly-owned subsidiary bought from TVS Credit Services for Rs 25,000 on 28th October 2026, with TVS Motor shareholders getting 1 share of the resulting company for every 1 TVS Motor share (47,50,87,114 shares, valuation by Bansi S. Mehta Valuers LLP, fairness opinion by JM Financial), and the resulting company to be listed; the same Composite Scheme also amalgamates the dormant wholly-owned TVS Motor Services Limited (total assets Rs 251.44 Cr, net worth Rs 198.93 Cr, nil turnover) into TVS Motor 'to streamline the group corporate structure', after which it is dissolved without winding up. Management's stated problem is that finance has outgrown its host: the demerged undertaking already turned over Rs 3,921 Cr of TVS Motor's Rs 35,770 Cr consolidated revenue in H1 FY27, and the Financial segment carries Rs 43,003 Cr of assets and Rs 33,288 Cr of liabilities against Automotive's Rs 23,868 Cr, which is why consolidated net debt/equity sits at 2.90x versus 0.37x standalone. The Scheme says the consumer finance business 'needs a separate strategy suited to its industry-specific risks, market dynamics and growth path', that 'the nature of, and competition in, the consumer finance and related business differ from those of the other businesses', and — the capital-structure crux — that 'a financial services company can have a higher leverage (as compared to the Demerged Company) for its growth'. The second stated problem is investor mismatch: a standalone entity 'can attract different sets of investors, strategic partners, lenders and other stakeholders having a specific interest in the consumer finance and related business', and the demerger will 'unlock the value of the Demerged Undertaking for the shareholders of the Demerged Company'. Chairman Sudarshan Venu framed it as 15 years of sustained investment reaching scale — TVS Credit plus Home Credit India serving 'more than 45 million customers across 100,000 touchpoints', plus the Varthana education-finance acquisition and the Jana Small Finance Bank stake — so the platform should now allocate capital to its own priorities while TVS Motor 'remain[s] focused on strengthening its leadership in mobility globally'. It follows the August 2026 step in which the group's NBFCs approved merging STPL Trading and Services into Home Credit India Finance (155.79 shares per 200) and then Home Credit India Finance and TVS Housing Finance into TVS Credit Services (9.94 per 180), expressly for 'consolidating the NBFCs within the group in terms of RBI directions'; alongside the demerger the board also bought STPL outright for Rs 530.08 Cr to pick up ~2.4% more of TVS Credit post-merger. No lender, partner or named investor is cited as having asked for the split.

**How it evolved:** Strikingly, the separation is absent from all seven earnings calls in the window (Jan 2025 through Jul 2026): management discussed TVS Credit only as a performance line — book Rs 26,647 Cr and PBT Rs 1,027 Cr in FY25 (28 Apr 2025 call), Rs 30,631 Cr and Rs 1,248 Cr in FY26 (13 May 2026), Rs 32,053 Cr and 2.6 crore customers in Q1 FY27 (21 Jul 2026) — while repeatedly describing fresh equity infusions into it (Rs 200 Cr in Q3 FY26 per the 28 Jan 2026 call, Rs 200 Cr across FY26, Rs 711 Cr in Q2 FY27 per the filing). The only hint of structural intent came from an analyst on the 31 Jul 2025 call asking about monetising or IPO-ing TVS Credit, which CFO Gopala Desikan shut down as 'not yet even discussed at the Board level'. The plan then surfaces entirely in filings: the 5 Aug 2026 NBFC-consolidation scheme (STPL → Home Credit India Finance → TVS Credit Services, citing RBI directions), then the 28 Oct 2026 board approval of the Composite Scheme of Arrangement that demerges the undertaking into Harita ARC Limited 1:1 and folds TVS Motor Services into TVS Motor, with the press release calling the demerger 'the next step in this strategic process'.

**What management expects from it:** For the finance platform: strategic autonomy, sharper capital allocation, freedom to run higher NBFC-style leverage, a dedicated investor/lender/partner base, and value unlocked via a 1:1 listed entity. For TVS Motor: a simplified group structure, operational synergies from absorbing TVS Motor Services, and undiluted focus on automotive/mobility leadership globally. Shareholders participate in both.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *Scheme* — The 28 Oct 2026 Composite Scheme demerges the consumer finance and related business undertaking from TVS Motor into Harita ARC Limited and simultaneously amalgamates wholly-owned TVS Motor Services Limited into TVS Motor. “The Scheme, inter alia, provides for: (i) the amalgamation of the Transferor Company with the Company; and (ii) the demerger of the Demerged Undertaking (as defined in the Scheme) from the Company into the Resulting Company on a going concern basis, in consideration for which the Resulting Company shall issue its shares to the shareholders of the Company in proportion to their shareholding in the Company.”
- *Scheme* — Stated rationale #1: structural simplification into two independent standalone platforms, each with its own strategy and capital plan. “The demerger will simplify the group structure and create focused businesses, with a clear segregation of the Demerged Undertaking and the Remaining Business.”
- *Scheme* — Stated rationale #2: the lending business has risk, competitive and growth characteristics unlike the vehicle business, so it needs its own strategy. “The consumer finance and related business needs a separate strategy suited to its industry-specific risks, market dynamics and growth path;”
- *Scheme* — The capital-structure crux — an NBFC can run far more balance-sheet leverage than a manufacturer; consolidated net debt/equity was 2.90x at 30 Sep 2026 against 0.37x standalone. “a financial services company can have a higher leverage (as compared to the Demerged Company) for its growth .”
- *Scheme* — Investor/lender mismatch is named explicitly: a pure-play finance entity can draw capital providers who want finance exposure, and this unlocks value for existing holders. “the independent company can attract different sets of investors, strategic partners, lenders and other stakeholders having a specific interest in the consumer finance and related business .”
- *Scheme* — Size of the carve-out: the demerged undertaking produced Rs 3,921 Cr of revenue in the period ended 30 Sep 2026 against TVS Motor's Rs 35,770 Cr consolidated turnover; shareholders get 1:1 shares and the new entity will be listed. “The turnover of the Demerged Undertaking for the period ended 30th September 2026 was Rs. 3,921 Crore out of the total turnover of Rs. 35,770 Crore of the Company .”
- *Scheme* — Press release frames the trigger as scale reached after 15 years of investment — TVS Credit plus Home Credit India at 45 million customers and 100,000 touchpoints, plus Varthana and Jana Small Finance Bank — needing a dedicated structure for capital allocation. “The consumer finance and related business have expanded in scale and scope and a dedicated st ructure will provide greater strategic focus, flexibility in capital allocation and the ability to pursue opportunities across the consumer finance and related sector s.”
- *Scheme* — Chairman Sudarshan Venu's framing: full value realisation for the finance platform while TVS Motor concentrates on global mobility leadership, with shareholders participating in both. “It positions them to realise the full potential of their assets and capabilities while enabling TVS Motor Company to remain focused on strengthening its leadership in mobility globally .”
- *Scheme* — The precursor step (5 Aug 2026): STPL merges into Home Credit India Finance, then Home Credit India Finance and TVS Housing Finance merge into TVS Credit Services — partly driven by regulator-led NBFC consolidation; TVS Motor separately paid Rs 530.08 Cr for STPL to gain ~2.4% more of TVS Credit. “consolidating the NBFCs within the group in terms of RBI directions.”
- *[Aug 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=fd52c6c1-59d2-406d-9bf3-2381f22aa01d.pdf)* — The only investor-side prod in three years of calls: an analyst asked about earlier plans to monetise or IPO TVS Credit Services, and the CFO said the board had not taken it up — no mention of a demerger. “And as far as the question is all about IPO, not yet even discussed at the Board level.”
- *[Jul 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=e99280ca-79c3-4fa1-8188-f0f34294abfa.pdf)* — Scale of the business being separated, as management last described it on a call: book up 19% to Rs 32,053 Cr, PBT Rs 283 Cr for the quarter, ~2.6 crore customers, ~62,000 touchpoints. “The book size of TVS Credit grew by 19%. Now it is at INR 32,053 crores as against INR 26,898 crores last year.”
- *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=d60c3c01-cbb0-4df1-9cba-9e23ccc6fc27.pdf)* — FY26 record finance earnings quantified on the call — the profit stream now leaving the listed automotive entity. “PBT has grown by 22%, INR 1,248 crores as against INR 1,027 crores during last year.”

*Not explained on the calls:* No call ever discusses the demerger; no margin, ROE, capital-release, cost, tax, debt-allocation or timeline numbers for either entity; no promoter-control or future-stake-sale intent disclosed.
