## INDIAGLYCO — India Glycols Ltd.

**CONFIRMED** (a demerger scheme is on the exchange record) · **LISTED <1Y — selling-pressure window; the bargain forms here** · score 4.3/10 · spin-off · 42 filing(s) from BSE-screener, CALLS, NSE, NSE-register · first 2025-11-14, latest 2026-11-02

> **Listing:** LISTED — Ennature Bio Pharma Limited trades since about 2026-11-02 (record date 2026-09-02)

**The stages, as filed:** exchange_noc (2025-11-20) → meetings (2026-03-24) → nclt_sanction (2026-01-16) → effective (2026-10-06) → record_date (2026-09-02) → listed (2026-11-02)

**Stated in the filings:** resulting company **Ennature Bio Pharma Limited**; demerged undertaking: s from the Demerged; entitlement **1 for every 3**; record date 2026-09-02; appointed date 2026-04-01.

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** Bio Pharma undertaking into Ennature Bio Pharma; Spirits and Biofuel undertaking into IGL Spirits Limited — class `value_unlocking`.

- *Insiders:* Promoter family leads both spins: U.S. Bhartia Chairman & MD of IGL Spirits, daughter Pragya Bhartia Barwale MD of Ennature; sons-in-law non-executive directors. Promoter group voted 3,99,67,854 shares 100% in favour.
- *What it reveals:* Cost apportionment splits value IGL 31.77%, Ennature 20.61%, IGL Spirits 47.62%. Q1FY27 revenue: IGL Rs 345cr, IGL Spirits Rs 694cr, Ennature Rs 90cr. Spirits earned 21-22% EBIT margins inside a chemicals-labelled parent; Ennature margins depressed (4.1% EBIT 9MFY26).
- *Selling pressure:* likely — Ennature small (2,23,42,255 shares, 1-for-3 odd lots, Rs 90cr quarterly revenue) and a different industry from chemicals parent.
- *Parent or spin:* both · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* Information Memorandum of Ennature Bio Pharma and IGL Spirits (approved 8 September 2026) — segment debt allocation and standalone margins.
- *In their words:* “Ennature Bio Pharma Limited will house the bio-pharma and bio-polymers businesses.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

Management presented the break-up of India Glycols into three listed companies — India Glycols Ltd (bio-based specialty and performance chemicals, glycols/bio-glycols, new specialties, industrial gases, plus the 49% Clariant IGL JV), IGL Spirits Ltd (IMFL, Indian Made Indian Liquor/country liquor, ENA and the bio-fuel/ethanol business) and Ennature Bio Pharma Ltd (plant APIs and nutraceuticals — thiocolchicoside, nicotine, curcumin brands — plus the small bio-polymers/guar gum business) — as a focus and investor-appetite problem, not distress and not a lender demand. On the 6 Feb 2025 call Rupark Sarswat said the idea was to run the companies differently because they have different focuses, to give them much more focus, and because different investors tend to have a different focus for investments, creating potential to unlock value; CFO Anand Singhal listed four benefits: independent growth for each business, reducing the risk of one business affecting the others, drawing focused investors, and clearer management and resource allocation. They sized the three P&Ls on 9MFY25 — chemicals Rs 1,079 cr at 13.6% EBITDA margin, IGL Spirits Rs 1,628 cr net at 14.4%, Ennature Bio Pharma Rs 178 cr at 14.9% — against FY24 reported segments of BSPC Rs 1,626 cr, bio-fuel Rs 512 cr and potable spirits Rs 5,575 cr gross. A named driver was premiumisation of IMFL: Sarswat called focus on the IMFL business one of the significant rationales, in a potable-spirits market management put at about $56bn in 2025 growing 7.2% to roughly $112bn by 2034, with the Amrut royalty/distribution tie-up, CSD and paramilitary registrations, Bacardi contract bottling and Kerala entry as the engines; conversely he argued the chemicals business would show up better once it got more focus. The scheme also split the balance sheet: of about Rs 1,200 cr of long-term debt, roughly Rs 500 cr was earmarked to chemicals and Rs 700 cr to liquor (restated in Nov 2025 as Rs 600 cr India Glycols and Rs 800 cr IGL Spirits), big capex was frozen until after the demerger so the separate companies could decide it, bank limits had to be re-allocated with the SBI-led consortium, and the credit rating stayed on watch list until completion. No outside party was said to have demanded the separation — the board initiated it on 4 Feb 2025; analysts pressed on listing and value unlock (Balasubramanian, Rohit Nagraj) and one investor objected to demerging a margin-squeezed Ennature (Jaswinder Singh, 11 Aug 2025); approvals came from shareholders (4,42,48,625 of 4,42,48,626 votes in favour) and unsecured creditors (36 of 36, 100% by value), with the secured creditors meeting dispensed with on 95.46% consent. To Saket Kapoor's objection that clubbing government-priced grain ethanol with liquor would dilute the liquor valuation, management answered with synergy — captive high-quality ENA, backward integration, scale, piped supply, better resilience and absolute margin — and said this seemed like the most optimal way going forward, not with a valuation argument.

**How it evolved:** First disclosed on the 6 Feb 2025 call as a composite scheme: amalgamation of promoter holding company Kashipur Holdings into IGL (so promoters held IGL directly) plus a three-way demerger, appointed date 1 April 2026, with all three companies to be listed via the NCLT route in 12-15 months. The board dropped the KHL amalgamation leg on 16 May 2025 and pursued the demerger alone; the 11 Aug 2025 call restated the rationale (different investor appetites, enhancing value) and deferred capex to the post-demerger companies, while 18 Nov 2025 added the per-entity debt split (Rs 600 cr / Rs 800 cr) funded partly by a Rs 467 cr promoter-and-friends preferential issue at Rs 915. By 12 Feb 2026 capex and the credit rating were both explicitly waiting on the demerger, and on 18 May 2026 management was awaiting the NCLT order expected 21 May. NCLT Allahabad sanctioned the scheme on 17 July 2026; it became effective 1 Sept 2026 (record date 2 Sept), with 1 IGL Spirits share per IGL share and 1 Ennature share per 3 IGL shares, and the two new companies listed on 2 Nov 2026 and began trading 4 Nov 2026.

**What management expects from it:** IGL: chemicals judged on its own — richer performance-chemicals mix, Clariant JV cash, debt-free by FY29. IGL Spirits: IMFL premiumisation plus captive ENA/ethanol synergy, carrying the larger debt. Ennature: branded nutraceuticals and clinicals rebuild. All three: dedicated focus, independent growth, own capital allocation, insulation from each other's risk, and focused investors unlocking value.

- *[Feb 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=1385769f-cd04-4add-bcad-ce6e44567146.pdf)* — Sarswat's first statement of purpose: three separate companies, run differently, to create focus and let different investors back different businesses, with value unlock as the outcome. “And the whole idea behind this is to run these companies differently.”
- *[Feb 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=1385769f-cd04-4add-bcad-ce6e44567146.pdf)* — Sarswat tied the structure to investor appetite and future outside money coming into individual businesses. “And also, to allow potential investments in different businesses because different investors tend to have a different focus for investments.”
- *[Feb 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=1385769f-cd04-4add-bcad-ce6e44567146.pdf)* — CFO Anand Singhal's four formal benefits of the scheme — independent growth, risk insulation, focused investors, better management and resource allocation. “The main benefits of the proposed scheme will be that the demerger will enable independent growth for each businesses. Separating the business will reduce the risk of one business affecting the others.”
- *[Feb 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=1385769f-cd04-4add-bcad-ce6e44567146.pdf)* — Singhal explicitly framed the shareholder-value objective as attracting a different investor base to each entity. “Will create a potential to unlock value for the shareholders by drawing focused investors.”
- *[Feb 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=1385769f-cd04-4add-bcad-ce6e44567146.pdf)* — Singhal sized each proposed entity on 9MFY25: chemicals Rs 1,079 cr at 13.6% EBITDA margin, IGL Spirits Rs 1,628 cr net at 14.4%, Ennature Rs 178 cr at 14.9%. “IGL Spirits, which is proposed to be the other Company which will be having the Liquor business and the Bio-Fuel business, is having 9MFY25 turnover of Rs. 1,628, this is on net basis with 14.4% EBITDA margin.”
- *[Feb 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=1385769f-cd04-4add-bcad-ce6e44567146.pdf)* — The original scheme also merged promoter vehicle Kashipur Holdings into IGL so promoters would hold IGL shares directly; this leg was later dropped. “The merger of Kashipur Holdings, holding Company with India Glycols, is largely keeping in mind that the promoters will have the direct shareholding of IGL in their names.”
- *[Feb 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=1385769f-cd04-4add-bcad-ce6e44567146.pdf)* — Sarswat named IMFL premiumisation as a principal reason for the separation, citing a potable-spirits market of about $56bn in 2025 growing 7.2% to ~$112bn by 2034. “one of the significant rationales for us is to provide the focus on the IMFL business, which you know is a very interesting business going forward.”
- *[Feb 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=1385769f-cd04-4add-bcad-ce6e44567146.pdf)* — Bio-polymers/guar gum was moved out of chemicals into Ennature; the Clariant JV stayed with chemicals because the JV sells chemicals and its profits flow there. “And the third one will be Ennature Bio Pharma, which will be Ennature as it is right now, and also taking the Bio Polymers business, which is a small business, from chemicals and putting it into Ennature Bio Pharma.”
- *[Feb 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=1385769f-cd04-4add-bcad-ce6e44567146.pdf)* — Saket Kapoor challenged the valuation logic of putting government-priced ethanol with liquor; Sarswat answered with captive-ENA synergy and resilience, not multiples. “So, we are clubbing the government regulated business of grain-based ethanol and the liquor part. So, does that gel better for getting the right valuation going ahead since other liquor companies may or may not be having this under the portfolio.”
- *[Feb 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=1385769f-cd04-4add-bcad-ce6e44567146.pdf)* — Sarswat conceded the choice of perimeter was a judgement call, and said shared corporate resources would continue so standalone costs did not balloon. “So far in the wisdom of people who sat together, this seemed like the most optimal way going forward.”
- *[Feb 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=1385769f-cd04-4add-bcad-ce6e44567146.pdf)* — Singhal confirmed all three companies would be separately listed through the NCLT route, with a 12-15 month timeline and appointed date 1 April 2026. “So this demerger will be effective from 1st April, 26 and all the three companies will be listed on the stock exchange.”
- *[May 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=d532715b-c088-4be2-b619-e7a41528d1e7.pdf)* — Debt was pre-allocated by business: of ~Rs 1,200 cr long-term debt, ~Rs 500 cr to chemicals and ~Rs 700 cr to liquor, with annual repayments of Rs 150-160 cr (liquor) and Rs 90 cr (chemicals). “Just to brief you as of now position, we are having about INR 1,200 crores long-term debt in the books of the company, out of which about INR 500 crores will go to the Chemical division and INR 700 crores will go to the liquor division.”

## INOXGREEN — Inox Green Energy Services Ltd.

**CONFIRMED** (a demerger scheme is on the exchange record) · **LISTED <1Y — selling-pressure window; the bargain forms here** · score 4.3/10 · spin-off · 24 filing(s) from CALLS, NSE, NSE-register · first 2025-11-01, latest 2026-08-24

> **Listing:** LISTED — Inox Renewable Solutions Limited trades since about 2026-08-01 (record date 2026-08-01)

**The stages, as filed:** meetings (2025-11-01) → nclt_sanction (2026-03-14) → effective (2026-05-04) → record_date (2026-08-01)

**Stated in the filings:** resulting company **Inox Renewable Solutions Limited**; demerged undertaking: ) of Inox Green Energy Services; entitlement **122 for every 2,000**; record date 2026-08-01.

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** The Power Evacuation Business (substation/evacuation infrastructure undertaking) of Inox Green, demerged into Inox Renewable Solutions Limited — class `value_unlocking`.

- *Insiders:* Inox Wind Limited, promoter and holding company, directly holds 51.13% of Inox Green; IRSL shares issued pro-rata to the same shareholders. Director/KMP stakes tiny (Bindu Saxena 12,640 shares). No separate incentive scheme stated.
- *What it reveals:* Removing ~Rs 1,000 crore gross block and Rs 50-55 crore annual depreciation leaves Inox Green a pure-play O&M business with ~50% EBITDA margins, tax shield and FY27 EBITDA guidance above Rs 600 crore; IRSL holds the capital-heavy, leveraged evacuation assets, losses and a Rs 96.8 crore tax demand
- *Selling pressure:* likely — Only 122 IRSL shares per 1,000 held - small odd-lot stakes; 4,89,82,030 shares spread to O&M holders; different industry (EPC/power evacuation), loss-making, heavily indebted
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* IRSL listing/trading approval intimation and its standalone financials - secured/unsecured debt and the Rs 96.80 crore AY2023-24 tax demand
- *In their words:* “Such consolidation in a single entity will lend enhanced focus to the Power Evacuation business.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

The separation is the demerger of Inox Green Energy Services Ltd's (IGESL) power evacuation / substation and common-infrastructure business into Inox Renewable Solutions Ltd (IRSL, formerly Resco Global Wind Services), leaving IGESL a pure-play renewable O&M company and consolidating all evacuation/EPC infrastructure in IRSL, which gets automatically listed. Management's core explanation is historical and structural: when IGESL was spun out of Inox Wind, the EPC business was slump-sold to Resco, but the already-commissioned substations and transmission lines could not be moved because, as Devansh Jain said in Aug 2024, shifting them 'would have entailed taking approval from over 200 customers and then arm twisting us in terms of renegotiating contracts and screwing the entire O&M business'; so IGESL's balance sheet stayed 'unnecessarily inflated' with assets on which it is 'actually the trustee', while all new substations were being built in Resco anyway ('no future CapEx under Inox Green at all', Feb 2024). The financial fix they repeatedly quantified: a gross block of ~INR 1,000 crore (net block ~INR 750 crore, Aug 2024) leaves IGESL, annual depreciation of ~INR 50-55 crore (~INR 13-17 crore a quarter) is eliminated, PBT rises by that amount, and only ~INR 3-5 crore a quarter (~INR 10 crore a year, Feb 2026) of revenue goes out with virtually no cost and no interest moving — Akhil Jindal put the benefit at '~INR 12-odd crore in the bottom line on a quarterly basis' (Nov 2024), turning reported PAT of ~INR 6 crore into ~INR 18-20 crore. They stressed the evacuation assets are not needed for O&M ('not required for O&M services per se... that is required for further providing a turnkey solution'), so IGESL becomes a zero-capex, asset-light annuity business where EBITDA equals PBT and cash PAT, helped by a ~INR 700 crore accumulated tax-loss shield that stays at company level, with 'significant improvement in ROE and ROCE' (Jun 2026). The Scheme's own rationale adds that risks, rewards, financial profile, competition and opportunities are 'separate and distinct' for O&M versus power evacuation, that the evacuation business 'is capable of attracting different set of investors, strategic partners, lenders and other stakeholders', that consolidating it into IRSL (which already does the same business) unlocks value and lends enhanced focus, and that the result is two listed entities each free to pursue its own strategy. On the IRSL side, management argued the infrastructure is itself a high-value platform — INR 175 crore raised at a ~INR 7,400 crore valuation (Sep 2025), ~10 GW of 'plug and play' evacuation infra made more valuable by the CERC hybridisation amendment — and that listing it 'will unlock substantial value for both Inox Wind and Inox Green' (Nov 2025). The push came from the promoters/board (valuers appointed Aug-Nov 2024, scheme approved 13 Nov 2024) with investors on calls repeatedly asking about rationalising subsidiaries and value unlocking; Akhil Jindal framed the purpose as giving shareholders optionality — 'a shareholder has got now a choice to hold any part of the business' — and shareholders, warrant holders, secured and unsecured creditors all approved it before NCLT Ahmedabad sanctioned it.

**How it evolved:** On the Feb 2024 call the idea did not exist yet; management only explained that all future common-infra capex would sit in Resco, not Inox Green, while legacy depreciation ran on. By the Aug 2024 and Nov 2024 (Oct 25, 2024) calls the board had appointed consultants and registered valuers to evaluate demerging the power evacuation business, pitched as a 'cleaner and asset-light balance sheet' worth ~INR 12 crore a quarter to the bottom line, and the board approved the Scheme on 13 Nov 2024; in Feb 2025 (Jan 31, 2025) Akhil Jindal said exchange approvals were due in February and NCLT would take 6-9 months, with IGESL holders getting ~20% of the renamed Inox Renewable Solutions. By Sep 2025 (Sep 1, 2025) stock-exchange no-objections were in and the scheme filed at NCLT Ahmedabad (approval expected in 2-3 quarters), IRSL had raised INR 175 crore at a ~INR 7,400 crore valuation, and the CERC hybridisation ruling made its infra far more valuable; Nov 2025 (Nov 14, 2025) reported shareholder and creditor approval, and Feb 2026 (Feb 13, 2026) said hearings were in final stages with listing 2-3 months out. NCLT sanctioned the scheme on 13 Mar 2026, it became effective 4 May 2026, and on the Jun 2026 (May 29, 2026) call management confirmed approval and booked the benefits as done — INR 1,000 crore gross block and INR 50-55 crore depreciation gone, ROE/ROCE improved — while refusing to give IRSL's standalone top line or EBITDA until listing; the record date was 1 Aug 2026 and 4,89,82,030 IRSL shares were allotted on 24 Aug 2026.

**What management expects from it:** Inox Green: asset-light pure-play O&M — Rs 1,000 crore gross block and Rs 50-55 crore depreciation gone, only ~Rs 10 crore revenue lost, EBITDA≈PBT≈cash PAT, better ROE/ROCE. IRSL: separately listed EPC/evacuation arm with its own investors, lenders and ~10 GW plug-and-play infra; IGESL holders get 122 IRSL shares per 1,000.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *[Feb 2024](https://inoxgreen.com/PDF/Transcription%20of%20INOX%20Green%20Energy%20-%20Q3%20FY24%20Earnings%20Conference%20Call.pdf)* — Pre-demerger baseline: management explained IGESL carries legacy substation gross block (4 GW capacity, 3 GW commissioned) with ~INR 13 crore quarterly depreciation, while all future common-infrastructure capex is being incurred in Resco Global, a 100% subsidiary of Inox Wind. “So, no future CapEx under Inox Green at all. So, whatever is the depreciation which is being incurred on a quarterly basis will continue until and unless our net block gets consumed.”
- *[Aug 2024](https://inoxgreen.com/PDF/MOSL-InoxGreenEnergy-Aug09-2024_IGESL.pdf)* — Board appointed consultants and registered valuers to evaluate the demerger; Mathusudhana framed it as producing a cleaner, asset-light balance sheet whose main benefit is eliminating depreciation. “The proposed demerger will significantly add value through depreciation elimination.”
- *[Aug 2024](https://inoxgreen.com/PDF/MOSL-InoxGreenEnergy-Aug09-2024_IGESL.pdf)* — Devansh Jain gave the historical reason the assets were stranded in IGESL: at the time of the EPC slump sale to Resco, only uncommissioned assets moved, and commissioned substations could not be shifted without re-opening contracts with over 200 customers. “We could not shunt it out from this balance sheet into Resco because that would have entailed taking approval from over 200 customers and then arm twisting us in terms of renegotiating contracts and screwing the entire O&M business.”
- *[Aug 2024](https://inoxgreen.com/PDF/MOSL-InoxGreenEnergy-Aug09-2024_IGESL.pdf)* — He added that IGESL's balance sheet was inflated by assets it merely holds as trustee (net block ~INR 750 crore), and that the remaining business is a zero-capex annuity with no land bank or future evacuation capex. “Inox Green's balance sheet is unnecessarily inflated thanks to these historical substations which are lying on its balance sheet of which we are actually the trustee.”
- *[Nov 2024](https://www.inoxgreen.com/PDF/MOSL-InoxGreenEnergy-Oct25-2024.pdf)* — Akhil Jindal quantified the P&L effect for Pritesh Chheda: the whole depreciation goes, only INR 3-4 crore of quarterly revenue leaves, and IGESL shareholders receive Resco shares in lieu, with valuation yet to be fixed. “Excluding the substation business, the revenue would be down by around Rs. 3 crores or Rs. 4 crores on a quarterly basis, and the whole depreciation will go away. So, broadly that will add around Rs. 12-odd crore in the bottom line on a quarterly basis.”
- *[Feb 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=a6149a06-42db-4b82-ae77-0dc15e5abe49.pdf)* — Mathusudhana answered Bhavik Shah's objection that the transferred assets would come back as opex: the evacuation and common infrastructure is not needed to run O&M at all, it belongs to the EPC/turnkey business, so margins are unaffected. “So as far as the power evacuation and the common infrastructure, we have developed is not required for O&M services per se. That is required for further providing a turnkey solution to the customers.”
- *[Feb 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=a6149a06-42db-4b82-ae77-0dc15e5abe49.pdf)* — Jindal described the post-demerger entity as an asset-light balance sheet with no depreciation, so EBITDA is the benchmark for PAT; the ~INR 700 crore accumulated tax losses stay with IGESL because they sit at company, not asset, level. “So when you're looking into the next year's balance sheet of Inox Green, it would be an asset-light balance sheet. And it would also have no depreciation charges as a continued item. What it means is that our profitability will be far more stronger.”
- *[Sep 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=ac349021-05a3-4a4e-84a8-edb5f23d90bd.pdf)* — Asked by Hansal Thakkar whether the subsidiaries would be rationalised into IWL shareholders' hands, Jindal said the whole intent of separating the businesses was shareholder optionality, and that no further corporate action is needed. “And I think from a shareholder's perspective, a shareholder has got now a choice to hold any part of the business. He can hold the O&M business, he can hold the infrastructure business, he can hold the entire value chain together under Inox Wind.”
- *[Sep 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=ac349021-05a3-4a4e-84a8-edb5f23d90bd.pdf)* — Mathusudhana restated the balance-sheet numbers (INR 1,000 crore gross block off, INR 50-55 crore annual depreciation eliminated, PBT up by that amount, ROE/ROCE up), with exchange no-objections received and the scheme filed at NCLT Ahmedabad. “Once the scheme is approved by the NCLT, the gross block of around INR1,000 crore will be off our balance sheet and subsequently the depreciation of approximately INR50 crores to INR55 crores annually will be eliminated, thereby increasing the PBT by that amount.”
- *[Sep 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=ac349021-05a3-4a4e-84a8-edb5f23d90bd.pdf)* — Sanjeev Agarwal gave the value case for the receiving entity: IRSL had just raised INR 175 crore at a ~INR 7,400 crore valuation, and the new CERC hybridisation rules multiply the value of its site infrastructure (Devansh: ~10 GW of plug-and-play infra). “We have recently raised INR175 crores at Inox Renewable Solutions at a valuation of approximately INR7,400 crores.”
- *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=12a9f200-8091-44c1-a30e-eb06b0e51134.pdf)* — With shareholder and creditor approval obtained, Devansh Jain framed the separation as a value-unlocking event for both the parent and IGESL, with IRSL listing as Inox Wind's EPC arm. “I believe that the de-merger and subsequent listing of Inox Renewable Solutions will unlock substantial value for both Inox Wind and Inox Green.”

## PICCADIL — Piccadily Agro Industries Ltd.

**CONFIRMED** (a demerger scheme is on the exchange record) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 4.3/10 · spin-off · 6 filing(s) from CALLS, NSE · first 2026-04-28, latest 2026-08-17

> **Listing:** NOT YET — scheme at 'exchange_noc' stage; the resulting company will list only after NCLT sanction, effectiveness and a record date; indicated timeline: Press release and earnings call (28–29 April 2026): demerger scheme filed with SEBI, "expects completion by the end of FY27"; NSE observation letter (14 August 2026): listing/trading must commence "within sixty days of receipt of the order of the Hon'ble High Court/NCLT"; shares frozen in depositories till trading permission.

**The stages, as filed:** exchange_noc (2026-08-17)

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** The Sugar Business — white crystal sugar, allied and food products — demerged into wholly owned Piccadily Food & Essentials Limited — class `value_unlocking`.

- *Insiders:* Not stated as a percentage; shareholding proportionate — no change in PAIL's pattern; PFEL's pre-scheme capital cancelled, no consideration. Promoter converted 6,36,942 warrants into PAIL shares, listed November 2025.
- *What it reveals:* Parent becomes pure-play alco-bev: FY26 distillery segment result Rs 23,658.72 lakhs vs sugar's Rs 494.79 lakhs on 20.53% of turnover; sugar segment liabilities Rs 22,166.79 lakhs exceed its assets Rs 10,553.97 lakhs, so leverage leaves with the stub.
- *Selling pressure:* likely — Entitlement is only 1 PFEL share per 9 PAIL shares; sugar is a different, seasonal industry premium-spirits holders did not buy.
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* Scheme explanatory statement: value of assets and liabilities transferred to PFEL, plus PFEL's abridged prospectus/Information Memorandum.
- *In their words:* “The effectiveness of the Scheme would result in the creation of two listed companies with proportionate shareholding with the Resulting Company housing the Sugar Business and the Company housing the Distillery Business.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

Management is demerging the Sugar Business of Piccadily Agro Industries Ltd. (PAIL) into Piccadily Food & Essentials Limited (PFEL), a wholly owned subsidiary, so that PAIL becomes a pure-play premium alco-bev company; CFO Natwar Aggarwal framed it on the April 29, 2026 call as "we want to be a global alco-bev company and in that pursuit we want to focus on our core brand portfolio," with the scheme Board-approved April 28, 2026, filed with SEBI, KPMG as adviser, and completion envisaged in FY27. The stated intent is to pool human and capital resources behind the Alco-Bev portfolio (Indri single malt, Camikara rum, Cashmir vodka, Whistler blended whisky) and to list sugar — described as a "traditional heritage business" — as a separate entity rather than sell it. The economics behind it are visible in the numbers management cited: Alco-Bev revenue grew 42% to INR 908 crore (from INR 639 crore) with 31.5% EBITDA margins and 45–50% IMFL margins, while sugar was only INR 233.05 crore of turnover (20.53% of the listed entity) and dragged Q4 standalone EBITDA margin down ~300 bps as sugar's quarterly EBITDA margin collapsed from 11% to 2%; the segment tables show the sugar segment result at a loss of INR 904.62 lakh in FY26 versus a loss of INR 327.13 lakh in FY25, with sugar segment assets of INR 10,553.97 lakh against segment liabilities of INR 22,166.79 lakh. Management also repeatedly blamed sugar seasonality for making quarter-to-quarter margins hard to read. The scheme's own rationale (Annexure B) lists focused attention for each core business and the ability to attract required investment, greater business focus and enhanced shareholder value, more efficient use of financial resources, managerial talent, technical skills and marketing resources, value unlock "through price-discovery of the individual entities," the "right operating architecture" with sharper individual strategies and "clear capital allocation," and separately listed companies attracting a specific set of investors with financial flexibility and "stronger capital market outcomes." Mechanically it is a mirror listing: no cash consideration, 1 PFEL share of INR 10 for every 9 PAIL shares (ratio fixed on sugar's turnover and assets), PFEL's pre-scheme capital cancelled, no change in PAIL's shareholding pattern, producing "two listed companies with proportionate shareholding." No investor, lender or business partner is identified anywhere as having demanded the separation — it is presented as a management/Board decision, recommended by the Audit Committee and Independent Directors, alongside the unrelated FY27 agenda of INR 250–300 crore incremental Indri revenue, INR 300–400 crore from the 200 KLPD Chhattisgarh plant, 60–70% growth and brand-side inorganic options.

**How it evolved:** Only one earnings call falls in the window, the FY26 call of April 29, 2026, and the demerger appears there already as a done decision rather than an idea being floated — announced in the CFO's opening remarks the day after the April 28, 2026 Board meeting approved the scheme and filed it with the exchanges/SEBI, with KPMG as partner and FY27 as the completion target. It resurfaced later in the same call only when Himanshu Shah of Dolat Capital pressed on intent (sell or separately list), drawing the explicit answer that sugar would be listed separately, not sold. The filings then track execution rather than rationale: the April 28, 2026 Regulation 30 outcome with the full Annexure B rationale, share entitlement ratio and sugar turnover of INR 233.05 crore (20.53%), the April 28, 2026 press release restating the pure-play framing, and the August 17, 2026 intimation of BSE/NSE no-adverse-observation letters dated August 14, 2026 (SEBI comments dated August 13, 2026) clearing the way for the NCLT petition. Earlier filings in the window (November–December 2025) concern only CCD and warrant conversions and never mention a separation.

**What management expects from it:** Alco-Bev PAIL becomes a pure-play premium spirits company: sharper focus, pooled human and capital resources, better capital allocation, and 31.5% alco-bev / 45–50% IMFL margins no longer diluted by seasonal sugar; 60–70% FY27 growth and 3–4x revenue in 3–4 years. Sugar, housed in PFEL, gets focused attention, its own investor set, price discovery, financial flexibility and ability to attract investment.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *[May 2026](https://www.piccadily.com/themes/piccadily/pdfs/piccadily_transcript_earnings_call_dated_29_4_26.pdf)* — The CFO announced the demerger of the sugar business into a new entity as a step toward becoming a global alco-bev company focused on the core brand portfolio, filed with SEBI with KPMG as partner and NCLT to follow, targeting completion in FY27. “A couple of announcements also, we want to be a global alco-bev company and in that pursuit we want to focus on our core brand portfolio.”
- *[May 2026](https://www.piccadily.com/themes/piccadily/pdfs/piccadily_transcript_earnings_call_dated_29_4_26.pdf)* — Timeline and process: scheme filed with SEBI, NCLT filing after SEBI go-ahead, completion envisaged within FY27. “Once we get go-ahead from SEBI, we will follow the due process of filing it to NCLT and we envisage to complete this process by FY '27 this year.”
- *[May 2026](https://www.piccadily.com/themes/piccadily/pdfs/piccadily_transcript_earnings_call_dated_29_4_26.pdf)* — Management restated the demerger purely as a focus measure alongside guidance of 60–70% FY27 growth and 3x–4x revenue in three to four years. “As mentioned earlier, we also in a process of demerger just to focus on the main Alco-Bev business.”
- *[May 2026](https://www.piccadily.com/themes/piccadily/pdfs/piccadily_transcript_earnings_call_dated_29_4_26.pdf)* — Asked by Himanshu Shah of Dolat Capital whether sugar would eventually be sold or listed, management said the intent is to pool human and capital resources for Alco-Bev only and to separately list sugar, which it called a traditional heritage business. “Yes, intent is very clear that we want to be a global Alco-Bev company. We want to pool our human and capital resources just for the Alco-Bev business.”
- *[May 2026](https://www.piccadily.com/themes/piccadily/pdfs/piccadily_transcript_earnings_call_dated_29_4_26.pdf)* — The separation is explicitly a separate listing of the heritage sugar business, not a divestment, so the company can focus only on the Alco-Bev portfolio. “So sugar business is like a traditional heritage business for us. So we want to separate it and list it as a separate entity than our Alco-Bev company and focus only on the Alco-Bev portfolio.”
- *[May 2026](https://www.piccadily.com/themes/piccadily/pdfs/piccadily_transcript_earnings_call_dated_29_4_26.pdf)* — Sugar was the main reason standalone Q4 EBITDA margin fell about 300 basis points, its quarterly EBITDA margin dropping from 11% to 2% — the dilution the demerger removes. “That is one of the major factor is because of sugar drop in business, sugar margins drop, which was 11% EBITDA margin last year and last year same quarter and 2% this year quarter.”
- *[May 2026](https://www.piccadily.com/themes/piccadily/pdfs/piccadily_transcript_earnings_call_dated_29_4_26.pdf)* — Management contrasted sugar's drag with Alco-Bev EBITDA margins of about 31.5% (and IMFL margins of 45–50%), which it expects to maintain or improve with premiumisation. “I would like to highlight one more point here that if you look at our Alco-Bev business EBITDA margins, which is in the range of, let's say, current year about 31.5%, which is one of the highest margin in any Alco-Bev competition.”
- *[May 2026](https://www.piccadily.com/themes/piccadily/pdfs/piccadily_transcript_earnings_call_dated_29_4_26.pdf)* — Sugar seasonality was also cited as what makes quarter-to-quarter margin comparison unreliable for the consolidated entity. “So as I said, that as you rightly said that overall our EBITDA margins are same on year-over-year basis, but quarterly one factor is a sugar because of seasonality of the sugar business.”
- *Scheme* — The April 28, 2026 Board outcome states the scheme demerges the Sugar Business into wholly owned subsidiary PFEL under Sections 230–232, creating two listed companies with proportionate shareholding — sugar in PFEL, distillery in PAIL. ““The effectiveness of the Scheme would result in the creation of two listed companies with proportionate shareholding with the Resulting Company housing the Sugar Business and the Company housing the Distillery Business.”
- *Scheme* — Sugar's scale is disclosed as INR 233.05 crore of FY26 turnover, 20.53% of the listed entity's total turnover. “The turnover of the Demerged Undertaking of the Company for the financial year ended 31% March 2026 is as follows:”
- *Scheme* — Scheme rationale: separating the undertaking lets each company give focused attention to its core business and attract the investment that business needs. “Demerger of the Demerged Business and Undertaking and transferrmg it to a separate company would enable both the Demergéd Company and. the Resulting Company to provide focused attention for growth of their core businesses and attract required investments for growing that business;”
- *Scheme* — Scheme rationale: value unlock via separate price discovery for each entity for existing shareholders. “The Scheme would unlock value for the overall-business portfolio through price-discovery of the individual entities for existing shareholders;”

*Not explained on the calls:* No sugar standalone P&L/debt split, lender or creditor consents, demerger costs, PFEL management, dividend or sale intent beyond listing; no investor, lender or partner named as requesting it.

## THOMASCOOK — Thomas Cook (India) Ltd.

**CONFIRMED** (a demerger scheme is on the exchange record) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 4.3/10 · spin-off · 15 filing(s) from CALLS, NSE, NSE-BM · first 2026-03-20, latest 2026-11-05

> **Listing:** NOT YET — scheme at 'nclt_sanction' stage; Sterling Holiday Resorts Limited will list only after NCLT sanction, effectiveness and a record date; indicated timeline: NSE observation letter (September 1, 2026): SHRL "shall ensure that steps for listing of specified securities are completed and trading in securities commences within sixty days of receipt of the order of the Hon'ble High Court/NCLT". On the May 13, 2026 earnings call Debasis Nandy said the demerger would take "12 to 15 months" and "We expect this process to get completed by Q1 of FY '28". March 20, 2026 filing: consolidation of share capital expected "within 15 to 18 months from the date of approval of the Scheme by the Board". NCLT first-motion order November 4, 2026 directs shareholder/creditor meetings within 60 days; final NCLT sanction still pending.

**The stages, as filed:** announced (2026-03-20) → exchange_noc (2026-09-01) → nclt_sanction (2026-11-05)

**Stated in the filings:** resulting company **Sterling Holiday Resorts Limited**; demerged undertaking: Resort Business of TCIL (Demerged Company) are transferred to Sterling Holiday Resorts.

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** TCIL's Resorts and Resort Management business — 6 Nature Trails resorts — transferred to Sterling Holiday Resorts Limited — class `value_unlocking`.

- *Insiders:* Promoters 100% of SHRL pre-scheme, 65.55% post (includes 7% held by TCIL); ESOP Trust 2.16% after 65,70,000 ESOP Options 2024 accelerate 7 working days before Record Date 1. Promoter: Fairbridge Capital (Mauritius)/Fairfax, 63.83% of TCIL.
- *What it reveals:* The demerged undertaking is tiny — INR 70 Crores turnover, ~0.4% of TCIL standalone. The real asset is SHRL itself: 78 resorts, ~3,800 rooms, FY26 revenue INR 5,487 mn, EBITDA 31%, PBT INR 1,142 mn, debt-free, cash ~INR 3,400 mn, 25 straight profitable quarters.
- *Selling pressure:* likely — Every TCIL holder gets 81 SHRL shares per 100; hospitality is a different industry from travel/forex, management targets "differentiated investor cohorts".
- *Parent or spin:* spin · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* Shareholder meeting notice: SHRL abridged prospectus, valuation report, post-demerger balance sheets of TCIL and SHRL.
- *In their words:* “Accordingly, the Board of TCIL is of the view that for better focus and maximum result, it is better to divest the Resorts and Resort Management Business into SHRL and subsequently list SHRL.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

Thomas Cook (India) Ltd (TCIL) is carving out its Resorts and Resort Management business — the six resorts it owns/operates directly under the Nature Trails brand, which it had itself absorbed from Nature Trails Resorts Pvt Ltd by slump sale for Rs 522.5 mn (appointed date 1 March 2025) — and demerging it into its wholly owned subsidiary Sterling Holiday Resorts Ltd (SHRL), which will then be separately listed on BSE and NSE. Management's stated logic is twofold: operationally, the resorts "would reap more benefit from being owned and operated by SHRL in light of their vast expertise in the hospitality industry" (SHRL ran 75+ resorts/3,700+ rooms at scheme date, 78 resorts/~3,800 rooms across 65 destinations by FY26-end, FY26 revenue INR 5,487 mn, EBITDA INR 1,701 mn at 31%, PBT INR 1,142 mn at 21%, 25 straight profitable quarters, debt-free with ~INR 3,400 mn cash); and financially, the split is meant to "unlock value" and "attract differentiated investor cohorts for each business segment," leaving TCIL to "concentrate our resources on our core Travel and Financial Services business." The demerged undertaking is tiny in revenue terms — INR 70 crores for the year ended 31 December 2025, ~0.4% of TCIL standalone turnover — so the driver is structural, not scale: SHRL's board says it "has matured over the years and is well poised to chart its own growth path and operate as a separate listed entity in the fast-growing hospitality industry," with two listed entities each pursuing "growth opportunities that are more aligned with their own industry dynamics." Bolted onto the same composite scheme are three capital-structure fixes aimed squarely at EPS and optics: consolidating four Re 1 shares into one Rs 4 share (47,69,50,562 shares becoming 11,92,37,641) to "better reflect the true market value" and "convey stronger financial stability and valuation metrics"; absorbing three dormant subsidiaries — TC Visa Services (India), Jardin Travel Solutions and Borderless Travel Services — that are "incurring unnecessary compliance and administrative costs"; and cutting face value from Rs 4 to Rs 3 with no payout to "right size the balance sheet and capital structure." Consideration is 81 SHRL shares of Rs 10 for every 100 TCIL shares of Re 1, with no cash; TCIL keeps its existing SHRL shares (~7%), promoters end at 65.55% of SHRL and public at 32.30%. The initiative came from the Board on the recommendation of the Audit Committee and an Independent Directors Committee — no lender, partner or named investor demand is disclosed anywhere in the calls or filings, though analysts had repeatedly pressed management on deployment of the ~INR 780-800 crore net cash pile and on Sterling's EBIT failing to scale with its room additions.

**How it evolved:** Across the May 2025, Aug 2025, Nov 2025 and Feb 2026 calls there is no hint of a separation: the only structural move discussed is the opposite direction — the March 2025 slump sale pulling Nature Trails' three Mumbai-area resorts (80-90 rooms, INR 10-15 crores revenue) into TCIL — while analysts push on cash use and on why Sterling's EBIT stayed flat at ~INR 129 crores despite adding 1,200-1,300 rooms, and on 6 February 2026 Mahesh Iyer still says "there are no conversations around either any kind of disbursement of cash to shareholders or for that matter, any acquisition." The Board then granted in-principle approval on 20 March 2026 and the full composite scheme (demerger, 4:1 consolidation, merger of three dormant subsidiaries, Rs 4-to-Rs 3 capital reduction) was announced that day. It was discussed on an earnings call for the first time on 13 May 2026, where Iyer framed it as a "strategic divestment"/value unlock, Vikram Lalvani confirmed "the demerger process from Thomas Cook has also been initiated," and Debasis Nandy reaffirmed the original 12-15 month timeline with completion expected by Q1 FY28. Execution then tracked that guidance without the plan itself changing: BSE no-adverse-observation on 31 August 2026, NSE no-objection on 1 September 2026, SHRL's registered office shifted from Tamil Nadu to Maharashtra effective 13 July 2026, and an NCLT Mumbai procedural order dated 4 November 2026 admitting the application and directing TCIL shareholder and unsecured-creditor meetings.

**What management expects from it:** TCIL: streamlined capital structure, resources focused on travel and financial services, improved EPS from the 4:1 consolidation, Rs 4-to-Rs 3 reduction and dormant-subsidiary merger, lower admin cost. SHRL: separate listing on BSE/NSE, own growth path in fast-growing hospitality, hospitality-expert ownership of the resorts. Both: differentiated investor cohorts, sector-aligned strategies, improved operational efficiency and profitability.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=d884e7c7-ee2e-41fb-b1b5-e6408e592685.pdf)* — First earnings-call disclosure of the March 2026 board approval, framed as a strategic divestment of the resort business into Sterling that unlocks shareholder value. “Before we move on to the segmental analysis, I will discuss the strategic divestment announcement that was made in March 2026, where the Board has granted in-principle approval for the demerger of our resort business into Sterling Holiday Resorts.”
- *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=d884e7c7-ee2e-41fb-b1b5-e6408e592685.pdf)* — Iyer's stated benefit for the remaining TCIL: a cleaner capital structure and resources concentrated on Travel and Financial Services (forex, corporate travel, MICE, DMS). “For Thomas Cook (India) Limited, this restructuring allows us to streamline our capital structure and concentrate our resources on our core Travel and Financial Services business.”
- *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=d884e7c7-ee2e-41fb-b1b5-e6408e592685.pdf)* — The face-value consolidation plus absorption of the three dormant subsidiaries is pitched explicitly as an EPS and corporate-structure simplification measure. “The consolidation of our face value per share, along with the merger of the three dormant subsidiaries, further simplifies our corporate structure and improves our Earnings Per Share, directly benefiting our shareholders.”
- *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=d884e7c7-ee2e-41fb-b1b5-e6408e592685.pdf)* — Lalvani places the demerger alongside Sterling's own next phase — brand re-architecture and expansion to 95 resorts/4,500 rooms in 2027 — as process already under way. “In parallel, as you are aware, the demerger process from Thomas Cook has also been initiated.”
- *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=d884e7c7-ee2e-41fb-b1b5-e6408e592685.pdf)* — Nandy gave the only timeline guidance: 12-15 months from board approval, NSE/BSE applications filed and queries being answered, completion expected Q1 FY28. “So when we took the Board approval for this particular demerger project, we said that it will take us 12 to 15 months.”
- *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=d884e7c7-ee2e-41fb-b1b5-e6408e592685.pdf)* — Sterling's readiness argument on the call: FY26 as an inflection year with revenue INR 5,487 mn, EBITDA 31%, PBT margin 21%, 25 consecutive profitable quarters and a debt-free balance sheet with ~INR 3,400 mn cash. “FY '25-'26 marks a defining year for Sterling, a decisive inflection point where scale, profitability and balance sheet strength have expanded simultaneously, not sequentially.”
- *Scheme* — Core operating rationale: the resorts belong with Sterling because Sterling has the hospitality operating expertise, catering to a different demographic with more curated experiences (adventure holidays, educational trips, corporate getaways). “TCIL and SHRL's Management believes that the Resort Business of TCIL would reap more benefit from being owned and operated by SHRL in light of their vast expertise in the hospitality industry.”
- *Scheme* — Sterling is presented as having outgrown subsidiary status and ready for its own listed existence in a fast-growing sector — the justification for subsequently listing SHRL on BSE and NSE. “Further, SHRL's Management is of the view that SHRL has matured over the years and is well poised to chart its own growth path and operate as a separate listed entity in the fast-growing hospitality industry.”
- *Scheme* — The value-unlock case is explicitly about attracting different investor bases to travel/financial services versus leisure hospitality, with each entity pursuing sector-specific growth strategies with agility. “Unlock value for the shareholders of TCIL by demerging the Resorts and Resort Management business into SHRL and to attract differentiated investor cohorts for each business segment”
- *Scheme* — Segregating verticals is expected to improve operating efficiency and profitability at both entities because each faces different industry dynamics. “In this manner, the two listed entities can each pursue growth opportunities that are more aligned with their own industry dynamics, leading to improved operational efficiencies and profitability.”
- *Scheme* — Scale of what is actually moving: the demerged undertaking's turnover was only INR 70 crores for the year ended 31 December 2025, about 0.4% of TCIL's standalone turnover — six Nature Trails resorts. “The turnover of the Demerged Undertaking for the year ended 31st December 2025 was INR 70 Crores representing ~0.4% of the total standalone turnover of the Company for the year ended 31st December 2025.”
- *Scheme* — Consideration is all-paper at 81:100, no cash; TCIL retains its existing SHRL stake, leaving promoters at 65.55% (including 7% held by TCIL) and public at 32.30% of SHRL. “for every 100 (One Hundred only) equity shares of Thomas Cook (India) Limited of face value of INR 1/- each credited as fully paid up, the issue and allotment by Sterling Holiday Resorts Limited of 81 (Eighty One only) equity shares of Sterling Holiday Resorts Limited of face value of INR 10/-each credited as fully paid up ("Share Entitlement Ratio").”

*Not explained on the calls:* No valuation methodology or derivation of the 81:100 ratio, no quantified value unlock or SHRL financials post-demerger, no accounting treatment of the capital reduction, no shareholder-vote or listing-date specifics.

## HEGAM — HEG Advanced Materials Ltd.

**CONFIRMED** (a demerger scheme is on the exchange record) · **LISTED <1Y — selling-pressure window; the bargain forms here** · score 4.2/10 · spin-off · 48 filing(s) from BSE-screener, NSE, NSE-register · first 2026-01-09, latest 2026-11-04

> **Listing:** LISTED — HEG Graphite Limited trades since about 2026-09-07 (record date 2026-09-07)

**The stages, as filed:** announced (2026-10-15) → meetings (2026-04-02) → nclt_sanction (2026-05-05) → effective (2026-08-24) → record_date (2026-09-07)

**Stated in the filings:** resulting company **HEG Graphite Limited**; demerged undertaking: — i.e., the Company's graphite business — is to be demerged from HEG Limited into HEG Graphite; entitlement **1 for every 1**; record date 2026-09-07; appointed date 2024-04-01; size hint: 0% of ebitda.

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** The Graphite Undertaking — graphite electrodes business plus overseas investment and TAWA power plant assets/liabilities — class `not stated`.

- *Insiders:* Ravi Jhunjhunwala is Chairman, MD & CEO of HEG Limited (Resulting Company); son Riju Jhunjhunwala chairs HEGAM. Promoter stake in new entity not stated.
- *What it reveals:* Graphite carried Rs 4,601.53 cr assets vs Rs 1,357.07 cr liabilities (June 30, 2026) and earned Rs 319.71 cr H1 FY27 PAT; parent keeps debt-free hydro with over Rs 300 cr annual cash flows and Rs 1,322.84 cr cash.
- *Selling pressure:* likely — 1 share issued to every HEGAM holder; shares still unlisted pending trading approval; graphite is a different industry from parent's advanced materials/power.
- *Parent or spin:* spin · *option pricing date:* not stated (ESOP 2026 approved by Board November 3, 2026; pricing formula 'As per Scheme (as determined by Nomination and Remuneration Committee)')
- *Read next:* HEG Limited's listing/trading approval intimation, and its standalone balance sheet borrowings of Rs 708.97 cr.
- *In their words:* “Under the Scheme, the graphite electrodes business was transferred to HEG Limited (earlier known as HEG Graphite Limited), and Bhilwara Energy Limited was amalgamated into the Company.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

HEGAM's separation is the "Composite Scheme of Arrangement" among HEG Advanced Materials Limited (formerly HEG Limited, the Demerged Company), HEG Limited (formerly HEG Graphite Limited, the Resulting Company) and Bhilwara Energy Limited (the Transferor Company): the legacy Graphite Undertaking — the graphite electrodes business, plus the overseas investment and the assets and liabilities of the TAWA power plant — was demerged into the Resulting Company on a going-concern basis with mirror shares issued to HEGAM shareholders, while Bhilwara Energy Limited was simultaneously amalgamated into HEGAM. As the filings present it, the purpose is to put the mature, cyclical electrodes business (FY26 revenue ₹2,568.50 crore, H1 FY27 ₹1,207.36 crore and PAT ₹192.33 crore, carrying ₹4,419.21 crore of segment assets and ₹1,245.85 crore of liabilities) in one listed vehicle, and leave HEGAM as a "technology-led, globally competitive advanced materials platform" spanning anode materials (TACC), graphene (HEG Graphene Materials), battery energy storage (Replus Engitech, 74% held) and green power. The amalgamation of Bhilwara Energy brings 278 MW of debt-free hydro (86 MW MPCL + 192 MW AD Hydro) plus 14 MW of wind into HEGAM, which the CFO says "provides a sound financial foundation for the Group" with "stable cash flows of over ₹300 crore" annually — i.e. the hydro cash flow and the ₹1,322.84 crore cash pile now sit against the heavy new-materials capex rather than against electrodes. The problem it solves is capital allocation and identity: HEGAM's board on 3 November 2026 approved a revised Phase-1 anode cost of ~₹2,350 crore (20,000 MT, COD June 2027, 61% built), a ₹1,606 crore Phase-2 to 44,000 MT by March 2029, a ₹475 crore crucible plant for "backward integration" and cost optimisation, and a ₹500 crore 500 MTPA graphene plant — none of which belong on an electrode balance sheet. The company also altered its main object clause to insert "Anode, Graphene, crucible, advanced carbon materials and other allied material" (CIN changed from L23109MP1972PLC008290 to L35100MP1972PLC008290) and implemented an ESOP of up to 98,93,970 options, so each entity can be objected, incentivised and financed on its own. Leadership was split along the same line: Ravi Jhunjhunwala moved to Chairman, MD & CEO of the demerged HEG Limited (graphite), while Riju Jhunjhunwala leads HEGAM and has now taken the chair of MPCL and AD Hydro. A lender appears in the record on the power side: CYHPL bought Statkraft's 49% of MPCL on 17 November 2025 and intends to merge MPCL and ADHPL into itself "for consolidating the hydro power asstes of the group in the CYHPL in line with undertaking given by CYHPL to ICICI Bank."

**How it evolved:** No earnings-call transcripts were supplied, so the sequence can only be traced through filings: by 19 January 2026 the Scheme was already public enough to warrant an investor "Webinar on Update on Composite Scheme of Arrangement," and the 49% MPCL buy-out from Statkraft (SPA 9 September 2025, closed 17 November 2025) had pre-positioned the hydro assets. Shareholders approved it at the NCLT-convened meeting on 5 May 2026 with requisite majority; the NCLT Indore Bench sanctioned it on 13 August 2026; the board fixed 1 September 2026 as Effective Date (Appointed Date backdated to 1 April 2024) and allotted the new shares on 7 September 2026, lifting paid-up capital from ₹38.60 crore to ₹65.96 crore. Only after effectiveness did the plan visibly widen from "separate graphite" to "build out advanced materials": the 3 November 2026 board added Phase-2 anode (44,000 MT), crucibles, graphene, an ESOP and the new object clause, while on 29–30 October 2026 the object-clause CIN change was registered and HEGAM had to publish the unlisted Resulting Company's results on its behalf pending listing.

**What management expects from it:** Graphite stands alone as HEG Limited (FY26 revenue ₹2,568.50 crore), pending listing. HEGAM becomes a focused advanced-materials platform — anode 20,000→44,000 MT, crucibles, 500 MTPA graphene, Replus BESS (1→6 GWh), 278 MW debt-free hydro giving ₹300 crore-plus annual cash flow and ₹1,322.84 crore cash to fund capex — with diversified revenues, ESOP-aligned talent and "multiple avenues for value creation."

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *Scheme* — The Scheme's core mechanic: the Graphite Undertaking — including the overseas investment and the TAWA power plant assets and liabilities — goes out to the Resulting Company, and Bhilwara Energy comes in. “the demerger of the Graphite Undertaking including overseas investment and assets and liabilities pertaining to TAWA power plant of the Company into the Resulting Company and amalgamation of the Transferor Company with the Company”
- *Scheme* — The press release states plainly what moved where on the 1 September 2026 effective date, and that the two sides are now reported separately as continuing and discontinued operations. “Under the Scheme, the graphite electrodes business was transferred to HEG Limited (earlier known as HEG Graphite Limited), and Bhilwara Energy Limited was amalgamated into the Company.”
- *Scheme* — Riju Jhunjhunwala frames the remaining entity's purpose as a technology-led advanced materials platform across anode, graphene, BESS and green power, with "research to revenue" as the motto. “Q2 FY27 reflects our continued progress towards building HEG Advanced Materials into a technology -led, globally competitive advanced materials platform.”
- *Scheme* — CFO Neha Rajvanshi explains the financial logic of pulling hydro in: the debt-free green power business funds and underwrites the developmental verticals. “Our Green Power Business, with its differentiated model, profitable operations, debt -free position and stable cash flows, provides a sound financial foundation for the Group.”
- *Scheme* — The scale of that foundation: 278 MW of hydro in Himachal (86 MW MPCL + 192 MW AD Hydro) plus 14 MW wind, all debt-free, against H1 FY27 cash of ₹1,322.84 crore. “Both operating hydro projects and the wind project are debt -free, and the existing hydro assets generate annually stable cash flows of over ₹300 crore.”
- *Scheme* — Immediately post-demerger the board sanctioned the capex the new entity exists to carry: Phase-1 20,000 MT anode revised to ~₹2,350 crore (COD June 2027), Phase-2 24,000 MT for ~₹1,606 crore to reach 44,000 MT by March 2029. “Proposal for expansion plan by increasing the capacity from 20,000 MT to 44,000 MT.  The estimated cost is ~ Rs. 1606 crore with target COD by March 2029.”
- *Scheme* — The ₹475 crore, 80,000-unit crucible plant is justified as backward integration into the anode line rather than as a new market. “The project is expected to strengthen backward integration, optimize procurement costs, and improve operational  efficiencies,  thereby supporting the long-term growth and competitiveness of the subsidiary.”
- *Scheme* — The ₹500 crore, 500 MTPA graphene plant in HEG Graphene Materials Limited is positioned as a new growth avenue built through a subsidiary. “The proposed project is expected to create a new avenue for business growth through the subsidiary, strengthen the Company's long-term business prospects, and contribute to sustainable  value  creation  for stakeholders”
- *Scheme* — The legal identity was re-pointed at the new businesses: the object clause was amended to insert anode, graphene, crucible and advanced carbon materials, which changed the CIN from L23109MP1972PLC008290 to L35100MP1972PLC008290. “Alteration of the main object clause of Memorandum of Association (MOA) of the company by inserting the objects relating to Anode, Graphene, crucible, advanced carbon materials and other allied material, subject to the approval of shareholders.”
- *Scheme* — A lender's requirement drives the parallel power-side restructuring: CYHPL, having bought Statkraft's 49% of MPCL on 17 November 2025, plans to acquire the remaining 51% and merge MPCL and ADHPL into itself. “Theproposed acquisition andmerger isbeing done forconsolidating thehydro power asstes of the group in the CYHPL in line with undertaking given by CYHPL to ICICI Bank.”
- *Scheme* — Shareholders, not just the board, carried the Scheme — approved at the NCLT-convened meeting of 5 May 2026, sanctioned by NCLT Indore on 13 August 2026, effective 1 September 2026 with 1 April 2024 as appointed date. “The equity shareholders at the NCLT -convened meeting held on May 05, 2026  have passed the resolution with requisite majority approv ing the Scheme .”
- *Scheme* — Management had been briefing investors on the Scheme well before effectiveness, via a dedicated webinar in January 2026. “Please find below the link for Video Recording of Webinar on Update on Composite Scheme of Arrangement held on 19th January, 2026 at 1600 hrs IST.”

*Not explained on the calls:* No earnings-call transcripts were provided, so no Q&A, no Scheme rationale clause, no share-exchange ratio, valuation, debt allocation, target multiples, or named investor/partner demands.

## LLOYDSENT — Lloyds Enterprises Ltd.

**CONFIRMED** (a demerger scheme is on the exchange record) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 4.2/10 · spin-off · 6 filing(s) from NSE · first 2025-11-11, latest 2026-05-19

> **Listing:** NOT YET — scheme at 'exchange_noc' stage; the resulting company will list only after NCLT sanction, effectiveness and a record date; indicated timeline: NSE letter dated May 15, 2026: "Lloyds Realty Limited shall ensure that steps for listing of specified securities are completed and trading in securities commences within sixty days of receipt of the order of the Hon'ble High Court/NCLT"; listing "is at the discretion of the Exchange" and subject to SEBI approval. Chairman, 9 July 2026: "our real estate business will be listed". Scheme still pending NCLT (applications filed; Observation Letters received 15 May 2026, valid six months).

**The stages, as filed:** exchange_noc (2026-05-16)

**Stated in the filings:** demerged undertaking: as deﬁned in the Scheme) of the; entitlement **1 for every 2**.

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** The Real Estate Business Undertaking of Lloyds Enterprises Limited, demerged into Lloyds Realty Limited, a new unlisted resulting company — class `value_unlocking`.

- *Insiders:* Not stated — no promoter/management stake in Lloyds Realty Limited disclosed; all holders, promoters included, receive 1 LRL share of Rs. 1 for every 2 LEL shares held
- *What it reveals:* Real estate segment assets Rs. 993.09 cr vs liabilities Rs. 553.40 cr, 9M FY26 sales Rs. 53.30 cr and segment result Rs. 0.88 cr, yet "nearly 14 million square feet of upcoming projects under development" across MMR, Panvel, Khopoli, Dadar, Thane
- *Selling pressure:* likely — Small real-estate entity split from a trading/engineering-and-investment holding company; newly listed, in no index; shares frozen until listing permission
- *Parent or spin:* spin · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* Lloyds Realty Limited's Information Memorandum and the scheme's valuation report — assets, liabilities and debt transferred to LRL
- *In their words:* “Importantly, as a result of the merger and demerger scheme approved during the year, our real estate business will be listed, unlocking its true potential and delivering greater value to shareholders.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

The separation at issue is the demerger of Lloyds Enterprises Limited's (LEL) Real Estate Business Undertaking into a new, separately listed vehicle, Lloyds Realty Limited (LRL), carried out inside a Composite Scheme of Arrangement under Sections 230–232 read with Section 66 of the Companies Act, 2013 that the Board approved on 22 December 2025; the same scheme first merges Lloyds Realty Developers Limited (LRDL, Transferor 1) and Indrajit Properties Private Limited (IPPL, Transferor 2) into LEL, so that all realty assets sit in one place before being carved out into LRL. The only rationale management itself states is in the Chairman's speech at the 40th AGM (9 July 2026): the merger-and-demerger scheme means 'our real estate business will be listed, unlocking its true potential and delivering greater value to shareholders', set against a realty platform spread across the Mumbai Metropolitan Region, Panvel, Khopoli, Dadar and Thane with 'nearly 14 million square feet of upcoming projects under development' — i.e. a capital-hungry pipeline that needs its own currency and price discovery. For the parallel group merger the Chairman gives the generic benefits: 'enhance operational efficiencies, optimize resource utilization, strengthen the overall business structure, and create sustainable long-term value for shareholders'. The filings show why real estate sat awkwardly inside LEL: for 9M FY26 the Real Estate segment did only ₹53.30 crore of revenue and ₹0.88 crore of segment result (down from ₹11.26 crore) on ₹993.09 crore of segment assets and ₹553.40 crore of segment liabilities, while Steel (₹492.80 crore revenue, ₹255.60 crore result) and Engineering (₹795.75 crore, ₹151.08 crore) carried the group, and subsidiary LRDL itself ran a ₹1.26 crore net loss; consolidated FY26 total income was ~₹2,200 crore against ~₹800 crore standalone, with LEL otherwise functioning as a holding/trading company (stakes of ~4.13% in Lloyds Metals and Energy, ~31% in Geomysore, and material subsidiary Lloyds Engineering Works with a group order book of ~₹8,000 crore and 44% PBT growth). No investor, lender or partner is named as having asked for the separation; the only parties on record demanding anything are the regulators — SEBI, NSE and BSE required LEL to disclose to shareholders the 'Need for the merger/demerger, rationale of the scheme and swap ratio', synergies, minority impact and a cost-benefit analysis, plus lender NOCs and 'Conditions imposed by lenders, if any'. The same unlock-by-listing logic recurs twice more in the group: LEWL's absorption of Lloyds Infra, Metalfab and Techno Industries to end 'silos' and create a ₹6,150 crore-order-book design-to-execution entity, and the SISCOL acquisition (88.12% for ~₹1,073.40 crore), where a DRHP within 30 months is meant to 'facilitate independent price discovery', market visibility and access to capital.

**How it evolved:** No earnings-call transcripts are on file, so the idea is traceable only through filings. It surfaces fully formed on 22 December 2025, when the Board approved the Composite Scheme (LRDL + IPPL into LEL, real-estate undertaking out into LRL) and filed it with BSE and NSE the same day; a week later (29 December 2025) the group announced the separate LEWL merger of LICL, Metalfab and Techno Industries, and the 9 February 2026 results notes restated the Scheme verbatim alongside a ₹500 crore NCD approval, the ₹361 crore Tata Capital/Bajaj Finance/Jio Credit borrowings and the block-deal sale of LEWL shares to Thriveni Earthmovers. On 15–16 May 2026 LEL received NSE's 'No objection' and BSE's 'no adverse observations' (with LRL's listing left to exchange discretion, an Information Memorandum, frozen shares and a 60-day post-NCLT listing timetable), followed on 18–19 May 2026 by exchange NOCs and CCI clearance for the LEWL merger; by the 9 July 2026 AGM the Chairman described the scheme as approved, an NCLT application filed, and the realty business as one that 'will be listed'.

**What management expects from it:** For the realty entity: a separate listing of the ~14 mn sq ft Mumbai-region pipeline, 'unlocking its true potential' and greater shareholder value. For the retained LEL group: enhanced operational efficiencies, optimised resource utilisation, a stronger business structure and sustainable long-term value, leaving a holding/trading company around LEWL (~₹8,000 crore order book, 44% PBT growth), Lloyds Metals, Geomysore and SISCOL.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *Scheme* — Board approval on 22 December 2025 of the Composite Scheme: LRDL and IPPL merge into LEL, and LEL's Real Estate Business Undertaking is demerged into Lloyds Realty Limited; filed with BSE and NSE the same day. “The Scheme is filed with Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) & National Stock Exchange (NSE) on December 22, 2025.”
- *Scheme* — The only explicit purpose management gives for the demerger, in the Chairman's speech at the 40th AGM (9 July 2026): a separate listing of the real estate business to unlock value, against a pipeline of nearly 14 million sq ft across MMR, Panvel, Khopoli, Dadar and Thane. “Importantly, as a result of the merger and demerger scheme approved during the year, our real estate business will be listed, unlocking its true potential and delivering greater value to shareholders.”
- *Scheme* — For the group merger leg, the Chairman offers only structural benefits, noting approvals from NSE, BSE and SEBI and an application filed with the NCLT. “This strategic merger is expected to enhance operational efficiencies, optimize resource utilization, strengthen the overall business structure, and create sustainable long-term value for shareholders.”
- *Scheme* — NSE's 15 May 2026 observation letter confirms the demerger is a route to a new listed realty entity, but conditions it on an Information Memorandum, newspaper advertisement, frozen shares until trading permission, and listing within 60 days of the NCLT order. “However, the listing of shares of Lloyds Realty Limited  is at the discretion of the Exchange.”
- *Scheme* — The parties actually demanding an articulated rationale are the regulators: SEBI and both exchanges ordered LEL to put the need, rationale, swap ratio, synergies, minority impact and cost-benefit analysis in the shareholder explanatory statement. “Need for the merger/demerger, rationale of the scheme and swap ratio, synergies of business of the entities involved in the scheme, impact of the scheme on the minority shareholders and cost benefit analysis of the scheme.”
- *Scheme* — Lenders are referenced only as a consent/disclosure requirement imposed by SEBI — NOCs from lending banks, FIs and debenture trustees, plus any lender-imposed conditions — not as instigators of the separation. “Conditions imposed by lenders, if any, may be disclosed to the public shareholders along with the impact of same on the scheme.”
- *Scheme* — The mirror-image transaction at material subsidiary LEWL (announced 29 December 2025) consolidates LICL, Metalfab and Techno Industries into one vertically integrated design-to-execution entity with a ~₹6,150 crore combined order book, ~38.1 crore new shares and equity rising from 147.42 to 185.52 crore shares, appointed date 1 April 2025. “By bringing Lloyds Infra, Metalfab, and Techno Industries under one banner, we are eliminating silos.”
- *Scheme* — The same unlock-by-separate-listing logic is applied to the June 2026 SISCOL acquisition (88.12% for ~₹1,073.40 crore; FY26 turnover ₹816.87 crore, net profit ₹43.42 crore), with a DRHP promised within 30 months of Stage 1. “The proposed listing of SISCOL is expected to facilitate independent price discovery of its business, enhance its market visibility and access to capital, and unlock value for all its stakeholders, including the Company as a significant shareholder.”
- *Scheme* — The filings' own numbers show the real-estate leg was the group's weakest earner before separation: 9M FY26 segment revenue of ₹53.30 crore and segment result of ₹0.88 crore (vs ₹11.26 crore a year earlier) on ₹993.09 crore of segment assets and ₹553.40 crore of segment liabilities, with LRDL itself loss-making. “We have not conducted a review of the Subsidiary (Lloyds Realty Developers Limited) included in the unaudited consolidated financial results. whose financial information reflects total revenues of <53.30 and total Net Loss after tax of t1.26. crores.”

*Not explained on the calls:* No earnings-call transcripts on file; no swap ratio, valuation, debt or asset split for LRL, no margin or capital targets, no timeline, no named investor or lender demand.
