## MAHSEAMLES — Maharashtra Seamless Ltd.

**CONFIRMED** (a demerger scheme is on the exchange record) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 4.2/10 · spin-off · 4 filing(s) from BSE-screener, NSE · first 2026-05-22, latest 2026-10-07

> **Listing:** NOT YET — scheme at 'announced' stage; MSL Seamless Tubes Limited will list only after NCLT sanction, effectiveness and a record date; indicated timeline: On 07 October 2026 (and earlier 22 May 2026): "Yes. The equity shares of MSTL and USL shall be listed and admitted to trading on BSE and NSE pursuant to the Scheme subject to receipt of requisite approvals from statutory and regulatory authorities." No expected listing date stated; Appointed Date 01st October 2026, NCLT approval pending.

**The stages, as filed:** announced (2026-10-07)

**Stated in the filings:** resulting company **MSL Seamless Tubes Limited**; demerged undertaking: 1 into MSL Seamless Tubes Limited; entitlement **1 for every 5**; appointed date 2026-10-01.

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** Two seamless pipe plants: Mangaon (125,000 MTPA) with Beed solar; Narketpally Telangana (200,000 MTPA) with Rajasthan solar and rig — class `value_unlocking`.

- *Insiders:* Promoter & Promoter Group get 70.3008% of each resulting company (1,88,40,507 of 2,67,99,850 shares), mirroring their MSL stake; no cash consideration; no other incentive disclosed.
- *What it reveals:* Separate reporting prices each plant's economics: UD1 Rs 793 crore turnover (16.98%), UD2 Rs 693 crore (14.84%), remaining Rs 3,185 crore (68.18%). Parent retains Nagothane plus Rs 3,115 crore treasury management said to back ~50% of market cap.
- *Selling pressure:* likely — Each spin tiny: ~15-17% of turnover, only 2,67,99,850 shares, 1 share per 5 held; rig/solar assets differ from pipes.
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* The full Scheme filed with NCLT: which specified assets, liabilities and the Rs 3,115 crore treasury stay with MSL.
- *In their words:* “The above share exchange ratios shall ensure same proportionate shareholding structure of Resulting Company 1 and Resulting Company 2 with Demerged Company and hence Scheme shall be value neutral to the Demerged Company's shareholders.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

This is not a sale but a three-way split by demerger: a Scheme of Arrangement approved by MSL's board (first on 22 May 2026, then re-approved 7 October 2026 with an Appointed Date of 1 October 2026) carves two 'Demerged Undertakings' out of Maharashtra Seamless into two wholly owned subsidiaries that will themselves be listed on BSE and NSE. Demerged Undertaking 1 — the Mangaon, Maharashtra seamless pipe plant (125,000 MTPA) plus the 10 MW captive solar plant at Beed — goes to MSL Seamless Tubes Limited (MSTL); Demerged Undertaking 2 — the Narketpally, Telangana seamless mill (200,000 MTPA), the Khetusar (20 MW) and Pokhran (5 MW) solar plants in Rajasthan, and the rig Jindal Explorer — goes to United Seamless Limited (USL), i.e. the asset base MSL bought out of IBC as United Seamless Tubulaar for INR477 crores plus INR73 crores of reactivation capex. On FY2025-26 operational turnover the split is Undertaking 1 INR793 crores (16.98%), Undertaking 2 INR693 crores (14.84%) and the residual company (Nagothane pipes, ERW, treasury) INR3,185 crores (68.18%) of INR4,671 crores. The board's stated reasons are that the undertakings have 'distinct geographies, product profiles, technologies used, operational requirements, customer profile and base, market focus, logistics consideration' — specifically three different mill technologies, CPE at Nagothane, MPM at Mangaon and FQM at Telangana, each needing its own modernization and technical expertise — so each should run as a focused, independently reported vertical. It also says manufacturing, drilling and renewable energy have 'different capital intensity and funding requirements', so splitting them allows better assessment of capital needs and more flexibility for expansion; the renewable plants are attached to the mills they can power; and the rig business, long described on calls as outside the core, is segregated because it has 'distinct operational and commercial characteristics as compared to the pipe manufacturing business'. No cash changes hands: shareholders get 1 share of INR5 in each resulting company for every 5 MSL shares, producing the same proportionate holding (promoter ~70.30%, public ~29.70%, 2,67,99,850 shares in each), which the filing calls 'value neutral'; creditor liabilities are neither reduced nor extinguished and travel with each undertaking. Notably, the nine earnings calls supplied — including Feb 2026, three months before the first board approval — contain no mention of a demerger at all; the only antecedents are repeated investor pressure to exit the rig and one shareholder's demand to split the company, and management's standing answer that it would continue 'in the steel pipe segment only' and that exit was 'for the Board to decide'.

**How it evolved:** The idea surfaced only as a rig exit: on the Feb 2024 call (30 Jan 2024) Chairman D.P. Jindal said of staying in rigs 'we have to take the appropriate decision at the right time', and on the Nov 2024 call (29 Oct 2024) an investor asked directly about demerging or selling the rig, to which management said it was something 'we want to do, but it is subject to Board approval'. Pressure widened over the next year: on the Feb 2025 call (28 Jan 2025) management personally agreed the rig-to-Jindal-Drilling structure 'doesn't look in line' with its governance clean-up, on the Jun 2025 call (27 May 2025) it confirmed 'there was a view of getting out of the rig business' with no board update, and on the Aug 2025 call (31 July 2025) a shareholder explicitly asked management to 'divide the company in two parts' — a holding company and a seamless company — and got only 'I don't have anything to add'. By the Nov 2025 call (5 Nov 2025) there was still 'no update on the proposal', and the Feb 2026 call (29 Jan 2026) discussed only cash conservation, treasury and a hunt for distressed acquisitions. The actual plan then appeared without any call commentary: board approval 22 May 2026, a 15 June 2026 notice that the Scheme was 'under further review', and a revised, re-approved Scheme on 7 October 2026 that widened it from a rig/holding split into a full three-way break-up of the three mills by technology, with 'related assets and liabilities' tightened to 'specified assets and liabilities' and 'mirror shareholding' restated as 'same proportionate shareholding'.

**What management expects from it:** Per the Scheme only: each mill run as a focused vertical with dedicated management and technology-specific modernization; sharper assessment and deployment of capital across pipes, drilling and renewables, with more flexibility for expansion; solar assets aligned to the mills they serve; the rig managed on its own terms; independent reporting improving transparency and performance evaluation; identical proportionate shareholding, so value-neutral. No margin, cost, ROCE or valuation figures were given.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *Scheme* — Two undertakings are carved out into two wholly owned subsidiaries, MSL Seamless Tubes Limited and United Seamless Limited, both to be listed, with an Appointed Date of 1 October 2026; the Mangaon 125,000 MTPA mill and the 10 MW Beed captive solar plant form Undertaking 1. “Demerged Undertaking 1: Seamless pipe manufacturing business of the Demerged Company located at Mangaon, Maharashtra (125,000 MTPA), captive solar power plant at Beed, Maharashtra (10 MW), along with the specified assets and liabilities of Demerged Undertaking 1.”
- *Scheme* — Undertaking 2 bundles the Telangana (Narketpally) 200,000 MTPA mill with the Rajasthan solar plants and the rig Jindal Explorer into United Seamless Limited — effectively re-separating the ex-United Seamless Tubulaar asset base and the rig in one entity. “Demerged Undertaking 2: Seamless pipe manufacturing facility of the Demerged Company located at Narketpally, Telangana (200,000 MTPA), solar power plants at Khetusar (20 MW) & Pokhran (5MW) in Rajasthan, rig Jindal Explorer along with the specified assets and liabilities of Demerged Undertaking 2.”
- *Scheme* — The headline justification is that one company holds businesses with nothing in common operationally — different geographies, products, technologies, customers and logistics — so each should be managed separately. “The said undertakings having distinct geographies, product profiles, technologies used, operational requirements, customer profile and base, market focus, logistics consideration, commercial considerations and growth opportunities.”
- *Scheme* — The most concrete operating reason given is that the three mills run on three different pipe-making technologies, each needing its own specialised management and modernization programme — which maps exactly onto the three-way split. “The manufacturing facilities operate on different technological platforms, including CPE technology at Nagothane, MPM technology at Mangaon and FQM technology at Telangana, each requiring specialized operational management, modernization initiatives and technical expertise.”
- *Scheme* — Capital allocation is cited: pipes, drilling and renewables have different capital intensity, so separation is meant to let each assess and fund its own needs — relevant given the stalled INR852 crore capex plan and the INR350 crore Nagothane hot-mill upgrade never started. “Efficient Capital Allocation: The manufacturing, drilling and renewable energy businesses have different capital intensity and funding requirements.”
- *Scheme* — The rig is singled out for segregation on the grounds that it is commercially unlike pipe manufacturing — the same objection investors had raised on calls for two years. “Focused Development of Rig Operations: The rig business has distinct operational and commercial characteristics as compared to the pipe manufacturing business.”
- *Scheme* — The renewable plants are deliberately attached to the mills they sit beside rather than kept central, framed as energy-management efficiency and sustainability support for each business. “The renewable power assets proposed to be transferred along with the respective undertakings are expected to provide better operational alignment, energy management efficiencies and support sustainability initiatives of the corresponding businesses.”
- *Scheme* — Separate financial and operational reporting per entity is itself presented as a benefit — transparency and performance evaluation — which speaks to the calls where management refused to give product-wise or mill-wise margins. “Improved Transparency and Value Creation: The proposed demerger would result in creation of focused business entities with independent financial and operational reporting, thereby enhancing transparency, improving performance evaluation and facilitating long-term value creation for stakeholders.”
- *Scheme* — No cash is paid; shareholders receive 1 INR5 share in each resulting company per 5 MSL shares, giving identical proportionate ownership (promoter 70.3008%, public 29.6992%, 2,67,99,850 shares each) and, the board says, value neutrality. “The above share exchange ratios shall ensure same proportionate shareholding structure of Resulting Company 1 and Resulting Company 2 with Demerged Company and hence Scheme shall be value neutral to the Demerged Company's shareholders.”
- *Scheme* — Lenders are explicitly left untouched: no arrangement or compromise with creditors, liabilities travelling with each undertaking — i.e. the split is not presented as lender-driven or a debt restructuring. “The liabilities towards the creditors of the Demerged Company and/or the Resulting Companies under the Scheme are neither being reduced nor being extinguished and the liabilities pertaining to the respective undertakings shall be assumed and discharged by the respective Resulting Companies in the ordinary course of business.”
- *Scheme* — The plan was not stable: approved 22 May 2026, pulled back for review on 15 June 2026, and re-approved only on 7 October 2026 with tightened wording ('specified' rather than 'related' assets, 'same proportionate' rather than 'mirror' shareholding) and slightly revised indicative share counts (promoter 70.2784% to 70.3008%). “This is further to the intimation dated 22nd May, 2026, about the approval of the Scheme of Arrangement by the Board of Directors of the Company, we have to inform you that the said Scheme is under further review and would be placed before any subsequent Board Meeting for its approval and would be submitted to Stock Exchanges thereafter.”
- *[Feb 2024](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=b72c7b85-4c69-46c2-a090-5ef0d9c829bd.pdf)* — The first hint of any separation was about the rig: asked whether MSL would keep two verticals, the Chairman declined to commit, while noting day rates had risen (~$40,000/day, expecting a new contract above $80,000). “Well, we have to take the appropriate decision at the right time.”

*Not explained on the calls:* No call ever mentioned it. Silent on where the ~INR3,500 crore treasury, debt, ERW and premium-connections subsidiary sit, on margins, valuation, lost shared overheads, and NCLT timing.

*Calls read (36 months):* [Nov 2023](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=132dfb4c-b880-4f4e-8e84-430872794cb3.pdf), [Nov 2024](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=527a8802-c766-46b3-bf40-c501d9bde473.pdf)

## RAYMOND — Raymond Ltd.

**CONFIRMED** (a demerger scheme is on the exchange record) · **LISTED 1–2Y — the second-year window** · score 4.2/10 · spin-off · 7 filing(s) from NSE, NSE-register · first 2024-07-11, latest 2026-11-02

> **Listing:** LISTED — Raymond Realty Limited trades since about 2025-05-14 (record date 2025-05-14)

**The stages, as filed:** record_date (2025-05-14)

**Stated in the filings:** resulting company **Raymond Realty Limited**; record date 2025-05-14; appointed date 2025-04-01; size hint: 13% of ebitda.

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** Real estate/realty business, demerged into Raymond Realty Limited; lifestyle business earlier demerged into Raymond Lifestyle Limited — class `regulatory_strategic`.

- *Insiders:* Promoter stewardship 48.87%–59.62% across the three listed entities; promoter largest shareholder and chairs the Board. Promoter-group JK Investors (Bombay) took 66,57,373 Raymond Ltd warrants at ₹497; Gautam Hari Singhania ultimate beneficial owner
- *What it reveals:* Realty holds 100-acre Thane land with ~₹25,000 cr revenue potential plus asset-light JDAs ~₹27,000 cr; H1FY27 pre-sales +111% to ₹1,602 cr, EBITDA +30%, but net debt ₹912 cr, D/E 0.8x and PAT down 14%
- *Selling pressure:* likely — Realty is a separate industry from lifestyle/engineering and contributed only ~23% of portfolio EBITDA in H1FY27
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* Raymond Realty Limited's own H1FY27 financials — ₹912 cr net debt, 1.70x net debt/EBITDA — against the ₹4,100 cr MMR launch pipeline
- *In their words:* “Having undertaken significant restructuring and demerger activities in recent years — including the demerger of its lifestyle and real estate business — Raymond is now positioned to pursue an accelerated, multi-sector growth strategy through its subsidiary companies”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

No earnings-call transcripts were supplied ("no transcripts on file"), so this reconstruction rests solely on Raymond Limited's filings. Management's own framing, set out in the EGM explanatory statements of May 25, 2026 and September 8, 2026, is that the separation is already executed — "the demerger of its lifestyle and real estate business" — leaving Raymond Limited as "a conglomerate which is in engineering businesses through its subsidiaries," namely JK Maini Precision Technology Limited (precision engineering and auto components) and JK Maini Global Aerospace Limited (aerospace / new-age industrial and technology-led businesses), while Raymond Lifestyle Limited (branded textile, branded apparel, garmenting, high-value shirting, emerging) and Raymond Realty Limited (100-acre Thane land ~₹25,000 cr revenue potential plus asset-light Mumbai JDAs ~₹27,000 cr potential) trade separately. The problem the structure is said to solve is focus and clean capital allocation: the Q2/H1 FY2027 group update (filed November 2, 2026) titles the result "Raymond Portfolio: Pure-Play Platforms" across three listed entities, each with its own ~75%-independent board (vs a ~50% top-100 Indian average), its own ring-fenced audit/pay/risk/related-party committees, its own CARE/CRISIL ratings (RLL AA/A1+, Raymond Realty and TenX A+/A-, JKMPTL A+/A1+, JKMGAL A/A1 within ₹9,476 cr rated debt) and its own balance sheet — group net debt/EBITDA 0.43x on TTM EBITDA of ₹1,738 cr and revenue of ₹13,115 cr, liquidity up from ₹571 cr in FY20 to ₹2,791 cr, and short-term debt cut from 74% of gross debt in 2020 to 38% in 2026 with 4.24-year average maturity. It also de-concentrates earnings: non-lifestyle verticals now generate 49% of YTD EBITDA (388.16 of 792), with engineering Raymond Ltd. posting H1FY27 income of ₹1,311 cr (+17%), EBITDA ₹203 cr (+22%), PBT ₹84 cr (+69%), aerospace & defence revenue ₹262 cr (+56%) and a ₹77 cr net cash surplus, against FY21 engineering revenue of just ₹141 cr and EBITDA of ₹22 cr. The separated, residual listed company is then being funded as an acquisition vehicle described as being "at a pivotal inflection point": ₹330.88 cr of 18-month warrants at ₹497 to promoter-group JK Investors (Bombay) Limited (29.83% to 35.91% diluted; ultimate beneficial owner Gautam Hari Singhania), then ₹214.71 cr at ₹645 to Minerva Ventures Fund (0% to ~4.31%, ultimate beneficial owner Ghanshyam Hurry), with 75% earmarked for Indian and international acquisitions in aerospace, automotive and defence including acquisition-debt repayment or bridge funding, and 25% for general corporate purposes, CARE Ratings appointed monitoring agency. Nobody outside is named as having demanded the separation: no investor campaign, lender covenant or JV partner appears in the texts; the visible external pressure is from the stock exchanges, whose queries forced a June 10, 2026 corrigendum and an October 22, 2026 restatement of the allottee's diluted stake. Running the other way, the January 27, 2026 Scheme folds wholly-owned Everblue Apparel Limited (denim garmenting, ₹10,858 lakh turnover) back into Raymond Limited "to enable simplified structure and greater management focus," so the pattern management describes is separation of the big consumer and property platforms combined with re-absorption of small subsidiaries into the listed engineering holdco.

**How it evolved:** The idea is presented as already settled rather than emerging: by the January 27, 2026 Everblue Apparel amalgamation filing, Raymond Limited is described as holding "investment in Engineering and Aerospace business through its subsidiaries" with standalone turnover of only ₹289 lakh, and the scheme's stated logic is simplification and management focus. The May 25, 2026 board outcome and May 27, 2026 EGM notice first spell out the post-separation rationale — demerger done, engineering holdco now raising ₹330.88 cr of promoter warrants for a multi-sector growth strategy through JKMPTL and JKMGAL — and that framing is repeated verbatim in the September 8/11, 2026 notice for the ₹214.71 cr Minerva Ventures Fund issue. The plan changed under exchange pressure: the June 10, 2026 corrigendum deleted "Capital expenditure and capacity expansion at subsidiary companies" and recast 75% of proceeds as acquisitions "including repayment of acquisition debt," the June 18, 2026 EGM passed with 31.72% of public-institution votes against, and the June 24-25, 2026 rumour verification on a German target (Deharde) was answered as speculative. By the November 2, 2026 Q2/H1 FY2027 group update the separation is marketed as three "Pure-Play Platforms" with per-entity boards, ratings and balance sheets, and the second raise (approved October 3, 2026 with 99.998% in favour) was granted exchange in-principle approval on November 6, 2026.

**What management expects from it:** Three focused listed platforms, each with its own board, ratings and balance sheet. Lifestyle: premiumisation, net cash of ₹69 cr. Realty: ~20% pre-sales growth, 17-19% EBITDA margin, ~20% ROCE, 9-10% PAT margin, debt/equity below 1.0x. Engineering Raymond Ltd.: aerospace scale-up at ~21% segment margins, operating leverage (PBT margin 6.4% vs 4.4%), and warrant capital for acquisitions without pre-funding dilution.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *Scheme* — The May 27, 2026 EGM explanatory statement states the separation is complete and defines what the residual listed company now is — an engineering holdco operating through JKMPTL and JKMGAL. “Raymond Limited ("Company") is a conglomerate which is in engineering businesses through its subsidiaries and has consistently invested in building world-class capabilities across its business verticals.”
- *Scheme* — The same statement (repeated in the September 11, 2026 notice) gives the explicit cause-and-effect: because lifestyle and real estate were demerged, the remaining entity can pursue a focused multi-sector engineering strategy. “Having undertaken significant restructuring and demerger activities in recent years — including the demerger of its lifestyle and real estate business — Raymond is now positioned to pursue an accelerated, multi-sector growth strategy through its subsidiary companies, including:”
- *Scheme* — Management frames the moment created by the separation as requiring fresh growth capital, which is what both warrant issues (₹330.88 cr to promoter group JK Investors (Bombay) Limited at ₹497, ₹214.71 cr to Minerva Ventures Fund at ₹645) are for. “The Company is at a pivotal inflection point in its growth trajectory.”
- *Scheme* — The November 2, 2026 Q2/H1 FY2027 group update brands the outcome of the demergers as three single-focus listed platforms: Raymond Lifestyle Limited, Raymond Realty Limited and Raymond Limited (Aerospace & Defence plus Precision Technology and Auto Components). “Raymond Portfolio: Pure-Play Platforms”
- *Scheme* — The same update argues the separation de-risks group earnings by removing reliance on the lifestyle business, quantifying the shift precisely for H1FY27. “Non-lifestyle verticals (Realty + Raymond Ltd.) now generate 49% of YTD EBITDA (388.16 of 792), signalling an increasingly balanced, multi-engine growth profile.”
- *Scheme* — Governance is presented as a deliberate consequence of splitting into three listed vehicles — independent boards and independently chaired audit, pay, risk and related-party committees at each entity, above what LODR requires. “This is not a statutory response to LODR, LODR would allow far less. It is a deliberate architecture.”
- *Scheme* — Each separated entity carries its own leverage, liquidity and rating profile: group net debt/EBITDA 0.43x, ₹1,738 cr TTM EBITDA, ₹3,382 cr cash, with Raymond Limited at -0.34x and Raymond Realty at 1.70x; the engineering arm reports a ₹77 cr net cash surplus. “Net cash surplus of Rs77 Cr as of September 2026, backing disciplined growth investments.”
- *Scheme* — Who actually put up money: the promoter group, not an outside activist or lender — the May 2026 issue is justified on promoter conviction and on speed versus a QIP or rights issue, given time-sensitive acquisition targets. “Promoter participation in the fund-raise demonstrates a strong personal commitment and conviction in the Company's strategic direction.”
- *Scheme* — The stock exchanges, not investors, forced disclosure changes: NSE (June 3, 2026) and BSE (June 8, 2026) queries produced a corrigendum that dropped subsidiary capex/capacity expansion and re-labelled 75% of proceeds as acquisition funding including acquisition-debt repayment. “Funding acquisitions of businesses in India and internationally across targeted growth sectors either directly or through subsidiary entities for organic and inorganic growth including repayment of acquisition debt upto 75% of the aggregate proceeds of the issue; and”
- *Scheme* — Public institutions were not uniformly convinced by the promoter-funded step: 31.72% of institutional votes polled went against the June 18, 2026 resolution (overall 96.36% in favour), whereas the October 3, 2026 Minerva resolution passed with 99.9978% in favour and institutions 100% in favour. “Whether promoter/promoter group are interested in the agenda/resolution? Yes”
- *Scheme* — Asked on June 24-25, 2026 about a reported German engineering acquisition (Deharde), the company neither confirmed a target nor denied the programme, pointing back to the stated objects of the warrant issue. “The Company evaluates various strategic opportunities in the ordinary course, for growth and expansion of its business.”
- *Scheme* — The January 27, 2026 Scheme of Amalgamation runs opposite to the demergers — wholly-owned Everblue Apparel Limited (denim garmenting, ₹10,858 lakh turnover, ₹376 lakh net worth) is absorbed into Raymond Limited with no shares issued, purely for structural simplicity and focus. “To enable simplified structure and greater management focus on the business, it is imperative for the Transferor Company to be merged into the Transferee Company.”

*Not explained on the calls:* No earnings-call transcripts were provided; filings never explain demerger mechanics, ratios, record dates, costs, who requested it, or why garmenting sits under the engineering holdco.

> **Listing:** LISTED — the resulting company trades since about 2025-05-22 (record date 2025-05-22)

**The stages, as filed:** nclt_sanction (2026-07-02) → effective (2026-02-10) → record_date (2025-05-22)

**Stated in the filings:** record date 2025-05-22.

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** Madura Fashion & Lifestyle Business, demerged from ABFRL into wholly owned subsidiary Aditya Birla Lifestyle Brands Limited, effective May 1, 2025 — class `not stated`.

- *Insiders:* Not stated. Documents only state every ABFRL shareholder on record date May 22, 2025 received 1 ABLBL share per ABFRL share; no promoter stake or incentive disclosure.
- *What it reveals:* The departed MFL business was the profitable half (FY25 discontinued-operations PBT Rs 230.97 crore on revenue Rs 7,618.62 crore), leaving a loss-making, cash-consuming parent: FY26 revenue Rs 8,177 crore, PAT loss Rs 830 crore, FCF positive only by FY29.
- *Selling pressure:* unclear — Documents give 1:1 distribution to all shareholders and listing date, but no size, index or shareholder-base detail; same fashion-retail industry.
- *Parent or spin:* spin · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* Aditya Birla Lifestyle Brands Limited's own standalone results — the demerged MFL business's post-listing revenue, margin and debt
- *In their words:* “The Equity Shares of the Resulting Company listed on BSE Limited and the National Stock Exchange of India Limited on June 23, 2025.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

The business being separated is the Madura Fashion & Lifestyle / western-wear branded-apparel business — Louis Philippe-type premium lifestyle brands plus Reebok, American Eagle, Van Heusen Innerwear and the (exited) Forever 21 — demerged out of ABFRL into a separately listed Aditya Birla Lifestyle Brands Limited (ABLBL), leaving in ABFRL the Pantaloons/OWND (ex-Style Up) masstige-value play, the ethnic portfolio (Sabyasachi, Tarun Tahiliani, House of Masaba, Shantnu & Nikhil, Tasva, Jaypore, TCNS/W-Aurelia), luxury (The Collective, Galeries Lafayette) and digital-first TMRW. Management's stated reason is a capital-allocation and focus problem inside one company: ABLBL is a mature, high-margin, cash-generating platform (FY25 normalized revenue INR7,830 crores, EBITDA margin 16.2%, up 100bps; Q4 FY25 EBITDA margin 17%, +200bps; brands at 19.3% FY25 margin, retail LTL 9-12%) whose growth lever — an 'aggressive' net 300+ store rollout, 200 of them own-capex — was 'underleveraged in the combined entity', so the demerger was explicitly designed to 'leave that cash for allowing that business to soar' and let it invest through downcycles when franchisees cannot. Conversely the retained ABFRL is a portfolio of loss-making/investment-phase businesses (TCNS, Tasva, Style Up/OWND, Galeries Lafayette, TMRW) that needed a clean, cash-rich balance sheet: ABFRL raised USD 490 million via QIP plus preferential issue (promoters paying a significant premium) to make demerged ABFRL 'debt-free' with gross cash of INR2,350 crores at consolidation, versus ABLBL starting with ~INR700-781 crores net debt to be repaid in 2-3 years. Dikshit framed the underlying problem as too many simultaneous growth bets starving each other of attention — 'Innerwear will get the attention which it would not have got when we had 5 or 6 such growth opportunities in front of us' — i.e. separation is about focus, differentiated capital structures (dividend-paying ABLBL vs. investment-funding ABFRL) and separate value-creation journeys. The same philosophy is applied one level down: TMRW was built as a separate company from 2021 precisely so it would raise its own capital (INR437 crores from ServiceNow Ventures for ~11%, INR440-450 crores equity in FY26, INR500 crores NCDs, ~INR800 crores cash) and eventually have 'its own public market journey'. Mechanically the demerger was Board-approved 19 April 2024, shareholder-approved 21 January 2025, NCLT-sanctioned 27 March 2025, effective 1 May 2025 with an appointed date of 1 April 2024, a 1:1 share entitlement (1,22,02,94,773 ABLBL shares allotted 26 May 2025) and ABLBL listed 23 June 2025; it also reset intercompany accounting, producing a one-off INR97 crore gain from ending inter-division elimination on Madura stock sold through Pantaloons and INR148 crore of depreciation not charged on discontinued operations. Targets attached to the split: ABLBL to 'double in scale' and expand margins over five years and pay dividends at the earliest opportunity; ABFRL to deliver 3x revenue and 2x margin over five years, with most of that margin uplift coming from turning TCNS, Tasva and TMRW from EBITDA-negative to profitable.

**How it evolved:** The demerger was Board-approved on 19 April 2024 and by the Feb 17, 2025 call was 'progressing well', with NCLT listed for the third week of March 2025, the USD 490 million QIP/preferential raise just closed, and guidance that ABLBL would open FY26 with INR700 crores debt while demerged ABFRL held ~INR1,300-1,500 crores cash; in that call the rationale sharpened from generic 'unlock value' into the specific point that Lifestyle Brands' store expansion had been 'underleveraged in the combined entity'. By the May 26, 2025 call it was 'successfully completed' — two 'focused fashion power houses', ABLBL shares allotted 1:1, ABFRL carrying INR2,350 crores gross cash, with the first explicit five-year targets (ABLBL to double in scale and pay dividends; ABFRL 3x revenue, 2x margin) and the clearest statement of cause, that a combined ABFRL with '5 or 6' growth opportunities starved businesses like Innerwear of attention. The Aug 14, 2025 call confirmed completion and listing on 23 June 2025 and extended the same logic to TMRW raising its own external capital, and by the Nov 2025/Feb 2026/May 2026 calls the demerger survives only as an accounting comparability footnote (the INR97 crore base-quarter gain) while the structural work shifts to simplification inside ABFRL — the Feb 5, 2026 Scheme amalgamating wholly-owned Jaypore E-Commerce and TG Apparel & Decor into ABFRL, NCLT-sanctioned 2 July 2026 and effective 1 August 2026.

**What management expects from it:** ABLBL: own cash flows fund 300+ net stores, scale to double and margins expand from 16.2%, INR781 crore net debt repaid in 2-3 years, dividends paid early. Demerged ABFRL: debt-free with INR2,350 crore cash to fund OWND, Tasva, TCNS, luxury and TMRW; 3x revenue and 2x margin in five years, chiefly by turning TCNS, Tasva and TMRW profitable; sharper focus and attention per business.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *[Feb 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=86aee500-e77b-4d18-9566-af83384f5a37.pdf)* — First formal framing of the separation: the western-wear brands business is being carved into a separate listed entity, ABLBL, with NCLT scheduled for the third week of March 2025 and completion expected in 2-3 months. “First, the demerger of western wear brands business into a separate entity, that is Aditya Birla Lifestyle Brands Limited, or ABLBL, is progressing well and set for completion within the next 2, 3 months.”
- *[Feb 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=86aee500-e77b-4d18-9566-af83384f5a37.pdf)* — The USD 490 million QIP plus preferential issue was raised inside the pre-demerger company specifically so the retained ABFRL would emerge debt-free with enough cash to fund its loss-making businesses until self-sustaining. “The fundraise within demerged ABFRL will strengthen its balance sheet by making it debt-free and leaving enough cash in the books to take care of the growth needs of its businesses until they become self-sustainable.”
- *[Feb 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=86aee500-e77b-4d18-9566-af83384f5a37.pdf)* — Capital structures were deliberately split asymmetrically — debt with the cash-generating lifestyle entity, cash with the investment-phase entity. “We expect ABLBL to start the next year with opening debt of INR700 crores, whereas demerged ABFRL will have a likely cash balance of approximately INR1,300 crores.”
- *[Feb 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=86aee500-e77b-4d18-9566-af83384f5a37.pdf)* — The sharpest stated rationale: Lifestyle Brands' store-expansion opportunity was under-exploited while inside the combined company, and the demerger was designed to free its own cash for that expansion (300+ stores, ~200 own-capex). “And one of the strategic rationale for the demerger was to leave that cash for allowing that business to soar.”
- *[Feb 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=86aee500-e77b-4d18-9566-af83384f5a37.pdf)* — A second, cyclical argument: as a standalone entity ABLBL can self-fund store rollout when franchisee partners pull back in weak demand periods. “Lifestyle Brands particularly also will have access to their own cash. So their ability to grow even in downtimes, when franchisees sometimes are not in a position to invest during the low time, the business will be able to sort of short circuit that and invest deeper.”
- *[Feb 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=86aee500-e77b-4d18-9566-af83384f5a37.pdf)* — The umbrella justification offered to investors was value unlock via two independently capitalised, independently growing entities. “The completion of these steps in the next 2, 3 months will enable us to unlock value through 2 independent entities, both with attractive growth potential and a strong balance sheet through a resilient growth-oriented business model sharpened over time.”
- *[May 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=29b83308-dd71-4b41-9802-e328e83350ee.pdf)* — Completion announced: demerger done, 1:1 entitlement, ABLBL shares allotted to ABFRL shareholders and listing targeted by end-June 2025. “We successfully completed the demerger, creating two focused fashion power houses, Aditya Birla Lifestyle Brands Limited, ABLBL; and Aditya Birla Fashion and Retail Limited, ABFRL, both now set on independent high-growth trajectories.”
- *[May 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=29b83308-dd71-4b41-9802-e328e83350ee.pdf)* — The underlying diagnosis stated plainly in answer to a question on why Innerwear had stagnated at ~INR500 crores since 2016 — one company carrying five or six growth bets could not give each the management attention and capital it needed, hence restructuring into separate entities. “I think as it becomes part of a company which is fundamentally profitable free cash flow generator and it's an important part of its growth journey, Innerwear will get the attention which it would not have got when we had 5 or 6 such growth opportunities in front of us.”
- *[May 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=29b83308-dd71-4b41-9802-e328e83350ee.pdf)* — Same answer gives the structural logic for the split: multiple growth opportunities in one company required separate capitalisation and structure. “ABFRL, the combined ABFRL business had multiple growth opportunities, and we realized at some point of time, that we'll have to capitalize it and structure it differently to pursue independent growth opportunities more aggressively.”
- *[May 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=29b83308-dd71-4b41-9802-e328e83350ee.pdf)* — Both halves were shown as independently healthy at separation — ABLBL Q4 margin +200bps (FY25 normalized revenue INR7,830 crores, 16.2% margin), demerged ABFRL Q4 EBITDA more than doubled to INR199 crores comparable. “Both entities delivered robust profitability, ABLBL clocking 200 basis points margin expansion, while demerged ABFRL more than doubling its EBITDA.”
- *[May 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=29b83308-dd71-4b41-9802-e328e83350ee.pdf)* — ABLBL is positioned as the self-funding, net-debt-INR781-crore, dividend-paying mature platform with a 300+ store FY26 pipeline, to double in scale over five years. “ABLBL shall be a dividend-distributing company at the earliest appropriate opportunity.”

## ABLBL — Aditya Birla Lifestyle Brands Ltd.

**CONFIRMED** (this company IS the resulting company of Aditya Birla Fashion and Retail Limited's demerger, listed on 2025-06-23 — the spun entity in its second year) · **LISTED 1–2Y — the second-year window** · score 3.6/10 · spin-off · 6 filing(s) from CALLS, NSE · first 2026-02-02, latest 2026-03-31

> **Listing:** THIS COMPANY IS THE SPIN-OFF — the resulting company of Aditya Birla Fashion and Retail Limited's demerger, listed on 2025-06-23 (515 days ago)

**The stages, as filed:** listed (2025-06-23)

**Stated in the filings:** entitlement **1 for every 1**.

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** Madura Fashion and Lifestyle ('MFL') branded apparel business demerged from Aditya Birla Fashion and Retail Limited — class `value_unlocking`.

- *Insiders:* Promoter stake not stated. Scheme: all ABFRL shareholders hold identical shareholdings in both companies. ABLBL Special Purpose ESOP — 2,09,236 shares allotted, 42,015 transferred from ESOP Trust; Employees' Welfare Trust from September 29, 2025.
- *What it reveals:* A ₹8,396 crore single-segment branded apparel business, FY26 EBITDA ₹1,429 crore (17%), pre-Ind AS PAT ₹313 crore versus reported ₹171 crore; net debt cut to ₹726 crore, first dividend paid, plus inherited ABFRL-era GST demands exceeding ₹310 crore.
- *Selling pressure:* likely — 1:1 shares allotted to entire ABFRL shareholder base on May 26, 2025; listed June 23, 2025 without any fundraise.
- *Parent or spin:* spin · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* Shareholding pattern / FY26 annual report for promoter stake and ESOP grants, and appeals against the ₹310 crore GST demand.
- *In their words:* “One of the primary reasons for demerger was to create an entity which can reinvest back more aggressively into growth.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

The only separation described in these documents is the one that created ABLBL itself: the Madura Fashion and Lifestyle ('MFL') business was demerged out of Aditya Birla Fashion and Retail Limited ('ABFRL'), approved by the ABFRL board on April 19, 2024, sanctioned by NCLT on March 27, 2025, effective May 1, 2025, with ABLBL shares issued 1:1 so shareholders hold identical stakes in both companies — ABLBL carries the four Lifestyle/Power brands (Louis Philippe, Van Heusen, Allen Solly, Peter England, plus formats like Peter England Red and the Philippe bridge-to-luxury store) and the Emerging portfolio (Reebok, Van Heusen Innerwear, American Eagle; Forever 21 was closed/restructured with a ₹98.33 crore exceptional charge and ~₹50 crore of EBITDA loss plus ~₹50 crore interest in the FY25 base), while ABFRL retains the newer 'tomorrow' businesses. Management's stated reason is capital allocation, not operations: the mature Madura cash flow had been funding other things. Ashish Dikshit (Q1 FY26, Aug 14, 2025): 'The cash generated by this business in the past has -- was used to actually kick start or acquire multiple new businesses. And the whole purpose of demerger was actually to need the cash for this business to grow faster.' He restated it in Q3 FY26 (Feb 3, 2026) as 'One of the primary reasons for demerger was to create an entity which can reinvest back more aggressively into growth,' quantifying it: the business throws off EBITDA cash of close to ₹900 crore, historical capex was only ₹150–200 crore (₹225 crore in the best years), and FY26 capex was taken 'north of INR300 crores, perhaps INR320 crores, INR330 crores' — which is also why debt fell only modestly. Separation also fixed the funding and payout frame: no equity fundraise in either entity (only the 'tomorrow business' excepted), borrowings split 'based on the allocation formula', a ₹500 crore NCD repaid in January 2026 and refinanced with 'no fresh borrowing', a stated path to debt-free in 2.5–3 years at ₹200–300 crore repayment a year, and, within year one post-demerger, a first dividend of 50 paise per share with a policy of ~15–25% of net profit. Visible results of that reinvestment: 300+ store additions in FY26 to 3,348 stores / 4.9 million sq ft / ~800 towns, FY26 revenue ₹8,396 crore (+7%), EBITDA ₹1,429 crore (+13%, margin 17%, +90bps), normalized PAT ₹209 crore (+61%), net debt ₹726 crore versus ₹781 crore. Nobody in these texts says investors, lenders or brand partners demanded the split; the only external pressure visible is analysts policing the no-fundraise promise and the debt-reduction pace.

**How it evolved:** The split was board-approved on April 19, 2024, NCLT-sanctioned March 27, 2025, effective May 1, 2025, with shares allotted May 26, 2025 and listing on June 23, 2025; the first post-demerger call (Aug 14, 2025) is where Dikshit framed the 'why' — cash previously used to kick-start/acquire new businesses would now fund this one, with 'first use of cash' for growth and 'only the subsequent part' for debt, ₹250 crore capex guided and debt-free in 2.5–3 years. Nov 5, 2025 added no new rationale, only execution and its cost — 65 store renovations in one quarter, debt up ~₹200 crore on festive inventory. Feb 3, 2026 sharpened it into a number: ~₹900 crore of EBITDA cash, capex lifted from ₹150–225 crore historically to ₹320–330 crore, explicitly explaining the small debt reduction, while Videesha Sheth challenged a ₹500 crore NCD against the no-fundraise commitment (answer: pure refinancing). By May 8, 2026 the emphasis shifted from reinvestment to returns — maiden 50 paise dividend 'within the first year of the company post-demerger', a 15–25% payout band, FY27 capex ~₹300 crore, and debt-free in three years described as achievable but 'not something that we are chasing'.

**What management expects from it:** For ABLBL: retained cash funds its own growth — capex up from ₹150-225 crore to ₹300-330 crore, 300+ stores a year, double-digit revenue growth, 7% steady LTL, Lifestyle margins ~20% improving on rent leverage, emerging brands to one-fourth of sales and rising EBITDA, debt-free in ~3 years, 15-25% dividend payout. For ABFRL: only implied — it keeps the newer 'tomorrow' businesses and the option to raise funds.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *Scheme* — The structure: ABFRL's board approved demerging the Madura Fashion and Lifestyle business into ABLBL on a going-concern basis, consideration being ABLBL shares to ABFRL's own shareholders — a pure separation, no cash and no change in ownership. “The Board at its meeting held on April 19, 2024, subject to necessary approvals, considered and approved the demerger of the Madura Fashion and Lifestyle ('MFL') Business under a Scheme of Arrangement between Aditya Birla Fashion and Retail Limited ('Demerged Company') and Aditya Birla Lifestyle Brands Limited ('Resulting Company').”
- *Scheme* — Mirror shareholding and 1:1 ratio: 1,22,02,94,773 shares of ₹10 allotted on May 26, 2025 to ABFRL holders of record May 22, 2025; NCLT sanction March 27, 2025, effective May 1, 2025, listed June 23, 2025. “The Scheme provided that all shareholders of the demerged company will hold Identical shareholdings in both the companies, post the demerger.”
- *Scheme* — Legacy liabilities travel with the demerged business: GST orders for FY2019-20 to FY2022-23 still issued in ABFRL's name land on ABLBL, including a ₹310.13 crore demand (tax ₹59.07 crore, interest ₹23.81 crore, penalty ₹227.26 crore) dated March 30, 2026, which the company says it will appeal. “Order is in the name of Aditya Birla Fashion and Retail Limited (ABFRL). However, it relates to the business of the Company, which got demerged from ABFRL, pursuant to a Scheme of Arrangement effective from May 1, 2025.”
- *CALL Aug 2025* — The core rationale, given by MD Ashish Dikshit in answer to Niharika Karnani asking where the cash goes now that it won't be invested into ABFRL: Madura's cash had been bankrolling the group's new business bets, and the demerger exists to keep it inside Madura. “The cash generated by this business in the past has -- was used to actually kick start or acquire multiple new businesses. And the whole purpose of demerger was actually to need the cash for this business to grow faster.”
- *CALL Aug 2025* — Explicit priority order for the retained cash — growth capex first (including the Lifestyle brands, not just Reebok and Innerwear), debt reduction only after that. “So the first use of cash would be to accelerate the growth in the businesses that we have.”
- *CALL Aug 2025* — The balance-sheet promise attached to the separation: ₹200-300 crore of debt repayment a year off a ~₹700 crore March-2025 base (which had risen ~₹200 crore in Q1 on festive inventory), reaching debt-free in 2.5-3 years; capex guided at ~₹250 crore for retail, shop-in-shops, warehouse, some manufacturing and technology. “we expect between INR200 crores to INR300 crores reduction each year. And that's why we had indicated an overall debt-free status in two and a half years to three years.”
- *CALL Aug 2025* — Growth ambitions the separated entity was given: Lifestyle Brands in early double digits off 15% Q1 retail LTL, and the emerging portfolio (Reebok, American Eagle, Van Heusen Innerwear) at 18-20%+, with Reebok already taken from ~₹200 crore/90 stores at acquisition to ~₹500 crore/180+ stores. “We expect the newer business to grow anything between 18 % to 20 %, while Lifestyle Brands business will grow in early double digits.”
- *CALL Nov 2025* — Reinvestment visibly ahead of deleveraging in the second quarter as a standalone: 75+ new stores, 65 company-owned store renovations in a single quarter (each taking 45-60 days of lost trading), working capital and debt up on early-festive and Bangladesh winterwear inwarding; no restatement of the demerger rationale on this call. “So, just to give you a sense, we did 65 store renovations in just the last quarter.”
- *CALL Feb 2026* — Dikshit restated the rationale in its sharpest form when asked why net debt had barely moved, and CFO Dharmendra Lodha framed it as the growth-capital rationale 'which we conveyed' at the time of demerger. “One of the primary reasons for demerger was to create an entity which can reinvest back more aggressively into growth.”
- *CALL Feb 2026* — The numbers behind it: ~₹900 crore EBITDA cash, historical capex of ₹150-200 crore (₹225 crore at best) versus FY26 capex of ₹320-330 crore — with ~80%+ of it going to Lifestyle Brands expansion and renovation — which management says is precisely why debt fell only from ₹1,000 crore (September) to ₹800 crore (December). “This year, our capex will be north of INR300 crores, perhaps INR320 crores, INR330 crores. And that's really why the debt reduction is not very large this year.”
- *CALL Feb 2026* — The no-fundraise commitment made at demerger was policed by Ambit's Videesha Sheth over a board-approved ₹500 crore NCD issue; management said debt came across on an allocation formula and the NCDs merely refinance a January repayment. “Yeah, you know, at the time of demerger, the company got the borrowings transferred based on the allocation formula.”
- *CALL Feb 2026* — Portfolio ambition for the separated entity: the emerging brands (Reebok 200+ stores, doubled from 100 at acquisition; Van Heusen Innerwear; American Eagle) to become a quarter of ABLBL, with Lifestyle margins at a four-year-high 20.6% in Q3 and emerging-segment profitability up 790bps. “This portfolio is expected to be one-fourth of overall ABLBL business in next 4 -5 years.”

*Not explained on the calls:* No one is named as having asked for it — no investor, lender or brand-partner demand; no dis-synergy, separation cost, valuation or re-rating argument; no ABFRL-side rationale; debt allocation formula undisclosed.

## TRIVENI — Triveni Engineering & Industries Ltd.

**CONFIRMED** (a demerger scheme is on the exchange record) · **LISTED <1Y — selling-pressure window; the bargain forms here** · score 3.6/10 · spin-off · 42 filing(s) from BSE-screener, CALLS, NSE, NSE-register · first 2025-10-29, latest 2026-10-09

> **Listing:** LISTED — Triveni Power Transmission Limited trades since about 2026-10-09 (record date 2026-07-22)

**The stages, as filed:** announced (2026-09-16) → exchange_noc (2026-06-04) → meetings (2025-11-04) → nclt_sanction (2025-11-04) → effective (2026-05-07) → record_date (2026-07-22) → listed (2026-10-09)

**Stated in the filings:** resulting company **Triveni Power Transmission Limited**; entitlement **100 for every 137**; record date 2026-07-22; appointed date 2025-04-01.

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** Power Transmission Business: high-speed and niche low-speed gearboxes, gear internals, defence products, aftermarket and retro-fitment services — class `value_unlocking`.

- *Insiders:* Promoter family runs TPTL: Dhruv M. Sawhney Non-Executive Chairman, Tarun Sawhney Managing Director for five years (subject to shareholder approval), Nikhil Sawhney director; 3,13,00,000 shares (29.9%) locked in to 2027/2029.
- *What it reveals:* PTB was only 4.45% of TEIL turnover but earned ~35-36% PBIT margins; cost-of-acquisition split gives it just 13.40%. Order book just under ₹500 crore (+25%), ₹340 crore capex, new defence facility, Swiss subsidiary, exports targeted above 50%.
- *Selling pressure:* likely — Sugar/ethanol holders receive 1 engineering share per 3 held; 7,34,54,338 free shares, 13.4% of cost basis, unrelated industry.
- *Parent or spin:* spin · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* TPTL's first standalone quarterly results — whether ~36% PBIT margin holds on the ₹500 crore order book post-capex.
- *In their words:* “For every 3(three) equity shares of the Demerged Company with a face value of INR 1 each held in the Demerged Company, every equity shareholder of the Demerged Company shall, without any application, act or deed, be entitled to receive 1 (One) equity share of the Resulting Company with a face value of INR 2 each, credited as fully paid up on the same terms and conditions of issue as prevalent in the Demerged Company”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

Triveni Engineering & Industries Ltd. (TEIL) put through a single composite scheme of arrangement that does two things: it amalgamates its ~61.77%-owned listed subsidiary Sir Shadi Lal Enterprises Ltd. (SSEL, the Shamli sugar/distillery unit) into TEIL, and it demerges TEIL's Power Transmission Business (PTB — high-speed/turbo gearboxes at Mysuru, plus the incubating defence business) into Triveni Power Transmission Ltd. (TPTL) for separate listing, which management described on the Feb 2026 call as being done 'to unlock value and to drive operational efficiencies' and in Feb 2025 as 'value unlocking that the Board of Directors has felt very important.' The problem being solved is that PTB's economics look nothing like the rest of TEIL: PTB ran PBIT margins above 34% in FY25 (PBIT ₹126.8 crore, +18.4%, on turnover up 27%, order booking ₹475+ crore), about 36% in H1 FY26 and 41% in Q2 FY26, against sugar and alcohol businesses whose output and input prices are both administered (SAP up ₹300/tonne in UP, no ethanol price revision for two years, maize at ₹20–26/kg, MSP unrevised), and whose FY25 segment profits fell on a 69bps recovery decline. Investors made exactly this point on the call: Bharat Shah of ASK Investment Managers told management that 'barring the Power Transmission business, which is relatively more robust, predictable economics and predictable outcomes,' the other businesses 'produce a very mercurial kind of an outcome,' and Tarun Sawhney conceded TEIL had not met its return profile on ethanol capital. Separation is also meant to let PTB fund and run its own growth: a board-approved capex of ₹340 crore in three tranches (taking gears capacity from ~₹400 crore to ~₹700 crore of output by September 2026, with just over ₹100 crore sanctioned for the defence facility and ₹231 crore incurred by 31 March 2026, of which ₹78 crore on defence), an export-led order book just under ₹500 crore (+25%), a Swiss subsidiary (Triveni Power Transmission GmbH, acquired 100% by TPTL), aftermarket at ~40% of gears, and a global addressable high-speed/turbo gear market of about $650–700 million. Crucially, TEIL deliberately did not do a clean 100% separation: it retains roughly 30% of TPTL, and Sawhney justified this by the defence business — 'we are incubating a Defence business, which we have large aspirations for,' where establishing pre-qualifications and the ability to bid involves 'balance sheet considerations… from a Group perspective,' plus the precedent of the Triveni Turbine separation, which he called 'actually quite a positive one for the Company.' Post-approval TEIL said ICRA reaffirmed its long-term rating at AA+ Stable, lifting it off watch, and that TPTL goes out 'armed with sufficient cash flows and a balance sheet' to fund its capex and opex.

**How it evolved:** The board approved the composite scheme on 10 December 2024, and the Feb 2025 (5 Feb) call was the first investor call after it — there Sawhney framed it as value unlocking, guided to NCLT approval 'by the end of this calendar year,' and defended the retained ~30% stake against Resham Jain's push for a clean structure; Bharat Shah's 'mercurial' critique of the commodity businesses came on the same call. By Jun 2025 (28 May) the scheme was stuck with SEBI with NCLT next, guidance slipped to 'middle of Q1 of next calendar year, Q4 of this fiscal year,' and Resham Jain asked for granular PTB disclosure ahead of listing, which Sawhney accepted as a 'welcome suggestion'; on Aug 2025 (30 July) approvals were still pending with SEBI and stock-exchange queries, with Sawhney allowing it 'could add another 30-odd days.' Nov 2025 (7 Nov) reported stock-exchange approval (observation letters 7 and 11 August 2025) and NCLT stakeholder meetings set for late November/early December, plus TPTL's 100% acquisition of Swiss step-down subsidiary Triveni Power Transmission GmbH; Feb 2026 (2 Feb) reported shareholder/creditor approval in December 2025, an NCLT hearing in February, systems work to let TPTL 'hit the ground sprinting,' and Sawhney's line that 'the next time we speak in all probability, this will be two separate companies.' On Jun 2026 (4 June) he confirmed the scheme effective 19 May 2026 after NCLT approval (orders 7 and 18 May), appointed dates of 1 April 2025 for the amalgamation and 1 April 2026 for the demerger, the SSEL record date of 3 June 2026, and guided to a TPTL listing 'by the end of August' with separate results and earnings calls for both companies — in the event the demerger record date was 22 July 2026, 7,34,54,338 TPTL shares were allotted on 28 July 2026 (TPTL thereby ceasing to be a subsidiary and becoming an associate), and TPTL listed and began trading only on 12 October 2026.

**What management expects from it:** TPTL: independent listing of a ~35% PBIT, export-led gears and defence business, self-funding its ₹340 crore capex toward ~₹700 crore of gears output, exports above 50%, aftermarket-led margins. TEIL: a cleaner sugar-distillery-water commodity platform with SSEL absorbed, AA+ Stable restored off watch, and cash flows for brownfield/greenfield expansion. Both: unlocked value, operational efficiencies, separate reporting.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *[Feb 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=32ebf539-4c61-4455-9d21-3cc24a97dd7a.pdf)* — First call after the 10 December 2024 board approval; Sawhney introduced the composite scheme — amalgamation of ~61.77%-held SSEL into TEIL and transfer of the PTB undertaking to wholly-owned TPTL — explicitly as a value-unlocking exercise by the Board. “I also wanted to provide an update on the Scheme, as you're all aware, this is in conjunction with value unlocking that the Board of Directors has felt very important.”
- *[Feb 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=32ebf539-4c61-4455-9d21-3cc24a97dd7a.pdf)* — Resham Jain of DSP Asset Managers challenged the structure, arguing TEIL's retained ~30% stake in TPTL would re-import a holdco discount and that a clean separation was needed for value to be unlocked. “It seems that Triveni Engineering will still be holding 30% stake even after demerger. So why such structure, if the value unlocking has to happen, it should have happened in a clean structure where Triveni would not be holding anything otherwise, the same Holdco discount will be applicable to the Power Transmission business once it gets demerged.”
- *[Feb 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=32ebf539-4c61-4455-9d21-3cc24a97dd7a.pdf)* — Sawhney's two reasons for keeping ~30%: the positive precedent of the Triveni Turbine separation, and — decisively — that the incubating defence business needs group balance-sheet backing to win pre-qualifications and be allowed to bid, since defence is co-located with gears in Mysuru. “The second and very, very important is because we are incubating a Defence business, which we have large aspirations for. In establishing pre-qualifications (PQs) and the ability to be able to quote, there are balance sheet considerations that even from a Group perspective that are very, very important to allow us to be in contention.”
- *[Feb 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=32ebf539-4c61-4455-9d21-3cc24a97dd7a.pdf)* — Bharat Shah of ASK Investment Managers made the investor case for separation directly — PTB is the predictable, brick-by-brick business while the regulated sugar/ethanol/water businesses swing unpredictably — and Sawhney conceded the ethanol capital had not met its return profile. “On a shorter-term basis, interplay of the other businesses always produces a very mercurial kind of an outcome, sometimes to delight, but other times to depress.”
- *[Feb 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=32ebf539-4c61-4455-9d21-3cc24a97dd7a.pdf)* — Same call quantified why PTB deserves its own listing: incremental board-approved capex of ₹60 crore taking gears capacity to ₹700 crore by September 2026 from ~₹400 crore, order book at an all-time-high ₹377 crore, and a global high-speed/turbo gear market of about $650–700 million. “The Board meeting of the Directors concluded yesterday had an important announcement of an incremental capex of ₹60 crore for the enhancement of capacity in the Power Transmission business. This will take the gears capacity to ₹700 crore by September 2026.”
- *[Feb 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=32ebf539-4c61-4455-9d21-3cc24a97dd7a.pdf)* — Initial timeline guidance: NCLT sanction expected by the end of calendar 2025. “As far as the Scheme of Arrangement is concerned, we anticipate approval from NCLT by the end of this calendar year.”
- *[Jun 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=24085d8d-b7bb-42bb-bd4f-8cb00e75ea19.pdf)* — Q4 FY25 call showed the margin gap the demerger exposes — PTB turnover up 27% with PBIT ₹126.8 crore (+18.4%) and PBIT margins above 34%, record Q4 revenue of almost ₹140 crore and PBIT ₹46.5 crore — while the scheme itself sat pending at SEBI, with separation guided to Q4 FY26. “So we're expecting that by the middle of Q1 of next calendar year, Q4 of this fiscal year, we will have the separation of the PTB business.”
- *[Jun 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=24085d8d-b7bb-42bb-bd4f-8cb00e75ea19.pdf)* — Resham Jain asked management to begin disclosing PTB in granular detail — customers, industry mix — precisely because it was about to be separately listed after being buried inside a much larger company; Sawhney accepted. “And since it was a part of a much larger company, the understanding of this business from the very granular perspective was much lower.”

PTB closing order book was a record ₹423 crore (+38%), with engineering order book just under ₹2,000 crore. “The amalgamation with Sir Shadi Lal and the demerger of the Power Transmission business. We are still awaiting regulatory approvals. We're following up continuously with SEBI.”

- *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=ec578aab-464f-47c2-8bc5-cb3982d61b3e.pdf)* — PTB PBIT margins improved more than 400bps YoY on product mix and cost optimisation (about 36% PBIT for H1, 41% in the quarter), and TPTL was equipped with its own CRM, digital-factory/digital-twin and SAP HANA systems ahead of standing alone. “Triveni Power Transmission Limited, a wholly-owned subsidiary of the company, has acquired a 100% stake in Triveni Power Transmission GmbH, a Swiss company.”

## ITC — ITC Ltd.

**CONFIRMED** (a demerger scheme is on the exchange record) · **LISTED 1–2Y — the second-year window** · score 3.3/10 · spin-off · 6 filing(s) from NSE, NSE-register · first 2025-01-06, latest 2026-05-21

> **Listing:** LISTED — the resulting company trades since about 2025-01-06 (record date 2025-01-06)

**The stages, as filed:** record_date (2025-01-06)

**Stated in the filings:** record date 2025-01-06; appointed date 2025-04-01.

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** ITC's Hotels business, distributed to shareholders under a Scheme of Demerger into separately listed ITC Hotels Limited — class `not stated`.

- *Insiders:* Documents state ITC Limited has no promoter/promoter group; post-demerger ITC Hotels Limited appears among ITC's associates, i.e. a retained equity-method stake. No management shareholding or incentives in the new entity stated.
- *What it reveals:* Separation revealed hotel assets carried far below fair value: FY2025 exceptional items of ₹15,179.43 crores (standalone discontinued operations) and a ₹15,617.37 crores gain on fair valuation of net assets distributed, against only ₹572.52 crores pre-exceptional PBT from hotels; parent retains cash-generative cigarettes.
- *Selling pressure:* likely — Hotels sits outside ITC's three stated business groups (FMCG, Paperboards/Paper & Packaging, Agri); documents disclose no index or shareholder-base detail.
- *Parent or spin:* unclear · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* The Scheme of Demerger of Hotels business, plus ITC Hotels Limited's own results behind ITC's ₹5,288.24 crores equity-method investment.
- *In their words:* “The Company is currently focused on three business groups : FMCG, Paperboards, Paper & Packaging and Agri Business.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

On the documents supplied, the business being separated is ITC's IT services arm, ITC Infotech India Limited (ITCI), a wholly owned subsidiary that is to be carved out of the unlisted group structure and listed on BSE and NSE through a strategic combination with listed Happiest Minds Technologies Limited (31 Aug 2026 filing). The mechanics are two-step: ITCI buys 3,36,61,700 shares (22.106% fully diluted) from promoters Ashok Soota and Ashok Soota Medical Research LLP for ~Rs 1,330 crores cash in two tranches (11.00% at Rs 390/share, 11.106% at Rs 400/share), funded by a Rights Issue of Rs 1,330 crores, after which Happiest Minds amalgamates into ITCI at 25 ITCI shares per 81 Happiest Minds shares (1:3.24) — implying Rs 405/share or Rs 6,167 crores for Happiest Minds and Rs 1,312/share or Rs 11,920 crores for ITCI pre-rights — leaving ITC with ~73.4% and Happiest Minds holders ~26.6%, and ITCI listed. The stated problem it solves is sub-scale: management says '> $1Bn revenue puts provider on the vendor management office radar' and gives the 'Right to Hunt' and 'Right to Win' large deals, so the combination targets US$1 billion revenue by FY28 on a pro-forma basis versus ITCI's FY26 IT services revenue of Rs 4,718 crores (PAT Rs 510 crores adjusted, 18.5% adj. EBITDA margin, 13,000+ employees, 5-yr CAGR 14%) and Happiest Minds' FY26 Rs 2,315.11 crores (FY25 Rs 2,060.84 crores, FY24 Rs 1,624.66 crores, 6,500+ employees, 5-yr CAGR 25%). It also fixes portfolio gaps: Americas mix rises from 27% to 38%, BFSI from 12% to 20%, Build:Run moves to 50:50, and Hi-Tech, EdTech and Healthcare verticals plus 800+ clients and 19,000+ professionals are added, against an industry backdrop of a ~$400 Bn AI-driven TAM by 2030, compression of ~$350 Bn of legacy services, cost-takeout deals at 30-40% savings and vendor consolidation. For ITC shareholders the explicitly stated benefit of separation itself is that it 'Creates a listed IT services platform, enabling independent value discovery and strategic flexibility', alongside ~10% revenue synergies, ~100 bps margin expansion and EPS accretion in the first full year. Nobody is recorded as having demanded it: ITCI's board moved under its own 'Orbit Next' strategy, ITC's board merely 'endorsed' it, and the only external party is the counterparty-seller Ashok Soota, who frames it as Happiest Minds finding 'a welcoming new home'; approvals needed are CCI/anti-trust, stock exchanges/SEBI, shareholders, creditors and NCLT, over ~15 months.

**How it evolved:** No earnings-call transcripts were provided, so the idea is traceable only through filings: ITC had already demerged its Hotels business (visible as discontinued operations with Rs 15,163.06 crores of exceptional items in FY2024-25 and ITC Hotels Limited now an associate), establishing the separation template. The IT separation surfaces fully formed on 31 August 2026, when ITCI's board approved both the 22.106% promoter-stake purchase and the Happiest Minds amalgamation that will list ITCI, endorsed the same day by ITC's board. Housekeeping then followed in the opposite, consolidating direction: on 1 September 2026 step-down subsidiaries Blazeclan Technologies and Cloudlytics were dissolved into ITC Infotech (appointed date 1 October 2024), tidying the entity to be listed, while on 2 November 2026 ITC moved the other way at the parent by absorbing wholly owned Sproutlife Foods (Yoga Bar) to 'reduce the number of operating entities'. The plan's indicative sequencing was set at board approval in Aug'26, Tranche 1 and exchange/SEBI no-objection around Q3FY27-early Q4FY27, shareholder/creditor meetings Mar-Apr'27 and ITCI listing in Q2-Q3 FY28.

**What management expects from it:** ITC Infotech: step change to ~US$1bn revenue by FY28 (from Rs 4,718 crores FY26), Americas mix 27%→38%, BFSI 12%→20%, Build:Run 50:50, ~10% revenue synergies, ~100 bps margin expansion, EPS accretive in year one, 19,000+ people, 800+ clients. ITC: a separately listed IT platform giving independent value discovery and strategic flexibility, while retaining ~73.4%.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *Scheme* — The separation vehicle is disclosed in the 31 August 2026 filing: ITC Infotech acquires 22.106% of Happiest Minds for cash and then amalgamates it, with ITCI's own shares to be listed on both Indian exchanges. “The shares of ITC Infotech are proposed to be listed on BSE Limited and the National Stock Exchange of India Limited.”
- *Scheme* — Transaction summary states the listing is the consequence of the merger, not an IPO or a demerger to ITC shareholders; ITC retains ~73.4% and Happiest Minds holders get ~26.6%. “Thereafter, Happiest Minds to merge with ITC Infotech pursuant to which ITC Infotech will be listed”
- *Scheme* — The value-creation case for ITC shareholders names independent price discovery as a benefit of having the IT business separately listed. “Creates a listed IT services platform, enabling independent value discovery and strategic flexibility”
- *Scheme* — Regulation 30 disclosure frames the deal as the execution of ITCI's existing standalone expansion strategy, aimed at a step change in revenue scale and competitiveness. “ITC Infotech's 'Orbit Next' strategy envisages rapid global expansion through capability led strategic partnerships.”
- *Scheme* — The industry slide gives the explicit scale threshold problem the separation-and-combination is meant to clear — being below US$1bn keeps ITCI off large buyers' vendor lists. “> $1Bn revenue puts provider on the vendor management  office radar”
- *Scheme* — Media statement sets the quantified target for the combined, listed entity: US$1 billion revenue by FY28 on a pro-forma basis, AI-first, with 19,000+ professionals. “ITC Infotech (ITCI), a wholly owned subsidiary of ITC Limited and a leading global technology services player, today announced the proposed strategic combination with Happiest Minds Technologies Limited (Happiest Minds) to create a scaled, future-ready, AI-first global technology services enterprise.”
- *Scheme* — Synergy slide quantifies what the combination is expected to deliver financially: roughly 10% revenue synergies, about 100 bps of margin expansion, and EPS accretion in year one. “Expected to be EPS accretive in first full year of combined entity operations”
- *Scheme* — ITC's Chairman Sanjiv Puri justifies it on complementarity of capability and culture rather than on any investor, lender or partner demand. “The coming together of our complementary strengths, deep domain expertise and future-ready capabilities will further enhance our ability to deliver cutting-edge solutions across geographies.”
- *Scheme* — The only external party pressing for a change of ownership is the Happiest Minds promoter selling the 22.106% stake, who wanted a larger home for his company. “We believe that ITC Infotech is the best partner for Happiest Minds to fulfil its destiny and we are pleased that our team will have a welcoming new home .”
- *Scheme* — ITCI's CEO Manas Chakraborty positions the rationale as capability completeness — full-stack AI-led transformation — rather than financial engineering. “Integrating Happiest Minds' Digital Engineering, Data, AI, and Cybersecurity capabilities with our deep domain expertise, cloud and engineering capabilities will enable us to serve as a full stack AI-led transformation partner.”
- *Scheme* — At the parent level ITC is simultaneously simplifying in the opposite direction, absorbing wholly owned Sproutlife Foods (Yoga Bar; FY26 turnover Rs 451.71 crores, total assets Rs 150.07 crores) on 2 November 2026. “Result in reduction of the number of operating entities to simplify the corporate holding structure.”
- *Scheme* — The 1 September 2026 filing shows pre-listing entity cleanup: step-down subsidiaries Blazeclan and Cloudlytics were merged into ITC Infotech with appointed date 1 October 2024. “Accordingly, with effect from 1st September , 2026, BTPL and CTPL stand  dissolved without winding up and have cease d to be subsidiaries of the Company.”

*Not explained on the calls:* No earnings-call transcripts supplied; filings never explain ITC's intent for its 73.4% stake, any ITC-shareholder entitlement, carve-out/dis-synergy costs, valuation basis, or the earlier hotels demerger's rationale.
