## STLTECH — Sterlite Technologies Ltd.

**CONFIRMED** (a demerger scheme is on the exchange record) · **LISTED 1–2Y — the second-year window** · score 2.9/10 · spin-off · 2 filing(s) from NSE, NSE-register · first 2025-04-24, latest 2026-08-21

> **Listing:** LISTED — the resulting company trades since about 2025-04-24 (record date 2025-04-24)

**The stages, as filed:** record_date (2025-04-24)

**Stated in the filings:** record date 2025-04-24.

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** STL's Global Services Business (system integration / services arm), demerged out of Sterlite Technologies into a separate company — class `unrelated`.

- *Insiders:* Not stated for STL Networks. In the parent, promoter Twin Star Overseas Limited held 42.90%, rising to 47.75% fully diluted on exercise of 4,53,00,000 warrants at Rs.110; ultimate beneficial owner Mr. Anil Agarwal
- *What it reveals:* Leaves a pure-play optical parent: Q2 FY27 record revenue INR 2,529 Cr, EBITDA INR 846 Cr, PAT INR 517 Cr, order book INR 35,274 Cr, net debt-free, CRISIL AA/Stable. Any Kakinada writ contingent gain now belongs to STL Networks, not STL
- *Selling pressure:* unclear — Documents give no size, shareholding, index or float details for STL Networks Limited
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* STL Networks Limited's own August 20, 2026 exchange disclosure and its standalone financials
- *In their words:* “Please note that pursuant to the Scheme of Arrangement approved by the Hon'ble National Company Law Tribunal, Mumbai, vide order dated February 14, 2025, STL's Global Services Business has been demerged into STL Networks Limited, effective from the close of business hours on March 31, 2025.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

The business being separated is STL's Global Services (system integration / network-deployment) business, demerged out of Sterlite Technologies Limited (STLTECH) into a separate listed entity, STL Networks Limited, rebranded 'Invenia', leaving STL as a pure optical business (optical fibre, fibre cable, specialty cable, optical connectivity) plus the small STL Digital IT-services arm. Management's stated reason was portfolio simplification and focus: Ankit Agarwal said on the May 2025 call that the demerger 'aligns with our goal of portfolio simplification and sets the stage for focused growth in each of the businesses,' and in Jul 2026 placed it in a multi-year clean-up in which STL exited, sold or shut down wireless solutions, OSS/BSS, active components and other businesses to be 'very, very focused on the optical fiber cable connectivity side.' The second reason was capital and working-capital drag: the services business was a project business with large net fund involvement, and on the Jan 2025 call management's stated priority for it was 'select projects intake to improve the profitability and optimize the net fund involvement,' with Tushar Shroff conceding receivables and contract assets in state-government projects like T-Fiber and MahaNet were liquidating slower than planned because they depended on state budgetary allocation. The scale difference management cited: Global Services did INR 289 crores of revenue in Q3 FY25 at only INR 20 crores EBITDA (6.8% margin), versus the optical business at INR 924 crores and INR 119 crores (12.9%); consolidated net debt was INR 2,195 crores at Q3 FY25 and the retained (post-demerger) business reported net debt of about INR 1,350 crores at Q4 FY25, with a stated target of taking net debt/EBITDA from ~3x to 2x. Structurally, management wanted a clean break rather than a carve-out on paper: in Nov 2025 Ajay Jhanjhari said 'the entire thought process of doing demerger is that there should not be any intercompany guarantees because that is a separate company,' and 'No relationship between STL and STL networks from that perspective.' The INR 2,600 crore BharatNet Phase III Jammu & Kashmir package (3-year build plus 10-year maintenance) went with the demerged entity, and STL now supplies cable to it on an arm's-length basis — in Jan 2026 described as 'our group company, Invenia has secured Jammu Kashmir package, where we will be supplying the cable on arm's length basis.' Each entity also got its own leadership and identity: Pankaj Malik as CEO of STL Networks under the Invenia brand, with shareholders receiving a 1:1 share entitlement on holdings as of April 24, 2025. Across the calls, no investor, lender or partner is named as having demanded the separation; the only shareholder pressure visible is generic complaints about poor equity returns and past cash burn (Q4 FY25 and Q1 FY26 calls), which management answered by pointing to the business exits, the ~INR 1,000 crore QIP of April 2024, and the demerger as portfolio simplification.

**How it evolved:** The idea is already in execution by the Jan 23, 2025 call, where it appears as a standing FY26 priority ('work towards completing the demerger of the services business') with the NCLT timeline laid out — scheme approved by shareholders and creditors July 10, 2024, petition admitted October 2024, final hearing January 30, 2025, listing targeted by Q1 FY26. On the May 16, 2025 call Ankit Agarwal declared it done, effective March 31, 2025, named the new entity STL Networks, the new brand Invenia, Pankaj Malik as CEO and the 1:1 share entitlement, and reported the retained business separately at INR 1,350 crores net debt. By Jul 25, 2025 the plan had slipped only on listing (NCLT approval received Feb 2025, shares expected to list 'by the end of August'), and by Nov 6, 2025 the emphasis shifted to completing the operational separation — no intercompany guarantees, a roughly year-long transition to transfer everything. Thereafter it is treated as finished history: Jan 23, 2026 references Invenia only as a BharatNet customer served at arm's length, and Jul 24, 2026 cites 'we've also demerged our system integration business into a separate entity' purely as evidence of focus.

**What management expects from it:** Focused growth in each entity: STL becomes a pure optical manufacturer chasing global top-3, 70-80% utilisation and 20% EBITDA versus ~13-14%, with net debt/EBITDA cut from ~3x to 2x (net debt INR 1,350 crores post-demerger versus INR 2,195 crores consolidated), no intercompany guarantees, and less capital tied up in project/working-capital-heavy services. Invenia gets its own brand, CEO and large-project mandate.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *[Jan 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=98f6b077-32ee-41f8-b96d-a36366cf2a48.pdf)* — Completing the demerger of the services business was listed as a formal FY26 strategic priority alongside building value-added services and cutting fund involvement in that business. “Concurrently we will work towards completing the demerger of the services business.”
- *[Jan 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=98f6b077-32ee-41f8-b96d-a36366cf2a48.pdf)* — CFO Tushar Shroff gave the regulatory timeline — scheme approved by shareholders and creditors on July 10, 2024, petition admitted with NCLT in October 2024, final hearing January 30, 2025 — with listing of the resulting company to follow, and a target of completing the demerger by Q1 FY26. “The final approval is expected in Q4 FY25 after which resulting company is anticipated to be listed on a stock exchanges.”
- *[Jan 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=98f6b077-32ee-41f8-b96d-a36366cf2a48.pdf)* — The services business was explicitly managed for lower capital absorption, not scale: Q3 FY25 revenue of INR 289 crores produced only INR 20 crores EBITDA (6.8%), and receivables/contract assets in state projects (T-Fiber, MahaNet) were stuck pending state budgetary allocation. “We will continue to build our capability towards value added services and system integration to improve our margins and reduce the fund involvement going forward.”
- *[May 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=3a33a16d-778d-4047-8e61-79e95df6983b.pdf)* — Ankit Agarwal announced completion effective March 31, 2025, with the demerged Global Services business operating as STL Networks under the new Invenia brand, Pankaj Malik as CEO, and a 1:1 share entitlement to STL shareholders based on holdings as of April 24, 2025. “This move aligns with our goal of portfolio simplification and sets the stage for focused growth in each of the businesses.”
- *[May 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=3a33a16d-778d-4047-8e61-79e95df6983b.pdf)* — The separation was framed as the last step of a multi-year pruning of the portfolio, after exiting wireless solutions and OSS/BSS, and alongside a ~INR 1,000 crore QIP to repair the balance sheet; the INR 2,600 crore BharatNet J&K package (deployment plus 10 years' maintenance) sat in the demerged entity, not in STL's reported order book. “This is part of the services business, which is now demerged.”
- *[Jul 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=8111472f-4f00-4159-9e5a-70f93bf1b0d8.pdf)* — CFO confirmed NCLT final approval was received in February 2025 and that STL Networks was a separate legal entity from March 31, 2025, with share listing still pending regulatory approvals and expected by end-August 2025 (versus the earlier Q1 FY26 / June target). “As of March 31, 2025, STL Networks Limited is now a separate legal entity.”
- *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=6103688c-1b5b-4922-b304-d2d348f60fea.pdf)* — Asked about intercompany loans, advances or guarantees with STL Networks, management said the purpose of the demerger was precisely to have none, while conceding the operational transfer takes about a year to complete. “So, STL networks, the entire thought process of doing demerger is that there should not be any intercompany guarantees because that is a separate company.”
- *[Jan 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=e0a51053-117e-457b-90f3-4487eed18370.pdf)* — The post-separation relationship is purely commercial: STL supplies optical fibre cable to Invenia's BharatNet Phase III Jammu & Kashmir package on an arm's-length basis, and also holds Manufacturing Authorization Forms with other BharatNet bidders. “And as you know, our group company, Invenia has secured Jammu Kashmir package, where we will be supplying the cable on arm's length basis.”
- *[Jul 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=8a08fac5-bc05-4f79-acee-f6a5076525cd.pdf)* — A year later Ankit cited the demerger, alongside exits from active components and other businesses, as proof of a deliberate narrowing to glass-fibre-cable-connectivity, and ruled out adjacent areas like transceivers and semiconductors. “We've consciously chosen to exit, sell off or shut down many businesses. So -- and we've also demerged our system integration business into a separate entity.”
- *Scheme* — The Aug 2026 filing records the legal mechanics: the Scheme of Arrangement was approved by NCLT Mumbai by order dated February 14, 2025, and the Global Services Business demerged into STL Networks Limited from the close of business hours on March 31, 2025, with litigation outcomes of that business (e.g. the Kakinada Smart City writ petition) now accruing to STL Networks. “Please note that pursuant to the Scheme of Arrangement approved by the Hon'ble National Company Law Tribunal, Mumbai, vide order dated February 14, 2025, STL's Global Services Business has been demerged into STL Networks Limited, effective from the close of business hours on March 31, 2025.”

*Not explained on the calls:* No standalone Invenia financials, valuation, debt split, separation costs, or capital allocation given; no investor, lender or partner named as requesting it; listing-date slippage unexplained.

*Calls read (36 months):* [Aug 2024](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=fb5088c5-7916-4e9a-97b1-03812320978e.pdf), [Jan 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=98f6b077-32ee-41f8-b96d-a36366cf2a48.pdf), [Jul 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=8111472f-4f00-4159-9e5a-70f93bf1b0d8.pdf), [Jul 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=8a08fac5-bc05-4f79-acee-f6a5076525cd.pdf), [Mar 2024](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=a5000d23-d4f3-41f2-ac2e-af2d6ab05dd4.pdf), [May 2024](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=ab8a5353-690d-44b9-9a2c-85e662c1313e.pdf), [May 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=3a33a16d-778d-4047-8e61-79e95df6983b.pdf), [Nov 2023](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=ada3a160-f761-4b79-bd64-2b5f16f5d072.pdf), [Nov 2024](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=46ac8e7e-9211-4d2f-beb8-498619b060ec.pdf), [Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=6103688c-1b5b-4922-b304-d2d348f60fea.pdf)

## REFEX — Refex Industries Ltd.

**CONFIRMED** (demerger in progress — read from the filings' text (no scheme-category filing names it): “Demerger of the Green Mobility Business Undertaking of RIL (vested in RIL pursuant to amalgamation of RGML with RIL) into Refex Mobility Limited ('Res”) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 5.7/10 · spin-off · 39 filing(s) from CALLS, NSE · first 2025-11-04, latest 2026-10-28

> **Listing:** NOT YET — scheme at 'nclt_sanction' stage; Refex Mobility Limited will list only after NCLT sanction, effectiveness and a record date; no listing timeline stated

**The stages, as filed:** exchange_noc (2026-03-17) → meetings (2026-08-05) → nclt_sanction (2026-06-24)

**Stated in the filings:** resulting company **Refex Mobility Limited**; demerged undertaking: are transferred to the Resulting Company and all the liabilities of Transferor Company; record date 2025-04-01; appointed date 2025-04-01; size hint: 2.5% of revenue.

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** Green Mobility Business Undertaking — cleaner-fuel/EV passenger transport and corporate fleet services — into Refex Mobility Limited — class `value_unlocking`.

- *Insiders:* Directors/KMP have no interest except directorship and shareholding; RIL holds 100% of RML pre-scheme (cancelled); post-scheme promoter and promoter group hold 56.57% of RML, mirroring RIL 1:1.
- *What it reveals:* Separation leaves parent as high-margin Ash & Coal handling (FY26 PAT ₹247cr, 17% EBITDA, ₹1,721cr orderbook) plus wind; the spin is small and loss-making (segment EBIT −₹38.2cr FY26, ~₹220cr net assets, RGML creditors ₹153cr) but 'progressing steadily towards profitability'.
- *Selling pressure:* likely — Tiny (2.5% of revenue, ~₹100cr turnover), loss-making, unlisted new entity in a different industry, distributed 1:1 to 92,973 shareholders.
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* Annexure 19 — assets and liabilities demerged into RML; then RML's Information Memorandum and the NCLT sanction order.
- *In their words:* “The Green Mobility Business is capable of attracting a different set of investors, lenders, strategic partners and other stakeholders and have significant potential for growth and profitability.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

The separation is the demerger of Refex's green mobility (electric-vehicle fleet) business out of Refex Industries Ltd (RIL), whose core is Ash & Coal Handling. Management structured it as a composite scheme in two steps: first merge the wholly-owned subsidiary Refex Green Mobility Ltd (RGML) into RIL, then demerge the Mobility Undertaking from RIL into a new, separately listed entity, Refex Mobility Ltd (RML), with mirror shareholding (1 RML share of Rs 2 for every 1 RIL share) and, as Dinesh Agarwal stressed, no valuation exercise required because RGML was a 100% subsidiary. The stated reason is investor fit and value discovery: 'the set of investor for the sustainable and the EV business is a completely different set of investor compared to what is there in the Refex Industries Limited,' so a parallel listing is meant to unlock value; the Scheme adds that the mobility business can attract a different set of investors, lenders and strategic partners, and that its risk, competition, financial profile and return ratios are distinct from ash & coal. The second driver is the drag mobility placed on consolidated results — Q1 FY26 showed standalone PAT of about INR33 crore against consolidated INR20.4 crore, with Green Mobility segment margin at minus 50%, prompting an investor to allege 'a miscalculation in your capital allocation'; management had already exited Bangalore airport B2C services to save INR6.82 crore of annual fixed cost. Post-demerger RIL becomes essentially a single-business company (Anil Jain: '95% business from ash and coal handling only'), while RML carries its own balance sheet — roughly INR220 crore of net assets and, per Jan 2026, 'all the debt etc. will also move to that entity' — and pursues asset-light, clean-fuel, enterprise-led growth toward profitability after crossing about INR100 crore of revenue in three years. Mechanically the appointed date is 1 April 2025, mobility was reported as discontinued operations from FY26, lender NOCs were a gating item, BSE/NSE no-adverse-observation letters came on 16 March 2026, the NCLT application was filed 26 March 2026, and the NCLT-convened shareholder and creditor meetings on 5 August 2026 approved the scheme unanimously (equity shareholders ~99.999% of value in favour).

**How it evolved:** Through FY25 (May 2024, Nov 2024, Apr 2025 calls) mobility was presented as a growth vertical to scale to 2,000 then 5,000 EVs, with no separation contemplated; the first visible pressure came on the Aug 13, 2025 call, where an investor attacked the capital allocation given minus-50% mobility margins, and Anil Jain replied 'point well taken, we will try and assess how to rework on these businesses.' The board approved the draft composite scheme on September 22, 2025, and it was first explained to investors on the Nov 6, 2025 call as a two-step merger-then-demerger into a separately listed Refex Mobility Ltd, with a six-to-seven-month timeline and no valuation needed. By Jan 21, 2026 the hold-up was 'final NOCs from the lenders', the net assets moving were quantified at INR220 crore with debt following, and completion was guided to end-April 2026; on May 27, 2026 BSE/NSE approvals were in hand, the NCLT filing done, and 75–90 more days guided. The timeline then slipped: creditor and shareholder meetings were only held August 5, 2026, and the October 28, 2026 press release still shows NCLT hearings pending with the next hearing on 28 October 2026.

**What management expects from it:** RIL becomes a near-pure Ash & Coal Handling play (95-100% of standalone revenue) with sharper focus and clearer capital allocation; RML operates independently, carrying its own debt and ~INR220 crore of net assets, pursuing asset-light clean-fuel and enterprise-led growth toward profitability; the 1:1 mirror listing lets a different investor set value the EV business and unlock shareholder value.

- *[Aug 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=308de71b-7879-459a-8396-d6990b0a31cb.pdf)* — An investor confronted management with the gap between standalone PAT (~INR32-33 crore) and consolidated PAT (INR20.4 crore), blaming mobility's minus-50% segment margin; this is the first on-record push to rework the business. “It seems to be there is a miscalculation in your capital allocation, sir. Why don't you focus on coal business and go one by one later on?”
- *[Aug 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=308de71b-7879-459a-8396-d6990b0a31cb.pdf)* — Anil Jain conceded mobility was pulling down consolidated results because EMIs start the day a vehicle is acquired while full utilisation takes 6-9 months, and accepted the need to restructure. “Point well taken, we will try and assess how to rework on these businesses to ensure that we remake them profitable, sir.”
- *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=f2733f9d-0910-4f38-8c2d-f74a1600e438.pdf)* — First disclosure of the structure on a call: a two-step composite scheme — RGML merges into RIL, then the Mobility Undertaking is demerged into a separately listed Refex Mobility Ltd — framed as unlocking focused value. “On this note, I would like to briefly mention that the de-merger of Refex Green Mobility Limited from Refex Industries Limited is in progress through a
composite scheme comprising two steps.”
- *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=f2733f9d-0910-4f38-8c2d-f74a1600e438.pdf)* — Because RGML is a 100% subsidiary, no valuation was done and shareholders simply get mirror shareholding in the new entity; value is left to the market after listing. BSE/NSE filing done, NCLT next, 6-7 months estimated. “As per the company and the process of merger and demerger process there is no valuations requirement to be done since the company holds 100, it is a 100 subsidiary and a mirror shareholding will happen, all the shareholder of Refex Industries Limited will be same shareholding as per the scheme which has been disclosed there.”
- *[Jan 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=63755f06-063b-42e8-b635-b18c38eb7a4a.pdf)* — Lenders were a gating party — final NOCs from lenders were the open item — and management confirmed the demerged entity carries its own debt and operating freedom; INR220 crore of net assets move to Mobility. “Once it is demerged, the Refex Mobility will run as a separate entity where it will have more liberty to do its own business and also it will have its own, all the debt etc. will also move to that entity.”
- *[Jan 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=63755f06-063b-42e8-b635-b18c38eb7a4a.pdf)* — Management quantified what leaves the consolidated balance sheet and confirmed RML will be a parallel separate listing rather than a sale. “It is a 100% subsidiary and Refex industry does not own any assets of the Refex Green Mobility. So it is a 100% subsidiary and it will be a parallel separate listing completely.”
- *[Jan 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=63755f06-063b-42e8-b635-b18c38eb7a4a.pdf)* — Post-demerger RIL is intended to be effectively a single-business company, with mobility no longer consolidated. “Green mobility will be demerged. So it will be a separate entity. Officially, on a standalone basis, Refex industries will have 100% business, maybe 95% business from ash and coal handling only.”
- *[Jun 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=f1aa0b70-a34f-4c91-8973-009a48c493d3.pdf)* — The clearest statement of rationale: the EV/sustainability business appeals to a different investor base, and separation is intended to unlock value, with mobility itself on a path to profitability after crossing ~INR100 crore revenue in three years. “The purpose of the demerger is because the set of investor for the sustainable and the EV business is a completely different set of investor compared to what is there in the Refex Industries Limited.”
- *[Jun 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=f1aa0b70-a34f-4c91-8973-009a48c493d3.pdf)* — Management framed the expected post-separation benefits for each entity — focus, capital allocation and value discovery — and said compliance was complete with only the NCLT court process (75-90 days) pending after BSE and NSE approvals. “We believe this structure will create sharper operational focus, clear capital allocation and stronger long-term value discovery for all the stakeholders.”
- *Scheme* — The scheme's own rationale rests on the distinct risk/return character of the two businesses and mobility's ability to draw its own investors, lenders and partners, enabling separate capital-market access. “The Green Mobility Business is capable of attracting a different set of investors, lenders, strategic partners and other stakeholders and have significant potential for growth and profitability.”
- *Scheme* — Shareholders receive a 1:1 mirror entitlement in RML (appointed date 1 April 2025; RIL's existing 50,000 RML shares cancelled), and the August 5, 2026 NCLT-convened meetings approved it with ~99.999% of equity value and unanimous secured/unsecured creditor support. “"1 (One) fully paid-up Equity Share of Rs.2 each of the Resulting Company shall be issued and allotted as fully paid up for every 1 (One) Equity Shares of Re. 2 each fully paid up held in the Demerged Company."”

*Not explained on the calls:* No valuation, margin or capital-raise plan for RML; no reason given for the merger-then-demerger structure; no debt split detail; repeated timeline slippage never explained.

# Partial spin-offs (subsidiary IPOs) — in full

## SBIN — State Bank of India

**CONFIRMED** (partial spin-off — SBI Funds Management Limited is listed since 2026-07-21) · **PARTIAL SPIN-OFF, LISTED <1Y — price the parent's stub against the listed piece** · score 6.2/10 · partial spin-off (subsidiary IPO) · 12 filing(s) from CALLS, NSE · first 2026-03-19, latest 2026-07-17

> **Listing:** PARTIAL SPIN-OFF, LISTED — SBI Funds Management Limited trades since 2026-07-21 (NSE equity list); the parent keeps its remaining stake

**The partial spin-off:** **SBI Funds Management Limited** (subsidiary); IPO stage: listed; NSE symbol SBIFUNDS; timeline: Allotment is expected to take place on or about July 18, 2026 (per the annexure to the letter dated July 11, 2026); the IPO was open for subscription by the pub.

> “We have been informed by SBIFM that it has filed a red herring prospectus dated July 8, 2026 with the Registrar of Companies, Mumbai – I at Mumbai ("RHP"), in relation to the proposed initial public o”

**Stated in the filings:** size hint: 0.7% of income.

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** SBI Funds Management Limited, the bank's asset management (mutual fund) subsidiary, partially listed via offer for sale — class `value_unlocking`.

- *Insiders:* SBI sells only up to 4.8851% (cut from 6.3007%) and retains the rest — "we are not fully exiting... still have potential to monetize further"; employees got Rs.54/share discount and ESOPs
- *What it reveals:* A dominant AMC carried at cost: total income Rs.4,969.09 crores, only 0.70% of SBI Group income, reserves Rs.3,533.09 crores; priced at Rs.574/share. Chairman cites "hidden reserves... in terms of strategic investments" not marked to market, plus Rs.2,200 crores special dividend
- *Selling pressure:* unlikely — Book-built IPO to bidding investors and 30 pre-IPO buyers, not distributed to SBI holders; no index exclusion stated
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *option pricing date:* Price band fixed July 8, 2026 at Rs.545 to Rs.574; Offer Price decided at Rs.574.00 per Equity Share on July 16, 2026
- *Read next:* SBIFM Prospectus dated July 16, 2026 — AUM, PAT and implied valuation at Rs.574 versus SBI's retained stake
- *In their words:* “State Bank of India has been informed that the Offer Price for the Offer has been decided to be Rs. 574.00 per Equity Share.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

The business being separated is SBI Funds Management Limited (SBIFM) — SBI Mutual Fund, the bank's asset-management joint venture with Amundi — which SBI is partially separating by listing it, not by demerging it; management repeatedly framed the purpose as "value unlocking" and, in Chairman C.S. Setty's words, "more importantly, value recognition for the industry" (Nov 2025), with SBI General Insurance named alongside AMC as the other listing candidate. The driver management gave was that SBI's own stock does not reflect the conglomerate's worth: Setty called SBI's valuation "a conundrum, considering our return on equity and growth metrics" (Nov 2025, with ROE 19.7%–20.68% and ROA >1% through FY26), and the same theme runs through the hidden-value argument on strategic holdings — of the group's ~7.3% NSE stake he said "the moment NSE gets listed, the whole shareholding by SBI will be available as reserve to us to mark to market" (May 2026). Explicitly NOT a capital-need story at first: in Nov 2025 Setty said "these two companies do not require capital at this juncture. Neither the parent requires because we just raised Rs. 25,000 crores" (the July 2025 QIP, India's largest, 4.5x oversubscribed on a >Rs. 1.1 trillion book, >60% cross-border), which is why timing was left to "respective boards"; by May 2026 the rationale had hardened into a capital one — the listing "will result in capital augmentation, CET-1" on top of CAR already up 115bps to 15.4%. The structure confirms it is monetisation, not a fix for the business: the IPO is a pure offer for sale (no fresh issue), SBI offering 6.3007% and JV partner Amundi India Holding 3.7006%, total up to 10.0013% / 203,709,239 shares at Rs. 1 face value, so no money reaches SBIFM itself. Management stressed that separation does not break the franchise link — SBIFM stays the country's largest AMC inside the "One SBI" cross-sell engine (a special dividend of ~Rs. 2,200 crore came up to the bank in Q3FY26, cross-sell/CVE income targeted at $1 billion, YONO "deep integration with subsidiary production"), and Setty was explicit that "Mutual fund, we are not fully exiting. So we still have potential to monetize further when market improves" (Feb 2026). The push came from the sell side and retail investors — Sushil Choksey (Indus Equity), Manoj Alimchandani and Kunal Shah (Citigroup) raised monetisation/value-unlocking on four of the five calls, Alimchandani even arguing in Feb 2026 that delaying the IPO five years could fetch three times the market cap — rather than from lenders or regulators; the only regulator-linked nudge cited was the SEBI chairman on NSE's listing. No problem with SBIFM's performance was ever offered as a reason: it was described only as "the largest AMC in the country," contributing Rs. 4,969.09 crore of FY26 total income, just 0.70% of group income.

**How it evolved:** May 2025 had no separation plan at all — only "we will continue to nurture these subsidiaries," while the bank instead took an enabling resolution for Rs. 25,000 crore of its own equity. By Aug 2025 Setty conceded "a couple of candidates for listing, but… there is no sense of urgency," and in Nov 2025 he named them — SBI AMC and SBI General — as the right candidates for "value unlocking" and "value recognition," with boards to set timing; the SBIFM stake-sale approval for 6.3007% followed on 6 Nov 2025 and the DRHP on 19 Mar 2026 (share count restated to 128,334,397 after a bonus issue and ESOP exercises). Feb 2026 added the retained-upside caveat ("we are not fully exiting") and May 2026 re-cast the deal as CET-1 capital augmentation to be completed within FY27. The plan then changed in execution in July 2026: a pre-IPO placement of 28,832,748 shares (1.4156%) to 30 investors at Rs. 574 for Rs. 1,655 crore on 9–10 July cut SBI's offer-for-sale from 6.3007% to 4.8851% (total offer 8.3933%), priced at Rs. 574 with allotment expected 18 July 2026.

**What management expects from it:** For SBIFM: a listed market price that recognises India's largest AMC, with SBI retaining control, banca distribution and future monetisation upside. For SBI: value unlocking and "value recognition," CET-1 capital augmentation supporting 13-15% credit growth, hidden reserves surfaced (as with NSE), and valuation converging on >1% ROA and 15%+ through-cycle ROE. No margin or focus benefit was claimed.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *[May 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=bba71336-f98b-40e2-8d50-c9435948876b.pdf)* — No separation on the table: subsidiaries framed purely as value creators to be retained, while the bank instead took an enabling resolution to raise Rs. 25,000 crore of its own equity. “Our subsidiaries are consistently performing well and continue to create significant value for all the stakeholders. We will continue to nurture these subsidiaries and maintain leadership position in the respective businesses.”
- *[Aug 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=2fa1b8da-c066-4091-b913-b10127270df1.pdf)* — First acknowledgement of listing candidates, asked for by Sushil Choksey (Indus Equity Advisors); Setty explicitly de-prioritised it because the Rs. 25,000 crore QIP had just closed. “No, as we mentioned that we definitely have a couple of candidates for listing, but the timing is not very… there is no sense of urgency there, I believe.”
- *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=ad15487a-d1a9-4e33-90e9-624255749750.pdf)* — The rationale stated in full for the first time, in answer to Choksey on the group's underperforming consolidated value: SBI AMC and SBI General named, with value unlocking and industry recognition of value as the purpose. “But among these four major subsidiaries, we definitely would be looking at, as I mentioned several times, SBI AMC and SBI General are right candidates for listing in our stable. It also provides some value unlocking and, more importantly, value recognition for the industry.”
- *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=ad15487a-d1a9-4e33-90e9-624255749750.pdf)* — Answering Kunal Shah (Citigroup) on what would trigger the decision, Setty ruled capital need out as a motive for either the subsidiaries or the parent, leaving timing and quantum to the subsidiary boards. “I think we need to just look at, see, one is, as I mentioned earlier also, that these two companies do not require capital at this juncture.”
- *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=ad15487a-d1a9-4e33-90e9-624255749750.pdf)* — The underlying grievance the separation is meant to address — SBI's own market valuation not tracking its ROE and growth — stated in the Chairman's opening remarks; Ashok Ajmera had quantified it as a Rs. 8.82 lakh crore market cap on Rs. 100 trillion of business versus Rs. 15.14 lakh crore for a Rs. 57 trillion peer. “Although the current valuations of SBI are a conundrum, considering our return on equity and growth metrics, we are confident that they will eventually align with our fundamental and operational metrics, the institutionalized nature of our business and our market leadership in the coming years.”
- *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=8fabbe0f-593e-4701-b565-d5fce57385a2.pdf)* — Retained-stake logic: asked by Manoj Alimchandani whether delaying the IPO five years could treble the market cap, Setty defended a partial sale that keeps future upside with SBI. “Mutual fund, we are not fully exiting. So we still have potential to monetize further when market improves.”
- *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=8fabbe0f-593e-4701-b565-d5fce57385a2.pdf)* — Why the AMC is worth separating while staying attached: it is already the country's largest AMC, upstreamed a Rs. 2,200 crore special dividend into SBI's Q3FY26 profit, and feeds a cross-sell income stream management targets at $1 billion. “If I have to talk about one-off, I think the one item which is a special dividend we have received, around Rs. 2,200 crores from SBI Mutual Fund.”
- *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=9a3280a0-5ce9-445e-a881-6b7c505e9a90.pdf)* — The rationale shifts to capital: with the AMC listing under way, Setty tied it to CET-1 augmentation supporting credit growth (the bank could already fund ~Rs. 12 trillion of growth, CAR 15.4%, up 115bps YoY). “We are also seriously, as you are aware, we have embarked on listing SBI AMC and hopefully in this financial year we will be able to complete, which will result in capital augmentation, CET-1.”
- *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=9a3280a0-5ce9-445e-a881-6b7c505e9a90.pdf)* — Same hidden-value argument applied to the group's ~7.3% NSE holding, which is not marked to market today — listing is the mechanism that converts unrecognised strategic stakes into reported reserves. “But as you mentioned, I think the moment NSE gets listed, the whole shareholding by SBI will be available as reserve to us to mark to market.”
- *Scheme* — 6 Nov 2025 board approval, restated in the 19 Mar 2026 DRHP filing: a pure offer for sale of up to 10.0013% (203,709,239 shares of Rs. 1 each) — SBI 6.3007% (128,334,397 shares) and JV partner Amundi India Holding 3.7006% (75,374,842 shares). No fresh issue, so no proceeds go to SBIFM. “The IPO comprises an offer for sale of up to 128,334,397 Equity Shares (amounting to 6.3007% of the paid-up equity share capital of SBIFML) by State Bank of India, and of up to 75,374,842 Equity Shares (amounting to 3.7006% of the paid-up equity share capital of SBIFML) by Amundi India Holding.”
- *Scheme* — Plan changed in execution: a pre-IPO secondary placement on 9–10 July 2026 moved 1.4156% of pre-offer capital to 30 investors at the eventual Rs. 574 offer price, raising Rs. 1,655 crore for SBI ahead of the book build. “State Bank of India had entered into share purchase agreements each dated July 9, 2026 to sell, in aggregate, 2,88,32,748 equity shares of SBIFM of face value Rs. 1 (one) each ("Equity Shares"), being equivalent to 1.4156% of pre-Offer share capital of SBIFM, to a total of 30 (thirty) investors at Rs. 574.00 per Equity Share, for an aggregate consideration of Rs. 1,655.00 crores.”
- *Scheme* — The 11 July 2026 addendum cut SBI's offer-for-sale by exactly the pre-IPO quantum, to 4.8851% (total offer 8.3933%); the offer was priced at Rs. 574 on 16 July with a Rs. 54 employee discount and allotment expected on or about 18 July 2026. “The size of the offer for sale by the State Bank of India in the IPO has been revised from up to 128,334,397 Equity Shares (amounting to 6.3007% of the paid-up equity share capital of SBIFM) to up to 99,501,649 Equity Shares (amounting to 4.8851% of the paid-up equity share capital of SBIFM).”

*Not explained on the calls:* No valuation target, expected proceeds, CET-1 basis points, or use of funds; no reason the offer was trimmed; Amundi's motive, SBI General's timeline, and post-listing distribution/royalty terms unexplained.

*Calls read (36 months):* [May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=9a3280a0-5ce9-445e-a881-6b7c505e9a90.pdf), [Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=ad15487a-d1a9-4e33-90e9-624255749750.pdf)

### The business being separated — its own numbers

**SBI Funds Management Ltd. (SBIFML / SBI Mutual Fund) — disclosed only as a subsidiary PAT line; within SBI's segment reporting it is subsumed in "Other Banking Operations"** · unit ₹ crore · Only PAT is disclosed for the entity, in the analyst presentations' subsidiary slides, stated as 'As per Ind AS, without OCI' and 'as published by respective subsidiaries'. > **Listing:** PARTIAL SPIN-OFF, LISTED — HDB Financial Services Limited trades since 2025-07-02 (NSE equity list); the parent keeps 74.1%

**The partial spin-off:** **HDB Financial Services Limited** (subsidiary); parent's stake after: 74.1%; IPO stage: listed; NSE symbol HDBFS.

> “On June 25, 2025, the Bank's subsidiary company, HDB Financial Services Limited ("HDBFS") launched its initial public offering ("IPO"), comprised of a fresh issuance of equity shares aggregating to ? ”

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** HDB Financial Services Limited, the Bank's non-deposit-taking NBFC subsidiary, separately listed via IPO (fresh issue plus Bank's offer for sale) — class `not stated`.

- *Insiders:* Bank retains 74.1% stake in HDBFSL post-IPO; HDB Employee Welfare Trust is consolidated as a subsidiary. No promoter or management stake or incentive in HDBFS is stated.
- *What it reveals:* Sale of 13,51,35,135 shares at Rs 740 raised Rs 10,000 crore, netting Rs 9,179.40 crore standalone gain (Rs 7,000.27 crore consolidated) — implying carrying value far below market; HDBFSL loan book Rs 1,146 billion, Stage 3 2.81%, CAR 21.8%.
- *Selling pressure:* unlikely — Listing was an IPO/offer for sale, not a share distribution to parent shareholders; no index exclusion or forced holder reshuffle stated.
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* HDBFS's own standalone financials and shareholding pattern — the Bank's residual 74.1% stake and its carrying value.
- *In their words:* “On June 25, 2025, the Bank's subsidiary company, HDB Financial Services Limited ("HDBFS") launched its initial public offering ("IPO"), comprised of a fresh issuance of equity shares aggregating to ₹ 2,500.00 crore and an offer for sale ("OFS") of equity shares by the Bank, aggregating to ₹ 10,000.00 crore.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

These texts contain no separation, demerger, spin-off or scheme of arrangement for HDFC Bank, and management never explains one; the question's premise is not supported by the documents supplied. The only business that was partly separated from the Bank is HDB Financial Services Limited (HDBFS), the group's non-deposit-taking NBFC, and that was done by listing it rather than by demerging it: a June 25, 2025 IPO comprising a fresh issue of Rs 2,500.00 crore plus an offer for sale of Rs 10,000.00 crore of the Bank's shares (13,51,35,135 shares of Rs 10 each at Rs 740 per share), after which the Bank still held 74.1%. Management gave no reason for the listing at all — no regulatory mandate, no capital need, no valuation argument, no investor or lender demand was cited; Sashidhar Jagdishan only reported that 'we carried out the HDB Financial Services listing process, wherein the bank also diluted some stake' and thanked IPO investors. The only strategic point made about HDBFS was in answer to Pranav Gundlapalle (Jul 2025), who asked about customer conflict between the two entities: management said HDBFS serves a segment 'a notch or two below' the Bank, with 'zero or very minimal overlap' expected to persist, i.e. the two are kept distinct by customer segment and pricing, not separated to fix a problem. Financially the event was treated as a one-off gain — Rs 9,179.40 crore standalone and Rs 7,000.27 crore consolidated (before tax, net of IPO expenses) — which Srinivasan Vaidyanathan later flagged (Jul 2026) as a base-effect distortion making reported PAT growth 5% versus 9.8% adjusted. Every other corporate action in these texts runs the other way: deepening the 2023 HDFC Limited merger (Apr 2026: e-HDFC home-loan customers' liability penetration up from 36% to ~50%, their CASA balances up from about Rs 50,000 crore to Rs 86,000 crore, 98% of new home loans opening a liability account, 23% carrying active Bank credit cards) and the Apr 16, 2026 board approval to invest up to Rs 1,000 crore in HDFC Life's preferential issue. The closest thing to a forward-looking separation hint is Jagdishan's unprompted remark on surplus capital (Oct 2025): if options arise 'to sort of delight shareholders, we would be more than happy to do so' — unspecified, with no business named.

**How it evolved:** Jul 19, 2025: the HDB Financial Services IPO and the Bank's stake dilution are reported as completed (listed Jul 2, 2025), with no rationale, and management answers only the question of bank-versus-HDBFS customer overlap. Oct 18, 2025: asked by Chintan (Autonomous) what the Bank will do with excess CET1, Jagdishan leaves the door open to unnamed 'other options... to delight shareholders' while stressing capital will be consumed once growth accelerates from FY27. Jan 17, 2026 filings quantify the transaction (Rs 10,000 crore OFS, Rs 9,179.40 crore standalone gain, 74.1% residual stake); Apr 16, 2026 the Board instead commits up to Rs 1,000 crore of fresh capital to subsidiary HDFC Life. Jul 18, 2026: the HDB gain is referred to only retrospectively, as a prior-year one-timer depressing headline PAT growth to 5% versus 9.8% adjusted — the idea never develops into any separation plan.

**What management expects from it:** Nothing was said about a separation, because none was announced. For the one partial carve-out, the HDBFS listing, management claimed no margin, capital, valuation or focus benefit; it cited only a Rs 9,179.40 crore standalone one-time gain (later called a base-effect distortion) and segment distinctness — HDBFS one to two notches below the Bank, with minimal customer overlap.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *[Jul 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=d1268138-e288-4335-9764-7a944dfa3570.pdf)* — The only partial separation disclosed in any call: HDBFS was listed and the Bank sold down part of its holding, reported as a completed process with no stated rationale. “During the quarter, we carried out the HDB Financial Services listing process, wherein the bank also diluted some stake, and which eventually culminated in the stocks being listed on 2nd of July.”
- *[Jul 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=d1268138-e288-4335-9764-7a944dfa3570.pdf)* — Asked by Pranav Gundlapalle (Bernstein) whether the Bank and HDBFS would end up chasing the same customers, Jagdishan said HDBFS sits a notch or two below the Bank's segment on customer profile and pricing. “HDB, we have maintained this. I think the segment that they cater to is about a notch or two below that of HDFC Bank.”
- *[Jul 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=d1268138-e288-4335-9764-7a944dfa3570.pdf)* — Management framed the two entities as permanently distinct by segmentation rather than as a business being carved out to solve a conflict. “There is zero or very minimal overlap at this juncture that will continue to stay for a long period of time.”
- *Oct 2025* — On the capital question (CET1 near 20%, draft RWA relief, ECL), Jagdishan said capital will be consumed once FY27 growth exceeds system growth, but left unnamed shareholder-friendly options open — the only forward-looking hint of any corporate action. “Having said that, if there are any opportunities that may arise in terms of other options that are available to sort of delight shareholders, we would be more than happy to do so.”
- *Scheme* — The Jan 17, 2026 filing quantifies the HDBFS sell-down: fresh issue of Rs 2,500 crore plus Rs 10,000 crore offer for sale by the Bank, 13,51,35,135 shares at Rs 740, producing a Rs 9,179.40 crore standalone gain (Rs 7,000.27 crore consolidated) with the Bank retaining 74.1%. “On June 25, 2025, the Bank's subsidiary company, HDB Financial Services Limited ("HDBFS") launched its initial public offering ("IPO"), comprised of a fresh issuance of equity shares aggregating to 2,500.00 crore and an offer for sale ("OFS") of equity shares by the Bank, aggregating to 10,000.00 crore.”
- *Scheme* — Six weeks before the Apr 2026 call the Board moved in the opposite direction, approving fresh capital into a subsidiary rather than any separation, subject to RBI approval. “the Board of Directors of the Bank, at its meeting held today i.e. on April 16, 2026, approved investment of an amount not exceeding Rs. 1,000 crore (Rupees One thousand crore only) in the preferential issue of equity shares to be made by HDFC Life Insurance Company Limited, a subsidiary of the Bank”
- *[Apr 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=a77abbbb-954a-4221-8240-67bf0da6ba1c.pdf)* — Kaizad Bharucha's merger-synergy update shows integration, not separation: e-HDFC mortgage customers' liability penetration up from 36% to ~50%, their CASA from about Rs 50,000 crore to Rs 86,000 crore, 60-65% paying EMIs from in-house accounts, 23% holding active Bank credit cards. “Net of attritions, net of acquisitions over this journey, this 36% has come as high as 50% within the last 2.5 years.”
- *[Jul 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=509cc499-6cb1-4d9f-8de9-9c7de6c70eef.pdf)* — The HDBFS transaction appears only as a prior-year one-timer distorting the growth base, with adjusted PAT growth of 9.8% versus 5% reported — the last mention of it in any call. “But last year included certain one-timers like HDB gains and then we had a floating provision counter-cyclical buffer that we added and some contingent provision and so on.”
- *[Mar 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=56739132-e21e-4503-aeb6-85f4f53c1244.pdf)* — At the special call on Atanu Chakraborty's resignation, the only structural change hinted at was an internal reorganisation of responsibilities, explicitly not a business separation and with nothing decided. “Yes, as I said, as we move forward, we will sort of re-examine our organization structure and with the consent and the advice of the board, we will announce it at the appropriate time.”

*Not explained on the calls:* Everything: no separation, demerger or scheme exists here. No reason, regulator, lender or investor demand, valuation case, timeline or margin/capital effect for the HDBFS listing is given.

## KPIL — Kalpataru Projects International Ltd.

**CONFIRMED** (partial spin-off — Linjemontage i Grästorp Aktiebolag is listed since 2026-09-25) · **PARTIAL SPIN-OFF, LISTED <1Y — price the parent's stub against the listed piece** · score 5.0/10 · partial spin-off (subsidiary IPO) · 5 filing(s) from NSE · first 2026-01-16, latest 2026-10-24

> **Listing:** PARTIAL SPIN-OFF, LISTED — Linjemontage i Grästorp Aktiebolag trades since 2026-09-25 (per the filings); the parent keeps 66.45%, comprising 34,042,919 shares

**The partial spin-off:** **Linjemontage i Grästorp Aktiebolag** (subsidiary); parent's stake 96.12% (49,240,500 shares) held by Kalpataru Power Transmission Sweden AB → 66.45%, comprising 34,042,919 shares; IPO stage: listed; exchange: Nasdaq Stockholm; timeline: "The first day of trading on Nasdaq Stockholm is expected to commence on 25 September 2026 and the shares will trade under the trading symbol "LMGAB"." (press r.

> “In accordance with Regulation 30 and other applicable provisions of the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 ("LODR Regulations"),”

**Stated in the filings:** size hint: 0.43% of net worth.

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** Linjemontage (LMG), KPIL's Swedish pure-play power-infrastructure EPC step-down subsidiary, partly sold and listed via IPO on Nasdaq Stockholm — class `value_unlocking`.

- *Insiders:* KPTS (KPIL wholly owned subsidiary) retains 66.45% / 34,042,919 shares, down from 96.12%; 360-day lock-up for Kalpataru Sweden, board and group management; employee/director shareholders sold 991,950 shares mainly to repay acquisition financing
- *What it reveals:* A high-return asset-light business priced publicly: FY25/26 net sales SEK 3,225m, adjusted EBITA SEK 245m (7.6%), R.O.C.E. 48.1%, net cash SEK 172.1m, order book SEK 4,349m, valued at SEK 2,356,557,000 — yet only ~11.14% of KPIL revenue and ~4.5% of its net worth
- *Selling pressure:* unlikely — No distribution to KPIL shareholders; IPO buyers chose the shares, cornerstone investors took SEK 290m, insiders locked up 360 days
- *Parent or spin:* — · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* LMG's prospectus on linjemontage.com (Q1 26/27 figures, Selling Shareholders) and LMG's traded price versus the SEK 46 offer
- *In their words:* “Linjemontage's Board of Directors and its majority shareholder, Kalpataru Sweden, a wholly-owned subsidiary of Kalpataru Projects International Limited ("Kalpataru India"), consider the Listing to be a strategic next step in Linjemontage's development.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

The business being separated is Linjemontage i Grästorp AB (LMG), KPIL's Swedish power-grid EPC subsidiary held through Kalpataru Power Transmission Sweden AB (KPTS) — separated not by demerger but by an offer-for-sale IPO on Nasdaq Stockholm (listed 25 September 2026), in which KPTS sold down from 96.12% to 66.45% rather than giving LMG new capital. The trigger management cited on the calls was value crystallisation and cash: LMG had compounded from ~INR1,000 crores revenue in FY24 to INR1,800+ crores in FY25 (PBT INR21 crores to INR70+ crores) to ~INR3,000 crores in FY26 with EBITDA ~INR200 crores and PBT ~INR170 crores (both up over 100%), i.e. SEK1.3bn to SEK3.2bn net sales at a 56.6% CAGR with adjusted EBITA margin rising from 4.4% to 7.6%, net cash of SEK172.1m, ROCE of 48.1% and an order book of SEK4,349m — yet it was only ~11.14% of KPIL's consolidated revenue and ~4.5% of consolidated net worth. Mohnot repeatedly placed the Sweden 'fundraise' inside the same bucket as the noncore exits (Vindhyachal road asset sold January 2026 for ~INR799 crores EV / INR600+ crores net, Indore real estate, Shree Shubham Logistics), i.e. as a source of 'further cash flows' to cut leverage and fund the INR800-900 crores/year capex programme and lift ROCE; the IPO delivered KPTS gross proceeds of ~SEK711.45m at SEK46/share, valuing LMG at SEK2,356.6m (~INR2,324 crores). The second problem it solves is that LMG's economics are structurally different from KPIL's: management argued a 6%-7% PBT in a 'mature market' is fine there because 'the ROCE numbers are very, very high and they are cash positive always' — a profile the consolidated KPIL multiple was not reflecting. LMG's own filings justify the separation on strategic grounds: visibility, credibility and brand recognition with customers, partners and employees, transparency, a platform for long-term value creation, a broadened shareholder base, and support for its ambition to lead Nordic power-infrastructure EPC in a Swedish serviceable market growing from ~SEK19bn (2025) to ~SEK31bn (2030) at 11% CAGR (transmission 17%), with ~80% of Sweden's transmission grid over 40 years old and Statnett planning NOK150-200bn of 2025-2034 investment. Pressure came from investors and analysts, not lenders: Carnelian and DAM Capital pushed management on why a T&D business sitting inside a T&D company needed its own listing, while cornerstone demand from Tredje AP-fonden and Unionen (SEK290m) anchored the book; LMG's management/employee shareholders (991,950 shares) sold mainly to repay the financing they had used to buy their shares. KPIL stressed continuity, not exit: KPTS 'indicated an intention to remain a long-term major shareholder', is locked up for 360 days, and LMG remains a step-down subsidiary.

**How it evolved:** The idea surfaced on the 19 May 2025 Q4 FY25 call, where Mohnot disclosed that the Board had approved appointing bankers and intermediaries to examine 'fundraising options' at Linjemontage — framed alongside the noncore clean-up (VEPL, Indore, Shubham); the 14 Feb 2025 call had contained no such plan, only LMG's record order book of INR3,143 crores. By 8 August 2025 (Q1 FY26) it had hardened into a disclosed 'strategic overview… including options related to IPO, subject to market conditions', and management refused to explain the logic when Carnelian asked why a T&D business inside a T&D company needed a separate listing, even withdrawing LMG margin guidance because the process had started. On 31 October 2025 Mohnot said the path was still undecided but expected 'some light' on valuation in FY26-27, and on 5 February 2026 he said the Sweden mandate was 'progressing well' and should throw off cash in FY26-27; by 15 May 2026 he described it only as 'some strategic investment coming into our Swedish subsidiary in whatever form it comes'. The form was fixed in the filings: KPTS board approval on 9 September 2026, prospectus and SEK46 price on 16 September, listing and ~32.1% offer on 25 September, and partial greenshoe exercise on 23-24 October 2026 leaving KPIL at 66.45%.

**What management expects from it:** For LMG: standalone visibility, credibility and brand with customers and employees; transparency; a growth platform and broadened shareholder base; revenue above SEK5bn, adjusted EBITA margin above 8%, net debt/EBITDA under 1.0x, 25% payout. For KPIL: ~SEK711m cash to cut debt and fund capex, value crystallised at SEK2.36bn, retained 66.45% control, higher ROCE and a cleaner noncore-free core EPC portfolio.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *[Feb 2025](https://kalpataruprojects.com/api/view-file/KPIL_Q3_FY25_Transcript.pdf)* — Baseline: no separation plan existed; LMG was simply presented as a record performer, with revenue doubling and an all-time-high order book of INR3,143 crores. “LMG's order book is at a all time high of INR3,143 crores.”
- *[May 2025](https://kalpataruprojects.com/api/view-file/KPIL_Q4_FY25_Transcript.pdf)* — First disclosure of the separation idea — the Board approved bankers and intermediaries to study fundraising options at Linjemontage, mentioned in the same breath as LMG's PBT rising from ~INR21 crores to ~INR70+ crores. “the Board has also approved appointment of bankers as well as intermediaries to look at fund options, fundraising options in Sweden Linjemontage in the last Board meeting, which we have declared to everyone.”
- *[Aug 2025](https://kalpataruprojects.com/api/view-file/KPIL_Q1FY26_transcript.pdf)* — Formalised as a disclosed 'strategic overview' with an IPO explicitly named as one of the options, and merchant bankers and advisers appointed; LMG had already begun preparatory steps. “We have initiated a strategic overview on LMG where various options are being evaluated, including options related to IPO, subject to market conditions.”
- *[Aug 2025](https://kalpataruprojects.com/api/view-file/KPIL_Q1FY26_transcript.pdf)* — An investor (Mihir Manohar, Carnelian Capital) pressed on exactly the question management never answered — why carve out a T&D business that already sits inside a T&D company; Mohnot declined to comment. “I just wanted to understand the thought process because I mean, it is also T&D business similarly sitting in KPIL.”
- *[Oct 2025](https://kalpataruprojects.com/api/view-file/KPIL_Q2_FY26_Transcript.pdf)* — Management explained LMG's different economic profile — lower PBT than KPIL's core but very high ROCE and permanently cash positive — the implicit valuation argument for separating it, with bankers still mandated and the path undecided. “As far as margins are concerned, I think that those are mature markets where a PBT of 6% to 7% is very reasonably good because the ROCE numbers are very, very high and they are cash positive always.”
- *[Feb 2026](https://kalpataruprojects.com/api/view-file/KPIL_Q3_FY26_Earnings_Call_Transcript-5th_feb_2026.pdf)* — The Sweden transaction was placed squarely in the monetisation/debt-reduction bucket alongside transmission assets, the last road asset and Shree Shubham Logistics, with cash expected in FY26-27. “We do not know which options and what timing it exactly is, but we have appointed bankers to look at exploring fund option raising at Sweden also, which I'm expecting in FY26-27 should give us further cash flows.”
- *[May 2026](https://kalpataruprojects.com/api/view-file/KPILQ4_FY26_Earnings_Call_Transcript_final.pdf)* — Final pre-IPO framing: a 'strategic investment' into the Swedish subsidiary grouped with remaining divestments as free-cash-flow events to strengthen the balance sheet, set against INR800+ crores of annual capex and net debt already down 50% to INR915 crores. “We also have some events of free cash flows coming in next year, whether it is through a few more divestments which are left, which might happen either next year or a year after that or whether it is through some strategic investment coming into our Swedish subsidiary in whatever form it comes.”
- *Scheme* — The 9 September 2026 filing/press release gives the official rationale — standalone visibility, credibility, brand and Nordic leadership ambition — and discloses LMG's scale: SEK3,225m FY26 revenue (~11.14% of KPIL consolidated revenue) but only SEK334m net worth (~4.5% of KPIL's). “The Listing is expected to enhance the Company's visibility, credibility and brand recognition among customers, partners and employees, and to support Linjemontage's long-term ambition to strengthen its position in the Nordics as one of the leading EPC providers within power infrastructure.”
- *Scheme* — Transparency, long-term value creation and a diversified shareholder base are the stated second leg, with KPTS committing to stay a long-term major shareholder (360-day lock-up) and LMG remaining a step-down subsidiary. “Becoming a publicly listed company will also provide greater transparency and a platform for long-term value creation, while diversifying the shareholder base.”
- *Scheme* — Structurally this is a pure sell-down, not a capital raise for LMG: 14,311,620 base shares plus a 2,146,743-share greenshoe at SEK46, ~32.1% of LMG, giving KPTS gross proceeds of ~SEK711.45m at a SEK2,356.6m (~INR2,324 crores) valuation and taking KPTS from 96.12% to 66.45% after the partial greenshoe exercise of 1,877,911 shares. “The Offering consists only of existing shares and the Company will therefore not receive any proceeds from the Offering.”
- *Scheme* — Demand was investor-led: Tredje AP-fonden and Unionen cornerstoned SEK290m, while LMG's own management/director/employee holders sold 991,950 shares chiefly to repay the borrowings used to buy them. “All individual Selling Shareholders other than Kalpataru Sweden are selling shares in the Offering primarily to repay financing arrangements relating to their respective acquisitions of shares in the Company.”
- *Scheme* — LMG's standalone financial targets quantify what separation is meant to unlock — revenue above SEK5bn, adjusted EBITA margin above 8% (from 7.6%), net debt/adj EBITDA below 1.0x and a 25% dividend payout — in a market growing 11% CAGR to SEK31bn by 2030. “Profitability : Linjemontage aims to reach an adjusted EBITA margin exceeding 8 per cent in the medium term.”

*Not explained on the calls:* Calls never explained why a listing over a trade sale, the valuation sought, use of proceeds, dilution to consolidated EPS, or minority/governance terms; management explicitly refused to give the rationale.

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

The business being separated is Reliance's FMCG/consumer-brands arm, Reliance Consumer Products Ltd (RCPL) — Campa, Independence, Good Life, Ravalgaon/Toffeeman/Lotus, Velvette, Glimmer, Enzo, SIL, Maliban, Alan's, plus acquisitions Udhaiyam, Manna, Sosyo, Goodness Group and the Toni & Guy/Brylcreem/Badedas/Matey brands — which was carved out of Reliance Retail Ventures Ltd (RRVL) under a composite scheme effective 1 December 2025: the 'Consumer Brands Business Undertaking' was demerged from RRVL into Tira Beauty Ltd (renamed RCPL), the old RCPL was dissolved, RRVL shareholders received 1 new RCPL share for every 2 RRVL shares, and the new entity became an 83.56% direct subsidiary of RIL rather than a retail subsidiary. The only rationale management actually articulates is in the Chairman's 16 January 2026 statement: the consumer products vertical is 'progressing on its accelerated growth trajectory with a focused organizational structure' — i.e. a dedicated, directly-held vehicle for a business scaling far faster than retail (Q3 FY26 Rs 5,000 crore, +60% Y-o-Y; 9M FY26 Rs 15,000 crore; FY26 Rs 22,000 crore, 2x Y-o-Y; Q4 FY26 Rs 7,350 crore; Q1 FY27 Rs 8,600 crore, 2x; Campa Rs 4,700 crore and India's 4th largest CSD brand; Independence Rs 2,600 crore; beverages over Rs 6,000 crore; 3rd largest packaged water player; 5,000+ distributors, 3 million outlets, 40 export markets; target Rs 1 lakh crore by FY2030). The problem it visibly solves, though never stated as the reason, is mixing an only-breakeven, capex-hungry FMCG build-out (12 plants, integrated food parks, Kurnool and 'one of the largest beverage plants in Asia', edible-oil facility in West Bengal) into Reliance Retail's P&L: on every call since, management has had to strip RCPL out to show the underlying retail trend — Q3 FY26 8.1% reported, Q4 FY26 11% reported vs ~14% adjusted, Q1 FY27 7.4% reported vs 11.6% adjusted — while Ketan Mody confirms RCPL itself is only 'breakeven on EBITDA terms'. Two parallel separations run alongside it: the Jio Platforms IPO (DRHP 19 June 2026 for a fresh issue of up to 27 crore shares of Rs 10, SEBI observation 28 August 2026, RHP 14 October 2026, priced at Rs 1,119 on 24 October 2026, with Rs 500 crore reserved for employees and Rs 2,500 crore for individual/HUF RIL shareholders), and the carve-out of AI/data-centre activity into 'Reliance Intelligence'/RIL so that JPL stays asset-light — capex at RIL or Reliance Intelligence, service provision and products accessed by Jio under long-term leases. No investor, lender or partner is recorded as having asked for any of this; analysts' only questions on the demerger were for like-for-like revenue and EBITDA adjustments, and management expressly deferred the EBITDA impact to the next quarter.

**How it evolved:** On the Oct 2024 call the consumer-brands business was still just a bullet inside Dinesh Taluja's retail section (general-trade revenue '250% plus' Y-o-Y) with no hint of separation. The 1 Dec 2025 scheme filings made it real — RCPL demerged out of RRVL into a directly held 83.56% RIL subsidiary — and on the 16 Jan 2026 call (Q3 FY26) RCPL got its own speaker (Ketan Mody), its own Rs 5,000 crore quarter, and the Chairman's 'focused organizational structure' line, while analysts (Investec's Harit Kapoor, CLSA's Vikash Jain) could only extract 'we will have to wait for the next quarter' on the margin impact. By 24 Apr 2026 RCPL presented through its own CFO (Ashutosh Goyal, FY26 Rs 22,000 crore) and retail growth was being quoted both reported and ex-demerger; by 17 Jul 2026 an RCPL Executive Director gave a Rs 1 lakh crore FY2030 ambition and admitted EBITDA breakeven. Over the same window the separation theme widened: AI data centres were explicitly moved out of JPL into Reliance Intelligence (Jan/Apr 2026 calls) and the JPL IPO moved from 'imminent' (Apr 2026) to DRHP (19 Jun 2026) to pricing at Rs 1,119 (24 Oct 2026).

**What management expects from it:** RCPL: a focused structure for accelerated growth to Rs 1 lakh crore by FY2030, with EBITDA rising from breakeven as capacity, food parks and supply chain scale. Retail: cleaner double-digit underlying growth plus ~8% margins, free to fund hyperlocal/digital commerce and double EBITDA in three years. RIL shareholders: direct 83.56%-held ownership and 1-for-2 shares; Jio stays asset-light with capex in Reliance Intelligence.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *Scheme* — The 1 Dec 2025 composite scheme demerged the Consumer Brands Business Undertaking from RRVL into Tira Beauty Ltd (renamed RCPL), dissolved the old RCPL, and paid RRVL shareholders 1 new RCPL share for every 2 RRVL shares. “in terms of the Scheme, as consideration for the demerger of the Consumer Brands Business Undertaking from RRVL to New RCPL, New RCPL will allot 1 (one) fully paid-up equity share of Rs. 10 (Rupees ten only) each for every 2 (two) fully paid-up equity shares of Rs. 10 (Rupees ten only) each of RRVL, to the shareholders of RRVL.”
- *Scheme* — The structural outcome: FMCG stops being a retail subsidiary and becomes a business RIL owns directly at 83.56%, with the pre-scheme RRVL-held capital of the new entity cancelled. “Accordingly, New RCPL will become 83.56% direct subsidiary of the Company.”
- *FILING 2026-01-16* — The only stated rationale anywhere in these documents: the Chairman frames the demerger as giving the consumer products vertical a focused organisational structure to support accelerated growth. “The demerger of consumer products business came into effect this quarter. With a broad and diverse product basket ranging from classic Indian brands to new age labels, the consumer products vertical is progressing on its accelerated growth trajectory with a focused organizational structure.”
- *CALL Jan 2026* — CFO V Srikanth confirmed the 1 December effective date and sized the separated business at over Rs 5,000 crore of quarterly turnover, growing 60% Y-o-Y — the growth differential versus retail's 8%. “On the FMCG side, the demerger happened on 1st December. And we are at more than 5,000 Crores of turnover, and this is 60% up on a year-on-year basis.”
- *CALL Jan 2026* — Ketan Mody opened RCPL's first post-demerger section by stating the new ownership line (direct subsidiary of RIL, not of Reliance Retail), with 9M revenue of Rs 15,000 crore and four brands above Rs 1,000 crore. “So RCPL became the direct subsidiary of RIL from 1st December 2025.”
- *CALL Jan 2026* — Asked by CLSA and Investec to quantify the EBITDA that left Reliance Retail with the demerger, Dinesh Taluja declined to give the number — the separation's margin arithmetic was never explained on the call. “We will have to wait for the next quarter.”
- *CALL Apr 2026* — From Q4 FY26 the demerger became a permanent adjustment in retail's reported growth: 11% reported, ~14% ex-RCPL for the quarter and 12% for the year. “Now, if you recollect, RCPL business was demerged out in the last quarter adjusted for that, the growth is almost 14%, for the full year the growth is 12% and if you exclude RCPL demerger the growth would be even higher.”
- *CALL Apr 2026* — RCPL began reporting through its own CFO with full-year scale figures — Rs 22,000 crore FY26 revenue (2x), Campa Rs 4,700 crore as India's 4th largest CSD brand, Independence Rs 2,600 crore, 12 plants, 5,000 distributors, 3 million outlets, 40 countries. “From an FMCG business perspective, we closed our revenue of Rs.22,000 Crores in 2026 and for the Q4 alone, we delivered a revenue of Rs.7350 Crores, both these are two times growth on the similar period for the last year.”
- *CALL Jul 2026* — A full year of the demerger now creates a ~4 percentage point gap between retail's reported and underlying growth, the clearest evidence of the optics the separation changes. “In terms of topline growth, as you would recollect, RCPL business was demerged out on 1st of December. So Q1 had the full revenue. Adjusted for that, the underlying revenue growth is 11.6%. On a reported basis, the growth is 7.4%.”
- *CALL Jul 2026* — The separated entity's own target is Rs 1 lakh crore of revenue by FY2030, with Q1 FY27 revenue of Rs 8,600 crore (2x) — but it is still only at EBITDA breakeven, with margins to come from scale and supply chain. “So, like we have announced, the target continues to kind of grow leadership in all categories and we have anyway announced the target is to kind of take this to Rs.1 lakh Crores on FY2030.”
- *CALL Jul 2026* — Ketan Mody conceded RCPL earns essentially nothing today — i.e. a breakeven, market-share-focused business was removed from a retail P&L running at ~8% EBITDA margin. “EBITDA, I would put it across since the concentration there, yes, we are breakeven on EBITDA terms, but EBITDA will improve as a scale and all the supply chain is kind of put it across but yes, right now the concentration more on the market share”
- *CALL Oct 2024* — Baseline before the separation: the same brands (Campa, Independence, Maliban, Ravalgaon) were reported as one line inside Reliance Retail, with no mention of any demerger or separate entity. “Consumer brands business continues to scale up very nicely. We are expanding our distribution network. The general trade revenues are growing at 250% plus on Y-o-Y basis.”

*Not explained on the calls:* No stated reason for separating rather than retaining RCPL, no RCPL margin, capex, funding or listing plan, no EBITDA quantification, no synergy loss, tax or governance discussion.

## CANBK — Canara Bank

**CONFIRMED** (partial spin-off — Canara HSBC Life Insurance Company Limited is listed since 2025-10-17) · **PARTIAL SPIN-OFF, LISTED 1–2Y — the stub against the piece, second year** · score 3.6/10 · partial spin-off (subsidiary IPO) · 2 filing(s) from NSE · first 2025-10-16, latest 2025-10-17

> **Listing:** PARTIAL SPIN-OFF, LISTED — Canara HSBC Life Insurance Company Limited trades since 2025-10-17 (NSE equity list); the parent keeps 36.50%

**The partial spin-off:** **Canara HSBC Life Insurance Company Limited** (subsidiary); parent's stake 51% → 36.50%; IPO stage: listed; exchange: National Stock Exchange of India Limited and BSE Limited; NSE symbol CANHLIFE; timeline: Filing dated 17.10.2025: "Canara HSBC Life Insurance Company Limited got listed today (17.10.2025)"; Canara Robeco Asset Management Company Limited got listed o.

> “In furtherance to our above referred letter on the captioned subject, Stock Exchanges are hereby informed that Canara Bank divested its stake in Canara HSBC Life Insurance Company Limited, Subsidiary ”

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** Minority stakes in two subsidiaries — Canara Robeco Asset Management and Canara HSBC Life Insurance — sold via IPO — class `value_unlocking`.

- *Insiders:* Canara Bank stays promoter: 38% of Canara Robeco, 36.50% of Canara HSBC Life; "Further dilution we don't foresee"; bank is their distribution franchisee earning commission
- *What it reveals:* Listing/dilution gain of ~Rs 1,930-2,006 crore booked in Q3 FY26; bank earns ~Rs 500 crore distribution income and ~Rs 320 crore subsidiary profit as parent, plus appreciation on retained stakes
- *Selling pressure:* unlikely — Documents describe divestment through IPO, not a share distribution to parent shareholders; no index exclusion stated
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* Q3 FY26 P&L line carrying the Rs 1,930 crore one-time listing gain, and the two subsidiaries' own published results
- *In their words:* “In furtherance to our above referred letter on the captioned subject, Stock Exchanges are hereby informed that Canara Bank divested its stake in Canara Robeco Asset Management Company Limited, Subsidiary through Initial Public Offer from 51% to 38%.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

On these texts there is no demerger, spin-off or scheme of arrangement at Canara Bank; the 'separation' management actually described and executed is the partial carve-out of two wholly-controlled financial subsidiaries into separately listed companies through IPOs — Canara Robeco Asset Management (stake cut 51% to 38%, listed 16.10.2025) and Canara HSBC Life Insurance (51% to 36.50%, listed 17.10.2025) — plus one involuntary transfer, the handover of Andhra Pradesh Grameena Bank (its RRB, 'the highest profit earning RRB') to Union Bank on DFS/NABARD orders effective 30 April 2025, booked at investment face value and producing an Rs. 1,883 crore exceptional consolidated entry. The stated reason for the IPOs was value unlocking of subsidiaries whose worth was trapped inside the bank's balance sheet: MD Satyanarayana Raju said Canara Bank was 'the first banker who could come to that listing in the current financial year, 2 subsidiaries simultaneously' and netted roughly Rs. 1,935–2,006 crore after IPO expenses (Rs. 1,930 crore as finally reported), with promoter-borne IPO charges of about Rs. 80 crore sitting in Q3 FY26 opex. A second reason was balance-sheet cushion: ED Majumdar framed the 'two IPOs, two divestments' as cushion 'in case of extreme adversity,' useful against the bank's known weak spots — sub-30% CASA, a 2.5% NIM and a pending ECL transition estimated at Rs. 10,000–13,000 crore. The problems it solves are therefore valuation/visibility and one-time capital, not operational separation: management stressed control and distribution are retained ('still we will be the leading major owner of those 2 subsidiaries'), that the bank remains the distribution franchisee across 10,066–10,131 branches earning roughly Rs. 500 crore of agency/cross-sell income and about Rs. 320 crore of subsidiary profit to the parent, and that the listed entities are run by their own boards at 'arm's length distance.' Nobody in these calls — no investor, lender or partner (HSBC, Robeco) — is named as having demanded the separation; the pressure came from analysts (Suri, Sushil Choksey, Anand Dama, Ashok Ajmera) asking about monetisation, loss of control premium and how much of the profit was one-off. The bank also flagged a future candidate, Canara Bank Securities, being recapitalised and re-platformed 'so that in future, that value also we can unlock,' while explicitly refusing to sell down Can Fin Homes.

**How it evolved:** The idea first surfaces as a pending transaction in the Jul 2025 call, where analysts probe the loss of majority/control premium and timing ('one will be in this quarter... subject to SEBI permission, the one will be in the next quarter'), and Majumdar reframes the two divestments as adversity cushion; the same call records the forced RRB exit to Union Bank. By Nov 2025 both IPOs are done (filings dated 16 and 17 Oct 2025) and the pitch shifts to execution bragging and quantum — almost Rs. 2,000 crore, Rs. 1,935 crore net, to be booked in Q3 — plus a stated next candidate, Canara Bank Securities. In Jan 2026 the gain is booked and specified (14.5% in Canara HSBC, 13% in Robeco, Rs. 2,006 crore) alongside Rs. 80 crore of promoter-absorbed IPO cost and the cross-sell payoff (Rs. 500 crore income, a Rs. 6,050 crore NFO in 15 days). By May 2026 the plan is explicitly closed — 'Further dilution we don't foresee' — and the Rs. 1,930 crore is treated as non-recurring, which is why FY27 EPS and ROE guidance was cut; the Jul 2026 call, under a new MD, retrospectively recasts the rationale as a standing 'threefold benefit' (agency commission, rising subsidiary valuation, appreciation of the bank's holding).

**What management expects from it:** For the bank: a one-time Rs. 1,930-2,006 crore gain, capital/ECL cushion (CRAR 17%, CET1 12.9%), continuing roughly Rs. 500 crore agency income, about Rs. 320 crore subsidiary profit, and appreciation on its retained 36.5%/38% stakes. For the subsidiaries: market-visible valuation, own boards, arm's-length professional management, while keeping access to 10,131 branches. No margin or cost-synergy claim was made.

- *[Jul 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=63e53b9a-e3de-49bb-827e-c48a7e7f4186.pdf)* — ED S.K. Majumdar framed the two IPOs/divestments as a financial cushion against adverse outcomes (he was answering a question about NIM/NII damage from further repo cuts), tying the separation to earnings protection rather than to strategy. “I don’t think sir with now as sir said two IPOs, two divestments are also coming in. There are some cushion for us in case of extreme adversity.”

Now we are focusing more on that fourth one, we want to strengthen that subsidiary so that in future, that value also we can unlock.”

- *[Jan 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=a231c04d-8c2c-45b3-bf71-af599183ad7b.pdf)* — The transaction cost sat with the bank as promoter — about Rs. 80 crore of IPO charges for the two offers were absorbed in Q3 FY26 other operating expenses. “One was IPO charges for Canara Robeco and Canara HSBC.
