- *[Jan 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=a231c04d-8c2c-45b3-bf71-af599183ad7b.pdf)* — ED Bhavendra Kumar justified keeping the distribution link after separation with hard numbers: roughly Rs. 500 crore of income from selling subsidiary products through 10,066 branches, and an insurance NFO that gathered Rs. 6,050 crore in 15 days against a Rs. 500 crore target. “our company has also benefited, and we are earning close to 500 crores income out of the subsidiaries by selling their products.”
- *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=23b397e1-108b-42cb-b9d4-6b1c32a0b2bd.pdf)* — The programme was declared complete — no further sell-down of Canara HSBC, Canara Robeco or Can Fin Homes is contemplated, with the Rs. 1,930 crore gain cited as already banked. “Further dilution we don't foresee sir. Already 14.5% in Canara HSBC and 13% in Robeco, we have already done that.”
- *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=23b397e1-108b-42cb-b9d4-6b1c32a0b2bd.pdf)* — The separation's accounting consequence was spelled out: the Rs. 1,930 crore listing gain was the single largest reason Q4 FY26 operating and net profit fell about Rs. 2,300 crore sequentially, and the reason FY27 EPS and ROE guidance was set lower. “this 1,930 crores will not be there because it is a one-time income. So next year it won't be there. That is why it has been kept at conservative level.”

*Not explained on the calls:* No use-of-proceeds, no capital-adequacy or ROE quantification from the sell-down, no control-premium or valuation framework, no HSBC/Robeco partner view, no Canara Bank Securities timeline.

## ICICIBANK — ICICI Bank Ltd.

**CONFIRMED** (partial spin-off — ICICI Prudential Asset Management Company Limited is listed since 2025-12-19) · **PARTIAL SPIN-OFF, LISTED <1Y — price the parent's stub against the listed piece** · score 3.6/10 · partial spin-off (subsidiary IPO) · 4 filing(s) from NSE · first 2025-12-06, latest 2025-12-19

> **Listing:** PARTIAL SPIN-OFF, LISTED — ICICI Prudential Asset Management Company Limited trades since 2025-12-19 (NSE equity list); the parent keeps 53.0%

**The partial spin-off:** **ICICI Prudential Asset Management Company Limited** (joint venture); parent's stake after: 53.0%; IPO stage: listed; exchange: Bombay Stock Exchange and National Stock Exchange; NSE symbol ICICIAMC.

> “Effective December 19, 2025, ICICI Prudential Asset Management Company Limited is listed on Bombay Stock Exchange and National Stock Exchange.”

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** ICICI Prudential Asset Management Company, the group's asset management and portfolio/advisory services subsidiary — class `not stated`.

- *Insiders:* Bank held 53.0% and PCHL 34.6% at March 31, 2026; Bank bought 2.0% more from PCHL primarily to keep majority shareholding if stock-based compensation is granted
- *What it reveals:* A listed price for a fee business earning Rs 33.0 billion PAT in fiscal 2026 vs Rs 26.5 billion in fiscal 2025, now also holding ICICI Venture's private equity, venture capital and real estate fund management business
- *Selling pressure:* unlikely — No shares distributed to Bank shareholders; listing came via PCHL's partial divestment, with the Bank retaining 53.0%
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* Slides 33 to 35 of the Q4-FY2026 investor presentation for ICICI AMC's standalone financials versus the Bank's 53.0% stake
- *In their words:* “Effective December 19, 2025, ICICI Prudential Asset Management Company Limited is listed on Bombay Stock Exchange and National Stock Exchange.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

There is no separation, demerger or spin-off of a business by ICICI Bank in these texts — the question's premise is not supported by the transcripts or the filing, and the dominant direction of travel is the opposite: consolidation of group entities into the Bank. The nearest things management actually described are four entity-level reorganizations. (1) Pension funds: the Board on July 19, 2025 approved acquiring 100% of ICICI Prudential Pension Funds Management Company Limited from ICICI Prudential Life Insurance, moving it from a step-down subsidiary of ICICI Life to a direct wholly owned subsidiary of the Bank; the share purchase agreement was executed January 12, 2026, and on the Jan 2026 media call Sandeep Batra said the rationale was that 'the synergy with the Bank will be better and the business will be able to expand in a much better fashion,' i.e. 'synergising with the banking set of customers'; ICICI Life booked a Rs. 1.1 billion gain on the sale, which was part of why its FY2026 PAT rose 34.6% to Rs. 16.00 billion (25.0% excluding the sale). (2) ICICI Venture's private equity, venture capital and real estate fund management business was approved in principle on May 8, 2025 for transfer to ICICI Prudential AMC, completed with ICICI Prudential AMC managing the transferred funds effective April 1, 2026; the stated purpose was 'offering of an integrated full range of investment asset classes, including private equity,' while ICICI Venture keeps only 'certain advisory activities' and 'certain residual funds' — ICICI Venture's PAT jumped to Rs. 1.5 billion in FY2026 from Rs. 0.2 billion in FY2025. (3) A small divestment of the Bank's entire stake in the NIIT Institute of Finance and Banking JV (set up around 2006), which Batra on Apr 2025 called 'a very small amount' done to 'rationalise and simplify our own portfolio where we want to remain focused on.' (4) Closure of the Offshore Banking Unit in the SEEPZ, Mumbai, for which RBI gave a no-objection letter in May 2026 (a prior OBU closure had already pushed Rs. 3.40 billion of negative foreign currency translation reserve into the Q4-FY2024 P&L). Against these, the Bank was pulling businesses in, not pushing them out: ICICI Securities was delisted on March 24, 2025 and became wholly owned (56 million ICICI Bank shares issued at a 67:100 swap, which Anindya Banerjee cited as the main reason net worth rose about Rs. 20,000 crore sequentially, 'while it's capital neutral'); the Bank bought ~2% more of ICICI Prudential AMC and ~2% more of ICICI Life, explicitly 'towards maintaining the Bank's majority shareholding' against stock-based compensation dilution; it infused Rs. 5.0 billion (including Rs. 500 crore in Q3-FY2026) into ICICI Home Finance, which Batra justified as meeting 'the regulatory requirement and expansion that is required from their business point of view'; and it acquired the remaining equity of I-Process Services. The only genuine ownership separations described are at the partner/JV level, not the Bank's: ICICI Prudential AMC listed on BSE and NSE effective December 19, 2025 following Prudential Corporation Holdings' February 2025 announcement of a 'potential listing and partial divestment of its stake,' and after PCHL agreed on May 17, 2026 to buy 75% of Bharti Life, ICICI Life applied to IRDAI to reclassify PCHL from 'promoter' to 'investor' and to rename itself 'ICICI Life Insurance Limited' (IRDAI approved the name change August 7, 2026).

**How it evolved:** No separation idea ever surfaces as such: on Apr 2025 (call of April 19, 2025) the only disposal discussed is the small NIIT Institute JV stake sale, framed as portfolio simplification, in the same quarter ICICI Securities was delisted into the Bank (March 24, 2025). The ICICI Venture PE/VC/real-estate fund management transfer was approved in principle on May 8, 2025 and the pension-fund acquisition on July 19, 2025 — the same day as the Jul 2025 call, where neither was mentioned and no analyst asked. By Jan 2026 (call of January 17, 2026) Batra confirmed the pension step-down subsidiary had been brought under the Bank, noting 'we explained this, I think, about two quarters back when we made the decision,' and the Oct 2025 transcript is unreadable so any interim discussion is unverifiable; the Apr 2026 call (April 18, 2026) contains no mention of any of it, and only the September 18, 2026 Annual Securities Report records the ICICI Venture transfer as effective April 1, 2026 and the PCHL promoter-to-investor reclassification.

**What management expects from it:** Nothing was said about a separation, because none was announced. For the moves that were made: the pension business gains Bank-customer synergies and faster expansion; ICICI Prudential AMC gains a full asset-class platform including private equity; ICICI Venture keeps only advisory and residual funds; ICICI Life booked a Rs. 1.1 billion gain. No margin, capital-release, valuation-unlock or focus claims were offered.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *[Jan 2026](https://www.icici.bank.in/content/dam/icicibank/india/managed-assets/docs/about-us/2026/transcript-earnings-call-jan2026.pdf)* — Batra confirmed the Bank had taken over the pension fund business from ICICI Life, explaining it was a step-down subsidiary and that the decision had been disclosed about two quarters earlier. “It was a step-down subsidiary. We explained this, I think, about two quarters back when we made the decision.”
- *[Jan 2026](https://www.icici.bank.in/content/dam/icicibank/india/managed-assets/docs/about-us/2026/transcript-earnings-call-jan2026.pdf)* — The stated rationale for moving the pension fund manager under the Bank was synergy with the Bank's customer base and faster expansion, not value unlocking or capital release. “We do believe that the synergy with the Bank will be better and the business will be able to expand in a much better fashion.”
- *[Jan 2026](https://www.icici.bank.in/content/dam/icicibank/india/managed-assets/docs/about-us/2026/transcript-earnings-call-jan2026.pdf)* — Asked directly whether the pension business had been acquired from the subsidiary, Batra confirmed it in one word; no numbers, consideration or targets were given on the call. “Yes, we have.”
- *[Apr 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=1a691340-05c5-4029-a15f-cdd78f457400.pdf)* — The only outright exit discussed on any call — the entire stake in the NIIT Institute of Finance and Banking JV set up around 2006 — was framed as immaterial portfolio simplification, with no consideration disclosed. “And over the period, we are just wanting to rationalise and simplify our own portfolio where we want to remain focused on.”
- *Scheme* — The one real carve-out of a business line in the texts: ICICI Venture's private equity, venture capital and real estate fund management business was approved for transfer to ICICI Prudential AMC on May 8, 2025, with ICICI Prudential AMC managing those funds from April 1, 2026. “On May 8, 2025, ICICI Venture Funds Management Company Limited's Board of Directors and ICICI Prudential Asset Management Company Limited's Board of Directors, in their respective meetings, approved, in principle, a proposal to transfer the private equity, venture capital and real estate fund management business of ICICI Venture Funds Management Company Limited to ICICI Prudential Asset Management Company Limited.”
- *Scheme* — The purpose of that transfer was to give ICICI Prudential AMC a complete asset-class platform, leaving ICICI Venture with only advisory work and residual funds. “The transaction enabled the offering of an integrated full range of investment asset classes, including private equity, by ICICI Prudential Asset Management Company Limited.”
- *Scheme* — The pension transaction was a Board-approved intra-group purchase to convert a step-down subsidiary into a direct wholly owned subsidiary, conditional on RBI and PFRDA approvals; the SPA was executed January 12, 2026. “The Board at its meeting held on July 19, 2025 approved the acquisition of 100% shareholding in ICICI Prudential Pension Funds Management Company Limited from ICICI Prudential Life Insurance Company Limited to make ICICI PFM a wholly owned subsidiary of the Bank, subject to the Reserve Bank of India, PFRDA and other necessary approvals.”
- *Scheme* — The seller side quantified it: ICICI Life's FY2026 PAT of Rs. 16.00 billion (up 34.6%) included a Rs. 1.1 billion gain on selling the pension subsidiary; growth was 25.0% excluding it. “The profit after tax of ICICI Prudential Life Insurance Company Limited grew by 34.6% year-on-year from Rs. 11.9 billion in fiscal 2025 to Rs. 16.0 billion in fiscal 2026, primarily driven by higher investment income from Shareholders' funds, which includes a gain of Rs. 1.1 billion realized from sale of 100% equity shareholding in ICICI PFM.”
- *[Apr 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=1a691340-05c5-4029-a15f-cdd78f457400.pdf)* — Direction of travel was consolidation, not separation: ICICI Securities was delisted and absorbed as a wholly owned subsidiary on March 24, 2025, with Bank shares issued to its public shareholders at a 67:100 swap. “Pursuant to the Scheme of Arrangement amongst ICICI Bank Limited and ICICI Securities Limited and their respective shareholders, ICICI Securities Limited has been delisted from stock exchanges on March 24, 2025 and became a wholly-owned subsidiary of the Bank.”
- *[Apr 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=1a691340-05c5-4029-a15f-cdd78f457400.pdf)* — Banerjee attributed the ~Rs. 20,000 crore sequential jump in net worth to the shares issued to ICICI Securities' minority holders, describing it as capital neutral rather than value creating. “So, we would have issued shares to the minority shareholders of ISec that would have, while it's capital neutral, it would have increased the net-worth by a substantial amount.”
- *Scheme* — Stake increases in the listed subsidiaries were defensive against stock-compensation dilution, not steps toward separation: ~2% more of ICICI Prudential AMC and ~2% of ICICI Life (taking it to ~52.8%). “This purchase was primarily for the purposes of maintaining the Bank's majority shareholding in ICICI Prudential Asset Management Company Limited were it to grant stock-based compensation.”
- *Scheme* — The only partner-level separation: Prudential Corporation Holdings signalled a partial exit from the AMC, which listed on December 19, 2025, and after agreeing to buy 75% of Bharti Life it is being reclassified from promoter to investor in ICICI Life, which is renaming itself. “Consequently, ICICI Prudential Life Insurance Company Limited has applied to IRDAI for the reclassification of PCHL from 'promoter' to 'investor', along with a proposal to change the name of the company from 'ICICI Prudential Life Insurance Company Limited' to 'ICICI Life Insurance Limited'.”

*Not explained on the calls:* Everything a separation thesis needs: no demerger exists. No consideration for NIIT or ICICI Venture's transfer, no pension AUM/economics, no lender, investor or partner demands, no analyst questions, and Oct 2025's transcript is unreadable.

**The stages, as filed:** meetings (2026-08-07)

**The partial spin-off:** **Aegis Vopak Terminals Limited** (subsidiary); parent's stake after: 44%; IPO stage: listed; exchange: BSE Limited and the National Stock Exchange of India Limited; NSE symbol AEGISVOPAK; timeline: listing of equity shares "with effect from June 2, 2025" (Chairman's speech at the 69th AGM, August 07, 2026).

> “This year also marked a significant achievement for one of our subsidiaries, Aegis Vopak Terminals Limited (AVTL), with successfully listing of its equity shares on BSE Limited and the National Stock ”

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** Aegis Vopak Terminals Limited (AVTL), the group's liquid and gas storage/terminalling subsidiary, separately listed — class `regulatory_strategic`.

- *Insiders:* Promoter Raj Chandaria is Chairman & MD; parent holds "44% shareholder of AVTL", earns ~25% margin developing assets billed to AVTL; Itochu took 10% of ATPL, intending 25%
- *What it reveals:* Parent keeps Mumbai liquid/LPG, distribution, sourcing, infrastructure development, treasury, INR 5,939 crore cash and no net debt, plus 44% of listed AVTL and a 25% EPC margin on terminals built for it
- *Selling pressure:* unlikely — AVTL listed via fresh INR 2,800 crore primary issuance, not a share distribution to parent shareholders; documents state no shareholding-pattern change
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* AVTL standalone results and shareholding — value of parent's 44% stake plus INR 5,939 crore cash versus parent market cap
- *In their words:* “This year also marked a significant achievement for one of our subsidiaries, Aegis Vopak Terminals Limited (AVTL), with successfully listing of its equity shares on BSE Limited and the National Stock Exchange of India Limited with effect from June 2, 2025, raised INR 2,800 crore through a primary issuance.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

Across these texts Aegis is not demerging a division to its own shareholders — one filing states plainly "Yes, transaction is outside the Scheme of Arrangement" — it is carving its port terminalling business out of Aegis Logistics Ltd (ALL) into the Royal Vopak joint venture Aegis Vopak Terminals Ltd (AVTL), IPO-ing it, and then migrating terminal assets into AVTL and its subsidiaries by slump sale; ALL retains Mumbai Liquid, Mumbai LPG, LPG/ammonia Distribution, Infrastructure Development (EPC), Sourcing and treasury. Management's stated reason is capital: the group is funding roughly USD 1.2 billion of gross capex (about INR 10,000 crores) by FY27 and a USD 5 billion pipeline to 2030 (including a non-binding INR 20,000 crore Vadhavan MoU, INR 1,675 crores at JNPA/J2, INR 525 crores per ammonia terminal), and Murad Moledina said the AVTL IPO's "primary objective was to reduce debt and strengthen the balance sheet enabling us to seize future growth opportunities and continue our GATI strategy" — GATI being Gateway Access to India. The dilution problem is answered two ways: in Nov 2024 he argued equity infused into the JV "will be value accrued into the holdco because we are eliminating interest cost which is a very high cost for infrastructure companies," so rising minority interest is offset by interest savings; post-listing he called it EPS accretive because reinvested proceeds more than compensate for profit shared with minorities. The split is engineered so cash returns to the parent: ALL (or a 100% subsidiary) builds the assets and bills AVTL at arm's length with a ~20–25% margin — 30% on signing the framework agreement (INR 500 crores of the INR 1,675 crore J2 project) and 70% on completion — so "we recover back whatever we have spent and the margin remains in cash," eliminated on consolidation but real at the standalone level, while ALL also keeps 44.71% of AVTL and management control, so AVTL is still consolidated line by line. Partner structure, not lender pressure, shapes it: Vopak dilutes equally alongside ALL; SEBI rules legally oblige a Phase-II equity infusion within three years; Itochu has taken 10% of Aegis Terminal (Pipavav) Ltd with intent to reach 25%; L&T (Kandla green ammonia) and Hindustan Zinc (15-year ammonia take-or-pay) sit on the project side. Consolidation of stragglers followed — Haldia's Hindustan Aegis LPG (25,000 MT, HPCL contract to 2038) moved 75% into AVTL, with 51% sold by Aegis Gas for INR 701.6 crores, and the Pipavav ammonia terminal transferred to ATPL for INR 525 crores — and performance has been strong throughout: FY26 revenue INR 8,333 crores (+23%), normalised EBITDA INR 1,599 crores (+36%), PAT INR 1,107 crores (+41%), EPS 25.59, cash and investments ~INR 5,939 crores versus INR 150 crores in FY22, consolidated debt-to-equity 0.04 and no net debt.

**How it evolved:** The idea surfaced only as press speculation: on the Aug 2024 call (Jul 31, 2024) Murad Moledina refused to engage on an AVTL fundraise news item — "nothing finalized as of now" — and Anil Sarin used that call to lobby against it on behalf of minority holders, asking that capital instead be raised in the Holdco; the Nov 2024 call (Nov 19, 2024) opened by disclosing the DRHP had been filed the previous day, with Moledina declining detail ("We are not at liberty to talk as of now") beyond saying proceeds would repay debt and that dilution would be shared equally by both partners and done in two phases. By the Aug 2025 call (Aug 8, 2025) AVTL was listed (June 2025, INR 2,800 crores raised, ALL at 44.71%) and the rationale was given formally — debt reduction, GATI, EPS accretion, Phase-II infusion legally due within three years — plus the first slump sales (Sea Lord's Mangalore terminal, business transfer agreements of Jun 19, 2025) and the rule that "most of the standard port terminals will be housed under the strategy GATI in Aegis Vopak." Thereafter it became mechanical: Nov 2025 (Nov 7) and the Oct 28–29, 2025 filings moved Hindustan Aegis LPG and Aegis Terminal (Pipavav) into AVTL (INR 701.6 crores for 51%; ALL retaining 34% indirectly, offset by ~INR 700 crores cash), Feb 2026 (Jan 30, 2026) defined the parent's remaining six businesses, the Mar 26 / Aug 24, 2026 filings assigned and executed the INR 525 crore ammonia BTA to ATPL, and the Jun 2026 call (Jun 9, 2026) plus the Sep 28, 2026 board approval of INR 6,000 crores of borrowing limits and INR 6,000 crores of fundraising confirmed the steady state: ALL builds and funds, AVTL owns.

**What management expects from it:** AVTL: debt repaid, balance sheet strengthened, ~25% EBITDA on matured assets, terminals consolidated for operational synergy, partner capital from Vopak and Itochu. Aegis Logistics: upfront 20–25% EPC margin returned in cash, 44.71% of AVTL plus management control and line-by-line consolidation, high-return distribution/sourcing/treasury retained, EPS accretion, 0.6x gearing, and funding for USD 5 billion of capex to 2030.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *[Aug 2024](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=d5eeb379-e933-48d9-aeb1-921a678ebcb6.pdf)* — Investor Anil Sarin explicitly lobbied against separately listing AVTL, saying minority holders would be confused about which entity to own and that capital should instead be raised in the listed Holdco; management called the discussion premature. “it would be so much better if you retain that in the consolidated hold and raise money in the Holdco.”
- *[Aug 2024](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=d5eeb379-e933-48d9-aeb1-921a678ebcb6.pdf)* — Asked directly about press reports of an AVTL IPO, the CFO would not confirm it, framing it only as one of several ways to fund the capex programme. “As far as the second news item is concerned, I can tell you, we always explore many possibilities of funding our capex program and nothing finalized as of now.”
- *[Nov 2024](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=65eba500-2091-45e4-803b-b6b3d3bd1264.pdf)* — On the day after the DRHP was filed, the CFO gave the core defence of the structure: equity raised in the subsidiary repays infrastructure debt, so interest savings offset the increase in minority interest and the holdco is left unaffected. “We have already said earlier that the equity infusion into the JV will be value accrued into the holdco because we are eliminating interest cost which is a very high cost for infrastructure companies.”
- *[Nov 2024](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=65eba500-2091-45e4-803b-b6b3d3bd1264.pdf)* — The Chairman stated the stated use of IPO proceeds — debt reduction plus general corporate purposes — while an investor asked whether the listed parent would simply become a holdco since the bulk of the business was moving into the JV. “The capital raise in AVTL will help the company reduce a certain portion of the outstanding debt and also some portion helped fund other general corporate purposes.”
- *[Aug 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=33def260-c9ef-4d18-85ef-3a82fdb609f4.pdf)* — Post-listing (AVTL listed June 2025, ALL holding 44.71% with management control, so still consolidated line by line), the CFO gave the formal rationale and said reinvested proceeds would more than compensate for profit now shared with minorities. “The primary objective was to reduce debt and strengthen the balance sheet enabling us to seize future growth opportunities and continue our GATI strategy.”
- *[Aug 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=33def260-c9ef-4d18-85ef-3a82fdb609f4.pdf)* — The Chairman tied the separation to a regulatory obligation: a second equity infusion into AVTL is mandated within three years under SEBI rules, which he said largely funds the USD 1.2 billion-to-USD 5 billion capex plan at 0.6x gearing capped at 3.5x EBITDA. “With the recently concluded Phase-I equity infusion by way of the IPO and as you know we are legally obliged to have a Phase-II equity infusion within the next 3 years under the SEBI regulations, the Capex therefore will be largely funded.”
- *[Aug 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=33def260-c9ef-4d18-85ef-3a82fdb609f4.pdf)* — The allocation rule between parent and AVTL was stated: standard port terminals go into AVTL under the GATI strategy, while other assets (e.g. the INR 250 crore Mumbai liquid expansion) stay in the parent, decided case by case on where value is maximised and whether partners are involved. “But yes, most of the standard port terminals will be housed under the strategy GATI in Aegis Vopak, for sure.”
- *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=06b0ba8f-8eb6-42e0-98c0-4cb53ff2ae90.pdf)* — Explaining the Haldia/Hindustan Aegis consolidation into AVTL, the CFO quantified the trade: holding drops from 51% to an indirect 34%, but roughly INR 700 crores of cash more than offsets the 17 points, and it lifts the subsidiary's EPS. “The 17% that drops is compensated by the surplus INR 700 crores, whatever is going to come in our hands.”
- *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=06b0ba8f-8eb6-42e0-98c0-4cb53ff2ae90.pdf)* — The cash mechanics of the two-entity structure were spelled out for a shareholder worried that the USD 5 billion capex benefits only AVTL: the parent builds at ~25% margin, is reimbursed in full plus margin, and also earns via its AVTL stake. “So, for AVTL, if we develop, then obviously, AVTL pays for the entire amount, including our margin. So, we recover back whatever we have spent and the margin remains in cash.”
- *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=1b37f48b-924c-4da8-a968-b646d3dc0653.pdf)* — Asked what is left in Aegis Logistics outside AVTL, the CFO enumerated the retained perimeter — and added that ammonia distribution is being added to it alongside LPG. “So we have Mumbai Liquid. We have Mumbai LPG. We have Distribution. We have Infrastructure Development. We have Sourcing and we have treasury.”
- *[Jun 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=d2ebd557-5ec3-4cb1-b90f-9d56e37dbbde.pdf)* — The steady-state operating model was confirmed: capex is incurred and the asset built at Aegis Logistics standalone (or a 100% subsidiary), billed as EPC, then transferred to Aegis Vopak, with consolidation capitalised at ALL's billed cost. “So, we will be doing capex at the Aegis level, the Aegis Logistics. And then after creating the asset, will we then transfer it to Aegis Vopak, am I right?”
- *Scheme* — The Aug 24, 2026 Business Transfer Agreement transferred the 36,000 MT Pipavav ammonia terminal to Aegis Terminal (Pipavav) Limited by slump sale for INR 525 crores, and states the transaction sits outside any Scheme of Arrangement and is a related-party transaction at arm's length. “The Transfer of storage terminal for Ammonia to ATPL will consolidate the terminalling services under the Group, enabling operational synergy.”

*Not explained on the calls:* No stated valuation of retained versus transferred businesses, no answer to the which-entity-to-own dilution objection, no Phase-II infusion size, terms or timing, no lender rationale.

**The partial spin-off:** **EAAA India Alternatives Limited** (subsidiary); parent's stake after: 83.88% held by the Company through all its subsidiaries (ESIPL holds 78.43%); IPO stage: listed; exchange: BSE Limited and National Stock Exchange of India Limited; NSE symbol EDELALTS; timeline: The offer period in relation to the IPO was closed on October 28, 2026. The shares were allotted to the investors on October 29, 2026 and admitted for listing a.

> “In continuation of our earlier intimations made in connection with the Initial Public Offering ("IPO") of EAAA India Alternatives Limited ("EAAA"), a subsidiary of the Company and in accordance with t”

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** EAAA India Alternatives Limited, the alternative asset management (investment manager to alternate-asset funds) business, part-listed via IPO offer for sale — class `value_unlocking`.

- *Insiders:* ESIPL, wholly owned subsidiary and "one of the promoters", sold 72,07,207 shares yet still holds 78.43%; EFSL through all subsidiaries holds 83.88%. Management incentives in EAAA not stated.
- *What it reveals:* IPO price Rs 1,665 values EAAA's ~6.47 crore shares near Rs 10,700 crore versus EFSL net worth of Rs 5,866 crore; Alternatives segment earned PBT Rs 241.40 crore on Rs 989.53 crore capital employed; FPAUM Rs 41,920 crore, up 33% YoY.
- *Selling pressure:* unlikely — No shares distributed to EFSL shareholders; EAAA shares were sold into a book-built IPO at Rs 1,665 to bidding investors.
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* EAAA's Red Herring Prospectus dated October 19, 2026 — fee-earning AUM, fee rates and the Rs 963.76 crore FY26 income mix
- *In their words:* “We are pleased to share that we have filed EAAA's DRHP for IPO in January and are on track for the listing, marking the first step towards building EAAA as a standalone institutionalized platform.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

On the documentary record available, Edelweiss is not executing a demerger scheme but a sequence of subsidiary-level separations that convert a holding-company conglomerate into separately capitalised, separately owned businesses — described in its own press release as "seven independent and well-governed businesses" each with "dedicated management teams and strong boards." The clearest stated reason is the Alternative Asset Management arm, EAAA India Alternatives: management said the IPO was "the first step towards building EAAA as a standalone institutionalized platform," i.e. separating the fastest-growing, fee-income business (FPAUM INR 41,920 Cr, +33% YoY; nine-month fund raise INR 7,576 Cr, +67% YoY; total income Rs 963.76 Cr in FY26 versus Rs 584.25 Cr in FY24; net worth Rs 1,075.54 Cr) from the credit-heavy parent so it can be valued and institutionalised on its own. Critically, the EAAA listing was a pure offer for sale by holdco subsidiary ESIPL (originally up to Rs 15,000 mn, cut to Rs 12,000 mn in the RHP, finally Rs 1,200 Cr gross / Rs 1,120.63 Cr net at Rs 1,665 per share) — no primary money went to EAAA, so the cash accrues to the Edelweiss holding structure, which fits the stated priority of "focused reduction in corporate net debt" (down 15% to INR 6,520 Cr over two years, with consolidated net debt INR 11,390 Cr and a 3.46x debt-equity ratio). The second separation is Housing Finance: Nido Home Finance was handed to a strategic majority investor, CA Sardo Investments (The Carlyle Group) with Salisbury Investments (Aditya Puri's family vehicle), investing ~INR 2,100 Cr — Rs 580.68 Cr of secondary for 45% plus Rs 1,446.14 Cr of primary equity and warrants at INR 193 — taking them to 58.26% immediately and 72.70% fully diluted within 18 months, so Nido "ceased to be a subsidiary" and Edelweiss fell to 38.91% (25.46% diluted). Here the separation solves a growth-capital problem Edelweiss itself was not funding: a business contributing only 5.47% of consolidated income (Rs 520.63 Cr) but consuming 13.99% of net worth (Rs 828.2 Cr) was recapitalised with third-party primary money, with Edelweiss retaining upside via a minority stake and "an additional payment based upon returns realized by CA Sardo Investments." The same template was applied to the Mutual Fund arm, where a 15% sale of Edelweiss Asset Management and Edelweiss Trusteeship to WestBridge moved both into joint control, crystallising a Rs 2,440 Cr unrealised and Rs 281 Cr realised gain (and a Rs 389 Cr deferred tax charge) — evidence that the separations are also being used to mark up carrying value and lift reported net worth/PAT (nine-month PAT Rs 549 Cr, +45% YoY). Taken together, the stated logic is: each business reaches scale, then gets its own owner, its own capital and its own valuation, while the parent de-levers.

**How it evolved:** This cannot be traced call by call: all ten earnings-call transcripts supplied (Nov 2023, May/Aug/Oct/Nov 2024, May/Aug/Nov 2025, Feb 2026, Apr 2026) contained no extractable text, so no dated management commentary is available. From the filings, the sequence is: EAAA's DRHP filed 19–20 January 2026 (OFS up to Rs 15,000 mn by ESIPL); on 10 February 2026 the Q3FY26 release framed it as "the first step towards building EAAA as a standalone institutionalized platform" and the same day the Carlyle/Salisbury definitive agreements for a majority of Nido were announced, with WestBridge's Mutual Fund investment consummated in that quarter; SEBI observations came 23 April 2026, the Nido transaction closed 25 September 2026 (versus a 31 July 2026 expectation), and the EAAA IPO was repriced down to Rs 12,000 mn in the RHP of 19 October 2026 before listing on 2 November 2026 at Rs 1,665. So the plan visibly scaled down in size (Rs 1,500 Cr to Rs 1,200 Cr) and slipped in timing, while widening from one business to three.

**What management expects from it:** EAAA becomes a listed, "standalone institutionalized platform" with its own valuation; Nido gets Carlyle/Puri growth capital and majority ownership while Edelweiss keeps 25–39% plus a returns-linked earn-out; Mutual Fund gains a strategic partner and a Rs 2,440 Cr value mark; the parent frees capital (Rs 1,120.63 Cr net OFS proceeds) to push corporate net debt below INR 6,520 Cr.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *Scheme* — The EAAA IPO is explicitly positioned as the first step in separating the alternatives business into a self-standing institutional platform, announced alongside the DRHP filing in January 2026. “We are pleased to share that we have filed EAAA’s DRHP for IPO in January and are on track for the listing, marking the first step towards building EAAA as a standalone institutionalized platform.”
- *Scheme* — The structural end-state management describes for the group is a set of separately governed operating companies rather than an integrated financial conglomerate. “Edelweiss is a diversified financial services company with seven independent and well-governed businesses.”
- *Scheme* — The separations sit directly under the stated priority of de-levering the holding company, with corporate net debt the metric management tracks. “Corporate net debt continues to be on path to reduction, with a 15% decline to INR 6,520 Cr over the last two years”
- *Scheme* — Housing Finance was separated by bringing in Carlyle and Aditya Puri's family vehicle as strategic majority owners with roughly INR 2,100 crores of new money. “has entered into definitive agreements (the Agreements) with CA Sardo Investments (an affiliate of The Carlyle Group (NASDAQ: CG)) and Salisbury Investments Private Limited (an investment vehicle of Aditya Puri and his family) (collectively Buyers) for the Buyers to invest approximately INR 2,100 crores to acquire a strategic majority stake in Nido.”
- *Scheme* — The Nido deal is a true deconsolidation, not a minority stake sale — Edelweiss gives up control of the housing finance book. “Consequent to the transaction, Nido will cease to be a subsidiary of the Company.”
- *Scheme* — Nido was absorbing far more of the group's capital than it contributed in income — 13.99% of net worth for 5.47% of income — which the recapitalisation by third parties addresses. “Income 520.63 5.47% Net Worth 828.2 13.99%”
- *Scheme* — Most of the Carlyle money is primary capital into Nido's balance sheet rather than cash out to Edelweiss: Rs 580.68 Cr secondary versus Rs 1,446.14 Cr of fresh equity and warrants. “Further, in accordance with the Agreements, Nido has also issued 2,59,06,736 equity shares and 5,18,13,472 warrants, to the Buyers, for an aggregate amount of INR 14,46,13,99,102.56.”
- *Scheme* — Edelweiss retains economic upside in the separated housing business through a retained minority stake and a contingent payment linked to Carlyle's realised returns. “Pursuant to the Agreements and subject to applicable laws, the Sellers (Edelweiss) may also receive an additional payment based upon returns realized by CA Sardo Investments from its investment in Nido.”
- *Scheme* — Control of Nido passes progressively to the buyers — 58.26% on closing rising to 72.70% fully diluted — while Edelweiss falls to 25.46%. “the Buyers now hold 58.26% shareholding of Nido which would be increased to 72.70% within 18 months, on a fully diluted basis post conversion of the warrants.”
- *Scheme* — The Mutual Fund business was separated on the same template, with a 15% strategic sale converting EAML and ETCL into jointly controlled entities. “Additionally, the WestBridge investment in Mutual Fund received its final approval from the regulators, and the deal has been consummated this quarter.”
- *Scheme* — That Mutual Fund separation crystallised very large accounting gains — Rs 2,440 Cr unrealised plus Rs 281 Cr realised — showing the separations also re-rate carrying values inside the consolidated accounts. “Pursuant to the terms of the SHA, the Group now has joint control for both of these Entities with the new investor, and consequently, in accordance with Ind AS 110 and Ind AS 28, these entities are now classified as jointly controlled entities under Ind AS accounting principles.”
- *Scheme* — The EAAA listing raised no primary capital for EAAA itself; proceeds went to the holding-company subsidiary ESIPL, consistent with using separation to fund parent de-leveraging. “The IPO comprises an offer for sale (“OFS”) for an amount not exceeding Rs. 12,000 million, which is proposed to be undertaken by Edelweiss Securities & Investments Private Limited (“ESIPL”), a wholly owned subsidiary of the Company.”

*Not explained on the calls:* All ten earnings-call transcripts were unextractable, so management's spoken rationale, investor/lender demands, use of proceeds, valuation targets, and any formal demerger scheme are absent.

> **Listing:** PARTIAL SPIN-OFF, IPO BOARD APPROVAL — JSW One Platforms Limited; Per the July 17, 2026 filing: "Completion date of the proposed IPO is not available as on date."

**The stages, as filed:** nclt_sanction (2026-07-03)

**The partial spin-off:** **JSW One Platforms Limited** (joint venture); parent's stake about 61% equity stake on a fully diluted basis (as stated in the May 14, 2026 earnings call); IPO stage: board approval; timeline: Per the July 17, 2026 filing: "Completion date of the proposed IPO is not available as on date.".

> “Pursuant to the Regulation 30 read with Schedule III of SEBI Listing Regulations, this is to inform you that the Board of Directors of the Company at its meeting held today i.e. July 17, 2026, inter a”

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** No demerger: BPSL's 4.5 MTPA steel business slump-sold into a 50:50 JFE JV; JSW One Platforms IPO stake sale — class `value_unlocking`.

- *Insiders:* JSW Shipping & Logistics (promoter group) held 17.35% of Piombino, swapped into JSW Steel shares, lifting promoters 45.32% to 46.74%. JFE nominee Hiroyuki Ogawa already on JSW board; JSW Steel holds ~61% of JOPL.
- *What it reveals:* BPSL steel business valued at Rs 31,500 crore equity / Rs 53,000 crore enterprise value for 4.5 MTPA, booking a Rs 18,051 crore exceptional gain and cutting net debt to ~Rs 54,000 crore (leverage 1.81x). JOPL is immaterial: Rs 68 crore net worth.
- *Selling pressure:* unlikely — No shares distributed to JSW shareholders; JOPL listing is an offer for sale of up to Rs 811 crores, 0.06% of consolidated net worth.
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* The Rs 24,483 crore slump-sale consideration and JFE's second Rs 7,875 crore tranche — check FY27 Q1 net debt and JV equity accounting.
- *In their words:* “The present transaction is aimed at securing the Company's growth in a financially prudent manner to enable it to pursue its aspirations across business cycles.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

The business being separated is Bhushan Power and Steel Limited's (BPSL) steel undertaking in Odisha — acquired through the IBC in 2021 and expanded from 2.75 MTPA to 4.5 MTPA — which JSW Steel carved out by slump sale on a going-concern basis to JSW Sambalpur Steel Limited for cash consideration of Rs.24,483 crores, after which JFE Steel of Japan (a strategic partner since 2009, with Mr. Hiroyuki Ogawa already a JFE nominee on JSW's board) took 50% of holding company JSW Kalinga Steel Limited for Rs.15,750 crores in two equal tranches, valuing the BPSL steel business at Rs.31,500 crores equity and Rs.53,000 crores enterprise value. Management's stated purpose was not to exit steel but to fund growth without stretching the balance sheet: the deal brought a cash inflow of ~Rs.32,000 crores and deleveraging of ~Rs.37,000 crores, of which ~Rs.30,000 crores was completed by 31 March 2026, taking net debt to ~Rs.54,000 crores and leverage from 2.91x (Dec-25) to 1.81x, with a credit-rating outlook uplift; the remaining ~Rs.7,900 crores was to follow with JFE's second tranche by end-June 2026. Jayant Acharya framed it as a 'double engine of growth' — the JV lets JSW expand faster in India while deleveraging, so JSW Steel alone targets 62 million tonnes by FY32 (raised from 50 mt by FY31) and the JFE and POSCO JVs add a cumulative 16 mt, ~78 mt in India and ~80 mt including Ohio, against a capex plan of Rs.1,26,000 crores plus up to another Rs.1,00,000 crores to FY33 where the JV spend is only JSW's equity share (~Rs.4,000-5,000 crores per Rs.25,000-30,000 crore project). For BPSL itself, the filings say the business has 'significant growth potential' and the JV will accelerate capacity with 'best-in-class technology' and high-end value-added products, and the Netrabanda 2 mt iron ore mine now sits inside the JV. The accounting consequences were spelled out: a Q4 FY26 exceptional gain of Rs.18,051 crores on the slump sale (within Rs.17,888 crores of net exceptionals), BPSL assets classified held for sale under Ind AS 105 from Dec-2025, a Rs.1,439 crore deferred tax asset recognised because BPSL's carried-forward unabsorbed depreciation would offset the capital gain (so 'the effective tax on this transaction is significantly lower'), deconsolidation at March-end with BPSL now equity-accounted under income from associates and joint ventures, and FY27 guidance of 29.75 mt production / 28.6 mt sales explicitly excluding JFE JV volumes. In parallel, Piombino Steel Limited — BPSL's parent, 82.65% JSW Steel and 17.35% promoter-group JSW Shipping & Logistics — was amalgamated into JSW Steel (10 JSW shares per 156 PSL shares) precisely so JSW could hold BPSL directly and transact on it 'without minority shareholders' involvement', while gaining 'additional cash to pursue its growth aspirations in a financially prudent manner'. No lender or investor demand is cited anywhere; the pressure visible in the texts is analysts probing the logic (Amit Murarka on running three balance sheets, Sumangal Nevatia asking why a second partner at all given the post-JFE balance sheet), while CCI cleared it on 20 January 2026 and shareholders approved the Piombino merger with 94.86% of votes cast (97.20% of public shareholders).

**How it evolved:** The simplification began on 17 October 2025, when the Board approved folding wholly owned subsidiaries Amba River Coke, Monnet Cement and JSW Retail & Distribution into JSW Steel (effective 1 August 2026) purely for group-structure and compliance reasons. The separation proper was announced on 3 December 2025: the Board approved the JFE 50:50 JV, the slump sale of BPSL's steel undertaking to JSW Sambalpur for Rs.24,483 crores, and simultaneously the merger of Piombino Steel into JSW Steel to hold BPSL directly without the 17.35% promoter-group minority; definitive JV, business-transfer and share-subscription agreements were signed the same day. Execution then ran to schedule — CCI approval 20 January 2026; the Q3 FY26 results on 23 January 2026 reclassified BPSL as held for sale, quantified equity value Rs.31,500 crores / EV Rs.53,000 crores, Rs.32,000 crores cash inflow and Rs.37,000 crores deleveraging, and booked a Rs.1,439 crore deferred tax asset; the slump sale completed 27 March 2026; and the 14 May 2026 call reported the JV entity formed by end-March, JFE's first tranche in, BPSL deconsolidated, Rs.18,051 crores of exceptional gain, leverage at 1.81x and tightened leverage caps. The ambition then widened rather than narrowed: a second 50:50 JV with POSCO was signed in April 2026 for a greenfield 6 MTPA plant in Odisha (via Saffron Resources, Rs.508.8 crore subscription), the India target was raised to 62 mt by FY32 plus 16 mt in JVs, and the Piombino merger was sanctioned by NCLT on 16 October 2026 and became effective 31 October 2026 (appointed date 1 January 2026) — alongside a separate partial monetisation, the 17 July 2026 approval to sell up to Rs.811 crores of JSW One Platforms shares in its IPO.

**What management expects from it:** For JSW Steel: Rs.37,000 crore deleveraging, leverage 1.81x, net debt Rs.54,000 crores, rating-outlook uplift, tighter caps (gearing 1.25x, leverage 3.00x), and cash to fund 62 mt by FY32 plus JV equity. For the BPSL JV: accelerated expansion toward ~10 mt using JFE technology and high-end value-added grades; now equity-accounted, so its EBITDA leaves JSW's P&L.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *Scheme* — The 3 December 2025 Board filing set out the structure: BPSL's steel undertaking sold by slump sale to JSW Sambalpur Steel Limited for Rs.24,483 crores cash, with JFE then buying 50% of parent JSW Kalinga for Rs.15,750 crores in two equal tranches. “Transfer of BPSL Steel business undertaking, by way of slump sale on a going concern basis to JSW Sambalpur Steel Limited ("JSW Sambalpur") for a cash consideration of Rs 24,483 crores, subject to customary closing adjustments as agreed in the transaction documents.”
- *Scheme* — The stated purpose was to fund JSW's 50 MTPA-by-FY31 ambition without balance-sheet strain, not to exit the asset. “The present transaction is aimed at securing the Company's growth in a financially prudent manner to enable it to pursue its aspirations across business cycles.”
- *Scheme* — For BPSL itself, management said the JV brings JFE's technology to accelerate capacity and move the product mix up-market; JFE has been a partner since 2009. “The BPSL Steel business has significant growth potential and this joint venture will enable acceleration of its capacity with best-in-class technology and enable production of high-end value-added steel products”
- *Scheme* — The Q3 FY26 press release put hard numbers on the valuation and the balance-sheet effect: Rs.31,500 crores equity value, Rs.53,000 crores EV, Rs.32,000 crores cash in and Rs.37,000 crores of deleveraging. “With this transaction, JFE will take a 50% stake in the BPSL Steel business at an equity value of ₹31,500 crores and enterprise value of ₹53,000 crores.”
- *Scheme* — The simultaneous Piombino Steel merger was justified as letting JSW Steel hold BPSL directly and transact on it without the 17.35% promoter-group minority, while releasing cash. “The merger ensures better alignment of the Transferee Company's long-term strategic interests by enabling it to directly hold the investment in Bhushan Power and Steel Limited ('BPSL'). This consolidation provides a platform to facilitate any transactions and investments related to BPSL's business, thereby enhancing strategic focus without minority shareholders' involvement;”
- *Scheme* — The company deliberately did not treat the carve-out as a discontinued operation — BPSL was never framed as a different line of business, only as capital released from the same business. “The Group has also assessed and concluded that transfer of BPSL's steel business undertaking does not qualify as "discontinued operation" as it is not a separate major line of business and forms part of overall steel operations of the Group.”
- *Scheme* — BPSL's accumulated tax losses were monetised against the sale gain: a Rs.1,439 crore deferred tax asset was recognised in Q3 FY26 on the strength of the expected capital gain. “Further, based on the reassessment of unrecognised deferred tax assets, the Group has recognised deferred tax assets (net) amounting to Rs. 1,439 crores as it is probable that carried forward unabsorbed depreciation will be recovered against the likely capital gains on the above mentioned transaction.”
- *[May 2026](https://jsw-steel-s3.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/jsw-steel-images/uploads/2026/05/JSWSteel-Earnings-May14-2026_vF.pdf)* — Acharya opened with the deleveraging as the headline benefit, ~Rs.37,000 crores in total with ~Rs.30,000 crores already done by March-end. “This transaction entails a deleveraging of approximately Rs.37,000 crores for JSW Steel, out of which about Rs.30,000 crores has been completed at March end.”
- *[May 2026](https://jsw-steel-s3.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/jsw-steel-images/uploads/2026/05/JSWSteel-Earnings-May14-2026_vF.pdf)* — Post-deal leverage fell to 1.81x with net debt ~Rs.54,000 crores and gearing 0.51x, and the rating outlook improved — versus net debt of Rs.80,347 crores and 2.91x at 31 December 2025. “Our credit rating outlook has seen an uplift, and we expect to see continued progress on this front.”
- *[May 2026](https://jsw-steel-s3.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/jsw-steel-images/uploads/2026/05/JSWSteel-Earnings-May14-2026_vF.pdf)* — Asked directly by Amit Murarka (Axis Capital) whether multiple simultaneous projects across three balance sheets is the new normal, Acharya confirmed the separation was designed to do two things at once. “So, as we had given you an indication earlier that the idea of the JV was to strategically grow faster in the country, while it helped us to deleverage as well.”
- *[May 2026](https://jsw-steel-s3.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/jsw-steel-images/uploads/2026/05/JSWSteel-Earnings-May14-2026_vF.pdf)* — He described the resulting architecture as two growth vehicles running in parallel, with JSW Steel tracked to 62 mt by FY32 and the JVs (JFE 10 mt, POSCO 6 mt) tracked separately. “So, we'll have a double engine of growth, one which JSW Steel will grow on and the other which the joint venture will grow on.”
- *[May 2026](https://jsw-steel-s3.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/jsw-steel-images/uploads/2026/05/JSWSteel-Earnings-May14-2026_vF.pdf)* — The sale produced a Rs.18,051 crore book gain inside Q4 FY26 exceptionals of Rs.17,888 crores, lifting reported PAT to Rs.19,243 crores against normalised PAT of Rs.3,475 crores. “This includes a gain of Rs.18,051 crores on slump sale of BPSL steel undertaking and Rs.163 crores exceptional charge on implementation of new labor code.”

*Not explained on the calls:* Nine of ten call transcripts are unreadable. Nothing explains why 50% rather than less, JV exit/control terms, BPSL's standalone margins or returns post-deal, or who initiated.

## AMBER — Amber Enterprises India Ltd.

**CONFIRMED** (partial spin-off — the IPO of IL JIN Electronics (India) Limited is in motion (DRHP filed)) · **PARTIAL SPIN-OFF, IPO IN MOTION — the parent's stub is priced once the piece trades** · score 4.3/10 · partial spin-off (subsidiary IPO) · 4 filing(s) from BSE-screener, NSE · first 2026-04-30, latest 2026-11-07

> **Listing:** PARTIAL SPIN-OFF, IPO DRHP FILED — IL JIN Electronics (India) Limited; date not fixed

**The stages, as filed:** announced (2026-04-30) → exchange_noc (2026-10-01) → nclt_sanction (2026-06-08)

**The partial spin-off:** **IL JIN Electronics (India) Limited** (subsidiary); parent's stake 89.72%; IPO stage: DRHP filed; exchange: BSE Limited and National Stock Exchange of India Limited.

> “IL JIN Electronics (India) Limited (formerly known as IL JIN Electronics (India) Private Limited), a material subsidiary of the Company, has filed the Draft Red Herring Prospectus dated 6th November 2”

**Stated in the filings:** appointed date 2025-04-01.

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** IL JIN Electronics, Amber's material subsidiary in electronics manufacturing services (EMS), being separately listed via proposed IPO — class `regulatory_strategic`.

- *Insiders:* Amber holds 60,98,240 IL JIN shares, 89.72% post rights issue (Rs 296.02 crore subscribed); promoters Jasbir Singh and Daljit Singh are directors on IL JIN's board; CCPS holders' maximum dilution ~30%
- *What it reveals:* Electronics division FY26 revenue Rs 3,268 crore (+49%), operating EBITDA Rs 287 crore (+89%), guided ~40% FY27 growth at 9.5-10% margins; IL JIN raised Rs 1,750 crore from marquee investors; bought 2018 as a Rs 300-crore, 3%-EBITDA company
- *Selling pressure:* unlikely — IPO, not a share distribution to Amber holders; Amber keeps 89.72%; offer size and index effects not stated
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* The DRHP dated 6th November 2026: IL JIN standalone financials, fresh-issue versus offer-for-sale split, and CCPS conversion terms
- *In their words:* “The IPO will be subject to receipt of the required regulatory approvals.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

The business being separated is Amber's Electronics / EMS arm, housed in IL JIN Electronics (India) Ltd — PCB assembly (~INR2,281cr of FY26 revenue), bare PCB through Ascent Circuits (98.5% owned), Shogini Technoarts (80%) and the Ascent-K/Korea Circuit HDI JV (~INR600cr), plus Power-One Microsystems (60%, power electronics, ~15% EBITDA) and 50.4% of Israel-listed Unitronics (industrial automation, 24-25% EBITDA) — leaving Amber with the RAC/consumer-durables division (INR8,383cr FY26) and Sidwal railway/defence (INR535cr). The stated driver is funding: essentially all of the group's capex sits in electronics, with more than INR4,500cr of ECMS investment approvals (Ascent multilayer INR991cr, Ascent-K HDI INR3,200cr, Shogini INR500cr), asset turns of only 0.75-1.1x, and the 48% MeitY plus 42% UP incentives arriving 5-6 years after the spend, so FY27 capex of INR1,800-2,000cr (INR1,100-1,200cr cash) and ~INR1,400-1,500cr in FY28 must be pre-funded against a board policy never to exceed 2x debt/EBITDA and Jasbir Singh's pledge to be net-debt-free. Management said investors asked for it: private equity funds were 'chasing to invest in the electronic division', and instead of loading Amber's balance sheet they raised INR1,750cr inside ILJIN (mostly CCPS, including ChrysCapital's INR1,100cr) while Amber separately did a INR1,000cr QIP. Separation also gives electronics its own margin and valuation identity — 2.8% EBITDA when ILJIN was bought in 2018 on INR300cr revenue, 6.9% FY25, 8.8% FY26, 10.8% in Q4 FY26, 26% ROCE, guidance of 40% FY27 growth at 9.5-10% and a $1bn revenue target at 11.5-12% EBITDA — against a weather-driven RAC business that saw quarters of -30% to -35% and nine bad seasons in 25 years. The outside CCPS holders also need a price: conversion happens 'based on the future multiple and valuation' (auditors provisioned up to ~30% dilution in NCI), which a listing supplies; and their presence already constrains group structuring, since management could not say whether the new Oppo mobile-phone business would sit in ILJIN 'because we have other shareholders also in the IL JIN cap table'. It is being done as a listing of the subsidiary, not a demerger: in April 2026 Amber put another INR296.02cr into an INR328.12cr ILJIN rights issue (89.58% to 89.72%); in July 2026 ILJIN split shares from Rs10 to Rs5, raised authorised capital to Rs250cr, issued a 25:1 bonus, converted from private to public limited, shifted its registered office from Pune to Greater Noida and resolved to explore fund-raising 'including... public issue'; the DRHP was filed on 7 November 2026. In parallel Amber is cleaning up the rest of the portfolio — merging wholly-owned AmberPR Technoplast into itself for compliance/cost reduction and peer benchmarking, and selling Sidwal's entire 49% Shivaliks (Titagarh Firema) JV for a nominal Rs1,09,798.85 after INR112cr of FY26 impairment/JV losses, 'to curtail future losses'.

**How it evolved:** The capex trigger appears first on the Jan 2025 call (Korea Circuit JV awaiting the ECMS scheme, Rs1,000cr+ threshold) and on 19 May 2025, when the funding answer is still vague — 'in touch with various institutions' — alongside an INR3,000cr application plan. By 30 July 2025 it has split into two named routes, an INR2,500cr QIP enabling resolution at Amber and 'private equity funds who are chasing to invest in the electronic division', with the $1bn/11.5-12% electronics ambition and a net-debt-free pledge framing why outside money must sit at ILJIN; on 7 Nov 2025 the INR1,750cr ILJIN raise (CCPS, ChrysCapital INR1,100cr pending CCI) and Amber's INR1,000cr QIP are both announced, and 10 Feb 2026 confirms the full INR1,750cr received with Amber still at 90% until CCPS convert. From there it becomes an exit path for those investors: 18 May 2026 ties conversion to 'future multiple and valuation' (~30% assumed dilution), 20 June 2026 shows the ILJIN cap table already constraining where new businesses can be placed, and the filings then execute mechanically — Mar/Apr 2026 rights issue, 11 July 2026 split, 25:1 bonus, public-limited conversion, registered office to Greater Noida and a 'public issue' resolution, and the DRHP on 7 Nov 2026 — none of it ever discussed on an earnings call.

**What management expects from it:** Electronics: self-funded ECMS PCB capex, $1bn revenue in ~3 years, margins from 2.8% (2018) toward 11.5-12%, double digits from FY27, ~26% ROCE, stickier high-entry-barrier industrial/defence mix. Amber: retains ~89.7%, frees cash for consumer durables and railway (30-35% growth, 16-17% margins), stays under 2x debt/EBITDA near net-debt-free; CCPS dilution finally priced off a market valuation.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *[Jan 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=813804ee-c3a7-4425-bb42-2057de6be8b1.pdf)* — The capex need that later drives the separation starts here: the Korea Circuit HDI/substrate JV is on hold pending the ECMS scheme, with a likely Rs1,000cr-plus minimum investment and 70-75% of it only reimbursed later by MeitY and the states. “So, on Korea Circuit we are waiting for Government to finalize the incentive scheme.”
- *[May 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=069162e3-fda9-42bb-9c69-0db5b0c2a202.pdf)* — With an INR3,000cr PCB application planned and subsidies spread over 5-6 years, management says the Electronics division is itself seeking third-party funding — the first hint of capital being raised at the subsidiary rather than at Amber. “So we are already in touch with various institutions for that.”
- *[Aug 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=445f7c35-5bf5-4f56-9d6f-e16495c40233.pdf)* — Two funding routes are named — an INR2,500cr QIP enabling resolution at Amber and private equity money targeted specifically at the electronics arm; the same call sets the constraint that drives it, a board cap of 2x debt/EBITDA and a goal to be net-debt-free by FY27. “Second direction is a lot of private equity funds who are chasing to invest in the electronic division.”
- *[Aug 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=445f7c35-5bf5-4f56-9d6f-e16495c40233.pdf)* — The separated entity is given its own standalone ambition and margin identity — $1bn revenue in three years at 11.5-12% EBITDA, versus ILJIN's 2.8% EBITDA on INR300cr when acquired in 2018. “With all the add -ups, we intend to take Electronics division to $1 billion by next 3 years with target EBITDA of 11.5% to 12% range.”
- *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=0bcb53ba-69d0-4386-9199-d20b4b029d9c.pdf)* — The raise happens at two levels simultaneously: INR1,750cr into ILJIN (mostly CCPS; INR370cr in September, INR280cr in October, ChrysCapital's INR1,100cr pending CCI) and a separate INR1,000cr QIP at Amber used mainly to cut debt. “We secured funding of INR1,750 crores from marquee investors.”
- *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=99744db3-5ae9-451c-8d73-b33d28177128.pdf)* — ILJIN's raise closes in full and Amber's stake stays at 90% only because the instrument is CCPS; the same call adds the ECMS approvals (Ascent-K HDI, Shogini) and 116 acres at Jewar that the money has to fund. “On the balance sheet front, ILJIN Electronics has successfully concluded fundraise with the entire INR1,750 crores received from marquee investors.”
- *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=469945ff-af54-4664-8bd7-ed051c694aff.pdf)* — The outside investors' economics depend on a valuation event: no dilution has occurred yet because CCPS convert off a future multiple, with auditors provisioning roughly 30% maximum dilution in non-controlling interest. FY27 capex is guided at INR1,800-2,000cr (INR1,100-1,200cr cash), net debt INR511cr rising to INR700-800cr. “It will happen in future based on the future multiple and valuation.”
- *[Jun 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=e758d7f3-9942-4baf-b20b-0e80b2d6971a.pdf)* — The ILJIN cap table already limits group structuring — management cannot say whether the new Oppo mobile-phone business (8m units year one, 13-15m year two, sub-INR50cr capex, 1.5-2% industry EBITDA) will sit inside ILJIN or directly under Amber. “But we will not be able to define it right now because we have other shareholders also in the IL JIN cap table .”
- *Scheme* — April 2026: Amber pre-funds ILJIN again, subscribing INR296.02cr of a INR328.12cr rights issue (12,46,430 shares), taking its holding from 89.58% to 89.72% — capital in before the listing, not a stake sale. “Further, pursuant to the allotment of equity shares under the rights issue by IL JIN on 21st April 2026, which has resulted in an investment of Rs. 296.02 Crore, Amber Enterprises India Limited (“Amber” or “the Company”) has subscribed to and been allotted 12,46,430 equity shares.”
- *Scheme* — July 2026: ILJIN is mechanically prepared for listing — Rs10 to Rs5 share split, authorised capital to Rs250cr, 25:1 bonus, conversion from private to public limited, registered office moved Pune to Greater Noida, and a board resolution to explore fund-raising modes including a public issue. “Evaluation and exploration of various fund-raising options to support its future growth initiatives.”
- *Scheme* — 7 November 2026: the separation becomes a formal partial listing of the electronics arm — a DRHP for ILJIN's IPO filed with SEBI, BSE and NSE, Amber retaining ~90% pre-offer. “IL JIN Electronics (India) Limited (formerly known as IL JIN Electronics (India) Private Limited), a material subsidiary of the Company, has ﬁled the Draft Red Herring Prospectus dated 6th November 2026 (“DRHP”), on 7th November 2026 with the Securities and Exchange Board of India, BSE Limited and National Stock Exchange of India Limited in connection with its proposed Initial Public Oﬀer (“IPO”).”
- *Scheme* — The rest of the group is being simplified in the opposite direction: wholly-owned AmberPR Technoplast (cross-flow fans) is merged into Amber — no shares issued, NCLT dispensed with meetings, appointed date moved to 1 April 2026 — for compliance savings, scale synergies and cleaner peer comparison. “more absolute and profound comparison with industry peers ie. benchmarking business performance with industry; and”

*Not explained on the calls:* Calls never discuss the IPO itself: offer size, fresh issue versus OFS, use of proceeds, valuation, Amber's post-listing stake, CCPS conversion terms, or why listing rather than demerger.

## FIRSTCRY — Brainbees Solutions Ltd.

**CONFIRMED** (partial spin-off — the IPO of Swara Baby Products Limited is in motion (DRHP filed)) · **PARTIAL SPIN-OFF, IPO IN MOTION — the parent's stub is priced once the piece trades** · score 4.3/10 · partial spin-off (subsidiary IPO) · 11 filing(s) from NSE · first 2025-12-26, latest 2026-10-07

> **Listing:** PARTIAL SPIN-OFF, IPO DRHP FILED — Swara Baby Products Limited; date not fixed

**The stages, as filed:** meetings (2026-08-29)

**The partial spin-off:** **Swara Baby Products Limited** (subsidiary); parent's stake 76.59%; IPO stage: DRHP filed; exchange: BSE Limited and National Stock Exchange of India Limited.

> “In this connection, we wish to inform you that Swara Baby has filed a DRHP dated July 02, 2026 with the Securities and Exchange Board of India, BSE Limited and National Stock Exchange of India Limited”

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** Swara Baby, the group's hygiene contract-manufacturing business (baby/adult diapers, sanitary napkins), via a separate IPO — class `unrelated`.

- *Insiders:* Brainbees holds 76.59% and remains Promoter of Swara Baby; it will sell up to Rs 3,000 million in the Rs 5,000 million OFS. Operations led by Mr. Alok Birla and Mr. Udit Birla; Supam Maheshwari and Gautam Sharma are non-executive directors.
- *What it reveals:* Swara Baby is "the largest contract manufacturer by value in Fiscal 2025" in Indian hygiene manufacturing, with FY26 revenue of Rs 11,639 million and EBITDA of Rs 1,927.70 million buried inside Brainbees' India multi-channel segment, while consolidated Brainbees posted an FY26 loss of Rs 2,036.58 million.
- *Selling pressure:* unlikely — No shares distributed to Brainbees holders; Swara Baby lists via fresh issue plus OFS, and Brainbees stays majority owner.
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* Swara Baby DRHP dated July 2, 2026 - Risk Factor No. 2, pages 23-24, on revenue dependence on Brainbees
- *In their words:* “With this expansive and global vision in contract manufacturing of disposable hygiene products with different capex and working capital needs, we decided to initiate the process of separately listing this business so that they can follow their independent journey.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

The business being separated is Swara Baby Products Limited, Brainbees' diaper/hygiene manufacturing subsidiary, which filed a DRHP on July 02, 2026 for an IPO of up to Rs 10,000 million (Rs 5,000 million fresh issue plus Rs 5,000 million offer for sale), with Brainbees itself selling up to Rs 3,000 million in the OFS (board approval July 01, 2026). Management's stated reason is drift in purpose: Brainbees invested Rs 906.17 million in 2020 for 53.45% (fully diluted) purely as backward integration — "to scale up our home brands within diaper category" with "more control on quality at scale, production timelines and continued innovation in diaper manufacturing" — but Swara then became the largest contract manufacturer by value in Fiscal 2025 in Indian hygiene manufacturing, adding adult diapers and sanitary napkins (similar absorbent raw materials and processes), third-party and multinational customers, and exports via a US subsidiary (Swara Corp, incorporated 08 December 2025). Brainbees' share of Swara's revenue fell from 27.03% in FY24 to 22.64% in FY26, so management says Swara "has charted a very different long term vision as compared to the original alignment with Brainbees," with "different capex and working capital needs" it should "bridge their own capital requirement" rather than draw on Brainbees' cash. On selling into the OFS despite holding cash, management argued "holding cash and holding an investment are two different capital allocation decisions" and that partial monetisation lets it "crystallize value, improve return on investment and maintain flexibility for future strategic opportunities." Control and commercials are explicitly unchanged: Brainbees stays Promoter at 76.59% (raised from 75.92% in a December 2025 swap that moved Solis Hygiene under Swara to put the hygiene vertical "under a single roof"), Swara remains a subsidiary, Brainbees' management has no involvement in running it (Alok Birla and Udit Birla lead; Supam Maheshwari and Gautam Sharma sit as non-executive directors), and "terms of trade" stay at arm's length with "no impact either on supply chain or pricing." Swara contributed Rs 11,639 million revenue in FY26 (Rs 9,004.39 million after eliminating Rs 2,634.61 million of inter-company sales) and Rs 1,445.7 million of adjusted EBITDA into the India multi-channel segment. No lender, partner or investor is named as having demanded it; analysts had only pushed on a separate asset, GlobalBees, where Supam said in August 2025 that "the most probable outcome for Globalbees... will be listing" given its separate board, management and investors (Premji, Lightspeed, Chiratae).

**How it evolved:** The idea first surfaced as an analyst question about a different unit: on the Aug 2025 call (Aug 13, 2025) Sachin Dixit asked whether FirstCry investors could expect liquidity from GlobalBees "getting demerged, having its own IPO," and Supam said listing was the most probable outcome over a few years; on the Feb 2026 call (Feb 13, 2026) Ajay Agarwal asked for GlobalBees listing timelines and got no answer. Meanwhile the hygiene business was quietly being tidied for separation — a December 26, 2025 intra-group restructuring put Solis Hygiene under Swara Baby to bring the whole hygiene vertical under one roof, lifting Brainbees' Swara stake to 76.59%. Neither the Feb 2026 nor the Jun 2026 call (May 26, 2026) mentioned Swara or any separation at all; on Jun 2026 Supam even said buybacks and similar capital actions had not been discussed internally or at board level. The plan then appeared fully formed in filings only — board approval of OFS participation on July 01, 2026, DRHP plus a management Q&A on July 02, 2026 — followed by a related narrowing at GlobalBees, whose non-core brand rationalisation culminated in the October 07, 2026 sale of its entire 51.54% in Mush Textile.

**What management expects from it:** Swara funds its own capex/working capital from the Rs 5,000 million fresh issue and pursues an independent global contract-manufacturing path; Brainbees crystallizes value, improves ROI and gains flexibility via up to Rs 3,000 million OFS cash, while keeping 76.59% control, Promoter status, consolidation of Swara's Rs 9,004 million revenue and Rs 1,445.7 million adjusted EBITDA, and unchanged arm's-length supply and pricing.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *[Aug 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=4e061dce-c165-4749-9bdb-c4d6dae5f4c6.pdf)* — Asked by JM Financial's Sachin Dixit whether FirstCry shareholders could get liquidity from GlobalBees being demerged or separately IPO'd, Supam framed listing as the likely eventual route and Brainbees' monetisation path over a few years. “Having said this, the most probable outcome for Globalbees as an outcome will be listing, which company and its shareholders will decide over a period of time, is when Brainbees also will find a monetization opportunity over a period of a few years.”
- *[Aug 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=4e061dce-c165-4749-9bdb-c4d6dae5f4c6.pdf)* — The structural argument for separability given for GlobalBees was that it already runs independently of Brainbees, with its own CEO, board and outside shareholders including Premji, Lightspeed and Chiratae. “The company has a separate management team, which is run separately and also it has its separate board, and also it has a separate set of investors as well, apart from Brainbees as well, which includes Premji, Lightspeed, and Chiratae, and so on and so forth.”
- *[May 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=b7f23ae4-cfbb-47ce-b8a9-a579caae0f24.pdf)* — Garima Mishra pressed on the CCPS infusion into GlobalBees; Gautam said it funded working capital, and that all three investor-directors who had stepped off the GlobalBees board participated in that round — the capital-need theme that later justifies Swara funding itself. “This is largely for taking care of their working capital requirement, Garima”
- *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=c27dd63f-321b-4b7b-af06-12c29e11d89d.pdf)* — Ajay Agarwal again asked directly for a GlobalBees listing timeline; the reply covered only Flipkart's revenue-recognition impact and GlobalBees' EBITDA growth (c.150% YoY in Q3, c.50% in 9M), with no timeline given. “And again on Globalbees, any plans on listing of Globalbees? Can you share the tentative timelines or any sense on the same?”
- *[Jun 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=c3d40b3d-ee57-4607-a1df-fcd732269f6b.pdf)* — Five weeks before the Swara DRHP, asked about the low valuation, takeover risk and buybacks, Supam said no such capital action had been discussed internally or by the board — and said nothing about any separation. “Yes, we have sufficient cash on the company, but we haven't discussed any of these buybacks and stuff like that so far, in our internal discussions or even board discussions.”
- *Scheme* — The July 02, 2026 DRHP filing states the original purpose of the 2020 Rs 906.17 million investment for 53.45%: backward integration to scale FirstCry's own diaper home brands with control over quality, timelines and innovation. “We wanted to scale up our home brands within diaper category and wanted to do backward integration to get more control on quality at scale, production timelines and continued innovation in diaper manufacturing.”
- *Scheme* — Core rationale: Swara outgrew the FirstCry ecosystem — multiple third-party and multinational customers, adult diapers and feminine hygiene, exports and a US subsidiary, with Brainbees' share of its revenue down from 27.03% (FY24) to 22.64% (FY26). “With Swara Baby's diversification across product lines, more channels, expansion into International geographies, the business has charted a very different long term vision as compared to the original alignment with Brainbees.”
- *Scheme* — Why not just fund Swara off Brainbees' balance sheet: its capex and working-capital profile differs, so it should raise its own money while Brainbees keeps supply and arm's-length pricing unchanged. “With this expansive and global vision in contract manufacturing of disposable hygiene products with different capex and working capital needs, we decided to initiate the process of separately listing this business so that they can follow their independent journey and bridge their own capital requirement.”
- *Scheme* — Why Brainbees sells up to Rs 3,000 million into the OFS despite ample cash: capital-allocation discipline and value crystallisation, while Swara stays a 76.59% subsidiary and Brainbees' management stays out of its operations. “Partial monetization of a successful investment allows us to crystallize value, improve return on investment and maintain flexibility for future strategic opportunities.”
- *Scheme* — Preparatory step on December 26, 2025: Swara Baby acquired 100% of Solis Hygiene (FY25 turnover Rs 240.73 crore, 3% of consolidated), with Brainbees swapping its 79.34% Solis stake for 56,26,738 Swara shares, lifting its Swara holding from 75.92% to 76.59%. “In order to bring the complete Hygiene vertical under a single roof, the restructuring is being done.”
- *Scheme* — The parallel pruning at GlobalBees: on October 07, 2026 it signed an MOU to sell its entire 51.54% in Mush Textile (brands Mush and BePlush, Rs 11.34 crore or 0.13% of FY26 turnover) for Rs 5,68,93,940 to Nihar Gosalia and Vaishvik Brahmbhatt. “Upon completion of the aforesaid transaction, Mush will cease to be a Subsidiary of GlobalBees and, accordingly, will also cease to be a Step-down Subsidiary of the Company.”
- *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=c27dd63f-321b-4b7b-af06-12c29e11d89d.pdf)* — The GlobalBees brand-rationalisation logic that frames the Mush exit: loss-making, slow-growing non-core brands were being exited, with core categories at 30% growth and 4.9% adjusted EBITDA versus 2% consolidated. “As you're aware, over the last few quarters, we've been speaking about rationalizing certain brands because they were delivering a relatively lower revenue growth as well as incurring losses.”

*Not explained on the calls:* No earnings call ever mentions the Swara IPO, its valuation, or use of OFS proceeds; GlobalBees listing timeline never answered; Mush sale pricing and loss unexplained.
