### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

These texts announce no separation: the only board-approved reorganisation is the opposite — a consolidation. On 29 September 2026 the boards of JSW Cement Limited (JCL) and its 66.23%-owned listed subsidiary Shiva Cement Limited (SCL) approved a Scheme of Arrangement under Sections 230-232 read with Sections 52 and 66, amalgamating SCL into JCL with appointed date 1 April 2026, no cash consideration, and a swap of 5 JCL shares of ₹10 for every 41 SCL shares of ₹2 (JCL's own SCL equity cancelled; the ₹100 crore of 1% OCCRPS it holds also cancelled). The problems management says it solves are: dependence on third-party clinker — SCL's 1.32 mtpa Sundargarh (Odisha) clinker plant becomes backward integration, 'avoiding third-party purchases and associated mark-ups'; split funding — a single entity can raise funds on 'more favorable terms' and inter-company guarantees disappear; two listed entities' duplicated administration, record-keeping, consolidation effort and legal/regulatory compliance; a broken balance sheet at SCL (FY26 turnover ₹435.17 crore, net worth negative ₹30.08 crore versus JCL's ₹5,995.28 crore and ₹7,029.47 crore), whose ₹133.92 crore accumulated losses are written off against its securities premium, while JCL's amalgamation adjustment deficit is set against its own premium account (left at ₹4,335.67 crore) — described as 'right sizing' the financial statements; and SCL's illiquid minority float, whose 33.50% public holders move into a larger, institutionally-held stock. Structurally it is tiny and non-dilutive: shares rise from 1,36,33,64,936 to 1,37,55,13,537, promoters from 72.02% to 71.39%, public from 27.03% to 27.67%. No investor, lender or JV partner is said to have asked for the Shiva merger; valuation was by PwC Business Consulting and BDO Valuation, with fairness opinions from SBI Capital Markets (JCL) and DAM Capital (SCL), JM Financial as exclusive financial advisor and Price Waterhouse & Co as tax adviser; closing is guided at 12-14 months subject to stock exchanges, SEBI, NCLT Mumbai and Odisha Industrial Infrastructure Development Corporation. The genuine separations in these texts are different and smaller: the ₹191.63 crore cash sale of Algebra Endeavour / Vadraj Energy Gujarat Ltd (a Gujarat power plant) to Nuvoco Vistas (SPA 17 November 2025), and JCL selling up to ₹123 crore of JSW One Platforms shares as Promoter Selling Shareholder in that company's IPO (board 13 August 2026, alongside JSW Steel's up to ₹811 crore).

**How it evolved:** The Shiva amalgamation never appears in any of the four earnings calls supplied — the consolidation theme surfaces only around the UAE clinker JV: on the 3 September 2025 Q1 FY26 call Kamlesh Bagmar (Lotus Asset Managers) argued holding Fujairah clinker through a JV 'don't make much sense for the shareholders', and CFO Narinder Singh replied the financial investors would exit over time and it would become a full subsidiary; on the 21 May 2026 Q4 FY26 call Raghav Maheshwari (Equirus) asked directly about merging the JV and was told 'not as of now', maybe in 2-3 years once the financial investor is given an exit, while the new 1.65 MTPA Fujairah grinding unit was instead placed in a wholly owned subsidiary at USD 39 million. The 13 February 2026 investor presentation disclosed the only completed carve-out — the Nuvoco SPA for Vadraj Energy Gujarat at ₹191.63 crore — and footnoted Shiva's 1.0 MTPA Sambalpur grinding unit built under a commercial arrangement with Bhushan Power and Steel. The Shiva merger then arrives fully formed in the 29 September 2026 board outcome and press release, and is restated as a 'Key Business Update' in the 27 October 2026 Q2 FY27 press release; the November 2025 call transcript is unreadable, so any discussion there cannot be checked.

**What management expects from it:** For JSW Cement: in-house clinker (1.32 mtpa) replacing third-party purchases and mark-ups, lower costs, single-entity funding on better terms, no inter-company guarantees, simpler compliance, category leadership and market share; securities premium of ₹4,335.67 crore absorbs the amalgamation deficit. For Shiva holders: shares in a larger, more liquid, institutionally-held entity; ₹133.92 crore of losses written off.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *Scheme* — The transaction is an amalgamation of the listed 66.23%-owned subsidiary Shiva Cement into JSW Cement, appointed date 1 April 2026, explicitly to create one unified platform rather than to separate anything. “Creating a consolidated cement platform supports Transferee Company's strategy, enabling category leadership, increased competitiveness, enhanced market share and efficient resource utilization.”
- *Scheme* — Core industrial logic is backward integration: Shiva's 1.32 mtpa clinker plant at Sundargarh, Odisha stops being a third-party-style supply and becomes internal, cutting external procurement and mark-ups. “The proposed amalgamation will result in backward integration of clinker manufacturing with the Transferee Company's cement manufacturing business.”
- *Scheme* — Financial rationale is single-entity borrowing capacity and the removal of inter-company guarantees between parent and subsidiary. “The proposed amalgamation will lead to greater ability of the consolidated entity to access and raise funds within a single entity on more favorable terms, leading to elimination of inter company guarantees and facilitate more efficient funding arrangements.”
- *Scheme* — Running two listed companies is called out as duplicated cost and compliance — two sets of records, two consolidations, two regulatory burdens. “The proposed amalgamation will result in a simplification of the existing corporate structure and eliminate administrative functions and duplications, reducing regulatory and legal compliances of two listed entities, eliminating multiple record keeping and reducing time and efforts for consolidation of financials at the group level,  consequently reducing the administrative costs of maintaining separate companies, while reducing the multiple legal and regulatory compliances.”
- *Scheme* — Shiva is financially impaired: paid-up equity ₹159.00 crore, FY26 turnover ₹435.17 crore and net worth negative ₹30.08 crore at 31 March 2026, against JSW Cement standalone turnover ₹5,995.28 crore and net worth ₹7,029.47 crore; ₹133.92 crore of accumulated losses are extinguished against its securities premium. “With effect from the Appointed Date, and upon coming into effect of the Scheme, the debit balance of Retained Earnings and SPA in the books of Transferor Company is likely to be  INR (133.92) crore and Nil respectively.”
- *Scheme* — The parent's amalgamation deficit is absorbed into its own securities premium, which is left at ₹4,335.67 crore — the 'right sizing' of both balance sheets. “With effect from the Appointed Date, and upon coming into effect of the Scheme, the balance of Amalgamation Adjustment Deficit Account is likely to be Nil. The balance of SPA in books of Transferee Company is likely to be INR 4,335.67 crore.”
- *Scheme* — Shiva's 33.50% public float is given liquidity: 5 JSW Cement shares of ₹10 per 41 Shiva shares of ₹2, lifting JSW Cement's count from 1,36,33,64,936 to 1,37,55,13,537 and promoters from 72.02% to 71.39%. “The public shareholders of the Transferor Company would become shareholders in the Transferee Company, which has a higher traded equity share base, greater market liquidity, and a diversified institutional investor base, thereby providing shareholders with enhanced liquidity, broader market participation, and improved opportunities for value realization.”
- *Scheme* — CEO Nilesh Narwekar framed it as integration and simplification, with completion guided at 12-14 months subject to exchanges, SEBI, NCLT Mumbai and Odisha Industrial Infrastructure Development Corporation. “The proposed merger is a strategic step towards creating a more integrated and efficient business.”
- *CALL Sep 2025* — The only consolidation pressure voiced by investors concerned the UAE clinker JV, not Shiva — Kamlesh Bagmar of Lotus Asset Managers argued holding Fujairah through a JV was poor for shareholders; the CFO said the financial investors would exit and it would become a full subsidiary, timeline undecided. “So lastly, like, doesn't it make a bigger sense to have, like, say, clinker capacity of Fuj airah under our own hold entirely?”
- *CALL May 2026* — Asked again about folding the Fujairah JV in, management deferred it to 2-3 years because a financial investor must first be given an exit — while the new 1.65 MTPA UAE grinding unit was put in a wholly owned subsidiary (USD 39 million) that consolidates into the parent, with the JV selling clinker to it at arm's length. “Not as of now. Probably going forward in next 2 -3 years, we will have a look because there is a financial investor sitting there, we'll have to provide exit to him.”
- *CALL Feb 2026* — The actual disposal in the period was non-core: Algebra Endeavour / Vadraj Energy Gujarat Ltd, owning a Gujarat power plant, sold to Nuvoco Vistas for cash; the November 2025 filing confirms the division contributed nothing to turnover, income or net worth. “Entered into a Share Purchase Agreement with Nuvoco Vistas Corp. Ltd. for the transfer of Vadraj Energy Gujarat Ltd. (owning a power plant in Gujarat), for a consideration of Rs. 191.63 crore”
- *Scheme* — Because Shiva is a subsidiary, the deal is a related-party transaction under LODR; arm's length rests on independent registered valuers (PwC Business Consulting, BDO Valuation) and a category 1 merchant banker fairness opinion, with no cash moving. “Additionally, the consideration to be discharged for the Scheme of amalgamation is determined by independent registered valuers on which a fairness opinion has been issued by an independent category 1 merchant banker, the transaction therefore is at arm's length.”

*Not explained on the calls:* No quantified synergy, cost-saving or clinker-volume numbers; no EPS or margin impact; no analyst Q&A on the merger (Nov 2025 transcript unreadable); Fujairah JV buyout timing unexplained.

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

The texts do not contain any management-stated rationale for a separation: what the filings actually show is not a demerger or carve-out of a business line but the government-directed partial listing of Coal India's existing wholly-owned coal subsidiaries through pure offers for sale by CIL, with no rationale, synergy argument or use-of-proceeds ever explained in the three earnings calls. The only stated 'why' anywhere in the material is a directive: the Ministry of Coal's Office Memorandum I/37811/2025 dated 16.12.2025 'advised CIL to take concrete steps to ensure further listing of subsidiaries namely MCL and SECL in the upcoming financial year', after which the CIL Board gave in-principle approval by circular resolution on 23.12.2025 for onward submission to DIPAM — i.e. the asker was the owner/government (MoC and DIPAM), not investors, lenders or partners. The word 'further' implies a programme already under way: Bharat Coking Coal Limited (BCCL) listed on 19.01.2026 after selling 465,700,000 equity shares of ₹10 face value at ₹23 per share, cutting CIL's holding from 100% to 90% (4,657,000,000 to 4,191,300,000 shares); Central Mine Planning & Design Institute Limited (CMPDIL) listed on 30.03.2026 after selling 107,100,000 shares of ₹2 face value at ₹172.00, cutting CIL from 100% to 85% (714,000,000 to 606,900,000 shares). Both remain subsidiaries, so no business is being separated operationally — only minority equity is being sold, and because each is an offer for sale by CIL, proceeds accrue to the parent and not to the subsidiary. The pipeline then moved to the two largest producers: MCL's DRHP dated 01.09.2026 and RHP dated 13.11.2026 for an OFS of up to 661,836,300 shares (₹2 face value), and SECL's DRHP dated 01.11.2026 for up to 668,056,100 shares (₹2 face value), each 'subject to receipt of applicable approvals, prevailing market conditions'. The calls supply only indirect context for why these particular units are separable: management described sharply different subsidiary economics and problems — MCL producing 89.4 mt in H1 FY24 with just 21,523 employees and very low overburden versus SECL/ECL carrying ~30-35 old underground mines and high manpower (CIL total ~2,35,000 employees in Nov 2023, ~2.20 lakh by May 2025, ~12,000 superannuating a year); SECL repeatedly missing targets (197 mt target vs 162 mt FY23; ~8-9 mt short in FY24; heavy rainfall and land acquisition in FY25); BCCL as the pure coking-coal entity (36.18 mt FY23, 41 mt FY24 target) whose output cannot be used fully 'because of the lack of washing capacities', prompting washery monetisation (2 mt Durga washery won by JSW Steel); and CMPDIL building CIL's in-house e-auction platform from Ranchi to phase out MSTC. None of that was ever linked by management to listing or separation, so any value-unlocking logic is inference, not something the company stated.

**How it evolved:** On the Nov 2023 call (21.11.2023) the only structural discussion was housing non-coal verticals in subsidiaries/JVs — CIL Solar PV Limited and CIL Navikarniya Urja Limited for 3,000 MW of solar, plus coal-gasification JVs with BHEL and GAIL. On the Feb 2024 call (19.02.2024) an investor explicitly asked whether these would become 'a separate demerged entity' and management refused the idea: subsidiaries and JVs already exist, 'we are not going to create any new subsidy. It is not in our discussion right now.' The May 2025 analyst meet (14.05.2025) contains no mention of listing, demerger or subsidiary IPOs at all — only operations, e-auction premiums, ₹80,000 crore capex and BCCL washery monetisation. The idea then appears only in filings, and top-down: MoC's OM of 16.12.2025 and the CIL Board's in-principle approvals of 23.12.2025 for MCL and SECL, followed by BCCL's listing (19.01.2026), CMPDIL's (30.03.2026), MCL's DRHP/RHP (01.09.2026 and 13.11.2026) and SECL's DRHP (01.11.2026).

**What management expects from it:** Nothing was stated. Across all three calls management gave no expectation for margins, capital, valuation or focus from any separation, and in Feb 2024 denied a demerger was under discussion. The filings assert only compliance with the MoC directive and dissemination of material information; each IPO is an offer for sale by CIL, so proceeds go to the parent and the subsidiaries stay subsidiaries.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *[Feb 2024](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=06da4b0a-5420-4ecc-aa42-737719710147.pdf)* — Asked directly whether the energy/renewables vertical would be hived off as a separate demerged entity, management rejected it — existing subsidiaries and JVs suffice and no such plan was under discussion. “We had already formed the joint ventures and the new companies, so those we'll pursue that. We are not going to create any new subsidy. It is not in our discussion right now.”
- *Nov 2023* — Structural separation at this point meant only putting non-coal businesses into dedicated subsidiaries — CIL Solar PV Limited and CIL Navikarniya Urja Limited — for a 3,000 MW solar net-zero programme, with 250 MW due by that year-end. “Sir now we have two subsidiaries, CIL Solar PV Limited and CIL Navikarniya Urja Limited.”
- *Nov 2023* — Management explained why subsidiary economics differ radically — MCL produced 89.4 mt with 21,523 employees on low stripping ratios and few underground mines, while SECL and ECL each carry ~30-35 old underground mines and legacy manpower that cannot be shed. “MCL has formed out in 1992, it was carved out from SECL, the deep coal field, and Talcher is from Central Coalfields. So relatively new mines, open cast mines, stripping ratio is very less.”
- *[Feb 2024](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=06da4b0a-5420-4ecc-aa42-737719710147.pdf)* — Management flagged SECL as the single lagging subsidiary against a 197 mt target (162 mt in FY23, 147 mt before), running 8-9 mt short on land shortage while five other subsidiaries were ahead of target. “In SECL, there is an issue in initially mega projects, two projects.”
- *[May 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=f26c1f2d-5905-47eb-b473-a448cab9c8ee.pdf)* — The two subsidiaries later put up for listing were named as the sources of FY25 volume slippage — SECL on abnormal rainfall and land acquisition, CCL on EC/FC clearances — with unmet demand rather than weak demand. “At SECL, the main issue was abnormally heavy rainfall, seasonal rainfall and certain issues related to land acquisition there and in CCL also issues related to clearances, EC and FC clearances from the Ministry for certain patches.”
- *[May 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=f26c1f2d-5905-47eb-b473-a448cab9c8ee.pdf)* — BCCL was described as a pure coking-coal entity whose output cannot be monetised for lack of washing capacity, addressed by monetising washeries — the 2 mt Durga washery auctioned to JSW Steel — and by consortium-based steel-coking linkages; supplies were ~3.7 mt, of which 2.4-2.7 mt washed. “So, BCCL, the entire production is basically coking coal. We are not able to use it fully because of the lack of washing capacities.”
- *[May 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=f26c1f2d-5905-47eb-b473-a448cab9c8ee.pdf)* — No listing, IPO, demerger or separation of any subsidiary was raised by management or by any analyst across the entire May 2025 analyst meet; the forward agenda given was 875 mt FY26 volumes, ~₹20,000 crore annual mining capex and ~₹80,000 crore over four-five years including gasification and thermal. “And for that also, equity is required. Based on that, this cash balance, as and when the capex will progress, the cash balance will also be getting deployed.”
- *Scheme* — The only stated cause of the separation programme is a government instruction: MoC's Office Memorandum I/37811/2025 of 16.12.2025, after which the CIL Board approved listing of MCL and SECL in principle by circular resolution on 23.12.2025 for onward submission to DIPAM. “Ministry of Coal, vide its Office Memorandum I/37811/2025 dated 16.12.2025 had advised CIL to take concrete steps to ensure further listing of subsidiaries namely MCL and SECL in the upcoming financial year.”
- *Scheme* — BCCL was the first to list: 465,700,000 equity shares of ₹10 face value sold at ₹23 per share (≈₹1,071 crore to CIL on those numbers), listed 19.01.2026, taking CIL from 100% to 90% — it remains a subsidiary, so this is a minority sell-down, not an operational separation. “As a result of the above, the Company's shareholding in Bharat Coking Coal Limited stands reduced from 100% to 90% (i.e., from 4,657,000,000 Equity Shares to 4,191,300,000 Equity Shares) of the issued and paid-up Equity Share capital of Bharat Coking Coal Limited.”
- *Scheme* — CMPDIL, the planning/design and in-house e-auction-platform arm, listed on 30.03.2026 selling 107,100,000 shares of ₹2 face value at ₹172.00 (≈₹1,842 crore on those numbers), reducing CIL from 100% to 85% while remaining a subsidiary. “Central Mine Planning & Design Institute Limited, pursuant to its IPO, has sold 107,100,000 Equity Shares at an offer price of ₹172.00 per share which were offered for sale by the Company.”
- *Scheme* — MCL, CIL's lowest-cost and largest producer, moved from DRHP on 01.09.2026 to RHP dated 13.11.2026 for an offer for sale of up to 661,836,300 equity shares of ₹2 face value held by CIL. “The RHP filing pertains to the proposed initial public offering ("IPO") of MCL comprising an offer for sale of up to 661,836,300 equity shares by Coal India Limited, which remains subject to receipt of applicable approvals, market conditions, and other relevant considerations.”
- *Scheme* — SECL, the chronic laggard on production, filed its DRHP dated 01.11.2026 for an offer for sale of up to 668,056,100 equity shares of ₹2 face value by CIL — the largest share count of the four and the second limb of the MoC directive. “The DRHP filing pertains to the proposed Initial Public Offering ("IPO") of SECL, comprising an Offer for Sale of up to 668,056,100 equity shares having a face value of INR 2 each, held by Coal India Limited.”

*Not explained on the calls:* Everything: no stated rationale, no valuation, margin, capital-allocation, cost-of-capital or focus argument, no use of proceeds, no pricing basis, and no explanation of why MCL, SECL, BCCL and CMPDIL were chosen or what happens to CCL, NCL, WCL and ECL.

> **Listing:** PARTIAL SPIN-OFF, IPO BOARD APPROVAL — GAIL Gas Limited; date not fixed

**The partial spin-off:** **GAIL Gas Limited** (subsidiary); parent's stake 100% (wholly owned subsidiary of GAIL); IPO stage: board approval; exchange: Indian stock exchanges.

> “This is to inform that GAIL Board in its meeting held today i.e. 30.10.2026 accorded in-principle approval for Listing of shares of GAIL Gas Limited, (a wholly owned subsidiary of GAIL) (GGL) on the I”

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** GAIL Gas Limited, GAIL's wholly owned city gas distribution subsidiary, listed via IPO diluting up to 25% — class `not stated`.

- *Insiders:* GGL is a wholly owned subsidiary of GAIL; GAIL dilutes equity in GGL upto 25%, retaining at least 75%. No management incentives stated.
- *What it reveals:* GGL Q3 FY26 turnover Rs.3,292 crore, PBT Rs.143 crore, PAT Rs.106 crore, 7.8 MMSCMD volume, 12,46,000 DPNG connections, 674 CNG stations; plus six GAs (0.55 MMSCMD, 215 CNG stations) transferred in by slump sale effective 01.01.2027.
- *Selling pressure:* unlikely — IPO route sells shares to willing subscribers; no distribution to GAIL shareholders, no index exclusion stated.
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* GGL's final IPO proposal to GAIL Board on valuation, price band, extent of dilution and modality
- *In their words:* “This is to inform that GAIL Board in its meeting held today i.e. 30.10.2026 accorded in-principle approval for Listing of shares of GAIL Gas Limited, (a wholly owned subsidiary of GAIL) (GGL) on the Indian stock exchanges through Initial Public Offering (IPO) route by diluting GAIL's equity in GGL upto 25%.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

The business being separated is GAIL's own directly-authorised city gas distribution (CGD) retail business — the six geographical areas Varanasi, Patna, Ranchi, East Singhbhum (Jamshedpur), Cuttack and Khordha (Bhubaneswar) — which the Board resolved to hive down into its 100% subsidiary GAIL Gas Limited as a slump sale on a going-concern basis, effective 01.01.2027, with the subsidiary then to be listed via IPO diluting up to 25% of GAIL's equity. Management's stated reason was structural, not financial distress: CMD Sandeep Kumar Gupta said it was 'in order to have a single entity for development of GAIL's CGD business and for bringing business synergy, efficiency and retail focused business approach' — i.e. GAIL group CGD was split across GAIL's own balance sheet (six GAs, 0.36–0.55 MMSCMD, 195→215 CNG stations and 3.53→4.64 lakh DPNG connections over FY25–Q3FY26, volumes up ~25% in FY25 but 'currently in their early stages of development'), GAIL Gas (16 GAs plus 9 JVs, 7.0→7.8 MMSCMD, 12.46 lakh DPNG connections, 674 CNG stations, FY25 turnover Rs 12,231 crore, PBT Rs 615 crore up 42%, PAT Rs 451 crore up 40%) and 72 group GAs in all. A pipeline-and-marketing parent was also an awkward owner of a retail business: management said 'we are constantly reviewing these CGDs to optimize costs and enhance efficiencies', and segment reporting of the CGD/marketing split was itself confusing analysts (the Rs 400 crore standalone-to-consolidated regrouping queried in Jul 2025). The upside case cited was CGD demand: a PNGRB projection of consumption rising '2.5 times to 3.5 times by 2030 and 6 times to 7 times by 2040 from the baseline of approximately 37 MMSCMD in FY 24' (~15% CAGR), PNGRB capping CNG/domestic-PNG tariffs at Zone 1 and expected GST inclusion lowering CGD input costs. For the IPO, the argument was scale and timing — 'GAIL Gas is one of the biggest company in the country in terms of city gas distribution... now is high time that we started the process of listing GAIL Gas' — with a consultant already selected and a roughly one-year timeline. The impetus came largely from sell-side investors (Citi's Saurabh Handa on restructuring CGD investments in Nov 2024; Alliance Services' Balaji Das on the IPO consultant in Oct 2025); the only external consent management named was CCEA, 'since these six GAs were authorized to GAIL by CCEA' — no lender or JV-partner demand was cited. Running in the opposite direction, GAIL simultaneously pulled Konkan LNG Limited in: it bought out MSEB Holding's 7,40,55,220 shares via a NCLT-approved capital reduction (paid 06.07.2026, GAIL to 100%) and then merged KLL (FY26 turnover Rs 741 crore, versus GAIL's Rs 1,41,483 crore) into GAIL to 'create a larger and stronger vertically integrated entity, simplify and rationalize group structure'.

**How it evolved:** The idea first surfaced only as an unprompted analyst question on the Nov 06, 2024 Q2 FY25 call, where R.K. Jain said no call had been taken on restructuring GAIL Gas — 'this is in our mind, but nothing concrete' — while adding that GAIL was 'looking for listing one or two JVs'; the Jan 30, 2025 call did not touch it. It became concrete at the May 14, 2025 annual analyst meet, where the CMD disclosed the Board's recommendation (passed 13.05.2025) to transfer the six GAs to GAIL Gas for a 'single entity... retail focused business approach', subject to CCEA. On Oct 31, 2025 the second leg appeared: GAIL confirmed it had started the GAIL Gas listing process, had selected a consultant, and expected 'a one year time line or so'; the Feb 02, 2026 Q3 FY26 call was silent on both. The filings then executed it: 31.07.2026 KLL merger into GAIL, and 30.10.2026 Board approval of the six-GA slump sale effective 01.01.2027 plus in-principle approval of a GAIL Gas IPO diluting up to 25%.

**What management expects from it:** One consolidated, retail-focused CGD entity with business synergy and efficiency; the six early-stage GAs (0.55 MMSCMD) folded into GAIL Gas's 7.8 MMSCMD platform (674 CNG stations, 12.46 lakh DPNG) to capture CGD demand rising 2.5–3.5x by 2030, aided by Zone-1 tariff capping and expected GST; price discovery and capital via an IPO of up to 25%. Parent keeps transmission/marketing; Konkan LNG's merger simplifies the group and adds its cargo-driven profit.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *[Nov 2024](https://gailonline.com/pdf/InvestorsZone/GAIL_Earnings_Call_Q2_FY25_11112024.pdf)* — Citi's Saurabh Handa raised the split of CGD investments between GAIL standalone and GAIL Gas and asked whether GAIL would restructure them — the first time the idea appears in the record. “On your City Gas investments, whether they are at the standalone entity or in GAIL Gas? Is there any thought process to look at restructuring these streamline these investments?”
- *[Nov 2024](https://gailonline.com/pdf/InvestorsZone/GAIL_Earnings_Call_Q2_FY25_11112024.pdf)* — Director (Finance) R.K. Jain confirmed restructuring was under internal consideration but that no decision existed, while separately flagging that GAIL was working on listing one or two JVs with an update promised in Q3. “As a company about GAIL Gas has not yet taken any call for restructuring of GAIL Gas. This is in our mind, but nothing concrete I can share with you right now.”
- *[Nov 2024](https://gailonline.com/pdf/InvestorsZone/GAIL_Earnings_Call_Q2_FY25_11112024.pdf)* — Alongside CGD restructuring, Jain said listing of group entities was already in progress and at 'a good stage', promising an update in Q3 FY25. “So also, we are looking for listing one or two JVs, which we are in the process and once we move forward and we take a call, we'll come back to you, but that we are certainly working and we are in a good stage.”
- *[May 2025](https://www.gailonline.com/pdf/InvestorsZone/GAIL%20Analysts%20Meet%20Q4%20FY25%2014.05.2025.pdf)* — CMD Sandeep Kumar Gupta disclosed the Board's 13.05.2025 recommendation to transfer GAIL's six directly-held CGD geographical areas to wholly-owned GAIL Gas Limited — the core rationale being one single, synergistic, retail-focused CGD entity. “In order to have a single entity for development of GAIL's CGD business and for bringing business synergy, efficiency and retail focused business approach, the Board has recommended to transfer six geographical areas of GAIL to its wholly owned subsidiary, GAIL Gas Limited.”
- *[May 2025](https://www.gailonline.com/pdf/InvestorsZone/GAIL%20Analysts%20Meet%20Q4%20FY25%2014.05.2025.pdf)* — The only approval condition management named was CCEA, because the six GAs (Varanasi, Patna, Ranchi, Jamshedpur, Bhubaneswar, Cuttack) had been awarded to GAIL by CCEA rather than won by GAIL Gas. “This is subject to approval of CCEA since these six GAs were authorized to GAIL by CCEA.”
- *[May 2025](https://www.gailonline.com/pdf/InvestorsZone/GAIL%20Analysts%20Meet%20Q4%20FY25%2014.05.2025.pdf)* — The six GAs were described as early-stage but fast-growing (volumes up ~25% in FY25, then ~0.4–0.45 MMSCMD) and under continuous cost review — the sub-scale retail assets being pushed into the dedicated CGD vehicle. “In the Financial Year 24-25, these six GAs have shown impressive growth with volumes increasing by approximately 25%. We are constantly reviewing these CGDs to optimize costs and enhance efficiencies.”
- *[May 2025](https://www.gailonline.com/pdf/InvestorsZone/GAIL%20Analysts%20Meet%20Q4%20FY25%2014.05.2025.pdf)* — The growth case for a standalone CGD entity rested on PNGRB's demand projection, supplemented by PNGRB's proposal to cap CNG/domestic-PNG tariffs at Zone 1 and expected GST inclusion to cut CGD input costs. “the CGD sector is anticipated to be the key driver of growth, with consumption expected to increase 2.5 times to 3.5 times by 2030 and 6 times to 7 times by 2040 from the baseline of approximately 37 MMSCMD in FY '24”
- *[May 2025](https://www.gailonline.com/pdf/InvestorsZone/GAIL%20Analysts%20Meet%20Q4%20FY25%2014.05.2025.pdf)* — GAIL Gas's own FY25 numbers framed the receiving entity as a scaled, improving business: turnover Rs 12,231 crore, PBT Rs 615 crore (+42%), PAT Rs 451 crore (+40%), 16 GAs owned plus 9 JVs. “During the current financial year, that is FY '25, GAIL Gas Limited's turnover stood at Rs. 12,231 crores as against Rs. 10,944 crores in FY '24. PBT increased by 42% and stood at Rs. 615 crores as against Rs. 434 crores in FY '24.”
- *[May 2025](https://www.gailonline.com/pdf/InvestorsZone/GAIL%20Analysts%20Meet%20Q4%20FY25%2014.05.2025.pdf)* — On the other entity later consolidated in, management said Konkan LNG (Dabhol) would swing to profit once the all-weather breakwater let it run 34–36 cargoes versus 21, worth roughly Rs 300 crore. “So this year certainly we were not in positive because of the breakwater issue. But going forward, we will have positive bottom line from KLL.”
- *Oct 2025* — An investor (Balaji Das) pressed on the GAIL Gas IPO and the consultant being hired for listing analysis, confirming the second leg of the plan was investor-driven. “And the second question is on, we had like on the listing of the GAIL Gas IPO actually. So, any further progress on consultant and when are the future plans actually for GAIL Gas actually, because we heard that we are hiring consultants for analysis of listing.”
- *Oct 2025* — Jain confirmed the listing process had begun — consultant selected, order imminent — and justified it on GAIL Gas's scale: 7.72 MMSCMD of volume and more GAs than any peer, with Bangalore alone at 1 MMSCMD. “And we in GAIL believe that now is high time that we started the process of listing GAIL Gas, in that regard we have already started the process of hiring of consultant.”
- *Oct 2025* — He put a roughly one-year timeline on the listing, contingent on the consultant's study — the only timing guidance given on the IPO. “So, we are on a path to study about listing of GAIL Gas and after conclusion of that study, certainly that study is very important for us, we expect a one year time line or so should be good enough.”

*Not explained on the calls:* No valuation, slump-sale consideration, IPO size or use of proceeds, standalone margin/ROCE or capex targets, CCEA timing, or why 25%; calls after Oct 2025 went silent.

**The partial spin-off:** **Indian Gas Exchange Limited** (associate); parent's stake 47.3% → 25%; IPO stage: DRHP filed; exchange: BSE Limited; timeline: At the IEX Analyst Meet held July 24, 2026 the CFO said "the good part is that they filed the DRHP in this month and hopefully (would be) getting listed soon"; .

> “In furtherance of our intimation dated December 03, 2025, and in terms of Regulation 30 of the SEBI Listing Regulations, we wish to inform that the Indian Gas Exchange Limited ("IGX"), an associate co”

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** Indian Gas Exchange (IGX), IEX's 47.3%-held natural gas spot exchange associate, partly sold via IPO — class `regulatory_strategic`.

- *Insiders:* IEX holds 47.3% of IGX and offers for sale up to 16,710,000 shares (22.3%), retaining 25%; management refused any IEX-shareholder reservation, calling it an independent IPO. Other incentives not stated.
- *What it reveals:* IGX is India's only natural gas exchange: FY26 volume 76.8 million MMBtu, PAT Rs 42 crore (up 28-35%), ~3% of India's gas consumption and 20% of the spot market, 40%+ volume CAGR, embedded inside IEX's Rs 492-493 crore consolidated profit.
- *Selling pressure:* unlikely — Listing is an IPO offer for sale by IEX, not a distribution of IGX shares to IEX shareholders; buyers self-select.
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* IGX's DRHP dated July 14, 2026 — offer size, IGX standalone financials and post-offer shareholding.
- *In their words:* “As you may be aware that we have already filed a DRHP (Draft Red Herring Prospectus) for IPO of IGX as we today hold 47.3% in IGX.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

The separation here is not a demerger of IEX's own operations but the carve-out of its gas arm, Indian Gas Exchange (IGX), via an offer-for-sale IPO, driven purely by PNGRB's exchange ownership rules, which cap any single shareholder at 25% and any trading member at 5%. IEX held 47.3%-47.5% of IGX and had to cut that to 25% within five years; that five-year window expired in December 2025, so IEX took a one-year extension from PNGRB, now running to 31 December 2026. Management said the original slippage was commercial, not strategic: 'there were huge challenges in the gas market and gas exchange' and the 'business ramp-up has not happened at the rate at which we were expecting it' (Nov 2025). With IGX now scaled - FY26 volume 76.8 million MMBtu (+28% YoY, over 40% CAGR), PAT Rs 41.9-42 crore (+35%), roughly 3% of India's gas consumption and 20% of the spot market, 23 delivery points versus 4 in FY22 and 10 contract types versus 6 - IEX chose the IPO over other divestment options and formally asked IGX to proceed. The DRHP was filed on 14 July 2026 with SEBI and BSE as a pure offer for sale of up to 16,710,000 shares by IEX, i.e. the 22.3% it must shed; no fresh issue, proceeds or valuation was discussed. The same ownership-cap logic makes IEX house each new commodity in its own company: Indian Coal Exchange Ltd was incorporated in June 2026 with board approval, a mineral exchange company is planned, and its shareholding rules are 'similar to what has been notified for the power exchange and the gas exchange.' The only parties asking for the separation were regulators (PNGRB; the Ministry of Coal rules for the coal exchange) - not investors, lenders or partners; investors asked only about timing and for a proportionate reservation in the IGX IPO, which Goel refused because it is 'an independent IPO'. Separately, management rejected the analyst suggestion that the exchange's clearing and settlement function must be hived into its own entity, saying the PSS Act requires registration, not separation, with no financial impact.

**How it evolved:** The idea surfaced on the Nov 2025 call (31 Oct 2025), where Goel disclosed the 25% PNGRB deadline of December 2025, blamed the slow gas-market ramp-up for the delay, said the regulator had assured an extension (IEX asked for eighteen months), and that IEX was 'considering different options for divestment'. By the Feb 2026 call (30 Jan 2026) the option had narrowed to an IPO: IEX had asked IGX to proceed, targeting completion within the year subject to SEBI clearance. On the Apr 2026 call (24 Apr 2026) the extension was confirmed to 31 December 2026 and the process was 'progressing well'. The DRHP followed on 14 July 2026, and at the Jul 2026 analyst meet (24 Jul 2026) Goel sized it as a 22.3% sell-down while also disclosing that Indian Coal Exchange Ltd had been incorporated in June 2026 as a separate company.

**What management expects from it:** Compliance first: IEX falls to 25% of IGX, keeping an associate stake in a business they expect to grow volumes 25-30% annually as gas prices fall; IGX gets its own listing and price. Each new commodity (coal, minerals) sits in its own company under the same 25%/5% ownership caps. No margin, capital or valuation benefit for IEX was claimed.

- *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=adc1e4df-3d65-4223-ab80-2062887ba7a8.pdf)* — Reason the deadline could not be met on the original schedule was weak gas-exchange ramp-up, and the route was still undecided at this point. “So we have applied to PNGRB and the regulator was quite supportive, and they have assured that they will give time extension. And we are also working out option s, we are considering different options for divestment and complying with the regulatory provisions.”
- *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=adc1e4df-3d65-4223-ab80-2062887ba7a8.pdf)* — Goel attributed the shortfall explicitly to gas market conditions rather than any strategic choice. “because in the past, there were huge challenges in the gas market and gas exchange. **What is being separated, as the documents put it:** NLC India Renewables Limited (NIRL) — the group's renewable energy assets, being IPO'd via Offer for Sale — class `regulatory_strategic`.

- *Insiders:* NIRL is NLCIL's wholly owned subsidiary; NLCIL's investment rose to ₹5,119.75 crore as on 12.10.2026; Board approved OFS of up to 10 crore shares held by NLCIL. Management stake not stated.
- *What it reveals:* Renewables, long buried in a lignite/thermal group, is now a priced standalone: segment assets ₹10,881.76 cr and H1 FY27 segment result ₹237.08 cr on revenue ₹462.27 cr; NLCIL has sunk ₹5,119.75 cr of equity into NIRL.
- *Selling pressure:* unlikely — No shares distributed to NLCIL holders — separation is via IPO/Offer for Sale by the parent, so no forced spin-off supply.

- *Read next:* NIRL's IPO offer document / DRHP, plus Power–Renewables segment assets (₹10,881.76 cr) and liabilities (₹6,646.10 cr)
- *In their words:* “The Board had earlier, at its meeting held on 12.01.2026, accorded in-principle approval for the listing of NIRL, which was duly intimated.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

The business being separated is NLC India Ltd's renewable energy (solar/wind) portfolio, carved out of the lignite-mining and thermal-power parent into NLC India Renewables Limited (NIRL), a wholly owned subsidiary. The filings state the reason explicitly as policy-driven monetisation, not a strategic idea originated by management: the 31.10.2025 intimation says the hive-off of 7 RE assets totalling 1,430 MW is 'under Asset Monetization Plan approved by the Ministry of Coal, Administrative Ministry', and the Q2 FY27 accounts repeat that it is 'In line with the National Monetization Pipeline and in consultation with the Ministry of Coal'. Scale cited: the 7 assets earned Rs 701.61 crore of revenue in FY25 (4.59% of consolidated revenue of Rs 15,282.96 crore) but carried net worth of Rs 3,869.26 crore (20.67% of owners' equity of Rs 18,722.97 crore) — i.e. a capital-heavy, low-revenue block being moved off the parent's balance sheet at book value, with consideration by equity shares/acknowledgement of debt, and Government of India approval already received. Execution was phased: Phase I (1,430 MW) transferred w.e.f. 01.01.2026; a second addendum dated 03.09.2026 added 708.96 MW (including a 4 MW green hydrogen project, assets at various stages of construction/operation) for Rs 853.97 crore, contributing only Rs 41.16 crore of FY26 revenue (0.24%) and Rs 925.08 crore of net worth (4.30%). The separate vehicle is visibly being used to raise third-party capital and partners that the parent could not house: a maiden green loan with Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation of JPY 15.464 billion (USD 100 million) under the ECB framework 'to fund renewable energy projects through its subsidiary NIRL', a PTC India JV for 2,000 MW, an OREDA MoU/JV, a DIPAM-approved JV with MAHAPREIT, an SJVNL 200 MW wind PPA and an NCRTC LoA for 110 MW captive solar — now sitting as step-down subsidiaries NARL, NRRL, NNRL, NORL and NPRL. The end state is a listing: the Board gave in-principle approval for listing NIRL on 12.01.2026 and on 04.11.2026 approved an Offer for Sale of up to 10,00,00,000 equity shares of Rs 10 each held by NLCIL in NIRL as part of NIRL's proposed IPO, after NLCIL injected a further Rs 2,000 crore of equity on 12.10.2026 taking its NIRL investment to Rs 5,119.75 crore.

**How it evolved:** The seven earnings calls tagged Feb 2024, Aug 2024, Nov 2024, Feb 2025, May 2025, Aug 2025 and Feb 2026 (held 10.02.2026) contain no extractable transcript text — six are scanned images and the Feb 2026 item is only the covering letter — so the idea cannot be traced call by call from these documents. From the filings the sequence is: in-principle approval for the Business Transfer Agreement to hive off the RE assets on 07.08.2025 (referenced in the 31.10.2025 intimation), BTA signed 31.10.2025 for 7 assets/1,430 MW under the Ministry of Coal's Asset Monetization Plan, transfer effected 01.01.2026, in-principle Board approval for listing NIRL on 12.01.2026, an addendum on 03.09.2026 adding 708.96 MW plus a 4 MW green hydrogen project, and OFS/IPO approval on 04.11.2026. The plan therefore widened from a one-off intra-group asset transfer at book value into a phased carve-out plus an IPO of the subsidiary, with the scope growing to include under-construction and green-hydrogen assets and five new partner-funded step-down subsidiaries.

**What management expects from it:** Not stated in words. The documents imply only: a dedicated, separately capitalised renewables vehicle (NIRL equity Rs 5,119.75 crore) able to raise third-party green debt (SMBC USD 100 million ECB) and partner equity via JVs with PTC, OREDA, MAHAPREIT, SJVNL and NCRTC, monetising assets per the Ministry of Coal plan and realising value through an NIRL IPO/OFS, leaving NLCIL focused on mining and thermal.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *Scheme* — The separation is a Ministry of Coal-mandated monetisation: 7 renewable assets of 1,430 MW hived off from NLCIL to wholly owned subsidiary NIRL under the approved Asset Monetization Plan, with Government of India approval already obtained. “we write to inform that the Company has entered into a Business Transfer Agreement with NLC India Renewables Limited (NIRL), a wholly owned subsidiary of the Company on 31st October, 2025, for proposed Hived off of the 7 Renewable Energy Assets with total Capacity of 1,430 MW from the Company to its Wholly Owned Subsidiary, NIRL, under Asset Monetization Plan approved by the Ministry of Coal, Administrative Ministry.”
- *Scheme* — The disclosed economics show a capital-heavy, low-revenue block: 4.59% of consolidated revenue but 20.67% of owners' equity, transferred at book value with consideration in shares or acknowledgement of debt. “Net worth of 7 RE assets is Rs. 3,869.26 Crore, which is 20.67% of Net-worth of NLCIL i.e., Rs. 18,722.97 Crore (Total equity attributable to owners) based on Audited Financial Statements of 31st March, 2025.”
- *Scheme* — Q2 FY27 accounts restate the driver as the National Monetization Pipeline and set out the two-phase mechanics, Phase II being 708.96 MW for Rs 853.97 crore under a second addendum. “In line with the National Monetization Pipeline and in consultation with the Ministry of Coal, NLCIL executed a Business Transfer Agreement (BTA) with NLC India Renewables Limited on 31st October 2025 for transferring 1,430 MW of renewable energy assets.”
- *Scheme* — The scope later widened beyond operating plants to assets still being built, including a 4 MW green hydrogen project, contributing only 0.24% of FY26 revenue and 4.30% of net worth. “Addendum to the Business Transfer Agreement with NIRL is signed on 03rd September, 2026 for proposed hiving off 708.96 MW of Renewable Energy Assets including a 4 MW Green Hydrogen Project which are at various stages of construction/ operation.”
- *Scheme* — The first transfer actually completed on 1 January 2026, converting the plan from intimation to executed carve-out. “The aforesaid transfer has been effected on 01st January, 2026, in terms of the Business Transfer Agreement executed between the Company and NIRL on 31st October, 2025.”
- *Scheme* — The end-point is an IPO of NIRL with NLCIL selling down: OFS of up to 10 crore shares approved on 04.11.2026, following in-principle listing approval on 12.01.2026. “Offer for Sale (OFS) of up to 10,00,00,000 (Ten Crore) equity shares of face value of Rs.10 each held by the Company in NLC India Renewables Limited (NIRL), Wholly Owned Subsidiary, as part of the proposed Initial Public Offering (IPO) of NIRL, subject to compliance with the applicable provisions of the SEBI (Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2018, and other applicable statutory and regulatory requirements.”
- *Scheme* — Lenders and partners are transacting with the subsidiary, not the parent: a maiden offshore green loan of JPY 15.464 billion (USD 100 million) from SMBC under the ECB framework is explicitly routed through NIRL. “Signed its maiden Green Loan agreement with Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation (SMBC) under the ECB framework , amounting to JPY 15.464 billion (USO 100 million), to fund renewable energy projects through its subsidiary NIRL.”
- *Scheme* — NIRL has become the JV platform for state and PSU partners (PTC India 2,000 MW, OREDA, MAHAPREIT with DIPAM approval, SJVNL 200 MW wind PPA, NCRTC 110 MW captive solar), now held as step-down subsidiaries. “NIRL signed a JV agreement with PTC India Ltd, for development of 2000 MW of green energy capacity and formation of JV company is in progress.”
- *Scheme* — The parent is funding the vehicle ahead of the IPO, taking its NIRL equity to Rs 5,119.75 crore, while renewables segment assets roughly doubled to Rs 10,881.76 crore from Rs 5,470.15 crore a year earlier. “The company invested 200,00,00,000 equity shares in NLC India Renewables Limited (NIRL ), wholly owned subsidiary of the company at Rs. IO per share aggregating to Rs. 2,000 crore on 12th October 2026.”
- *Scheme* — The structure deliberately avoids a merger/demerger scheme: it is a related-party slump sale at book value between holding company and wholly owned subsidiary, so Regulation 37A does not apply. “No amalgamation/ merger is envisaged. Hence compliance w.r.t. Regulation 37A of SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015, is not applicable as the transaction is being entered between the Company and its Wholly Owned Subsidiary i.e. NIRL.”

*Not explained on the calls:* No call transcripts were extractable, so no management commentary, margin, valuation, capital-allocation or focus rationale; IPO size, pricing, timing, use of proceeds and residual NLCIL stake are unstated.

### The business being separated — its own numbers

**Power - Renewable (quarterly statements label it "Power - Renewables"); the entity being separated is NLC India Renewables Limited (NIRL), a wholly owned subsidiary incorporated 14.06.2023 to take over existing operational renewable assets (1,420 MW, NBV ₹5,107 crore as on 31.03.2024) under Asset Monetization** · unit ₹ crore · Revenue = 'External Sales' for the Power - Renewable segment (consolidated Ind AS 108 segment note); the segment has no inter-segment sales, so External Sales = Total Revenue. Operating_profit = 'Segment Result', defined in the quarterly statement as Profit(+)/Loss(-) before tax and interest from each segment (i.e. segment EBIT before finance cost, other income and unallocable corporate expenses) — it is NOT EBITDA and NOT PBT. The 'Operating Profit' line in the segment note (FY2026 ₹3,747.90 cr; FY2025 ₹3,732.56 cr) is group-level after other income and unallocable expenses, not segment-level. ## Rights and preferential offerings — who is buying

A rights issue hands the paper to existing holders; a preferential issue of equity or warrants hands it to named buyers at a fixed price. The notes' question is the same for both: are the insiders putting money in? ## How this was built

- **Filings:** NSE's corporate-announcements feed read month by month for the 2024-06-13 → 2026-11-15 window and filtered to the 752 official NiftyTotalMarket constituents; BSE via its daily RSS (accumulating) and the BSE-sourced per-company lists on screener.in. Each filing is classified by category and headline, its attachment reduced to text and re-classified from the text. Stored in `IndividualStockAnalysis/India/Announcements/NiftyTotalMarket/`.
- **Confidence:** confirmed = a Demerger / Scheme filing or a scheme text that demerges is on the exchange record; probable = a subsidiary listing in motion or a scheme whose nature the documents do not settle; indicated = news verification, denial or calls alone.
- **Listing:** from the record date and listing filings; where neither exists, what the filings and calls say about timing, or that nothing is stated. The 4–10 week note is the typical gap between record date and listing seen in these filings, not a forecast.
- **Rationale:** every passage in the last 36 months of the stored calls where the separation was discussed, plus the scheme's rationale section, read by the judge; each point links to its transcript. Transcripts and presentations are indexed in `InvestorPresentations/NiftyTotalMarket/_concall_links.csv`.
- **Parent numbers:** the stored consolidated P&L and cash-flow statements (screener.in); growth and margins computed here. P/E from the live Nifty 500 market file, else latest stored close ÷ latest fiscal-year EPS. Charts are Mermaid xychart blocks (render on GitHub).
- **Segment numbers:** the last three annual reports and twelve quarterly presentations (`AnnualReports/`, `InvestorPresentations/`, page-marked text), their segment-reporting pages read by the judge with document and page per number; growth and margins computed here. Where the pages do not carry the figures, the report says so.
- **Judge:** claude-opus-5 read the schemes, three years of calls and the segment pages; reads only the documents shown to it, must quote, cached per document hash and model.
- **Score:** share of checklist items answered yes (1) or partly (½), on 10 — visibility of the pattern in the documents, not stock quality.
- **Coverage:** `_coverage.csv` lists, per highlighted company, which of the above was found and which was not.
